chapters.title: Chapter 301
paragraphs: Go Jun was utterly confident.
I can do this.
It had been some thirty years since he first met Lee Jungryong, after losing his parents in the Great Cataclysm and becoming an orphan.
“I’ve had my eye on you for some time. Would you like to come with me?”
“Me?”
“Yes. You have exceptional talent.”
Only then did Go Jun understand.
How a mere orphan like him had grown up with the finest education in the best possible environment. Who the anonymous benefactor he had never once seen truly was.
Lee Jungryong was no Daddy Long-Legs from a fairy tale, but that alone was reason enough to follow him.
“Yes, sir.”
“From now on, call me Master.”
That was how it all began.
He had to learn strange movements and unfamiliar ways of breathing alongside other children, but Go Jun loved every moment of it.
His tiny hands blistered, then formed calluses. The skin split, healed, and hardened... Go Jun’s life followed much the same path.
The pain made him stronger, until at last he came to stand at Lee Jungryong’s right hand.
“Starting today, you’re the Head of Security.”
“Please tell me what I should and shouldn’t do.”
“Follow my orders. Never defy them. That is all.”
His Master’s answer burned itself deep into Go Jun’s mind.
He lived his life by the path Lee Jungryong laid out for him—sometimes in the shadows, sometimes in the light...
He carried out countless tasks for Lee Jungryong, never once leaving room for error.
Unlike the Hunters who inflated their reputations and reveled in flashy lives, Go Jun concealed his true strength and quietly completed every assignment Lee Jungryong gave him.
Even within the Ares Guild, everyone could only speculate about his abilities. Lee Jungryong alone knew the true extent of his strength.
“Doesn’t it frustrate you?”
“What do you mean?”
“Always remaining by my side.”
“I’ve never thought about it.”
“With your abilities, you could make a name for yourself anywhere right now.”
“I have no interest in such things. I will always remain by your side, Master.”
“Ha ha. You seem even more dependable than usual today.”
Go Jun had meant every word. Every member of the security team had received Lee Jungryong’s teachings, but no other Disciple worshipped and revered him as blindly as Go Jun did.
Exceptional ability and unwavering loyalty.
Ironically, those two virtues were precisely what led Go Jun to defy Lee Jungryong’s orders.
“If it hadn’t been for my Master’s special order... you would have died here.”
“Your Master? Oh, Jungryong?”
“How’s Jungryong doing? Isn’t it about time he started looking for a place in a retirement community?”
It was an insult Go Jun could not endure. To him, Lee Jungryong was a parent, a Master, and practically a god.
It was only natural for a fanatic to lose his mind when someone insulted the god he worshipped.
You filthy bastard... I’ll tear you apart.
The moment his Master’s order to avoid a clash with the Peace Guild was wiped clean from his mind, aura had already gathered around his fist.
“If you think this will end the same way it did last time... I’ll make you regret it.”
Go Jun already knew Jin Taekyung’s abilities from their brief clash at the hospital a week ago.
But that confrontation had taken place under his Master’s orders. At the time, Go Jun had displayed less than half his true strength.
Now Jin Taekyung would pay dearly for underestimating him.
I’ll go all out and finish this in a single blow.
He did not care about the aftermath. He only wanted to punish the bastard who had insulted his Master as brutally as possible.
And Go Jun had absolute confidence in his strength.
“Die!”
Whoooosh!
His fist shot forward like a ray of light, accompanied by a terrifying crack of displaced air.
Only three steps separated him from Jin Taekyung.
The bastard stood there smiling broadly, his arms spread wide. He was completely defenseless.
In a world that seemed to slow around him, Go Jun’s fist drove forward with enough force to punch straight through Taekyung’s chest.
Taekyung did not move an inch.
It’s over, brat.
A triumphant smile had just begun to curl Go Jun’s lips when—
Kkwaaang!
A thunderous boom split the sky.
But Go Jun never heard it. An overwhelming recoil surged through his fist as lava-like heat swept through his insides.
What is this...?
His vision flashed white. Agony engulfed him, as though a red-hot blade were churning through his stomach.
His mouth fell open, and something came pouring out.
“Bleeergh!”
Splaash.
Go Jun doubled over like a shrimp and vomited up his insides, his eyes bulging.
Blood.
There was blood everywhere. Unidentifiable pale objects lay scattered throughout the dark-red pool soaking the ground.
It did not take him long to realize they were pieces of his internal organs.
“W-what the hell...?”
As Go Jun stared in shock at the pool of his own blood, a foot suddenly entered his field of vision.
“Didn’t you say you’d make me regret it?”
“Strange. Doesn’t look like much to me.”
He did not need to raise his head to know.
He knew whose foot was planted in his blood. He knew who spoke with that ice-cold voice, blazing with barely contained heat.
How...? How did I lose in a single blow...?
One clash.
That single clash had become a pillar of fire, reducing the painstaking tower Go Jun had spent thirty years building to ashes.
How is this possible?
His entire body trembled.
Pain?
No.
What ruled him now was fear—an emotion he had felt from only one person in his entire life.
His Master, Lee Jungryong.
“Raise your head.”
That very fear seized Go Jun by the hair and slowly dragged his head upward.
A foot submerged in a pool of blood. A straight, steel-hard leg. A torso covered in the supple, powerful muscles of a wild beast.
And then...
A fierce light burned in his eyes.
Within the black forest, surrounded on all sides by faint darkness, two eyes filled with flame stared down at Go Jun.
“Give your Master a message.”
Hot breath brushed his ear. A whisper quiet enough for him alone to hear followed.
“As long as I’m here, no one lays a hand on the Peace Guild.”
Go Jun’s eyelids quivered. A hoarse voice slipped between his blood-soaked lips.
“What... are you?”
“Me?”
A moment later, the answer echoed not in his ears, but directly inside his head.
—A descendant of the Fire King. I am the successor to the Blazing Flame.
The voice was like an auditory hallucination.
Go Jun did not realize it was Sound Transmission, nor did he understand the meaning behind the words.
Only one word filled his mind.
Monster...
The last thing Go Jun saw was Jin Taekyung’s playfully smiling face.
Then his body toppled like a rotten old tree.
Slump. Thud!
A suffocating silence descended.
No one dared to speak. No one could even move. Hundreds of trembling pairs of eyes swept over my entire body.
I stared absently at the unconscious Go Jun, then gave a brief assessment.
“So why the fuck did you have to start shit? You’re nothing special, asshole.”
The air froze in an instant.
When I looked away from Go Jun and turned my head, sharp gasps erupted all around me.
One person reacted more violently than the rest.
“Mr. President.”
“Eek!”
Lee Woojoong, the Seoul Branch President, jumped and averted his eyes before answering.
“D-did you call me?”
“Why are you suddenly speaking so formally? You were talking pretty informally just a minute ago.”
The President’s face turned deathly pale as he stammered.
“M-me? I was?”
“Don’t you remember?”
“Lately, lately my memory hasn’t been so good. I keep forgetting things...”
“Oh, is that so? Then you must have already forgotten everything that happened between us today.”
“Judging by your expression, your memory seems just fine.”
If he still could not take the hint after all that, he never would have risen to such a high-ranking position.
The President hurriedly shook his head.
“No. Of course not. I-I’ll make sure everyone keeps their mouths shut.”
“Keeps their mouths shut?”
“Gah! That’s not what I meant.”
“The people who came with you must have bad memories too. Right?”
“Y-yes. Yes, exactly. They all suffer from short-term amnesia. Isn’t that right?”
More than two hundred Association Hunters had followed their direct superior into the Gate. Every one of them began nodding frantically.
“That’s right.”
“Of course. I don’t even remember my own name.”
“Wait. Where am I? Who am I?”
Who the hell said that last one?
I barely managed to suppress my urge to check his face.
“Well, that works out nicely.”
I smiled broadly. The President and the other Hunters forced themselves to smile along with me.
Not that I expected this to keep everything quiet. There were far too many witnesses for that.
Next up...
“Who’s in charge over there?”
“I am.”
A sharp-eyed middle-aged man stepped forward. He was an A-rank Hunter and a team leader in the Ares Guild.
Still looking as though he could not believe his eyes, he glanced between me and the fallen Go Jun before biting his lip.
“I don’t know what happened between you and Team Leader Seok... but you’ve made a serious mistake.”
Judging by his words, he clearly did not know the exact circumstances behind the incident.
I grinned.
“These things happen. What can you do?”
“Aren’t you worried about how the Vice Guild Master will react when he hears about this?”
“Not worried, no. I am looking forward to it, though. Be sure to report everything to Mr. Lee Jungryong.”
The middle-aged man flinched, as did every Ares Guild member lined up behind him.
I could not tell whether it was because of the way I addressed Lee Jungryong or my shameless attitude.
Then again, I was far more interested in how Lee Jungryong would react to the report than in what any of them thought.
Looks like old Jungryong is in for one hell of a headache.
In this little production, Lee Jungryong had been cast as the cleanup man.
Since he would not want word getting out, he would have to cover people’s eyes and ears, then switch off any loudspeakers that might spread the story.
It hasn’t even been two weeks since that incident, and he’s already showing his teeth again... Impressive. Truly.
We had barely finalized our deal, yet Lee Jungryong had bared his teeth again the instant an opportunity presented itself.
The thought sent a chill down my spine.
What if I really had died here?
That would have ended the fight then and there. Without me, the Peace Guild would never be able to stand against the giant that was Ares.
It also drove one fact home all over again.
If I let my guard down in this fight for even a moment, it’s over.
There would be no truce in this war. Only an end. Our enemies would keep watching for the slightest opening to bare their teeth again.
“Whew.”
In any case, I had done the bare minimum to settle matters.
Or so I thought.
Four pairs of eyes bored into me with terrifying intensity.
Dozens more demanded an explanation.
Ah. I forgot about our Guild.
I had forgotten the most important thing. But where was I supposed to begin? And how much was I supposed to tell them?
After a moment’s thought, I opened my mouth.
“I went to take a piss.”
Silence flowed through the area.
Then Song Song spoke in a gentler voice than I had ever heard from her before.
“Taekyung.”
“Yeah?”
“Can I kill you?”
“...I’ll explain once we’re outside.”
Right. Let’s get out of here.

chapters.title: Chapter 302
paragraphs: More than thirty minutes had passed since the rescue team was deployed.

Hunters from other Guilds who had been assigned to guard the perimeter against any unforeseen incident had already drawn their weapons, while broadcast crews reported on the situation with microphones and cameras.
The commotion was not limited to the ground.
Dozens of combat helicopters circled overhead, and countless camera-equipped drones roamed the sky, broadcasting the entire scene across Korea.
“What are you watching so intently?”
“A live news broadcast.”
“News? You barely even watch variety shows. What got into you? Did something happen?”
“Do you carry your phone around as a decoration? It’s been over two hours since all hell broke loose over that Named Monster, asshole. Try checking the internet once in a while.”
“Holy shit. ‘Named Monster Appears... Jin Taekyung Presumed Dead.’ Is this for real?”
“I don’t know. I can’t hear, so stop talking to me.”
At home, at school, at work, and even aboard crowded public transportation during rush hour, everyone was staring at a television or the phone in their hand.
The live stream on HunterTV’s iTube channel had passed one hundred thousand concurrent viewers long ago.

└ Did Lord Fuck really die? └ Don’t say shit like that. └ I’m not trying to be pessimistic. Honestly, at this point, his chances of survival are slim. The golden window for a rescue operation is fifteen minutes, and there hasn’t been a word for over an hour. On top of that, they’re dealing with a Named Monster. └ Still, that rescue force was no joke. I’ve never seen so many A-rank Hunters gathered in one place. └ That’s my point—what are they rescuing? You don’t rescue a corpse. You recover it. No wonder the Peace Guild Team Leader was screaming that they were fucking bastards earlier. Safety matters, sure, but saving the person should come first. └ Facts: Lord Fuck is already considered almost certainly dead. The deployed Hunters appear to be focused on raiding the Named Monster rather than rescuing him. Since there’s been no word from the rescue team either, we can’t rule out that the battle has already begun—or that they’ve been wiped out. └ What? Wiped out? What happens if they get wiped out too? └ What do you mean, what happens? The Named Monster goes on a foodie tour. It’ll probably start by eating the people waiting outside as appetizers. The surrounding area is already under an emergency evacuation order. └ Fuck, I’ve got such a thick layer of fat I wouldn’t even taste good. Can’t we just cook it some ramen instead? ; └ Are you another fucking idiot? You think it’ll go back into the Gate just because it’s full? └ Guys, for a Named Monster like that, what’s its people max? └ What the hell does “people max” mean? └ The maximum number of people it can take. └ Another idiot has joined the chat. └ Do the assholes cracking jokes right now have nothing but udon noodles for brains? Have you thought about what’ll happen if monsters come out instead of people the next time the Gate opens?
As one commenter had bluntly pointed out, the situation was more serious than it seemed.
The Hunters deployed there possessed overwhelming strength, but their opponent was a Named Monster.
If it possessed power beyond anything they could imagine, the result would be catastrophic.
There had been cases where a single powerful Named Monster caused tens of thousands of casualties and destroyed an entire city.
As time passed, tension began to spread through the chat as well.

└ There really hasn’t been any news. Someone should’ve come out by now. └ Aren’t rescue operations normally like this? └ Nope. Communication devices don’t work inside Gates, so normally someone has to come out every thirty minutes and report that they’re still alive. └ Then why hasn’t anyone come out? They said the battle site was just a stone’s throw from the Gate. └ Are they fighting the Named Monster? Shouldn’t they deploy Central Plains forces?
Just then, the broadcast caught the Gate’s magic field rippling like a wave.
At the same time, the chat that had been consumed by heated arguments began scrolling upward at a maddening speed.
└ They’re coming out!!! └ The magic field just moveddddd! └ Go go go go go go go! └ Please let it be people. └ I want to see Lord Fuck. I hope he’s alive.
On the internet, on television, and at the scene itself, countless people—roughly half the population of Korea—watched the change taking place at the Gate.
Then, in the next moment—
Whoooosh!
The swirling magic field of the Gate began vomiting out several objects.
Human arms and legs. Clad in gleaming armor and armed with weapons, they marched out in neat ranks.
They were not monsters, but the Hunters who had entered earlier.
“Woooooah!”
The explosive cheer from the crowd startled the middle-aged man in a suit at the head of the group.
But he soon broke into a broad smile, his double chin folding as he waved.
“Yes! I’ve returned, everyone! We’re all safe!”

└ I’ve been wondering for a while—who’s that guy? └ Lee Woojoong. It’s written “Seoul Branch President,” but you pronounce it “idiot.” Everyone already knows he’s incompetent. └ Why is that asshole Lee Woojoong grandstanding? └ The guy went in on a rescue operation and he’s the only one wearing a suit, lmao. └ Lee Woojoong, man boobs, whatever—quit blocking the screen and move.
Criticism flooded the chat.
The cameras mounted on the drones avoided Lee Woojoong and filmed the Hunters emerging behind him.
First came the government-affiliated Hunters from the Association, which had led the operation. Then the cameras captured the Ares Guild members walking out with grim expressions.
They were carrying a stretcher covered with a large sheet. As it swayed with each step, one blood-soaked hand slipped out from beneath the cloth.
Pop-pop-pop! Click, click!
Camera flashes burst from every direction. A wave of mourning spread through the people watching.
└ Ah... I was hoping it wouldn’t end like this. └ Jin Taekyung really did die. └ May he rest in peace. └ May he rest in peace. I hope he finds peace in heaven.
Just as everyone was swept up in grief, a voice rang out.
“Whoa. Why are there so many?”
The news anchor solemnly reporting Jin Taekyung’s death, the photographers hammering their shutters, and even the chat being flooded with messages wishing the deceased peace—
Everyone stopped what they were doing and stared wide-eyed at one person.
“Wow, look at all these cameras. By the way, is it really okay to broadcast something like this live?”
The young man looked around in fascination.
There was no one who did not know the name of the man wearing simple leather armor with a spear strapped to his back.
└ ...Isn’t that Jin Taekyung? └ Huh? └ ??? └ Why is hyung coming out of there...? └ Am I the only one seeing a ghost?
As everyone floundered in a pit of confusion, one field reporter was the first to recover. He thrust a microphone toward Jin Taekyung.
“A-are you Jin Taekyung?”
“No, this is Patrick.”
“What?”
“I’m kidding. It’s me.”
This asshole was making jokes? On live television?
Reeling from the completely unexpected dumb joke, the reporter pulled himself together and asked another question.
“So you weren’t dead.”
“Seeing as I’m doing this interview here, it looks like I didn’t.”
“Then who was the person on the stretcher that came out earlier?”
“Oh, him.”
Jin Taekyung scratched his neck before answering.
“Well, how should I put it... He’s a Hunter who was injured while fighting bravely. His injuries aren’t that serious, so he’ll recover soon.”
“Then where is the Named Monster?”
“The Named Monster? There isn’t one.”
“What? Are you saying there was never a Named Monster in the first place?”
“No, there was.”
Jin Taekyung calmly added,
“Now there isn’t.”
It was the moment a legend was born.
“There’s something I’d like to ask...”
Team Leader Choi suddenly looked up from the newspaper covered in squiggly foreign writing.
“Why exactly are you in my office, Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
“Why? Am I not allowed to drop by?”
“I’m asking because you come here more often than I do, and I’m the owner.”
“Come on, these things happen. I only stopped in for a minute to see you.”
“The door was locked.”
“It was open.”
“You broke the lock.”
“Really? How strange.”
“I’m asking just in case—really, just in case...”
Team Leader Choi removed his glasses and asked calmly,
“Do you come here because of the seventeenth-century-style Russian imperial sofa made by the Russian furniture master Sorkovache?”
Sprawled across the sofa, I answered,
“Absolutely not.”
“Do you realize that saying that while lying there makes you rather unconvincing?”
“Nope. Ah, this is comfortable.”
The price tag was uncomfortable, but once I lay back on it, I could not tear myself away.
As befitted a chaebol—no, a third-generation hero—Team Leader Choi’s office was packed with things like this.
A state-of-the-art hologram TV with incredible picture quality was one of them.
“The next video we’d like to show you is the sensational clip that’s set the past week on fire. Johnson, have you seen it?”
On the screen, a Black man nodded in response to a question from a long-nosed white man. Looking at him, I could not help wondering why his name was Johnson.
“Of course, Conan. I’ve already memorized every line.”
“What line?”
“You know, the last thing he said.”
It was a popular American talk show, famous enough that even I had heard of it.
The co-host, Johnson, spoke with a solemn expression.
“It wath there. Now it’th gone.”
“Ha-ha! That was exactly the same!”
Exactly the same, my ass. Does he have actual snails in his ears instead of cochleae?
I shook my head and turned off the TV.
They were bound to play that interview again as stock footage, so turning it off now was the wise choice.
“Your popularity shows no sign of fading.”
“I know. I said it without thinking. I had no idea it would become this big.”
“I’m afraid I see it differently.”
Team Leader Choi had already whipped up a cup of coffee. He sat down across from me and continued.
“It wasn’t the words that became a hot topic. It was the man who said them. You hunted two Named Monsters, and you did it alone. Of course the entire world is paying attention.”
A week had already passed, but the impact of that day had not faded. If anything, the flames were raging hotter than ever.

My official interview video on iTube passed two hundred million views within twenty-four hours, shattering the record previously held by an idol singer. Edited clips and all kinds of memes poured in from every corner of the world.
And on top of that...
“We’ve received another interview request from the American broadcaster CNM.”
“Another one?”
“I already told you that BCC in the United Kingdom made an offer. They want to invite you as a special guest and said they can give you up to twenty minutes for a live interview.”
“How special. Seriously.”
Interview requests were pouring in from the flagship broadcasters of major countries anyone would recognize by name.
Of course, I had not accepted a single one. By now, merely hearing about them made my head throb.
“Are you still considering it?”
“Yes. If it’ll help the Peace Guild grow, I should do everything I can, but...”
I lowered my voice until only Team Leader Choi could hear me.
“It’s all a lie.”
That was right. This was the most important part.
None of what surrounded me was actually true.
Team Leader Choi spoke with a tense expression.
“That... Did you bring it again today?”
“Of course.”
With the solemn expression of a priest performing a ritual to summon a god, I chanted the incantation.
“Come forth, Warlordmon!”
Inventory. Summon.
At the command I uttered in my mind, a glossy black skull appeared on my palm, making a tremendous racket.
“Who are you calling Warlordmon?! I am the master of the Black Forest and the commander of the great Army of the Dead! I’m a Skeleton Warlord!”
“Warlordmon, forward roll!”
“You insane human!”
“Warlordmon, Quick Attack!”
Papapapapat!
Team Leader Choi watched me clutch the Warlord’s skull and shake it at insane speed. Then he muttered as though he had attained enlightenment.
“Why on earth did you capture that thing and bring it back...?”

They said the battle site was just a stone’s throw from the Gate. └ Are they fighting the Named Monster?
Shouldn’t they deploy Central Plains forces?
Just then, the broadcast caught the Gate’s magic field rippling like a wave.
At the same time, the chat that had been consumed by heated arguments began scrolling upward at a maddening speed.
└ They’re coming out!!! └ The magic field just moveddddd! └ Go go go go go go go! └ Please let it be people. └ I want to see Lord Fuck.
I hope he’s alive.

Whoooosh!

Human arms and legs.
Clad in gleaming armor and armed with weapons, they marched out in neat ranks.
They were not monsters, but the Hunters who had entered earlier.
“Woooooah!”
The explosive cheer from the crowd startled the middle-aged man in a suit at the head of the group.

I’ve returned, everyone!
We’re all safe!”

Pop-pop-pop!
Click, click!

A wave of mourning spread through the people watching.

The news anchor solemnly reporting Jin Taekyung’s death, the photographers hammering their shutters, and even the chat being flooded with messages wishing the deceased peace—

There was no one who did not know the name of the man wearing simple leather armor with a spear strapped to his back.

chapters.title: Chapter 303
paragraphs: A week earlier, the four people who heard my whole story had reacted in ways that were both alike and completely different.
“You captured a Named Monster alive, took control of it, and used it for raids? Hahaha! You crazy bastard!”
“...Are you actually fucking insane?”
“I’m sorry to ask this, but... have you truly lost your mind, Hunter Jin Taekyung?”
“You’ve gone insane. I’ll pretend I never heard any of this.”
Im Kkeokjeong was the only one who laughed. Song Song, Butler Kim, and Team Leader Choi looked at me as though I belonged in a psychiatric ward.
But what else could I have done? The moment the interview ended, the media erupted like an active volcano, and in less than an hour, I became a celebrity known to half the population of Korea.
“I should have stopped it then.”
Papapapapat!
Team Leader Choi lamented as he watched Warlordmon perform Quick Attack.
But the water had already been spilled, and for such a spectacular mess, it had been cleaned up remarkably well.
“Still, everything worked out.”
Even the government audit team, renowned for its thoroughness, failed to uncover the truth behind the incident.
That was only natural. No one could have imagined what had really happened. Besides, there was plenty of evidence to support the official story.

“The magical-power distribution survey conducted with a magical-power meter passed without issue, and they recovered both fragments of the Skeleton Warlord’s armor and pieces of its bones. It was an open-and-shut case.”
Everything left traces behind.
Unlike the other Skeletons, which had either melted or shattered under One Annihilation, the Warlord’s incredibly durable bones had retained their shape.
Still saturated with immense magical power, they were accepted as crucial evidence proving both the Named Monster’s existence and its defeat.
“Come to think of it, didn’t they put those soup bones up for auction? I wonder how much they sold for.”
“Soup bones?! Do not refer to my noble body in such a manner!”
“You still haven’t grasped your situation. Warlordmon, Body Slam.”
Thump! Thump! Thump!
The Warlord bounced off the office walls like a tennis ball, clicking its jaw mournfully.
“Ah, my loyal soldiers. How I long to see you.”
“So, where’s this month’s tribute of troops?”
“...I shall replenish their numbers as soon as possible.”
Just then, the office door opened with a click.
A pair of shapely legs began to step inside, then stopped short. Looking up into a pair of light-brown eyes, I asked,
“What are you doing? Aren’t you coming in?”
“...Jin Taekyung, you crazy bastard. If you were me, would you want to walk into a room where someone was playing ball with a talking skeleton?”
“Yeah.”
I waved the Skeleton Warlord at the disgusted Song Song.
“Warlordmon, scare her.”
“Eeeeeeeek! Don’t! I said don’t!”
“Warlordmon, wag your tail.”
“I do not have a tail.”
“Then use Quick Attack.”
Papapapapat!
“Urrrgh, urrrghhhh!”
“Eeeeeeeek!”
Thank God for the sound-blocking spell.
Just as Song Song’s screams and the Skeleton Warlord’s howls blended into a perfect a cappella harmony, Team Leader Choi’s phone rang on the table.
“Everyone, please be quiet for a moment.”
Team Leader Choi stared intently at the screen. Several minutes passed before he finally spoke.
“I think I’ll need to step away.”
“Did something happen?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head at my question.
“I’ll tell you once this matter is confirmed. And, Miss Song.”
“Yes?”
“First, cancel the additional raid scheduled for next week. I expect to be neglecting my duties for the next several days, so please assist Butler Kim.”

These days, even ten of Butler Kim would not have been enough. On top of handling the aftermath of the incident, he was leading the Guild members on raids and continuing his training in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
Of course, the five of us, myself included, were dividing the work between us. But as the Guild Master, he was busy on a completely different level.
“Got it. That’s easy enough. It’s not like we can make Uncle Kkeokjeong do it.”
Song Song nodded readily, then paused and looked at me.
“But what are you going to do?”
“Me?”
“Who else would I be talking about?”
“Warlordmon, Quick—”
“If you do that one more time, I’ll kill you. I mean it.”
“...Attack.”
That was probably enough.
I casually slipped Warlordmon into my Inventory as it spasmed reflexively like one of Pavlov’s dogs.
“I’m getting ready to leave.”
“Leave? I’m working overtime today.”
“I have somewhere to be.”
“Oh, really? What could possibly be so important that you get to leave on time while everyone else keeps working?”
I answered with a huge yawn.
“An exam.”
“An exam? What exam?”
“What do you think? Don’t you even know what day it is?”
Song Song blinked for a moment, then her eyes widened.
It was the middle of November. No matter how busy someone was, they knew what day it was. This was an exam important enough for the news to run a countdown to it.
“Are you taking the college entrance exam?”
“Are you crazy? My sister is.”
I checked the clock on the office wall.
Five in the afternoon. If I left now, I should arrive around the time the exam ended.
“I’m heading out. Hang in there. You too, Song-i.”
I rose from the soft sofa and left the office.
I could picture Mom praying fervently near the test center and Hayeon working her way through the questions.
I’m worried. She probably hasn’t been able to study properly lately because of me.
For the past few months, the various incidents surrounding me had exposed Hayeon to the media and forced her to endure intense attention from everyone around her.
For a student on the verge of taking the college entrance exam, it was devastating.
I feel bad.
I could only hope her results reflected all the effort she had put in.
With anxiety gnawing at me, I headed for the test center. An hour later, I saw Hayeon’s gloomy face and realized my fears had come true.
“You... Never mind. You worked hard.”
“Yes, sweetheart. You’ve worked so hard.”
At Mom’s and my words, Hayeon gave us a faint smile.
“Well, look who actually showed up. I can barely remember the last time I saw your face.”
“My little sister is taking the college entrance exam. Of course I had to come, you brat.”
“Even after disguising yourself like that?”
“Is it that obvious?”
“Yeah. Sunglasses and a mask at night look terrible. They make you stand out even more.”
“Damn it. No wonder people have been staring at me.”
“Are you an idiot? Of course they’re going to stare when you’re so obviously disguised.”
Her smile was gray and wilted, without a trace of energy. Seeing how completely drained she looked only made me feel guiltier.
“Are you okay?”
Hayeon answered with a miserable expression.
“No.”
“I’m sorry. It’s because of me.”
“I thought I’d get a perfect score, but I got one question wrong in English.”
“Here I am, your own brother, making things harder for you. I’m so ashamed I can’t even look you in the face... What did you just say?”
“I got one wrong! I missed a perfect score on the college entrance exam by one question!”
Thud! Thud!
I stared blankly as Hayeon kicked the ground in frustration.
Is she insane?
She had missed only one question across every subject on the college entrance exam?
I knew she was smart, but I had no idea she was this smart.
No, more importantly, how does she already know she got one wrong?
Was that why she had come out thirty minutes late?
Either way, one thing was certain. This winter was going to be a fairly warm one for our family.
And...
“I got one wrong! One more correct answer and I would’ve had a perfect score, but I missed it!”
If I left that lunatic alone, the students and parents around us would cast a net over heaven and earth to hunt us down.
“Stop talking nonsense and let’s go eat.”
“Let go! What would someone with seventh-tier school grades know about how I feel?”
“Keep your voice down. Please.”
I grabbed my hysterical sister by the back of the neck and dragged her away. From inside my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord muttered,
“Blood truly cannot lie.”
You’re getting one hundred Quick Attacks. Guaranteed.
Time flew by.
With Hayeon’s college entrance exam finally over, our family moved back into our old house once the remodeling was complete. Mom shed tears of joy at the unexpected gift.
“Son... Thank you so much. I don’t know what to say.”
“It’s nothing. Please don’t say that.”
“I’m grateful too, son.”
“Hayeon, now that the college entrance exam is over, would you like your life to be over too?”
Taking care of something that had been on my mind for so long left me feeling much lighter.
Even so, something still nagged at me.
They might go after my family.
Taking someone’s family hostage was a simple but effective tactic.
I didn’t think Lee Jungryong, who had a weakness, would resort to such a method, but I had to prepare for the worst.
I’ll keep making money anyway. There’s no reason to be stingy.
High-ranking Hunters earned so much that people called them walking small and midsize businesses.
But even those top Hunters couldn’t compare to my income.
I cleared raids several times faster than other people, and I often fought solo.
For a Hunter, exceptional skill naturally led to wealth.
And if there was one more thing that came with it, it was fame.
“Butler Kim, could you handle the interview and advertising offers that have come in for me?”
“All of them?”
“No. Just the important ones that pay well.”
Even though I accepted only a tiny fraction of the hundreds of offers, an enormous sum poured into my account.
That was how much interest people had in me, both in Korea and abroad.
A few advertisements, interviews, and appearances on television talk shows. That was more than enough.
The number in my bank account became morbidly obese, and the Peace Guild’s stock price soared.
Two birds with one stone. A double windfall.
“May I ask you for one important favor?”
“Anything. Just say the word.”
“Please find me a security company. A reliable one.”
“Heh-heh. Leave it to me.”
Mom and Hayeon never noticed a thing.

They did not know that the houses on either side of ours and across the street had secretly been purchased. Nor did they know that several seemingly happy married couples were actually undercover bodyguards.
They were only puzzled.
“Son, did you know a lot of married couples live around here?”
“Really?”
“Yes. I run into them whenever I go to the neighborhood market. Some are young and some are older, but none of them have children.”
“It’s the age of low birth rates.”
“Oppa, only two men live next door. They walk around with their arms linked.”
“...It’s the age of gender equality.”
That made them stand out way too much!
A few days after I asked the company to rearrange its personnel, I received a KakaoTalk message from Hayeon.
Jin Hayeon └ Jin Hayeon: Wow └ Jin Hayeon: This time two women moved in └ Jin Hayeon: They walk around with their fingers interlaced all the time;;
Could this security company really be trusted?
Contrary to my concerns, the bodyguards did an excellent job.
Reports came in every thirty minutes, and they never took their eyes off my family.
I was so busy I barely had time to breathe, but everything was proceeding smoothly. Even so, there was one disappointment.
Leveling up.
Ding.
System You defeated a Lv.70 Skeleton Archer! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP! - The difference in power is substantial. The amount of EXP gained is drastically reduced.
“Oh, shit. God, please!”
Despite my desperate pleas, the EXP factory was no longer much help to me.
Three or four level-ups. That was all I got out of it.
“Heh-heh. I do not understand this EXP or leveling up you speak of, but this is excellent news. Human, this is where greed leads!”
“But if I erase you, I can probably squeeze out one more level-up, right?”
“...I shall try harder. Please, anything but that!”
“Whew. I’ll put that off for now. But you’ll keep paying your tribute in troops.”
“Why?! You just said you gain nothing from killing my soldiers anymore!”
“That’s true for me. Our Guild members still need to gain experience.”
“Experience?”

“We can use them to give our people some combat practice. Have your subordinates rehearse their acting. Tell them to make it convincing without letting on that they’re going easy on us. Of course, you know what happens if anyone on our side dies, right?”
“...You intend to suck the marrow from my bones. Just how cruel can the human race be?”
The Skeleton Warlord lamented, but I already held its leash.
The new Guild members gained experience in combat that was almost real against the Skeletons, who made excellent supporting actors.
That’s right. Train hard and grow big and strong.
It was exactly one week after Hayeon’s college entrance exam when Team Leader Choi reappeared.
“It’s been a while, everyone. But before we catch up, there’s something I need to show you.”
With a tired voice and a stiff smile, he looked at us, pulled a USB drive from inside his jacket, and connected it to the hologram TV.
“This video came from China.”
Beep.
The video began playing with a cold electronic tone.

sentences.text: A week earlier, the four people who heard my whole story had reacted in ways that were both alike and completely different.
“You captured a Named Monster alive, took control of it, and used it for raids?
Hahaha!
You crazy bastard!”
“...Are you actually fucking insane?”
“I’m sorry to ask this, but... have you truly lost your mind, Hunter Jin Taekyung?”
“You’ve gone insane.
I’ll pretend I never heard any of this.”
Im Kkeokjeong was the only one who laughed.
Song Song, Butler Kim, and Team Leader Choi looked at me as though I belonged in a psychiatric ward.
But what else could I have done?
The moment the interview ended, the media erupted like an active volcano, and in less than an hour, I became a celebrity known to half the population of Korea.
“I should have stopped it then.”
Papapapapat!
Team Leader Choi lamented as he watched Warlordmon perform Quick Attack.
But the water had already been spilled, and for such a spectacular mess, it had been cleaned up remarkably well.
“Still, everything worked out.”
Even the government audit team, renowned for its thoroughness, failed to uncover the truth behind the incident.
That was only natural.
No one could have imagined what had really happened.
Besides, there was plenty of evidence to support the official story.
“The magical-power distribution survey conducted with a magical-power meter passed without issue, and they recovered both fragments of the Skeleton Warlord’s armor and pieces of its bones.
It was an open-and-shut case.”
Everything left traces behind.
Unlike the other Skeletons, which had either melted or shattered under One Annihilation, the Warlord’s incredibly durable bones had retained their shape.
Still saturated with immense magical power, they were accepted as crucial evidence proving both the Named Monster’s existence and its defeat.
“Come to think of it, didn’t they put those soup bones up for auction?
I wonder how much they sold for.”
“Soup bones?!
Do not refer to my noble body in such a manner!”
“You still haven’t grasped your situation.
Warlordmon, Body Slam.”
Thump!
Thump!
Thump!
The Warlord bounced off the office walls like a tennis ball, clicking its jaw mournfully.
“Ah, my loyal soldiers.
How I long to see you.”
“So, where’s this month’s tribute of troops?”
“...I shall replenish their numbers as soon as possible.”
Just then, the office door opened with a click.
A pair of shapely legs began to step inside, then stopped short.
Looking up into a pair of light-brown eyes, I asked,
“What are you doing?
Aren’t you coming in?”
“...Jin Taekyung, you crazy bastard.
If you were me, would you want to walk into a room where someone was playing ball with a talking skeleton?”
“Yeah.”
I waved the Skeleton Warlord at the disgusted Song Song.
“Warlordmon, scare her.”
“Eeeeeeeek!
Don’t!
I said don’t!”
“Warlordmon, wag your tail.”
“I do not have a tail.”
“Then use Quick Attack.”
Papapapapat!
“Urrrgh, urrrghhhh!”
“Eeeeeeeek!”
Thank God for the sound-blocking spell.
Just as Song Song’s screams and the Skeleton Warlord’s howls blended into a perfect a cappella harmony, Team Leader Choi’s phone rang on the table.
“Everyone, please be quiet for a moment.”
Team Leader Choi stared intently at the screen.
Several minutes passed before he finally spoke.
“I think I’ll need to step away.”
“Did something happen?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head at my question.
“I’ll tell you once this matter is confirmed.
And, Miss Song.”
“Yes?”
“First, cancel the additional raid scheduled for next week.
I expect to be neglecting my duties for the next several days, so please assist Butler Kim.”
These days, even ten of Butler Kim would not have been enough.
On top of handling the aftermath of the incident, he was leading the Guild members on raids and continuing his training in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
Of course, the five of us, myself included, were dividing the work between us.
But as the Guild Master, he was busy on a completely different level.
“Got it.
That’s easy enough.
It’s not like we can make Uncle Kkeokjeong do it.”
Song Song nodded readily, then paused and looked at me.
“But what are you going to do?”
“Me?”
“Who else would I be talking about?”
“Warlordmon, Quick—”
“If you do that one more time, I’ll kill you.
I mean it.”
“...Attack.”
That was probably enough.
I casually slipped Warlordmon into my Inventory as it spasmed reflexively like one of Pavlov’s dogs.
“I’m getting ready to leave.”
“Leave?
I’m working overtime today.”
“I have somewhere to be.”
“Oh, really?
What could possibly be so important that you get to leave on time while everyone else keeps working?”
I answered with a huge yawn.
“An exam.”
“An exam?
What exam?”
“What do you think?
Don’t you even know what day it is?”
Song Song blinked for a moment, then her eyes widened.
It was the middle of November.
No matter how busy someone was, they knew what day it was.
This was an exam important enough for the news to run a countdown to it.
“Are you taking the college entrance exam?”
“Are you crazy?
My sister is.”
I checked the clock on the office wall.
Five in the afternoon.
If I left now, I should arrive around the time the exam ended.
“I’m heading out.
Hang in there.
You too, Song-i.”
I rose from the soft sofa and left the office.
I could picture Mom praying fervently near the test center and Hayeon working her way through the questions.
I’m worried.
She probably hasn’t been able to study properly lately because of me.
For the past few months, the various incidents surrounding me had exposed Hayeon to the media and forced her to endure intense attention from everyone around her.
For a student on the verge of taking the college entrance exam, it was devastating.
I feel bad.
I could only hope her results reflected all the effort she had put in.
With anxiety gnawing at me, I headed for the test center.
An hour later, I saw Hayeon’s gloomy face and realized my fears had come true.
“You...
Never mind.
You worked hard.”
“Yes, sweetheart.
You’ve worked so hard.”
At Mom’s and my words, Hayeon gave us a faint smile.
“Well, look who actually showed up.
I can barely remember the last time I saw your face.”
“My little sister is taking the college entrance exam.
Of course I had to come, you brat.”
“Even after disguising yourself like that?”
“Is it that obvious?”
“Yeah.
Sunglasses and a mask at night look terrible.
They make you stand out even more.”
“Damn it.
No wonder people have been staring at me.”
“Are you an idiot?
Of course they’re going to stare when you’re so obviously disguised.”
Her smile was gray and wilted, without a trace of energy.
Seeing how completely drained she looked only made me feel guiltier.
“Are you okay?”
Hayeon answered with a miserable expression.
“No.”
“I’m sorry.
It’s because of me.”
“I thought I’d get a perfect score, but I got one question wrong in English.”
“Here I am, your own brother, making things harder for you.
I’m so ashamed I can’t even look you in the face...
What did you just say?”
“I got one wrong!
I missed a perfect score on the college entrance exam by one question!”
Thud!
Thud!
I stared blankly as Hayeon kicked the ground in frustration.
Is she insane?
She had missed only one question across every subject on the college entrance exam?
I knew she was smart, but I had no idea she was this smart.
No, more importantly, how does she already know she got one wrong?
Was that why she had come out thirty minutes late?
Either way, one thing was certain.
This winter was going to be a fairly warm one for our family.
And...
“I got one wrong!
One more correct answer and I would’ve had a perfect score, but I missed it!”
If I left that lunatic alone, the students and parents around us would cast a net over heaven and earth to hunt us down.
“Stop talking nonsense and let’s go eat.”
“Let go!
What would someone with seventh-tier school grades know about how I feel?”
“Keep your voice down.
Please.”
I grabbed my hysterical sister by the back of the neck and dragged her away.
From inside my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord muttered,
“Blood truly cannot lie.”
You’re getting one hundred Quick Attacks.
Guaranteed.
Time flew by.
With Hayeon’s college entrance exam finally over, our family moved back into our old house once the remodeling was complete.
Mom shed tears of joy at the unexpected gift.
“Son...
Thank you so much.
I don’t know what to say.”
“It’s nothing.
Please don’t say that.”
“I’m grateful too, son.”
“Hayeon, now that the college entrance exam is over, would you like your life to be over too?”
Taking care of something that had been on my mind for so long left me feeling much lighter.
Even so, something still nagged at me.
They might go after my family.
Taking someone’s family hostage was a simple but effective tactic.
I didn’t think Lee Jungryong, who had a weakness, would resort to such a method, but I had to prepare for the worst.
I’ll keep making money anyway.
There’s no reason to be stingy.
High-ranking Hunters earned so much that people called them walking small and midsize businesses.
But even those top Hunters couldn’t compare to my income.
I cleared raids several times faster than other people, and I often fought solo.
For a Hunter, exceptional skill naturally led to wealth.
And if there was one more thing that came with it, it was fame.
“Butler Kim, could you handle the interview and advertising offers that have come in for me?”
“All of them?”
“No.
Just the important ones that pay well.”
Even though I accepted only a tiny fraction of the hundreds of offers, an enormous sum poured into my account.
That was how much interest people had in me, both in Korea and abroad.
A few advertisements, interviews, and appearances on television talk shows.
That was more than enough.
The number in my bank account became morbidly obese, and the Peace Guild’s stock price soared.
Two birds with one stone.
A double windfall.
“May I ask you for one important favor?”
“Anything.
Just say the word.”
“Please find me a security company.
A reliable one.”
“Heh-heh.
Leave it to me.”
Mom and Hayeon never noticed a thing.
They did not know that the houses on either side of ours and across the street had secretly been purchased.
Nor did they know that several seemingly happy married couples were actually undercover bodyguards.
They were only puzzled.
“Son, did you know a lot of married couples live around here?”
“Really?”
“Yes.
I run into them whenever I go to the neighborhood market.
Some are young and some are older, but none of them have children.”
“It’s the age of low birth rates.”
“Oppa, only two men live next door.
They walk around with their arms linked.”
“...It’s the age of gender equality.”
That made them stand out way too much!
A few days after I asked the company to rearrange its personnel, I received a KakaoTalk message from Hayeon.
Jin Hayeon └ Jin Hayeon: Wow └ Jin Hayeon: This time two women moved in └ Jin Hayeon: They walk around with their fingers interlaced all the time;;
Could this security company really be trusted?
Contrary to my concerns, the bodyguards did an excellent job.
Reports came in every thirty minutes, and they never took their eyes off my family.
I was so busy I barely had time to breathe, but everything was proceeding smoothly.
Even so, there was one disappointment.
Leveling up.
Ding.
System You defeated a Lv.70 Skeleton Archer! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP! - The difference in power is substantial.
The amount of EXP gained is drastically reduced.
“Oh, shit.
God, please!”
Despite my desperate pleas, the EXP factory was no longer much help to me.
Three or four level-ups.
That was all I got out of it.
“Heh-heh.
I do not understand this EXP or leveling up you speak of, but this is excellent news.
Human, this is where greed leads!”
“But if I erase you, I can probably squeeze out one more level-up, right?”
“...I shall try harder.
Please, anything but that!”
“Whew.
I’ll put that off for now.
But you’ll keep paying your tribute in troops.”
“Why?!
You just said you gain nothing from killing my soldiers anymore!”
“That’s true for me.
Our Guild members still need to gain experience.”
“Experience?”
“We can use them to give our people some combat practice.
Have your subordinates rehearse their acting.
Tell them to make it convincing without letting on that they’re going easy on us.
Of course, you know what happens if anyone on our side dies, right?”
“...You intend to suck the marrow from my bones.
Just how cruel can the human race be?”
The Skeleton Warlord lamented, but I already held its leash.
The new Guild members gained experience in combat that was almost real against the Skeletons, who made excellent supporting actors.
That’s right.
Train hard and grow big and strong.
It was exactly one week after Hayeon’s college entrance exam when Team Leader Choi reappeared.
“It’s been a while, everyone.
But before we catch up, there’s something I need to show you.”
With a tired voice and a stiff smile, he looked at us, pulled a USB drive from inside his jacket, and connected it to the hologram TV.
“This video came from China.”
Beep.
The video began playing with a cold electronic tone.

chapters.title: Chapter 304
paragraphs: Every source of light in the office had been blocked out. As the holographic video began playing in the darkness, I suddenly felt as though I were standing at the scene myself.
This place is...
Everything was gray. I couldn’t see an inch in front of me.
Only after an eagle’s massive wing swept dangerously close did I realize where the footage had begun.
The sky.
The drone recording the scene descended rapidly, escaping the fine dust that filled the air.
Whoooosh.
After plunging through the fierce wind for some time, it finally emerged above a city engulfed in flames.
Boom! Rumble-rumble-rumble!
“Eeeeeek!”
“Aaaaaah!”
Factories belching smoke exploded one after another. Towering buildings toppled like dominoes, while people who looked like tiny dots screamed and fled in every direction.
Pandemonium.
There were too many of them to count.
Thousands were visible at a glance. Including those beyond the camera’s view, there had to be tens of thousands.
“What the hell is this...?”
A groan escaped me before I could stop it. Was this because of some factory explosion?
No. It was because I had spotted creatures racing through the maze-like city, spreading destruction and slaughter wherever they went.
“Grrrrrrr!”
“Graaah!”
Massive bodies. Strength and Agility that could only belong to monsters.
Their eyes gleamed with killing intent as they swept across their surroundings. Then, letting out hideous roars, they began searching for targets.
Why are there monsters out there?
The question lasted only a moment before I realized the answer myself.
There was only one possibility.
A Monster Wave.
During the Great Cataclysm, Gates had been passageways connecting Earth to another world known as the Demon Realm.
But after the Demon King Asmodeus disappeared, the monsters’ power weakened, and Gates became doors that only humans could freely pass through.
There was one exception.
If the mana inside a Gate exceeded its capacity, everything changed.
When a dam breaks, the water comes rushing out.
That was a Monster Wave, and the holographic video was showing us the result.
“Kyaaaaaa!”
“P-please, save me...!”
Crunch!
The camera zoomed in on the massacre unfolding in the heart of the city.
Monsters slaughtered and destroyed without restraint while humans died helplessly around them.
Some were impaled on monsters’ claws. Others were trampled to death beneath the feet of the fleeing crowd.
Amid that maelstrom of chaos, a mother and daughter running for their lives caught my eye.
“Bingbing! Hold Mommy’s hand tight!”
The woman had barely shouted the words when—
Whoosh! Thunk!
A spear flew from a dark alley, pierced her chest, and buried itself in the ground.
She vomited up a mouthful of blood, then her body went limp.
The child burst into tears at the sight of her mother dying before her eyes.
“Mommy!”
But it wasn’t over yet. More than a hundred Orcs poured from the dark alley and advanced on the child.
They had taken up ideal positions to block the fleeing civilians’ escape routes.
One Orc who appeared to be their leader raised an axe and brought it down toward the crying child.
Whish! Slice!
“Krk?”
The leader stared down at its arm in confusion.
The thick arm holding the axe had been cleanly severed below the elbow. Before the Orc stood a man who hadn’t been there a moment ago.
“How dare mere monsters lay hands on the people of Zhonghua?”
A dazzling aura flashed.
Slice!
The leader’s head was severed. Before it could even hit the ground, a thunderous cry burst from the man’s mouth.
“Public Security Armed Forces Department!”
“Yes!”
The answer rang out.
The man was not alone. Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces, their armor emblazoned with China’s Five-Starred Red Flag, were streaming onto the battlefield even now.
The man shouted, his eyes blazing.
“Kill every last one of those stinking bastards!”
“For the people!”
Sh-sh-sh-shk!
With a tremendous roar, more than a thousand Hunters charged forward.
Despite the enormous losses it had suffered during the Great Cataclysm, China still had a population of well over a billion.
The strength of each individual was unknown, but it would not be an exaggeration to say that China could mobilize more Hunters than any other country in the world.
“Wipe them all out!”
“Waaah! Long live the People’s Republic of China!”
A thousand Hunters charged as one.
The monsters rampaging through the city weren’t about to stand by and watch. Every kind of monster converged in one place, their numbers easily surpassing a thousand as well.
“Gwoooooo!”
“Kya-woo!”
Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!
Monsters and humans. Humans and monsters.
Two waves that could never coexist surged toward each other.
Eyes shining with resolve, and killing intent directed at the enemy.
The force of the scene filled the office, so overwhelming that it was hard to believe we were watching a holographic video.
High above, the drone captured the two forces rapidly closing the distance between them.
Five hundred meters. Three hundred. One hundred...
Just as the deafening noise reached its peak and the two sides were about to collide—
“Perish in hellfire. Fire Rain.”
A cold voice utterly devoid of life.
At the same time, the gray sky split open.
Kiiiiing.
It was a sight unlike anything I had ever seen.
About thirty meters in the air, not far from the drone, the empty space peeled open as though something had sliced through it.
A massive ball of flame emerged from a vortex writhing with black energy.
Whoooosh!
The Chinese Hunters stopped in their tracks without realizing it and stared blankly at the sight.
“This can’t be.”
“This is... a dream.”
Unfortunately for them, it was all real.
Crack!
The sphere of flame, dozens of meters in diameter, split into four pieces. Each of those four divided into dozens more, and those dozens shattered into hundreds of fragments.
Then the rain of fire struck the earth.
Whoooom! KABOOM!
Rrrrrumble!
The deafening explosions dyed everything red.
The drone was thrown off balance by the aftershock. When it finally steadied itself, the being responsible for creating that spectacular scene was staring directly at it.
“A human device, I see.”
Its voice held neither inflection nor vitality.
The figure wore a robe covered in strange patterns, its hood pulled low. It extended one finger toward the drone.
I shall kill you all and take everything. Those who set foot upon my territory will pay with their lives.
Bzzzzzt!
The instant that finger, gnarled like the root of an ancient tree, moved, the video vanished in a burst of static.
The gray sky choked with fine dust disappeared. So did the scene below, a sight that could only be called the end of the world.
With the hologram gone, a heavy silence descended over the office.
I was the first to speak.
“What the hell is that bastard?”
“He is the man responsible for this Monster Wave. No—he isn’t a man, so I suppose that isn’t quite the right word.”
Team Leader Choi continued in a subdued voice.
“A Named Monster. A Lich. That is what he is.”
A Lich.
A fallen archmage. An apex monster reigning at the top of the pyramid of countless undead.
The Lich that had supposedly vanished after the Great Cataclysm had appeared. It had caused an enormous catastrophe, as though celebrating its return after several decades.
Team Leader Choi unplugged the USB drive and spoke.

“November fifth. This footage was recorded exactly ten days ago by a reconnaissance drone belonging to Chinese intelligence. It shows a small city near Nanchong City in Sichuan Province. The estimated number of casualties so far is approximately three hundred thousand. An accurate count is still unavailable.”
Sichuan.
I was more familiar with it as the region where Qingcheng and Emei of the Nine Sects and One Gang were located, along with the Tang Clan, one of the Five Great Families.
Of course, Murim was an entirely different world that merely resembled China, and what the hologram had shown us was a catastrophe on an unimaginable scale.
“Three hundred thousand?”
“Yes.”
“That’s fucking insane...”
“And that figure covers only the first twenty-four hours after the Wave began.”
A chill ran down my spine.
Three hundred thousand estimated casualties in a single day. Had humanity suffered this much damage from a Monster Wave even once since the Great Cataclysm?
“Are Liches normally this powerful?”
I directed the question not at Team Leader Choi but at Butler Kim, the only one among us who had lived through the Great Cataclysm.
His eyes trembled like ripples on water.

“Of course not. The Liches I saw with my own eyes during the Great Cataclysm were all immensely powerful, but... that one is on an entirely different level. Its fire magic gave me goose bumps just watching it.”
Butler Kim was an A-rank mage who specialized in fire magic.
If a man who had been through hell and back during the Great Cataclysm said that, it showed just how powerful this Lich was.
Where the hell did something like that come from?
The burning city and the people collapsing in pools of blood lingered before my eyes. The enormous rain of fire that had hammered the earth was a disaster in the truest sense of the word.
I remembered the declaration the creature had made to the camera at the very end.
I shall kill you all and take everything. Those who set foot upon my territory will pay with their lives.
No one else could have understood what it said, but I could.
Thanks to the Integrated Language Pack, part of the System, I had heard every word clearly and understood what they meant.
That merciless undead monster would never be satisfied with a single small city.
Three hundred thousand people in one day? With the power it had displayed, the number of casualties might already be ten times higher by now.
“Goddamn it...”
I didn’t particularly like China, but no sane person could look at a catastrophe like this and laugh that they had gotten what they deserved.
The thought of all those people dying helplessly—and the little girl crying over her dead mother—left a bitter taste in my mouth.
Then something occurred to me.
Wait.
Now that I had recovered somewhat from the shock, one thing struck me as strange.
A catastrophe of this magnitude had happened ten days ago, yet the world remained peaceful.
And more importantly...
Where did Team Leader Choi get this information?
If it had been the Ares Guild—or Lee Jungryong—I could have understood. They were one of the world’s leading Guilds, and their intelligence network was exceptional.
But Team Leader Choi was just a team leader in an ordinary mid-sized Guild. If even he knew about this, news of the Sichuan disaster should already have been playing on broadcasts around the world.
There’s something going on.
I wasn’t the only one who had reached that conclusion.
Everyone was staring at Team Leader Choi, silently demanding an explanation.
He wasn’t the kind of person who would fail to notice.
“One week ago, I received an unexpected message.”
That was the day Hayeon finished her college entrance exam.
Team Leader Choi had spent a long time staring at his phone that day before leaving, saying that something important had come up.
“It was from China, wasn’t it?”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Yes. More precisely, it was a request for one particular person to take part in this crisis.”
“Forget everything else for a second. China specifically asked for me?”
“Yes. ‘He’ wanted you.”
“Who’s he?”
A name slipped from Team Leader Choi’s lips.
“Xiao Yang.”
“Gah!”
“Xiao Yang?”
“Young Master. Is that true?”
The moment they heard the name, everyone in the room stared wide-eyed. Naturally, I did the same.
I gaped at Team Leader Choi before finally managing to speak.
“X-Xiao Yang asked for me?”
“Yes.”
“But who’s Xiao Yang?”
Why did they all look like that? It was possible that I didn’t know.
Team Leader Choi’s eyelids twitched for a long moment before he finally spoke.
“Xiao Yang is the General Secretary of China’s Central Committee.”
“Jongseok?”
“The General Secretary! The Chairman—the Chairman of the country!”
Well, fuck me.
