Two waves that could never coexist surged toward each other.
Eyes shining with resolve, and killing intent directed at the enemy.
The force of the scene filled the office, so overwhelming that it was hard to believe we were watching a holographic video.
High above, the drone captured the two forces rapidly closing the distance between them.
Five hundred meters.
Three hundred.
One hundred...
Just as the deafening noise reached its peak and the two sides were about to collide—
“Perish in hellfire.
Fire Rain.”
A cold voice utterly devoid of life.
At the same time, the gray sky split open.
Kiiiiing.
It was a sight unlike anything I had ever seen.
About thirty meters in the air, not far from the drone, the empty space peeled open as though something had sliced through it.
A massive ball of flame emerged from a vortex writhing with black energy.
Whoooosh!
The Chinese Hunters stopped in their tracks without realizing it and stared blankly at the sight.
“This can’t be.”
“This is... a dream.”
Unfortunately for them, it was all real.
Crack!
The sphere of flame, dozens of meters in diameter, split into four pieces.
Each of those four divided into dozens more, and those dozens shattered into hundreds of fragments.
Then the rain of fire struck the earth.
Whoooom!
KABOOM!
Rrrrrumble!
The deafening explosions dyed everything red.
The drone was thrown off balance by the aftershock.
When it finally steadied itself, the being responsible for creating that spectacular scene was staring directly at it.
“A human device, I see.”
Its voice held neither inflection nor vitality.
The figure wore a robe covered in strange patterns, its hood pulled low.
It extended one finger toward the drone.
I shall kill you all and take everything.
Those who set foot upon my territory will pay with their lives.
Bzzzzzt!
The instant that finger, gnarled like the root of an ancient tree, moved, the video vanished in a burst of static.
The gray sky choked with fine dust disappeared.
So did the scene below, a sight that could only be called the end of the world.
With the hologram gone, a heavy silence descended over the office.
I was the first to speak.
“What the hell is that bastard?”
“He is the man responsible for this Monster Wave.
No—he isn’t a man, so I suppose that isn’t quite the right word.”
Team Leader Choi continued in a subdued voice.
“A Named Monster.
A Lich.
That is what he is.”
A Lich.
A fallen archmage.
An apex monster reigning at the top of the pyramid of countless undead.
The Lich that had supposedly vanished after the Great Cataclysm had appeared.
It had caused an enormous catastrophe, as though celebrating its return after several decades.
Team Leader Choi unplugged the USB drive and spoke.
“November fifth.
This footage was recorded exactly ten days ago by a reconnaissance drone belonging to Chinese intelligence.
It shows a small city near Nanchong City in Sichuan Province.
The estimated number of casualties so far is approximately three hundred thousand.
An accurate count is still unavailable.”
Sichuan.
I was more familiar with it as the region where Qingcheng and Emei of the Nine Sects and One Gang were located, along with the Tang Clan, one of the Five Great Families.
Of course, Murim was an entirely different world that merely resembled China, and what the hologram had shown us was a catastrophe on an unimaginable scale.
“Three hundred thousand?”
“Yes.”
“That’s fucking insane...”
“And that figure covers only the first twenty-four hours after the Wave began.”
A chill ran down my spine.
Three hundred thousand estimated casualties in a single day.
Had humanity suffered this much damage from a Monster Wave even once since the Great Cataclysm?
“Are Liches normally this powerful?”
I directed the question not at Team Leader Choi but at Butler Kim, the only one among us who had lived through the Great Cataclysm.
His eyes trembled like ripples on water.
“Of course not.
The Liches I saw with my own eyes during the Great Cataclysm were all immensely powerful, but... that one is on an entirely different level.
Its fire magic gave me goose bumps just watching it.”
Butler Kim was an A-rank mage who specialized in fire magic.
If a man who had been through hell and back during the Great Cataclysm said that, it showed just how powerful this Lich was.
Where the hell did something like that come from?
The burning city and the people collapsing in pools of blood lingered before my eyes.
The enormous rain of fire that had hammered the earth was a disaster in the truest sense of the word.
I remembered the declaration the creature had made to the camera at the very end.
I shall kill you all and take everything.
Those who set foot upon my territory will pay with their lives.
No one else could have understood what it said, but I could.
Thanks to the Integrated Language Pack, part of the System, I had heard every word clearly and understood what they meant.
That merciless undead monster would never be satisfied with a single small city.
Three hundred thousand people in one day?
With the power it had displayed, the number of casualties might already be ten times higher by now.
“Goddamn it...”
I didn’t particularly like China, but no sane person could look at a catastrophe like this and laugh that they had gotten what they deserved.
The thought of all those people dying helplessly—and the little girl crying over her dead mother—left a bitter taste in my mouth.
Then something occurred to me.
Wait.
Now that I had recovered somewhat from the shock, one thing struck me as strange.
A catastrophe of this magnitude had happened ten days ago, yet the world remained peaceful.
And more importantly...
Where did Team Leader Choi get this information?
If it had been the Ares Guild—or Lee Jungryong—I could have understood.
They were one of the world’s leading Guilds, and their intelligence network was exceptional.
But Team Leader Choi was just a team leader in an ordinary mid-sized Guild.
If even he knew about this, news of the Sichuan disaster should already have been playing on broadcasts around the world.
There’s something going on.
I wasn’t the only one who had reached that conclusion.
Everyone was staring at Team Leader Choi, silently demanding an explanation.
He wasn’t the kind of person who would fail to notice.
“One week ago, I received an unexpected message.”
That was the day Hayeon finished her college entrance exam.
Team Leader Choi had spent a long time staring at his phone that day before leaving, saying that something important had come up.
“It was from China, wasn’t it?”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Yes.
More precisely, it was a request for one particular person to take part in this crisis.”
“Forget everything else for a second.
China specifically asked for me?”
“Yes.
‘He’ wanted you.”
“Who’s he?”
A name slipped from Team Leader Choi’s lips.
“Xiao Yang.”
“Gah!”
“Xiao Yang?”
“Young Master.
Is that true?”
The moment they heard the name, everyone in the room stared wide-eyed.
Naturally, I did the same.
I gaped at Team Leader Choi before finally managing to speak.
“X-Xiao Yang asked for me?”
“Yes.”
“But who’s Xiao Yang?”
Why did they all look like that?
It was possible that I didn’t know.
Team Leader Choi’s eyelids twitched for a long moment before he finally spoke.
“Xiao Yang is the General Secretary of China’s Central Committee.”
“Jongseok?”
“The General Secretary!
The Chairman—the Chairman of the country!”
Well, fuck me.

chapters.title: Chapter 305
paragraphs: “Are you feeling any better? You can’t have fully recovered yet.”
“...I’m fine.”
“If it gets too hard, take a rest. You may still be young, Team Leader Seok, but if you keep pushing yourself, you’ll wear yourself down.”
“I have no excuse.”
Lee Jungryong shot a glance at Go Jun, who answered with a pale face, and clicked his tongue inwardly.
I never expected him to go down so easily.
Go Jun was the most useful blade Lee Jungryong possessed.
Although his abilities were not known outside their circle, Lee believed that fewer than five people in all of Korea could stand against him.
Of course, two of those people were Cheon Taemin and Lee himself.
To take him down in a single move... He exceeded my expectations.
Lee could no longer deny it. He had underestimated Jin Taekyung and the Peace Guild.
The gap in strength was laughable, yet he was the one who kept getting humiliated.
His gaze settled on Go Jun’s bowed head.
“Go Jun.”
Go Jun looked up. Lee calling him by name meant this was a conversation between Master and Disciple, not between the Vice Guild Master and his Head of Security.
“Yes, Master.”
“You are the Disciple I poured my heart and soul into training. Never forget that.”
“I have never forgotten it for a single moment. You are more than a parent to me, Master.”
Lee Jungryong nodded at the unwaveringly loyal answer.
Go Jun fell short as a Disciple in many ways, but his loyalty was second to none.
Lee had held off until now in the faint hope that it would not be necessary...but the time had come to sharpen his blade further.
“You were not defeated. You merely fell. I will give you the strength to rise again.”
“Strength, you say?”
“For now, that is all you need to know. I will make you strong enough to defeat Jin Taekyung with your own hands.”
Go Jun’s body trembled as he bowed deeply.
“Thank you, Master.”
“Always remember that your Master believes in you.”
Despite his warm voice, Lee Jungryong’s eyes had sunk to unfathomable depths.
Oblivious to that fact, Go Jun raised his flushed face. By then, the faint sound of someone approaching could be heard beyond the door.
“He’s finally here.”
Go Jun frowned at Lee Jungryong’s mutter.
“He missed the agreed-upon time.”
“Let it go. He’s only in the first year of his term. He wants to enjoy it while he can, before he becomes a lame duck.”
“Even so, to keep you waiting...”
“Team Leader Seok. Remember your position.”
“Understood.”
Go Jun returned from Lee Jungryong’s Disciple to the Ares Guild’s Head of Security and fell silent.
Not long afterward, the door opened and five or six people entered.
The middle-aged man leading them strode toward Lee Jungryong and extended his hand.
“I apologize for keeping you waiting. Traffic was particularly bad today. It reminded me once again how valuable an escort vehicle can be. Ha ha.”
His manner was courteous yet confident. He was someone who could offer his hand first to Lee Jungryong, the de facto leader of the Ares Guild.
The middle-aged man wearing the Korean flag pin on his chest had every right to do so.
Lee Jungryong shook his hand with a faint smile.
“Think nothing of it. Thank you for making the trip, Mr. President.”
Baek Hanseong, the twenty-seventh President of Korea and the youngest person ever elected to the office at the age of forty, nodded.
“It’s been a while, Vice Guild Master Lee. Is this the first time we’ve met since my inauguration at the beginning of the year?”
“That’s right. We seem to be meeting more often than I expected.”
“Pardon me? Ha ha.”
Baek Hanseong let out a dry laugh at Lee Jungryong’s answer.
He knew full well how much power the man before him wielded.
People even said that Korea had two presidents and that the Ares Guild House was another Blue House.
He never once visited the Blue House during the previous president’s term.
The major Guilds were impregnable fortresses built from power and wealth.
And Lee Jungryong, the man who held the Ares Guild in the palm of his hand, enjoyed a status surpassing even that once held by the heads of the chaebol conglomerates.
There were two reasons Baek Hanseong could meet with such a man now, even unofficially.
First, he was still early in his term and enjoyed the full support of the people. Second, they had a matter in which they could help each other.
“They say people become more relaxed as they grow older. I suppose that doesn’t apply to me.”
“You really are refreshingly direct.”
Baek Hanseong understood the meaning behind Lee Jungryong’s subtle remark and held out a pristine white document envelope.
“An unofficial diplomatic letter from Chairman Xiao Yang.”
“Unofficial, as expected.”
“Yes. As you know, that’s how it is.”
The People’s Republic of China. As its formal name suggested, China remained a deeply rooted communist state.
The Communist Party leadership wanted neither unrest among the people nor any loss of faith in the Party.
“You’ve managed to conceal damage on that scale. I’m not sure whether to call that impressive.”
“If the truth comes out, all of China will descend into chaos. By then, there will be no going back.”
Among the tiny number of people who already knew the truth, however, the incident was being called the Sichuan Catastrophe.
The Chinese Communist Party leadership had announced that a major earthquake had struck and deployed the People’s Liberation Army to seal off the surrounding area.
“A Lich, was it? That Named Monster ended up helping China’s Central Committee, albeit unintentionally. I hear even satellites from the United States can’t see what’s happening inside.”
“It’s spatial distortion magic. Extremely powerful spatial distortion magic.”
“I see. I’m still completely ignorant when it comes to magic.”
“It may have helped the Central Committee, but it will have a negative effect on the war situation. We have no idea what is actually happening in there.”
Unlike his unhurried voice, Lee Jungryong’s eyes raced across the words on the documents.
A short while later, after confirming everything, a quiet mutter escaped between his lips.
“Thirty A-rank Hunters and two hundred B-rank Hunters...”
The documents from China were a contract to hire them as mercenaries and resolve the crisis.
They also contained one clause that Lee Jungryong could not overlook.
“They singled me out.”
President Baek Hanseong nodded.
“They say the Central Military Commission strongly insisted on it. They believe the Ares Guild and your role, Vice Guild Master Lee, will be decisive in this matter.”
“I imagine so. The situation must be growing desperate enough to spiral out of control.”
“As you know, China has a great many Hunters, but relatively few of them are truly elite.”
“That has always been China’s problem.”
Tap. Tap. Tap.
Lee Jungryong’s fingers slowly tapped the documents. A calculator was whirring inside his head.
The forces China had requested amounted to twenty percent of the Ares Guild’s total strength.
No. If Lee Jungryong joined them, that figure rose to fifty percent. Fewer than twenty S-rank Hunters existed in the entire world, and each one was an absolute powerhouse.
They must be desperate.
This was not the first offer China had made.
Three days earlier, Lee Jungryong had held a secret meeting with the Chinese ambassador to Korea. The footage shown alongside the proposal had far surpassed his expectations.
That was tremendous magic.
The ability to command more than several thousand monsters. Magic with overwhelming destructive power.

It was on an entirely different level from the Liches he had encountered during the Great Cataclysm. He had seen only a single spell, but that had been more than enough to grasp the danger this incident posed.
However...
Danger always comes with a commensurate reward.
Establishing a foothold in a dictatorship was never easy.
The Sichuan Catastrophe was a disaster to some, but an opportunity to others. And the terms China had offered were sweet—so sweet that Lee worried one of his competitors might seize them first.
As long as I’m there, this operation cannot fail.
Having reached his decision, Lee Jungryong finally spoke.
“I accept China’s proposal.”
“That is a wise decision.”
A smile appeared on President Baek Hanseong’s lips.

If the Ares Guild made a major contribution to resolving the crisis, it would yield considerable diplomatic benefits as well. As someone who wanted to achieve something significant during his term, Baek could not have been more pleased.
“I’m the one who should be grateful that I can help my country and Your Excellency. However...”
Baek Hanseong’s smile faded at Lee Jungryong’s next words.
“I heard a rumor that similar proposals were made not only to the Ares Guild, but also to several of the other ten largest Guilds in Korea.”
“I know it’s an unfounded rumor. But I thought I’d ask you, just in case.”
After a brief silence, Baek Hanseong answered.
“It seems a baseless rumor has leaked out. Nothing of the sort will happen.”
At that moment, the chief secretary standing behind Baek Hanseong thought to himself:
I’ll have to remove tomorrow’s unofficial meeting with the heads of Korea’s ten largest Guilds from the schedule.
Only after pruning away those irritating stray branches did Lee Jungryong smile brightly.
“Just as I thought. I understand. I’ll select the necessary personnel immediately.”
But Baek Hanseong was not finished.
“The rumor about the ten largest Guilds is false, but it isn’t entirely baseless.”
Lee Jungryong paused while gathering the documents.
“What do you mean?”
“Among the Guilds that received China’s proposal, there is one that does not belong to the ten largest Guilds.”
“Don’t tell me...”
A sudden thought flashed through Lee Jungryong’s mind.
At the same time, Baek Hanseong opened his lips.
“The Peace Guild, to which Hunter Jin Taekyung belongs.”
Lee Jungryong’s face hardened.
Again. Once again, that bastard was getting in his way.
Those three syllables—Jin Taekyung—were beginning to irritate him even more than the name Choi Minwoo.
“That is rather inconvenient.”
Lee Jungryong’s voice rasped like sandpaper.
That green president, with a shelf life of only five years, had known about this and done nothing to stop it.
Lee was aware of the new president’s anti-Ares political leanings, but wasn’t this tantamount to openly making an enemy of him?
Suppressing the shout threatening to burst out of him, Lee Jungryong spoke.
“When there are too many boatmen, the ship ends up on a mountain.”
“I’m aware.”
“Your Excellency, this is not a matter that can be handled so simply...”
Baek Hanseong’s calm reply cut him off.
“The owner of the boat personally called for those boatmen. There was nothing I could do.”
“The owner of the boat... Surely not?”
“Yes. Chairman Xiao Yang named them personally. He specifically requested that Vice Guild Master Lee, the Ares Guild, and Hunter Jin Taekyung all participate.”
Lee Jungryong’s eyelids trembled.

At the sight, President Baek Hanseong felt the same thrill he had experienced when he defied everyone’s expectations and won the presidential election. Suppressing the smile threatening to escape, he glanced down at his watch.
“The Peace Guild is a very small operation, so perhaps that’s why they prepared so quickly. They should already be aboard their flight by now.”
—You treacherous human.
“Wow. So this is first class.”
—I was wrong to think you merely treacherous and foolish. I humbly apologize.
“Damn, these cushions are incredible. What kind of alcohol do they have?”
—You are mad. A lunatic. A mad bastard. A crazy fuck!
“Look how spacious these seats are. I could live here.”
—You insane human! Don’t go!
God, he’s noisy as hell.
Pretending not to hear the Skeleton Warlord screaming inside my Inventory, I asked Team Leader Choi, “How much does one of these cost?”
Team Leader Choi launched into his answer as if he had been waiting for me to ask.
“This new model from Focke-Wulf, the German aircraft manufacturer renowned for its outstanding technology—”
Here we go again.
I hurriedly cut him off before he could start explaining the history of Focke-Wulf’s founder.
“I don’t know if it’s Focke-Wulf or Pokémon Black Friday, but I’m asking how much a plane like this usually costs.”
“An aircraft like the one we’re on now should cost a little over one hundred billion won.”
“Hmm. I should buy one.”
Anyone who overheard me would have stared at me as if I were insane.
But it wasn’t impossible.
I recalled the conversation Team Leader Choi and I had shared only a few hours earlier.
“It's a shame, but please tell Grandpa Jongseok I can’t go.”
“It isn’t Grandpa Jongseok. It’s Chairman Xiao Yang. In any case, that is unfortunate.”
I’m sorry too. Promoting my name and raising the Guild’s standing both sound good, but that place is a bit much.
They offered ten billion won.
How much?
Ten billion won. If you go beyond the promised period of one week, they’ll calculate an additional ten billion won per week.
Weekly pay? T-ten billion won a week?
It can’t be helped.
B-but I’m still not going. With thousands of monsters and a crazy skeleton mage, even I have to draw the line. It’s not like I’m some money-crazed bastard.
They say they’ll pay fifty trillion won to whoever kills the Lich.
Ah, now I suddenly feel like eating something spicy. I hear Sichuan cuisine is incredibly hot and savory...
Fuck it. Let’s go.
All the preparations were completed at lightning speed. Only Team Leader Choi and I would be leaving for China.
Chairman Xiao Yang had only wanted me in the first place anyway.
This isn’t about the money.
I was going solely to help the suffering people of China and raise the Guild’s standing.
With my face full of noble resolve, I turned to Team Leader Choi.
“But, Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“If I make fifty trillion won... Do I split that with the Guild too?”
“Let’s settle this before we go. Money matters need to be handled cleanly.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me in disbelief before answering.
“We’ll split it nine to one.”
This guy was something else too.
As we stared at each other like we were both human garbage, an announcement came over the cabin speakers and the private jet sent by China began to take off.

Lee Jungryong paused while gathering the documents.
“What do you mean?”
“Among the Guilds that received China’s proposal, there is one that does not belong to the ten largest Guilds.”
“Don’t tell me...”
A sudden thought flashed through Lee Jungryong’s mind.
At the same time, Baek Hanseong opened his lips.
“The Peace Guild, to which Hunter Jin Taekyung belongs.”
Lee Jungryong’s face hardened.
Again.
Once again, that bastard was getting in his way.
Those three syllables—Jin Taekyung—were beginning to irritate him even more than the name Choi Minwoo.
“That is rather inconvenient.”
Lee Jungryong’s voice rasped like sandpaper.
That green president, with a shelf life of only five years, had known about this and done nothing to stop it.
Lee was aware of the new president’s anti-Ares political leanings, but wasn’t this tantamount to openly making an enemy of him?
Suppressing the shout threatening to burst out of him, Lee Jungryong spoke.
“When there are too many boatmen, the ship ends up on a mountain.”
“I’m aware.”
“Your Excellency, this is not a matter that can be handled so simply...”
Baek Hanseong’s calm reply cut him off.
“The owner of the boat personally called for those boatmen.
There was nothing I could do.”
“The owner of the boat...
Surely not?”
“Yes.
Chairman Xiao Yang named them personally.
He specifically requested that Vice Guild Master Lee, the Ares Guild, and Hunter Jin Taekyung all participate.”
Lee Jungryong’s eyelids trembled.
At the sight, President Baek Hanseong felt the same thrill he had experienced when he defied everyone’s expectations and won the presidential election.
Suppressing the smile threatening to escape, he glanced down at his watch.
“The Peace Guild is a very small operation, so perhaps that’s why they prepared so quickly.
They should already be aboard their flight by now.”
—You treacherous human.
“Wow.
So this is first class.”
—I was wrong to think you merely treacherous and foolish.
I humbly apologize.
“Damn, these cushions are incredible.
What kind of alcohol do they have?”
—You are mad.
A lunatic.
A mad bastard.
A crazy fuck!
“Look how spacious these seats are.
I could live here.”
—You insane human!
Don’t go!
God, he’s noisy as hell.
Pretending not to hear the Skeleton Warlord screaming inside my Inventory, I asked Team Leader Choi, “How much does one of these cost?”
Team Leader Choi launched into his answer as if he had been waiting for me to ask.
“This new model from Focke-Wulf, the German aircraft manufacturer renowned for its outstanding technology—”
Here we go again.
I hurriedly cut him off before he could start explaining the history of Focke-Wulf’s founder.
“I don’t know if it’s Focke-Wulf or Pokémon Black Friday, but I’m asking how much a plane like this usually costs.”
“An aircraft like the one we’re on now should cost a little over one hundred billion won.”
“Hmm.
I should buy one.”
Anyone who overheard me would have stared at me as if I were insane.
But it wasn’t impossible.
I recalled the conversation Team Leader Choi and I had shared only a few hours earlier.
“It's a shame, but please tell Grandpa Jongseok I can’t go.”
“It isn’t Grandpa Jongseok.
It’s Chairman Xiao Yang.
In any case, that is unfortunate.”
I’m sorry too.
Promoting my name and raising the Guild’s standing both sound good, but that place is a bit much.
They offered ten billion won.
How much?
Ten billion won.
If you go beyond the promised period of one week, they’ll calculate an additional ten billion won per week.
Weekly pay?
T-ten billion won a week?
It can’t be helped.
B-but I’m still not going.
With thousands of monsters and a crazy skeleton mage, even I have to draw the line.
It’s not like I’m some money-crazed bastard.
They say they’ll pay fifty trillion won to whoever kills the Lich.
Ah, now I suddenly feel like eating something spicy.
I hear Sichuan cuisine is incredibly hot and savory...
Fuck it.
Let’s go.
All the preparations were completed at lightning speed.
Only Team Leader Choi and I would be leaving for China.
Chairman Xiao Yang had only wanted me in the first place anyway.
This isn’t about the money.
I was going solely to help the suffering people of China and raise the Guild’s standing.
With my face full of noble resolve, I turned to Team Leader Choi.
“But, Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“If I make fifty trillion won...
Do I split that with the Guild too?”
“Let’s settle this before we go.
Money matters need to be handled cleanly.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me in disbelief before answering.
“We’ll split it nine to one.”
This guy was something else too.
As we stared at each other like we were both human garbage, an announcement came over the cabin speakers and the private jet sent by China began to take off.

chapters.title: Chapter 306
paragraphs: As the enormous fuselage of the Boeing 747-8 VIP lifted into the sky, Jin Taekyung, who had been bouncing excitedly in his seat, sprang up and began roaming the cabin.
“Wow, this isn’t a plane. It’s practically a hotel suite! Team Leader, look over here. There’s even a bed!”
At his endless exclamations, Choi Minwoo pressed a hand to his forehead. Anyone watching would think they were going on an overseas vacation instead of heading to a battlefield.
“Um... Mr. Jin?”
“Hang on. I’m going to ask what kind of liquor they have.”
The private jet sent by China’s Central Committee had three Chinese flight attendants. Jin Taekyung called one of them over and began speaking to her in fluent Chinese.
No way. He’s practically a native speaker.
His command of the language was so natural that he could have been born and raised in China.
Choi Minwoo also had a talent for languages and spoke several fluently, but he was nowhere near Jin Taekyung’s level.
He had heard Taekyung was terrible at school. When on earth had he learned to speak Chinese that well?
Then a thought flashed through Choi Minwoo’s astonished mind.
Come to think of it, he talks to monsters too.
Jin Taekyung was, after all, the man who could speak the Demon Realm language—which even renowned linguists struggled to decipher—and curse fluently in it to boot.
When Choi Minwoo had asked how that was even possible, the only answer he received was that it was a trade secret.
...Let’s just stop thinking about it. That’ll be easier on my mind.
Giving up always made life easier. Besides, this was hardly the first time something like this had happened. Taekyung would tell him when the time came.
Resigning himself to that, Choi Minwoo accepted the glass the flight attendant poured for him.
“What is this? It’s clear, so I assume it’s some kind of vodka.”
“First Dew Fresh.”
“Heh. I didn’t expect it, but they actually had soju. First Dew tastes best on the rocks.”

Jin Taekyung dropped onto one of the cabin sofas and downed glass after glass. Appalled by the way he kept knocking them back, Choi Minwoo asked, “Are you possessed by the ghost of someone who died of thirst?”
“I’m drinking in advance. Going back and forth is a hassle.”
“Excuse me?”
“Never mind. It’s nothing.”
After muttering that cryptic remark, Jin Taekyung asked, “You said it would take five or six hours, right?”
“That’s how long it should take to reach Chengdu International Airport in Sichuan Province. It could take longer in an emergency.”
“What kind of emergency?”
“What else could it be?”
The emergency Choi Minwoo meant was the Lich’s monster army occupying Chengdu.
“Of course, that’s highly unlikely. By now, enormous numbers of People’s Liberation Army troops and Hunters should be defending the city.”
One hundred million people lived across an area twice the size of the Korean Peninsula.
Chengdu was the administrative capital of Sichuan Province. If Chengdu fell, it would be as good as losing the entire province.
Jin Taekyung waved a hand after listening to Choi Minwoo.
“Come on. You can’t rule something out just because it’s unlikely. If we could do that, Monster Waves wouldn’t happen in the first place.”
“Of course, that’s true, but...”
“Always assume the worst. Don’t count on the best.”
He tossed out the words casually. Anyone could have said them, but coming from Jin Taekyung, they somehow felt different.
How should Choi Minwoo put it? Beneath all that carelessness lay meticulous caution and the hard-earned instincts of a seasoned veteran.
He’s a strange man.
There were times when Choi Minwoo found Jin Taekyung uncanny.
It wasn’t a matter of skill or combat experience.
Whenever they talked, Choi Minwoo would suddenly get the feeling that Taekyung had survived far more than just one or two crises.
Even though he’s younger than me.
Noticing Choi Minwoo’s contemplative stare, Jin Taekyung paused with his glass halfway to his lips.
“What? Want some vodka instead?”
“No. First Dew is fine.”
“Right? It has such a clean taste...”
Jin Taekyung trailed off and scowled.
“This bastard’s throwing another fit.”
“I wasn’t talking to you, Team Leader. Some asshole won’t stop squawking.”
Choi Minwoo glanced at the flight attendants and lowered his voice.
“The Skeleton Warlord?”
“Yeah. He’s been raising hell about not wanting to go to China.”
“Because of the Lich.”
“Even if they’re both Named Monsters, they’re in completely different classes. And the Lich is a high-ranking undead monster, too.”
If the Lich was a big shot, the Skeleton Warlord was a nobody. Becoming a Named Monster did not change the vast difference in their origins.
Besides, the Lich that had appeared this time was powerful enough to stand apart even from those seen during the Great Cataclysm.
Choi Minwoo’s expression grew serious.
“Mr. Jin.”
“Ah, shut up already! Sorry, what?”
“Something has been going wrong lately.”
“Did you throw out your back?”
“No. I mean the way things are going in the world.”
“Oh, the atmosphere. Same here. I want to live peacefully, but all these pieces of shit keep raising hell from every direction... Ah, I wasn’t talking about you, so shut up.”
A headache struck Choi Minwoo without warning. He rubbed the space between his brows.
“I’m talking about Gates and monsters.”
“Oh.”
Jin Taekyung looked up from his argument with the invisible Skeleton Warlord.
“It is strange. Normally, we might see one Named Monster every few years, but two of them have shown up in the span of a few months.”

“Gate accidents have also risen sharply this year. The media, always eager to tear someone apart, are blaming careless Guilds and individuals. But I’m not convinced. The International Gate Research Institute has reached the exact opposite conclusion.”
Choi Minwoo handed him a tablet. Across its screen, in large, bold letters, were the words Investigation Results: Sudden Increase in Gate Mana.
“They haven’t made an official announcement, but the matter is already considered settled. Mana density has been rising rapidly inside a considerable number of Gates.”
“That’s the real cause of the recent spate of Gate accidents?”
“Yes.”
Mana was the source of a monster’s power. If the mana density inside a Gate increased, the monsters within it would naturally grow stronger.
And above all...
“I’ve got the proof right here.”
At Jin Taekyung’s words, Choi Minwoo nodded.
The Skeleton Warlord. According to what Taekyung had told him a few days earlier, the Named Monster had evolved.
The change had been so sudden that even the Warlord himself did not know why it had happened.
“The Lich that appeared this time may have experienced the same growth in power.”
“I expected something like that to some extent. But...”
Jin Taekyung swept back his long hair.
“This is going to be fucking brutal.”
“That’s why we need adequate countermeasures. According to some of the information I obtained regarding this incident...”
“I’ll look at it later.”
“Excuse me?”
“I’ve got a lot to catch up on right now.”
“Catch up on? Right now?”
The Boeing 747-8 VIP was cruising at an altitude of twenty-five thousand feet.
What overdue business could he possibly deal with up here?
Jin Taekyung’s answer only left Choi Minwoo more baffled.
“I’m going to sleep.”
“Sleep? At a time like this?”
“I haven’t been able to sleep at all lately.”
“W-wait a moment.”
“Don’t wake me under any circumstances. This is the answer for now.”
What kind of person was this?
Before Choi Minwoo could stop him, Jin Taekyung crawled into the bed inside the cabin. Choi Minwoo could only gape.
“Oh, right. Team Leader Choi.”
Jin Taekyung poked his head back out, his expression grave.
“Please turn off the lights.”
The moment his head touched the pillow, Jin Taekyung fell peacefully asleep.
Watching him, Choi Minwoo thought:
The profit split is nine to one. No exceptions.
Ding.
System Login complete.
I opened my eyes to the hardness of a wooden pillow and bed instead of a soft pillow and mattress.
Above me was the wholly unfamiliar ceiling of a Murim Alliance pavilion.
I’m back.
A full month had passed since I left. In the Murim, not even two shichen would have passed.
I turned my head to the right and saw a small old man fast asleep.
Even with sunlight streaming through the window and shining directly on his face, he—the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang—did not stir.
“I’m back, Old Master.”
I had just murmured the words and started to rise when—
“Oh. Mm. Ah.”
“There. That’s good. Yeah.”
I stared down at Hyuk Mujin, who was writhing like a worm in the corner of the room.
I’m pretty sure I left him on guard duty before logging out.
I told this lunatic to stand guard, and he was having a wet dream.
My greatest regret in life was that I couldn’t record this and share it in the Jin Family of Taiyuan group chat.
I could still kick him in the ass, though.
Bam!
“Urgh!”
“Wake up, you Tokyo Hot bastard.”
The pain jolted Hyuk Mujin out of his blissful dream, and he sprang to his feet.
“Captain, you’re awake!”
“Yeah. Looks like you just got up too.”
Hyuk Mujin’s eyes darted around as an awkward smile crept across his face.
“Ah, well. Something came up.”
Did something come up, or were you about to come?
I glared at Hyuk Mujin in disgust and let out a deep sigh.
Fine. This was all my fault for trusting him.
“Whew. How long were you asleep?”
“Not long. I swear.”
“Then nothing unusual happened while you were awake?”
“Yes. Until two shichen ago, I kept watch so thoroughly that I wouldn’t have let even a single ant get inside.”
I thought about that for a moment.
“If it was two shichen ago, wasn’t that when I had just fallen asleep?”
“Well, now that you mention it... But I really wasn’t asleep for long.”
“Right. Two shichen isn’t long.”
“Yes, yes.”
“Our Mujin followed me into my dreams to protect me, huh?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded furiously.
“That’s right! I, Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, pledge my unwavering loyalty to you, Captain!”
“My, what a good boy.”
I chuckled and picked up the flower vase beside the bed.
“Then why did you make such strange moaning sounds while guarding me in my dream?”
“Gasp.”
“Who did you meet? Mimi from Honghwaru? Kirara from Tokyo-ru? Or the filial daughter from the soft tofu restaurant?”
I’d had it. Just looking at that bastard made rage burn in my chest until I could barely breathe.
I raised the flower vase high, and Hyuk Mujin cautiously backed away.
“P-please let me off just this once.”
“I’ve let you off five hundred times already.”
“Then since you’ve let me off five hundred times, just one more time...”
“Hold still.”
Whoosh!
At that moment, three things happened simultaneously.
First, the flower vase in my hand shot forward with tremendous force.
Second, it narrowly grazed the crown of Hyuk Mujin’s bowed head and flew toward the door.
Third, with impossibly perfect timing, the door opened and someone walked in.
“How is Great Hero Jeok’s condi—”
Bam!
The squat old man carrying a small cloth-wrapped bundle could not finish his sentence.
His eyes went slack as he stared at Hyuk Mujin and me. His lips moved several times before he slowly crumpled.
Thud. Crash!
The flower vase that had struck him squarely in the forehead rolled away, while acupuncture needles and all manner of medical instruments spilled from his bundle.
The Luoyang Strange Physician had come at first light to check on Jeok Cheongang’s condition.
And that was how he collapsed with a concussion.

chapters.title: Chapter 307
paragraphs: “The world looks new.”
Those were the first words out of the Luoyang Strange Physician’s mouth when he regained consciousness one shichen later.
His tone and voice were so gentle that I could hardly believe he was the same old man who had been flying into a rage before I returned to the modern world.
“A-are you all right?”
“Of course I’m all right. My head hurts a little, but these things happen.”
I was starting to get scared.
How eccentric did someone have to be for people to call him the Strange Physician to his face?
Yet one flower vase to the head had transformed him into a completely different person.
Even the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, who had rushed over after mistaking the commotion for an attack by Dark Heaven, asked him anxiously, “Strange Physician, are you sure you’re all right?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician smiled faintly and nodded.
“Ha-ha, Great Hero Mae. You need not worry about this old man. Just take special care to ensure that this promising young man isn’t injured in the coming war.”
“Elder...!”
This was the greatest physician in Henan. A true doctor!
And I had actually grumbled to Mae Jonghak that such a good man was a quack.
Overcome with emotion and shame, I bowed my head. Then the Luoyang Strange Physician’s voice reached my ears.
“Because if that young man were gravely injured and I had to treat him, I might just drive a large acupuncture needle into one of his lethal acupoints with this very hand. Ha-ha.”
“A physician cannot commit murder, can he?”
So that was what he meant by making sure I didn’t get hurt.
A chill ran down my spine as I raised my head. The Luoyang Strange Physician met my gaze and smiled like the kindly old man next door.
“Great Hero Jeok’s Disciple or not, I ought to gouge those eyes right out. Ha-ha.”
Forget the old man next door. He was more like the murderer next door.
Still wearing a bandage wound tightly around his head and laughing like a lunatic, the Luoyang Strange Physician began the examination of Jeok Cheongang that he had put off for a while.
Whatever his personality, he was the greatest physician in Henan and a medical master counted among the ten best in the world.
But after examining Jeok Cheongang for a little over an hour, he reached much the same conclusion as before.
“I don’t know. This is truly strange.”
“There’s... no way to treat him?”
“You’re asking whether there’s no way to treat him?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician gave me a displeased look before continuing.
“There is no incurable illness under heaven. But how can I find a treatment when I don’t even know the name of the disease?”
This was hopeless.
If we at least knew what the illness was, we might be able to find a treatment somehow. But this meant it was an unknown disease.
I took Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled hand in mine.
Why can’t someone as strong as you wake up?
Was it because he couldn’t bear the shock of losing his closest friend after already losing his Disciple?
No. The Jeok Cheongang I knew was far more steadfast than that.
Then...
The aftereffects of the Dance of the Fire God and Demon? Or did that bastard Blood Lord pull some kind of trick?
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon was a double-edged sword that consumed even its user’s life. Its power must have been more than the aged Jeok Cheongang could bear.
And the Blood Lord, one of Dark Heaven’s core figures, was exactly the kind of bastard who would resort to some dirty trick.
The Luoyang Strange Physician groaned under his breath.
“No demonic qi has seeped into him, and he hasn’t been poisoned. But if this continues, his qi channels will slowly become blocked. That much is certain.”
Mae Jonghak’s eyes and mine flew open at the same time.
“What? What does that...?”
“Strange Physician, didn’t you say his life wasn’t in danger?”
“You weren’t listening properly. I clearly said his life was not in danger for now.”
The Luoyang Strange Physician continued slowly.

“I could tell from his pulse today that he is different from yesterday. If Great Hero Jeok remains in this state and does not wake up, all his qi acupoints will become blocked, and he will be reduced to an ordinary countryman.”
“Are you saying he won’t regain consciousness until after he loses his martial arts?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician shook his head.
“I cannot guarantee even that. And even if Heaven helps Great Hero Jeok awaken, his body has already outlived its natural span. How much longer could it possibly endure?”
I felt as though someone had struck me in the back of the head with a hammer.
As the Luoyang Strange Physician said, Jeok Cheongang had already lived for more than a hundred years.
The Fire King might endure for another ten or twenty years, but only because he possessed tremendous internal energy and martial arts.
How much time would remain for Jeok Cheongang the old man, rather than Jeok Cheongang the Fire King?
“Six months. If we continue guiding his qi through his acupoints, we might buy him another couple of months, but no more.”
“Six months... Is there really no other way?”
“You insolent brat. Do you need to make this old man repeat himself twice before you’ll be satisfied?”
He didn’t know what the disease was, so he didn’t know how to cure it.
The Luoyang Strange Physician’s answer was so firm that it doused the tiny spark of hope.
But he was also the one who rekindled it.
“That is why you must find the Divine Physician.”
“The Divine Physician?”
My mind snapped fully awake, as if someone had dumped a bucket of ice water over my head. I opened my eyes wide and asked:
“Who is the Divine Physician?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician stared at me in surprise.
“...You don’t know the Divine Physician?”
“He sounds like a physician. A really skilled one.”
“His sobriquet is Divine Physician, so of course he is! Even a stray dog in a back alley would know that much. Great Hero Mae, is this fellow really a martial artist?”
Mae Jonghak, who had been standing a step away, stopped the enraged Luoyang Strange Physician.
“Calm down, Strange Physician.”
“There are limits to ignorance, even for a complete outsider. How can he not know the Divine Physician?”
“Hmm. He must be famous.”
“...What?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician and I whipped our heads around at the same time. Mae Jonghak was smiling innocently.
Where have I seen that smile before?
Oh, right.
Wearing a smile exactly like Cheongpung’s, Mae Jonghak said, “I’ve been secluded deep in the mountains for nearly thirty years, you see. Ha-ha.”
“What are you talking about? It has already been more than forty years since the Divine Physician made his name known throughout the martial world.”

Mae Jonghak fell silent for a moment after the Luoyang Strange Physician’s blunt correction. Then he replied, “Come to think of it, it has been more than forty years for this old man as well. It was so long ago that I got confused.”
That was dark, Chuseong.
The Divine Physician.
Just as his sobriquet suggested, his medical skills had reached the realm of the divine.

It was said that he had appeared at the edge of the continent more than forty years ago and performed feats of medicine bordering on the miraculous. After treating thousands of patients by himself and stamping out an epidemic, he earned the sobriquet Divine Physician.

“Afterward, the Divine Physician continued to share his medical skills freely. He never turned away a patient who came to him and never accepted any payment. He was a true physician whose character was as lofty as his medical ability.”
“Ooh, a god-tier doctor.”
“The powerful figures of the world tried to retain him as an honored guest, but every time, he vanished without a trace. He would say only that he intended to care for patients in the lowest places.”
“Ooh, the Medicine Immortal Hong Gil-dong.”
“He always covered his face with a white veil, so no one ever saw what he looked like, but...”
“Ooh, the masked physician.”
The Luoyang Strange Physician, who had been about to continue, picked up a large acupuncture needle a handspan long.
“I’ll shut that mouth of yours for you.”
“I’m sorry. It just slipped out.”
“Even with Great Hero Mae here, this young brat’s mouth never stops. Isn’t that right?”
Mae Jonghak’s eyes lit up.
“Ooh, the Divine Physician.”
After that, the Luoyang Strange Physician, now half a sage, gave us a kind but concise explanation of the Divine Physician.
He was universally recognized as the greatest physician under heaven and a man of noble character.
And...
“No one knows his identity?”
“Did I not tell you that he always wears a veil while practicing medicine?”
“Even so, he’s been active for over forty years. How can no one know what he looks like?”
Seriously, one good gust of wind should have been enough to expose his face.
But the Luoyang Strange Physician shook his head.
“Someone may know. But no one in the world has ever properly identified him.”
“Why? Because he always ran away before anyone could track him down?”

“The witnesses contradicted one another every time. Some commoners said the Medicine Immortal was an old man with white hair, while others claimed he was a shaven-headed Buddhist nun. No matter how people tracked down and cajoled those who had seen the Medicine Immortal, their accounts never matched. How could anyone possibly find him?”
“Huh.”

“His reputation among the common people is absolute. So many of them willingly served as his eyes and ears and helped conceal his identity that even the imperial palace eventually gave up searching for him.”
“I understand that this Divine Physician is impressive, but...”
I stared incredulously at the Luoyang Strange Physician’s pleased smile.
“How am I supposed to find someone even the imperial palace gave up on?”
“Oh. Good point.”
Was he joking right now?
When my expression darkened, the Luoyang Strange Physician suddenly burst into hearty laughter.
“Don’t worry. Would I have brought him up if I had no plan at all?”
“Just as I thought. I knew I could trust you, Elder.”
“Ten years ago, I heard the tales of the Divine Physician and was so deeply impressed that I set out on a medical tour.”
“Oh, a medical tour.”
I had heard about such things in passing when I was still holed up with the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Just as martial artists went on dueling tours, physicians went on medical tours.
The Luoyang Strange Physician had followed the trail of the Divine Physician’s deeds, crossing the continent from its most remote reaches over the course of five years.
“It was rewarding and brought me great joy. But for a man already past sixty, it was also an arduous journey.”
Still, he had found something at the end of it.
“Something I had only imagined came to pass.”
The unexpected gift had come to him in a slash-and-burn farming village in the southern part of the continent.
The slash-and-burn farmers, who barely had enough to eat and had received no education, told him about a benefactor who had treated their illnesses and departed only a few months earlier.
“You folks have nothing that needs treatment. I’ll leave a few silver coins behind, so use them to restore your strength.”
“What is it? I’m sorry, but this is all the money I have left...”
“That isn’t it. Are you perhaps a physician from Luoyang?”
“Why do you ask?”
“The benefactor who treated us not long ago said that if a physician surnamed Oh came from Luoyang, we should give him this.”
What they handed him was a jade-colored shard from a porcelain bottle.
That shard now rested in the Luoyang Strange Physician’s hand.
“What is this...?”
“Read what’s written on it.”
Faint writing remained on the shard in his wrinkled palm.
Chinese gallnuts from Sichuan are the finest.
What the hell did that mean?

As I stared at it in confusion, the Luoyang Strange Physician explained, “Chinese gallnut is a widely used medicinal ingredient. With this one line, the Divine Physician was subtly telling me that he was in Sichuan.”
“...That’s what you got from it?”
“I’m telling you, that’s what it means.”
“Then if I say Japanese adult videos are the best, does that mean I’m in Japan?”
“What kind of insane nonsense is that? Great Hero Mae, isn’t this fellow completely mad?”
Looking ready to die of curiosity, Mae Jonghak asked, “What in the world are these ‘adult videos’?”
“That’s not important right now!”
The Luoyang Strange Physician, hopping mad, placed the shard in my palm.
“Look closely! Can’t you feel it? The Divine Physician’s desperate desire to exchange medical knowledge with me!”
“What desperate desire...?”
I picked up the shard to examine it more closely.
At that exact moment—
Ding.
System Quest Item Trace of the Divine Physician acquired! You can infer his whereabouts from Trace of the Divine Physician! Quest Find Mr. Shin in Sichuan generated!
I looked at the Luoyang Strange Physician and murmured, “I can feel it. His feelings.”
And now I could see it too.
A way to treat Jeok Cheongang.

chapters.title: Chapter 308
paragraphs: “Go to Sichuan. If anyone can help him, it will be the Divine Physician.”
The Luoyang Strange Physician was one of the ten greatest physicians under Heaven.
And he had spoken with absolute certainty. Find the Divine Physician. His medical skills were the best under Heaven.
There’s hope.
If I found the Divine Physician, I could save Jeok Cheongang.
I looked at Jeok Cheongang, lying there as peacefully as if he were asleep, then bowed to the Luoyang Strange Physician.
“Thank you. Truly.”
The Divine Physician was a man so shrouded in mystery that no one knew his identity.
Without the token of the Divine Physician that the Luoyang Strange Physician had given me, I would have felt as if I had been dropped into the middle of a vast ocean.
“Ahem. Is that all I get? Words?”
“Would you like me to bring you a souvenir?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician chuckled at my joking reply.
“You insolent brat. Instead of wasting time spouting nonsense, start packing your bags right now.”
“Oh. Right.”
Even by the roughest estimate, the journey from Henan to Sichuan was several thousand li. Even with my movement technique, it would take nearly a month.
And there’s no guarantee I’ll find the Divine Physician right away.
I looked at the Quest window, which I had not yet closed, and muttered inwardly.

System Quest Find Mr. Shin in Sichuan You have acquired the only trace left behind by the Divine Physician. The Divine Physician is the greatest physician under Heaven. At present, he is the only hope capable of waking Jeok Cheongang. You must scour the vast land of Sichuan and find him! Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Possession of Trace of the Divine Physician Mission: Find the Divine Physician and receive treatment (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: Jeok Cheongang’s death
Just look at that ridiculous Quest Grade.
I was looking for one person, yet the Grade was Supreme Peak.
Fortunately, the trace he’d left behind years ago had narrowed his whereabouts down to Sichuan. But the place was so damn vast that finding him would still be brutal.
Modern Sichuan Province was about twice the size of the Korean Peninsula, wasn’t it?
Murim and the modern world were completely separate worlds. But from what I’d experienced so far, the size of the land and the way people lived were similar.
The thought of searching all of Sichuan for someone whose name and face I didn’t even know was daunting.
Fuck. It’d probably be easier to find Mr. Kim in Seoul.
But what choice did I have? There was no decision to make. I had to find the Divine Physician, no matter what it took, if I wanted Jeok Cheongang to live.
Jeok Cheongang had six months left.
If I continued guiding qi through his acupoints, I might be able to buy him another month or two. But that was the absolute limit of the time Jeok Cheongang had left.
I’ll find him before time runs out.
To do that, I needed to cut down the time the search would take. My mind raced before I finally spoke.
“May I ask you for a favor?”
It might require an enormous amount of manpower and money.
But the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak, offered a solution without hesitation.
“I’ll write letters to the Sichuan Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng.”
“Thank you.”

The Sichuan Tang Clan was one of the Five Great Families. If I could also secure the cooperation of the Emei Sect and Qingcheng Sect, both pillars of the Nine Sects and One Gang, the search would become much easier.
But my request didn’t end there.
“Since you’re already helping me, could I ask you to add a few more things?”

“Hm. Everyone is on edge after the bloodbath at Shaolin. With Dark Heaven and the Demonic Cult believed to be on the move, they may not be able to offer much help. For martial artists affiliated with a sect, their own sect must come first.”
“I don’t need that much help.”
“Tell me anything that I—or Huashan—can do.”
“Just assign me a few people. That will be enough.”
“Do you have anyone in mind?”
“Yes.”
I nodded and gave him several names.
A short while later, Mae Jonghak and the Luoyang Strange Physician left the pavilion and walked along slowly as they spoke.
“Are you certain about this? I understand that meeting the Divine Physician has been your lifelong wish.”
“My lifelong wish...”
At Mae Jonghak’s words, the Luoyang Strange Physician gazed into the distance as he recalled the past.
“It was. He was the reason I abandoned my official post and took up acupuncture needles.”
The Luoyang Strange Physician had once been a promising young scholar.
His grandfather had been the head of the Guozijian, the empire’s highest educational institution, and had served as the late Emperor’s tutor when he was Crown Prince.
A scholar’s blood ran true. His father and two older brothers had also entered government service and made names for themselves at court.
If a plague hadn’t broken out the year the Luoyang Strange Physician placed first in the imperial examination, he likely would have followed the same path.
“More people died than I could count. As my duties required, I sorted them into the dead, the survivors, and those destined to die.”

As a young man newly entered into government service, the Luoyang Strange Physician had believed without question that the august Emperor would order relief grain released and dispatch imperial physicians to bring the plague under control.
He had believed every civil and military official would do everything in their power to save the suffering people.

“I was mistaken. While the people died of plague, the Emperor expanded a detached palace for his new consort, and the powerful divided among themselves everything that should have gone to the people.”
“What did you do?”

“I wrote lies as facts. Under my brush, a hundred thousand seok of grain, wealth, and medicinal supplies became aid distributed to the sick. The imperial physicians who had been attending the scholar-officials became true physicians laboring to suppress the plague.”
“That must have been painful.”
“It was. When I returned home after leaving the palace, I found imperial physicians sent by the Emperor waiting there. They had come to treat my grandfather’s mild cold.”
That was when he first learned that the world put a price even on human life.
The Luoyang Strange Physician’s knuckles whitened around the cloth bundle containing his acupuncture needles.
“Then I heard about the Divine Physician. A physician who risked death to treat the sick at the very source of the plague. One man who brought the plague under control and saved thousands of lives.”
He immediately returned to the palace, destroyed every record he had written, and left the government.
He had to sever all ties with his family, but he didn’t care.
He traded his brush for acupuncture needles and studied medical texts instead of the Four Books and Three Classics.
“I was called a quack more times than I can count. Sometimes I saved patients already sitting at death’s door. Many other times, I failed to cure them and had to watch them go.”
As a physician, he witnessed the countless cycles of birth, aging, illness, and death.
Twenty years later, the promising young official had become known as the Luoyang Strange Physician.
“None of it would have been possible without the Divine Physician. Without him, I would have become a puppet of that rotten court.”
Mae Jonghak smiled faintly.
“So one Divine Physician gave rise to another.”
“What nonsense. I’m content to remain the Strange Physician. There is only one Divine Physician under Heaven.”
The eyes of the famously eccentric Luoyang Strange Physician sparkled like a boy’s.
Mae Jonghak couldn’t help laughing at the sight.
“Good grief. Perhaps I should take back the Divine Physician’s token while I still can.”
“Heaven is Heaven because it lies beyond our reach. If I truly wished to find him, I would have left for Sichuan ten years ago, when I first received the token. My place is here. Besides...”
The Luoyang Strange Physician continued with a bitter smile.
“How could an old quack who still cannot cure a single patient dare show his face before the Divine Physician? This is enough for me.”
“Thank you. With hostile forces stirring everywhere, if Great Hero Jeok recovers, the entire Murim will owe you a great debt.”
“Come now, what has gotten into you? That doesn’t suit you at all.”
The Luoyang Strange Physician waved him off with exaggerated modesty. Then a mischievous look crossed his face.
“Are you practicing in advance?”
“Practicing what?”
“Your gravitas as the Alliance Leader. Ha-ha.”
“Ah. That?”
Mae Jonghak scratched the back of his head, looking uncomfortable.
“I have no idea who keeps spreading that rumor. I’ve already turned the position down several times...”
“As things stand, no one is more qualified than you, Great Hero Mae.”
“Don’t say that. Everyone is simply anxious, and their anxiety is driving them to make the wrong choice.”
The bloodbath at Shaolin Temple had sounded the alarm.
A hidden force known as Dark Heaven had emerged.
With the appearance of an enemy whose existence had never before been revealed, the leaders of orthodox Murim had cautiously begun discussing one subject.
The re-formation of the Murim Alliance.
“Someone else is better suited to the position. At the very least, this old man is not.”
“Do you truly believe that?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician raised a hand and pointed toward the sky.
Dawn had only just broken, and the moon and stars still lingered above.

“One God has vanished, and the Ten Kings have grown old. From what I have seen with my own eyes, Great Hero Mae possesses both formidable martial arts and an upright heart. You are the man best suited to lead the Murim Alliance, the symbol of the orthodox faction.”
“Come now. I’ve already told you this old man absolutely cannot do it. With so many people in the world, why would anyone make me the Alliance Leader?”
“Then who do you believe would be suitable?”
Mae Jonghak thought for a moment before answering.
“Right. Senior Peng, the Thunderbolt Saber King, is nearby.”
“His temperament is far too...”
“What’s wrong with Senior Peng? I like that fiery personality of his. He’s manly.”
“He would make a fiery wreck of the Murim Alliance. In the manliest way possible.”

“Then Senior Zhuge Gonghu would be perfect. He once served as Chief Strategist of the Murim Alliance, and his Supreme Peak immortal arts and outstanding formation techniques earned him a place among the Ten Kings...”
“He’s dead.”
“What? Since when?”
“More than ten years ago.”
“Good heavens...”
Mae Jonghak had been away for so long that he no longer knew who was alive and who was dead.
After letting out a long groan, he asked, “Do you happen to know what became of the other two members of the Three Saints?”
“The Bow Saint has also been missing for more than twenty years. As for the last one... frankly, he shouldn’t even be considered.”
“Hm? Why not?”
The Luoyang Strange Physician stared at Mae Jonghak in disbelief.
“Who in their right mind would nominate the Slaughter Saint as Alliance Leader?”
“What’s wrong with him? His martial arts go without saying, and he is thorough by nature. He would be perfect as Alliance Leader.”
“The problem is that he uses those martial arts and that thorough nature to murder people for a living. The greatest assassin under Heaven as Alliance Leader? How could that possibly work?”
“Is that so? Now that you mention it, you may have a point.”
Watching Mae Jonghak scratch vigorously at the back of his head, the Luoyang Strange Physician wondered:
Is orthodox Murim really going to be all right like this?
Meanwhile, preparations for Jin Taekyung’s departure were moving at lightning speed.
The first person to come running when he heard I was leaving was Jin Wikyung.
“My youngest.”
I answered while stuffing everything I needed into my traveling bag.
“Yes?”
“This eldest brother has just heard something unbelievable.”
“Believe it. It’s true.”
“W-where did you say you were going?”
“Sichuan.”
“H-how long will you be gone?”
“Six months. Maybe another month or two if it takes longer.”
“No!”
Jin Wikyung cried out as if overcome with grief.
“Where are you going at a dangerous time like this?”
“Sichuan.”
“I know! That is why I cannot let you go!”
“I’m still going.”
With a grim expression unlike any I’d ever seen on him, Jin Wikyung declared, “I forbid it.”
“Oh. Then I’ll veto your veto.”
“With Father away, I am both the Lesser Family Head and acting Family Head! You cannot defy my orders!”
“What happens if I do?”
“I will have no choice but to punish you according to family law.”
“Then strike me from the family register.”
“How can you say such a thing?”
From the look on his face, the world was going to end in ten minutes.
I left Jin Wikyung, who was reeling from the shock, and rose to my feet.
Jeok Cheongang, still unconscious, was secured to the wooden back carrier on my back with silk.
It might be too late if I find the Divine Physician and bring him all the way back here.
That was why I’d chosen this method.
I would take Jeok Cheongang to Sichuan with me.
“Heave-ho.”
This should hold well enough for me to use my movement technique, at least to some extent.
I let out a deep sigh at the pleading look in Jin Wikyung’s eyes.
“Don’t worry so much. Nothing like what you’re imagining is going to happen.”
“Take the Jin Dragon Squad. At least take the Jin Dragon Squad with you.”
The Jin Dragon Squad might be the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite force, but right now they’d only be deadweight slowing me down.
I tossed my fully packed traveling bag to one of the men nearby.
“That’s why I’m taking the Vice Squad Leader with me.”
Hyuk Mujin caught the bag and thumped his chest confidently.
“Leave it all to me, Lesser Family Head!”
“...Lesser Family Head?”
“Ah, it’s nothing. Please take good care of my youngest.”
Jin Wikyung patted Hyuk Mujin on the shoulder, looking as if he trusted him about as far as he could throw him.
That was when—
“Benefactor! When are we leaving? Huh? Benefactor?”
“...We’re leaving now, so please shut your mouth.”
Was bringing that guy really the right decision?
A sudden wave of regret hit me, but Cheongpung was perfect for this mission, which required a small, elite group.
At least there’s no questioning his strength.
If anything went wrong on the journey, Cheongpung alone would be worth an army.
“Sichuan! The Divine Physician! This is so exciting!”
It still wasn’t too late. Maybe I should just leave him behind.
Locked in a fierce internal struggle, I left the pavilion.
The final member of our party was waiting at the entrance.
“Long time no see.”
At my greeting, he answered with a gloomy expression.
“Requesting me was a poor choice.”
“No. You have to come with us.”
“My Myriad-Li Chasing Wind Movement Technique...”
“You only learned it to the fifth stage.”
“H-how do you know that?”
“...Have you learned anything past the fifth stage?”
The Oseong-and-Haneum villain.
No, the final member was Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect.
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and Gung Gibang.
Now that I saw the three of them together, this lineup was no joke.
I sighed.
“All right, let’s go, you three Bermuda Triangle bastards.”

Shin in Sichuan You have acquired the only trace left behind by the Divine Physician.

You must scour the vast land of Sichuan and find him!

Modern Sichuan Province was about twice the size of the Korean Peninsula, wasn’t it?
Murim and the modern world were completely separate worlds.

The thought of searching all of Sichuan for someone whose name and face I didn’t even know was daunting.
Fuck.
It’d probably be easier to find Mr.
Kim in Seoul.

I’ll find him before time runs out.

chapters.title: Chapter 309
paragraphs: It had already been three days since I left Luoyang with the Bermuda Triangle.
I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Mujin.”
“Huff, huff. Yes?”
Hyuk Mujin lay sprawled facedown over a rock beside a stream, looking ready to breathe his last.
He had made tremendous progress over the past year, but the limits of his internal energy and martial arts had quickly caught up with him.
Gung Gibang’s keeping up reasonably well, but even he’s falling short.
As befitted the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, Gung Gibang possessed one of the finest movement techniques among the young prodigies. Even so, he was still a step below Cheongpung and me.
What good was learning the Myriad-Li Chasing Wind Movement Technique, supposedly the fastest movement technique in the Beggars’ Sect, when he had only mastered it to the fifth stage?
“Gung Gibang.”
“Huff... Why’d you call me?”
His breathing was ragged.
He was in better shape than Hyuk Mujin, but he was having just as hard a time.
And then there was the last one...
“Benefactor, would you like a dumpling?”
“You eat plenty yourself.”
“I ate plenty on the way. I’m full.”
“Then take a shit and eat some more.”
“Wow! What a great idea!”
That was Cheongpung for you.
Anyone who had enough energy to stuff himself with dumplings between bursts of movement technique was a monster, all right.
Though I had no room to talk when I was in about the same shape as Cheongpung despite carrying Jeok Cheongang on the wooden frame strapped to my back.
I scratched the side of my head as I looked at the three of them.
Hmm. This isn’t going to work.
From Henan, through Shaanxi, and all the way to Sichuan.
The journey spanned several thousand li. Even on horseback, it would take at least a month.
But we didn’t have that kind of time.
If we wanted to shorten the journey drastically, we needed drastic measures.
“Huff... Captain, why did you call me?”
“Oh, no particular reason.”
I turned to Hyuk Mujin.
“That thing I asked you to hold on to. You still have it?”
“What thing?”
“The chain.”
“What are you talking about...? Oh, that thing you used to wear with all those weights dangling from it?”
“Yeah.”
It was a chain specially crafted by the Fire Gate Clan from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.

Just before the Star-Array Grand Banquet began, I had removed the chain along with the iron ball. When Hyuk Mujin heard that it was made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, his eyes had lit up, and he had quickly taken it.
“You brought it, right?”
He was quick on the uptake, if nothing else.
Sensing trouble, Hyuk Mujin’s eyes darted about.
“No. I left it somewhere safe.”
“Really?”
“Yes.”
“Then let’s do this. If I search you and find it, you die.”
“Ah, silly me. Now that I think about it, I did bring it.”
Clink.
Only then did Hyuk Mujin begin unwinding the chain wrapped around his torso beneath his shirt.
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was both impossibly hard and remarkably light. Apparently, he had wrapped it around himself as makeshift armor.
It could serve as temporary armor or a weapon, and the material alone was worth an enormous fortune.
No wonder Hyuk Mujin looked as if his soul were being torn from his body as he handed it over.
“Didn’t you give this to me to use? I was saving it to make a weapon later...”
“I told you to hold on to it. Did I say you could keep it?”
“You can’t just give someone something and take it back.”
“I borrowed it too. It belongs to the Fire Gate Clan. How do you think Old Master will react if he wakes up and finds you carrying it?”
“...Please take it. Hide it somewhere I’ll never have to see it again.”
“Good choice. Gibang!”
Chain in hand, I called the bewildered Gung Gibang over and got to work.
The two of them stared blankly at me, wearing expressions that clearly asked what I was doing. Then they spoke at the same time.
“What are you doing?”
“What kind of pointless bullshit is this?”
Rattle, rattle.
I answered calmly.
“Can’t you see? I’m tying a knot with the chain.”
“No, I mean, why are you wrapping it around my waist...?”
“Hold on. Untie this.”
“There. Done.”
I proudly admired the fruits of my labor.
Hyuk Mujin, Gung Gibang, and finally me. The three of us were strung together with the chain like dried fish.
“Everyone well rested?”
“What rest? It hasn’t even been fifteen minutes!”
“Untie us this instant!”
I beamed and shook my head.
At the same time, my dantian began to churn, sending ninety years’ worth of internal energy surging into my legs.
“All right. Let’s run.”
Fwoooosh!
“Waaaaagh! You lunatic!”
“The Captain’s lost his mind! He’s trying to kill me!”
Chained to me, Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin tore off like wild boars with their tails on fire.
At the commotion, Cheongpung came scrambling out of the nearby brush, where he had been relieving himself with his ass bared, and raced after us.
“Benefactor! I’m coming too!”
I don’t think that bastard wiped.
No. He must have.
I desperately pushed the thought from my mind and unleashed my movement technique.
Time flew as quickly as the scenery streaking past us, and in only two days, we accomplished the astonishing feat of reaching the border between Henan and Shaanxi.
Trudge. Trudge.
Broken ranks. Exhausted faces.
The dozens of people trudging wearily onward were all members of an Escort Bureau.
The armed escorts were exhausted. So were the caravan porters, bundled in thick clothing as they led the horses and carts.
And it wasn’t merely because their trading journey had already lasted four months.
“Hwaran.”
At the voice in her ear, a pair of faintly gleaming black eyes turned to the side. Her clear voice followed.
“Yes, Uncle Heo?”
A middle-aged man with a graying beard quietly approached the head of the procession. After a moment’s hesitation, he sighed.
“Chief Escort Seok has passed away.”
The slender figure swaying gently in the saddle went rigid. A moment passed before her trembling voice emerged.
“So in the end... he’s gone.”
“The poison reached his marrow. There was nothing more we could do. I’m sorry.”
“You have nothing to apologize for, Uncle. Brother Seok—no, Escort Leader Seok died because of me.”
Ju Hwaran bit down hard on her lip beneath her veil.
It’s true. Everything happened because I lacked virtue.
Escort Leader Seok, who had grown up with her like a brother, and the thirty-two people who had died before him—all of their deaths had been caused by her poor judgment.
Father. What am I supposed to do?
Ju Hwaran raised her head toward the sky.
It was black as ink, studded with countless stars. Above them, a man’s face appeared in her mind.
Her father, Ju Hogun, had fallen into qi deviation while cultivating two years earlier and had hovered between life and death ever since.
To have such a beautiful and gifted daughter—this father could ask for nothing more. Ha-ha!
Ju Hogun had said it so often that it had become a habit.
Another man might have adopted a son to carry on his line, but Ju Hogun loved his beautiful and talented only daughter and had always taken pride in her.
You alone will succeed me. The Yongbong Escort Bureau’s past fifty years will be nothing compared to what you accomplish in the future.
Everyone in Shaanxi knew how completely Ju Hogun doted on his daughter.
But as Ju Hwaran grew older, people realized that he wasn’t simply a foolishly indulgent father.
She was brilliant enough to master the Escort Bureau’s ledgers before she had even turned twenty, and beautiful enough to be named one of the Three Flowers of Jiangbei.
On top of that, she was a master of martial arts skilled enough to be counted among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, the greatest young prodigies of the orthodox Murim.
That was Ju Hwaran.
And yet...
Where did it all go wrong?
Ju Hwaran swallowed the sigh welling up from deep within her chest.
Everything around her was collapsing—and only two years had passed since she took over the Yongbong Escort Bureau in place of her stricken father.
“Hwaran, are you all right?”
At least she still had her people.
The fifty years of goodwill her grandfather and father had built through benevolence and virtue were now the only pillar holding her upright.
Ju Hwaran forced a smile at Heo Jun, the Chief Escort, who spoke to her with concern.
“You don’t need to worry about me, Uncle Heo.”
“I’m glad to hear it.”
Heo Jun nodded, his expression somber.
Ju Hwaran was only twenty-one.
She already possessed much, but she was still too young for her heart to have hardened enough to bear it all.
Burdened by such terrible guilt, she needed someone to watch over her. That was all he could do.
Ju Hwaran understood how he felt. Steadying her voice, she said, “It’s getting dark. We’ll camp here tonight. Please make the preparations.”
“A good idea.”
“And... prepare the funeral as well.”
Escort Leader Seok was the thirty-third casualty of this journey.
It was time to lay to rest the man who had been beside Ju Hwaran since childhood.

Salt could slow the decay of his body, but by the time they completed their escort mission, the poison remaining within him would undoubtedly have reduced his flesh and bones to a handful of bloody water.
“All right. Rest here for a while.”
“Everyone else is working. How could I rest? Don’t worry about me. Go.”
Heo Jun nodded slightly and gave a hand signal. The procession soon came to a halt.
There was still a chill in the air, but the broad stretch of land was perfect for camping. Ju Hwaran planned to replenish her strength here and cross the mountain early the next morning.
We’re almost there.
Ju Hwaran stared at the mountain shrouded in darkness.
Its stones were black, giving Black Stone Mountain its name. Once they crossed it, this escort mission would enter its final leg.
They had suffered countless losses, but if the escort journey succeeded, the Yongbong Escort Bureau would have a chance to catch its breath.
It’s seven days and nights from here to Mount Zhongnan. We don’t have much time to spare, but if we make it safely across Black Stone Mountain, it should be enough.
The question was how Black Stone Mountain’s master would receive them.

Of the countless mountain strongholds belonging to the Green Forest Alliance, Black Stone Stronghold was powerful enough to rank among the Eighteen Strongholds. Its Stronghold Lord was a Peak master renowned for wielding an axe with uncanny skill.
If the travel-worn Yongbong Escort Bureau clashed with Black Stone Stronghold, they might suffer even greater losses than they already had.
Please, let nothing happen.
Ju Hwaran had just turned away when—
Rustle.
A faint sound reached her ears.
Something had stepped on a dry leaf, and it wasn’t a wild animal.
A red alarm bell instantly rang in Ju Hwaran’s mind.
An enemy!
Shing!
Ju Hwaran drew the flexible sword at her waist and shouted like a thunderbolt.
“Who’s there?”
Her sharp cry rang through the darkness.
Chief Escort Heo Jun noticed the danger almost simultaneously and led the escorts into a protective ring around her.
“Protect the Young Bureau Head!”
“Yes, sir!”
Clang, clang, clang!
Keen-edged weapons flashed beneath the dim moonlight.
At that moment, the brush more than five hundred feet away began to stir.
“Well, well. If it isn’t the brave escorts of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
A towering giant emerged, a huge axe strapped across his back. At the sight of him, Heo Jun let out a low groan.
“Heavenly Axe...”
“Oh, Brother Heo. I’ve heard all about how busy you’ve been wiping some little girl’s ass lately.”
“You dare!”
A graceful figure suddenly stepped forward beside the stiffly standing Heo Jun.
“Perfect timing. We were just about to pay the toll.”
“We’ll see.”
Heavenly Axe grinned and gave his axe a shake.
“Let’s take a look at the goods first. Then we’ll talk.”
Rustle, rustle, rustle!
Behind his axe, hundreds of Green Forest bandits emerged.

“Ah, silly me.

Clink.
Only then did Hyuk Mujin begin unwinding the chain wrapped around his torso beneath his shirt.
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was both impossibly hard and remarkably light.

I was saving it to make a weapon later...”
“I told you to hold on to it.

“You can’t just give someone something and take it back.”

How do you think Old Master will react if he wakes up and finds you carrying it?”
“...Please take it.

Rattle, rattle.

Untie this.”

Done.”

Fwoooosh!

You lunatic!”
