There are plenty of struggles behind the scenes, and armed conflicts break out from time to time.”
“Well, so what if we can’t expand?
I’ll tell my eldest brother we should get along with you.”
Ju Hwaran stared at me with an odd expression before letting out a quiet laugh.
“I’d appreciate that.”
Wow.
I almost gasped out loud.
All she had done was laugh.
How could that be so beautiful?
I swallowed the exclamation rising in my throat just as murmuring voices reached me from behind.
“My word.
That’s the first woman I’ve ever seen who’s more beautiful than Young Lady Lee Seowol.”
“Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran is one of the Three Flowers of Jiangbei.
I don’t know who Lee Seowol is, but how could she possibly compare?”
“As if you’re one to talk.
Gung Gibang, go scrub yourself on a rock in the stream.
That grime is so filthy it makes me sick.”
“What’s wrong with me?”
“You’re a beggar, aren’t you?”
“Hah.
That’s true, I suppose.”
An innocent voice followed.
“That’s not true.
Young Lady Lee Seowol is pretty too.”
“What’s gotten into Cheongpung?
I didn’t know you could say things like that.”
“And Gung Gibang looks pretty to me too.”
“...Then go wash up in the stream with pretty Gung Gibang.
Pay special attention to your eyes.”
There was no need to look.
It was the Bermuda Triangle.
Normally, I would have at least introduced them, but the level of their conversation was so low that I was embarrassed to say anything.
I was forcing out an awkward cough when Ju Hwaran poked her head past my shoulder.
“Who are those people?”
“I don’t know.”
“You came here together.”
“They’re just traveling companions.”
“Really?”
“I swear it on the heavens.”
I had lowered my voice as much as I could, but the Bermuda Triangle still overheard me.
They erupted like wildfire.
“Captain!
Are you ashamed of us?”
“Am I embarrassing?”
“Benefactor!
I’m fine!
Please be ashamed of me!”
“...They’re actually my friends.”
“Anyone can see that.”
Anyone can see that?
Somehow, that was even more devastating.
Ju Hwaran laughed softly at my expression, then gave the three of them a fist-and-palm salute.
“I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
It is an honor to meet my Benefactors.”
I wasn’t sure what those three had done to deserve being called Benefactors, but the Bermuda Triangle bowed their heads anyway.
“I am Hyuk Mujin, one of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan’s foremost elites, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad, and the right-hand man of the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
I calmly corrected him.
“Not the Vice Squad Leader—the acting Vice Squad Leader.
And he isn’t my right hand.
He’s more like the pinky on my left.”
Gung Gibang spoke next.
“I am the beggar Gung Gibang.”
“He’s the next-generation beggar boss.”
Finally, it was Cheongpung’s turn.
“Hello!
You’re pretty!”
“As you can see, he’s a little unwell.
He may not be the sharpest, but he’s a good friend.”
After the whirlwind of introductions and my helpful explanations, Ju Hwaran’s lips parted slightly.
Her large black eyes practically quaked.
“So, let me make sure I understand...
The pinky on your left hand, the next-generation beggar boss, and the slightly dim but kind friend?”
“Yes, exactly.”
“I’ve never heard anyone introduced that way before.”
“Would you like me to repeat it?”
“No, thank you.”
She let out a deep sigh, then studied them one by one.
“I, too, have heard of the Swift Wind Sword, who rendered distinguished service during the campaign against the northern mounted bandits.”
Hyuk Mujin stared at Ju Hwaran in bewilderment.
Swift Wind Sword?
I had no idea when he had acquired such a sobriquet, but judging by his reaction, it seemed to be real.
Before anyone could respond, Ju Hwaran continued.
“And the gentleman beside him is Young Hero Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar and Disciple of Great Hero Myriad-Mile Pursuit, the Beggars’ Sect Leader.”
“P-Pleased to meet you.”
“Lastly, it is an honor to meet Young Hero Cheongpung, the Huashan Divine Dragon.
My grandfather and father always spoke of Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint, as a hero of benevolence and righteousness.”
Huashan Divine Dragon was the sobriquet people had given Cheongpung after the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
Cheongpung’s eyes widened in surprise.
“Wow!
How do you know all that?”
Ju Hwaran smiled brightly.
“Because I’m the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
The answer was brief, but it said a great deal.
We had left Henan only a few days after the Star-Array Grand Banquet ended.
She gathers information quickly.
Unlike Cheongpung and Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin was an unknown newcomer who had operated only in Shanxi Province.
The fact that she knew both his name and his sobriquet so precisely meant that Ju Hwaran was even more meticulous and clever than I had expected.
Dagger Hidden Flower.
A flower hiding a dagger.
And she had more than one dagger hidden away: Peak-level martial arts, a keen mind, and beauty that could captivate anyone.
She more than deserved her place among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, the martial world’s foremost young prodigies.
Interesting.
With all that, she should be good at running an Escort Bureau too.
According to Gung Gibang, however, the past two years had brought the Yongbong Escort Bureau one hardship after another.
I shook the question from my mind.
Eh, what difference does it make if I worry about it?
Finding the Divine Physician was more urgent.
We had already lost nearly a shichen here.
If we wanted to reach our destination before dawn, we needed to get moving now.
“Young Lady Ju, I think we should be going.”
Ju Hwaran flinched at my sudden declaration.
“Now?”
“I have something urgent to take care of.”
“It’s already so late.
Why don’t you spend the night here and leave in the morning...?”
“That might be difficult...
We need to reach Xi’an by tomorrow.”
“Ah.”
Ju Hwaran hesitated as though she had something to say, then finally spoke.
“Will I be able to see you again?”
“Of course.
If fate brings us together.”
I lowered my head and was about to turn away when Ju Hwaran called after me.
“I will never forget the debt I owe you for saving our lives.”
“I’m not so sure about that.
Even if I hadn’t been here, you would have avoided the worst, so you don’t need to be that grateful.”
“What?”
“You would have suffered some losses, of course.”
She still doesn’t know?
Well, that was understandable.
I smiled at the bewildered Ju Hwaran, glanced at the fierce-eyed young escort, and turned away.
System Level 110: Song Ilseom
The Murim really is a vast place.
Someone that skilled is working as an escort?
He was the source of the gaze I’d felt this entire time.
Thanks to him, the back of my head had prickled the entire time I was speaking with Ju Hwaran.
But why has that bastard been glaring at me like that?
Did I somehow become his sworn enemy?
Apparently, I wasn’t the only one who had noticed his hostile gaze.
Cheongpung followed close behind me and whispered.
“Benefactor, did you feel it too?”
“Yeah.
I don’t know why he’s acting like that, but he’s being incredibly obvious.”
“Right?
Maybe he’s interested in Benefactor.”
Please stop talking bullshit.
The four figures shot away like the wind.
As Ju Hwaran watched their backs recede, someone approached her.
“Hwaran.”
“Ah, Uncle Heo.”
Heo Jun had finished binding the bandits and dealing with the aftermath.
He followed Ju Hwaran’s gaze and turned his head.
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
He truly is an extraordinary young man.
The others are no different.”
“I know.
They say rumors from the martial world can’t be trusted... but in this case, they seem to have understated the truth.”
Ju Hwaran recalled the martial prowess Jin Taekyung had displayed.
It had been an overwhelming sight.
Watching him had sent a thrill through her, but it had also left her bitter.
If only I had strength like that.
If she had, the Yongbong Escort Bureau would never have ended up in its current state.
Ju Hwaran swallowed the words on the tip of her tongue and spoke.
This time, she sent them through Sound Transmission, carrying them on her internal energy.
—Uncle Heo.
Keep an eye on Escort Captain Song.
Heo Jun was seasoned enough to be the Chief Escort.
Without revealing anything on his face, he brought up another subject and replied through Sound Transmission.
—Hwaran.
Are you suggesting...?
—It’s only a suspicion for now.
But too many things don’t add up.
The leak of confidential information about the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.
The attacks that had continued without pause for the past four months.
Ju Hwaran intended to cut out the betrayal that had taken root deep within the bureau.
Especially the last thing Jin Taekyung said.
He had said that even without him, the worst would never have happened.
That meant there was a master within the Yongbong Escort Bureau capable of easily defeating Heavenly Axe and handling the enemies.
And... that look in his eyes.
It had lasted only an instant, but she had seen it clearly.
Jin Taekyung’s gaze had lingered on Song Ilseom as he turned away.
And his eyes had held a faint trace of surprise.
There’s definitely something going on.
Ju Hwaran suddenly thought back over the past two years—the countless failures she had endured while leading the Escort Bureau before she had even turned twenty.
What if those failures had come from trusting people too easily?
What if someone had betrayed her?
What was she supposed to do then?
Whoooosh.
As the cold wind whipped around her, Ju Hwaran stood there for a long time.
“Could you provide me with a quiet room?”
The man was dressed in white.
He was strikingly handsome, and his words and manner were so courteous that anyone who heard him would find it difficult to refuse.
He brought to mind a proud, solitary crane, and the Captain of the Guards standing at the entrance found himself wondering.
Who is he?
I’ve never seen him before.
Xi’an Tower was, as its name suggested, one of Xi’an’s foremost pleasure houses.
Staying there required not only money, but also the status to match.
As a result, its guests tended to be the same familiar faces.
But he’s a young man who came alone, without a carriage or servants...
Under normal circumstances, he would have been turned away without a second thought.
Yet something about the young man nagged at him.
That was why the Captain of the Guards had dismissed his subordinates and come to receive him personally.
“Have you visited our pleasure house before?”
“No.
My circumstances don’t permit such luxuries.”
The young man smiled sheepishly and rubbed his cheek.
The Captain of the Guards’ eyes widened.
That’s...!
Pale crimson blossoms had been embroidered on the young man’s snow-white sleeve.
They were unmistakably plum blossoms in full bloom.
A stammer slipped from between the guard captain’s lips.
“M-May I ask your honored name?”
“I’m a Daoist named Baek Museong.”
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane!”
Baek Museong, direct Disciple of Huashan Sect Leader Heavenly Sword True Person, smiled faintly.

chapters.title: Chapter 313
paragraphs: Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong.
There was no one in Shaanxi—or anywhere in the Murim—who didn’t know that name.
Baek Museong was the direct Disciple of Heavenly Sword True Person and had been called the future of Huashan since childhood.
Sharp-eared, gossip-loving busybodies traded rumors about the Sword Saint’s youngest Disciple, but even they never doubted that Baek Museong would one day become the Sect Leader of Huashan.
“I hear the Huashan Divine Dragon’s martial prowess has already surpassed that of the Elders of the Nine Sects and One Gang. He truly is a genius who comes along perhaps once in a century.”
“Even so, no matter what anyone says, Huashan’s Lone Crane is bound to be the next Sect Leader. Baek Museong is simply of a different caliber. He was born with everything a Sect Leader needs.”
“That’s true. Does he lack martial skill? Character? If not him, who else could possibly become Sect Leader?”
The people drinking and chatting on the first floor of Xi’an Tower had no idea that the subject of their conversation was passing right behind them.
“I’ve long heard of your renown, Great Hero Baek. It’s an honor to meet you.”
“Great Hero? Please, you flatter me.”
“Not at all. I’m merely calling a Great Hero a Great Hero. How could that possibly be flattery?”
Baek Museong could only smile awkwardly at the Captain of the Guards’ fervent gaze.
Such attention was nothing new to him.
As Huashan’s standing rose after faltering in the wake of Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s withdrawal from the world, so too did the burden on Baek Museong’s shoulders grow heavier.
The Sect Leader.
For Baek Museong, who was only in his early thirties, it was a distant and weighty title.
He was inwardly shaking his head at the thought when the Captain of the Guards stopped walking.
“This is the place.”
“This is...?”
“Even in Xi’an Tower, which we proudly call the finest establishment in Shaanxi, there is only one private annex.”
Baek Museong looked around at the garden adorned with jade and the interior filled with luxurious furnishings, his expression troubled.
“I’m sorry, but I don’t have enough money on hand to stay in a private annex. Could you provide me with a quiet room instead?”
“Haha, you’re every bit as frugal as I heard.”
The Captain of the Guards continued with a hearty laugh.
“Please don’t worry. The proprietor has repeatedly instructed us that whenever a guest from Huashan arrives, we are to provide the utmost hospitality and charge them nothing.”
“The proprietor said that?”

“Yes. There was some trouble with the Zhongnan Sect last autumn, but it was resolved with Huashan’s help. The other two members of the Three Plum Blossom Elites—your Junior Brothers—played a major role.”
“Ah, I see. It happened while I was in secluded training, so I knew little about it.”
“To be honest, I only heard about it myself. I’ve barely been working here a month. Haha.”
Only then did Baek Museong nod in understanding.
It wasn’t as though he had spent the past year idling.

Meeting Cheongpung, a prodigy for the ages, and Jin Taekyung had come as both a tremendous shock and a fresh source of motivation. That was why Baek Museong had decided to enter secluded training for an entire year.
It was time well spent.
The insight he had gained during his training had made him stronger and given him greater depth.
And he wasn’t the only thing that had changed. Huashan’s position was now incomparable to what it had been a year ago.
Even the government offices, which were heavily staffed by Zhongnan’s lay Disciples, now turned to Huashan first whenever trouble arose.
If Master’s letter is true, that’s only natural.
Five days earlier, a messenger eagle sent by his Master, Heavenly Sword True Person, had brought astonishing news.

The blood calamity at Shaolin. The death of Dharma King Hong Dao. And the report that Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was being considered as a candidate for the Alliance Leader of the new Murim Alliance, which was being revived after decades.

“In any case, everyone around me is in an uproar. Even my friends have been asking me about it. They say their children seem to have a talent for martial arts and wonder whether they might be accepted into Huashan, if only as lay Disciples.”
Baek Museong recognized the meaning behind the Captain of the Guards’ pointed gaze and smiled bitterly.
The man looked well past forty. He, too, must be a parent who wanted his child to enter Huashan.
But Baek Museong pretended not to notice.
“Well, if fate brings them together, perhaps it will happen. But does a child truly need to learn martial arts? At that age, growing up healthy is enough.”
“...I see.”
As the Captain of the Guards’ face fell, Baek Museong murmured inwardly.
If you knew about the bloody storm that will soon sweep in, you wouldn’t look so disappointed.
Rumors about the blood calamity at Shaolin had already begun to leak out here and there.
But the existence of Dark Heaven remained a top-secret known only to a handful of people. As one of those few, Baek Museong could sense what was coming.
A bloody wind would soon sweep through the Murim. Dark clouds would cover the sky, and thousands upon tens of thousands of weapons would tumble across the ground alongside their owners.
The wails of children who had lost their parents and parents who had lost their children would echo from every direction.
I’ll stop that from happening. I will—and Huashan will.
Surely everyone in the Murim felt the same.
The Captain of the Guards was tilting his head at the sudden heaviness in Baek Museong’s expression when—
“Where is the chief manager? Chief Manager!”
“Young Hero, the chief manager has stepped away for a moment. So please, calm yourself—”
“Calm myself? After being treated with such disrespect, do I look like I’m in any state to calm down?”
“A-as I explained, the private annex is already occupied. We’ll show you to a special room, so please calm down.”
“Shut up! I must have the private annex today, so get out of my way!”
“Oh, Young Hero!”
Bang! Crack!
The shouting drew closer amid the clamor. The Captain of the Guards knitted his brows.
“I apologize for showing you such an unpleasant scene. It seems my subordinates have failed to handle the matter properly.”
“Please, think nothing of it. I understand completely.”
No matter how carefully Xi’an Tower selected its guests, it was still a pleasure house. All sorts of insects were bound to swarm a flower garden.
“Still, it’s barely noon, and he already sounds quite drunk.”
“It happens from time to time. He appears to be the son of some powerful family, but we’ll settle the matter and send him home. Great Hero Baek, you needn’t concern yourself.”
Baek Museong let out a hearty laugh and shook his head.
“Haha, I’m not so sure. You’d better remain here.”
“Pardon?”
“He doesn’t seem to be an ordinary scion of a powerful family.”
“What do you mean...?”
The Captain of the Guards faltered. Amid the continuing uproar, he had sensed someone approaching rapidly.
A martial artist!
As the situation grew more serious by the second, the cries of the guards protecting the inner courtyard rang out alongside hurried footsteps.
“Stop!”
“You cannot pass beyond this point!”

Xi’an Tower was frequented by high officials and powerful nobles, so the quality of its guards was correspondingly high. Yet even those battle-tested First Rate martial artists were no match for the drunken man’s rampage.
“You lowly Third Rate trash from wandering martial artist backgrounds dare...”
“Gah!”
Whoosh! Thud-thud-thud!
Short cries of alarm from the guards and the fast, powerful sounds of impacts rang out. In an instant, the area outside the private annex fell silent.
Then rough, unsteady footsteps began to approach, driving the silence away.
He took down six First Rate martial artists in an instant while that drunk?
A master—and not just any master. A Peak master.
Just as the Captain of the Guards’ face hardened and his hand moved toward his sword hilt, Baek Museong gave a small shake of his head.
“I think I should handle this.”
“Great Hero Baek, that’s...”
“It’s all right. We’ve met several times before. He’ll back down for my sake, if nothing else.”
“You mean...?”
“Our connection goes back several generations. Ah, of course...”
Baek Museong scratched his cheek and added,
“It isn’t exactly a harmonious connection.”
At that moment, a thought flashed through the Captain of the Guards’ mind like lightning.
First came the words Zhongnan Sect. Then the name of a man.
“C-could it be?”
He had only been the Captain of the Guards at Xi’an Tower for a little over two weeks, but he had already heard so many rumors about that man that his ears ached.
A man whose temperament was as extraordinary as the sect he came from.
The Captain of the Guards grimaced and was about to speak the man’s name when—
Boom!
The door of the private annex, made from sturdy blackwood, exploded. Splinters flew in every direction.
Baek Museong smiled faintly at the young man approaching with a staggering gait and a face flushed red with alcohol.
“It’s been a long time. Have you been well?”
At the same moment—
“Why are you here?”
The face of Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon, twisted like that of a fiend.
“Wow! Wowww!”
“Please stop shouting. Everyone’s staring.”
“Benefactor! Candied fruit over there!”
“That damn candied fruit. Aren’t you sick of it yet?”
“No!”
“Then just open your own shop!”
“Can the candied-fruit vendor come with us all the way to Sichuan?”
“No, you lunatic...”
“They sell thin noodles over there! They say the broth is made with beef!”
Cheongpung, you little bastard. You’re like a rubber ball that could bounce off in any direction without warning...
I quickly grabbed Cheongpung by the back of his neck as he scampered toward a roadside food stall.
“Please, let’s just act like human beings. That’s all I’m asking. Like human beings!”
“Candied fruit... thin noodles...”
“Just wait a little longer, and I’ll feed you until your belly bursts!”
“Really?”
“How many times do I have to say it? So please shut your mouth and follow me quietly, okay?”
Of course, I wouldn’t be feeding him with my money. It would be Huashan’s money, but that was all the same in the end.
We were supposed to pass straight through here, too.
According to our original schedule, there hadn’t been any need to stop in Xi’an at all.
But before we left, Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan, had asked us to stop by Xi’an. Since it was Cheongpung’s hometown, we had decided to pass through while we were at it.
We had been pushing ourselves for nearly seven days and nights without eating or washing properly. I also wanted to enjoy some hospitality and get at least one full day of rest.
I was told Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, would be waiting for us.
It had already been more than a year since I’d last seen him.
Before I left for Anhui with Jeok Cheongang, Baek Museong had said this to me.
“Contact me whenever you come to Shaanxi. I’ll treat you properly. Haha.”
When he promised me the full course, I’d wondered if the guy was from Busan, but apparently it hadn’t been empty talk.
At least, judging by the fact that we were meeting like this today.
“By the way, where’s Xi’an Tower?”
A passerby I’d stopped had told me we only needed to follow the main road straight ahead. But why was the street so crowded? I couldn’t see the end of it.
As I looked around, a finger caked in black grime pointed toward a building in the distance.
“That is Xi’an Tower.”
“Where? Oh, you’re right. How did you know?”
Gung Gibang, the future boss of all beggars, answered proudly.

“It is the finest place to beg. Even the food they leave behind and throw away is fit for a sumptuous feast, and because people of high status come and go, they give plenty of alms. Every beggar knows this place.”
So it was a Beggars’ Sect hotspot.
I shook my head and headed toward Xi’an Tower.
When we reached its enormous main entrance, wide enough for ten people to pass through at once, a guard who appeared to belong to Xi’an Tower bowed his head.
“I’m sorry, but we’re closed today.”
“...What? Is it a day off?”
“Not exactly. A slight problem arose during business hours.”
“Oh.”
I hadn’t expected that.
I glanced to the side and saw Cheongpung looking as though he was about to burst into tears.
Scratching my head, I spoke to the guard.
“Isn’t there any way around it? We had an appointment today. His name is Baek Museong. I was told you’d know him if I gave you his name.”
“Again, I’m sorry, but at the moment— Excuse me? Did you say Great Hero Baek Museong?”
“Yes. Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane.”
Cheongpung called out desperately.
“Martial Nephew Baek! Where are you, Martial Nephew Baek? Can you hear my stomach growling?”
The guard looked back and forth between us, then flung open the tightly closed main gate.
“I’ll escort you to the private annex immediately!”
What the hell?
Why the sudden change in attitude?
Did Baek Museong stand us up?
My guess was wrong.
We followed the guard as he raced ahead almost fast enough to fly and arrived at a nearly devastated private annex.
Baek Museong was waiting for us there, sword drawn.
Wow. This really is the full course.
This kind of shit makes me sick of being a martial artist.

I’ll stop that from happening.
I will—and Huashan will.
Surely everyone in the Murim felt the same.
The Captain of the Guards was tilting his head at the sudden heaviness in Baek Museong’s expression when—
“Where is the chief manager?
Chief Manager!”
“Young Hero, the chief manager has stepped away for a moment.
So please, calm yourself—”
“Calm myself?
After being treated with such disrespect, do I look like I’m in any state to calm down?”
“A-as I explained, the private annex is already occupied.
We’ll show you to a special room, so please calm down.”
“Shut up!
I must have the private annex today, so get out of my way!”
“Oh, Young Hero!”
Bang!
Crack!
The shouting drew closer amid the clamor.
The Captain of the Guards knitted his brows.
“I apologize for showing you such an unpleasant scene.
It seems my subordinates have failed to handle the matter properly.”
“Please, think nothing of it.
I understand completely.”
No matter how carefully Xi’an Tower selected its guests, it was still a pleasure house.
All sorts of insects were bound to swarm a flower garden.
“Still, it’s barely noon, and he already sounds quite drunk.”
“It happens from time to time.
He appears to be the son of some powerful family, but we’ll settle the matter and send him home.
Great Hero Baek, you needn’t concern yourself.”
Baek Museong let out a hearty laugh and shook his head.
“Haha, I’m not so sure.
You’d better remain here.”
“Pardon?”
“He doesn’t seem to be an ordinary scion of a powerful family.”
“What do you mean...?”
The Captain of the Guards faltered.
Amid the continuing uproar, he had sensed someone approaching rapidly.
A martial artist!
As the situation grew more serious by the second, the cries of the guards protecting the inner courtyard rang out alongside hurried footsteps.
“Stop!”
“You cannot pass beyond this point!”
Xi’an Tower was frequented by high officials and powerful nobles, so the quality of its guards was correspondingly high.
Yet even those battle-tested First Rate martial artists were no match for the drunken man’s rampage.
“You lowly Third Rate trash from wandering martial artist backgrounds dare...”
“Gah!”
Whoosh!
Thud-thud-thud!
Short cries of alarm from the guards and the fast, powerful sounds of impacts rang out.
In an instant, the area outside the private annex fell silent.
Then rough, unsteady footsteps began to approach, driving the silence away.
He took down six First Rate martial artists in an instant while that drunk?
A master—and not just any master.
A Peak master.
Just as the Captain of the Guards’ face hardened and his hand moved toward his sword hilt, Baek Museong gave a small shake of his head.
“I think I should handle this.”
“Great Hero Baek, that’s...”
“It’s all right.
We’ve met several times before.
He’ll back down for my sake, if nothing else.”
“You mean...?”
“Our connection goes back several generations.
Ah, of course...”
Baek Museong scratched his cheek and added,
“It isn’t exactly a harmonious connection.”
At that moment, a thought flashed through the Captain of the Guards’ mind like lightning.
First came the words Zhongnan Sect.
Then the name of a man.
“C-could it be?”
He had only been the Captain of the Guards at Xi’an Tower for a little over two weeks, but he had already heard so many rumors about that man that his ears ached.
A man whose temperament was as extraordinary as the sect he came from.
The Captain of the Guards grimaced and was about to speak the man’s name when—
Boom!
The door of the private annex, made from sturdy blackwood, exploded.
Splinters flew in every direction.
Baek Museong smiled faintly at the young man approaching with a staggering gait and a face flushed red with alcohol.
“It’s been a long time.
Have you been well?”
At the same moment—
“Why are you here?”
The face of Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon, twisted like that of a fiend.
“Wow!
Wowww!”
“Please stop shouting.
Everyone’s staring.”
“Benefactor!
Candied fruit over there!”
“That damn candied fruit.
Aren’t you sick of it yet?”
“No!”
“Then just open your own shop!”
“Can the candied-fruit vendor come with us all the way to Sichuan?”
“No, you lunatic...”
“They sell thin noodles over there!
They say the broth is made with beef!”
Cheongpung, you little bastard.
You’re like a rubber ball that could bounce off in any direction without warning...
I quickly grabbed Cheongpung by the back of his neck as he scampered toward a roadside food stall.
“Please, let’s just act like human beings.
That’s all I’m asking.
Like human beings!”
“Candied fruit... thin noodles...”
“Just wait a little longer, and I’ll feed you until your belly bursts!”
“Really?”
“How many times do I have to say it?
So please shut your mouth and follow me quietly, okay?”
Of course, I wouldn’t be feeding him with my money.
It would be Huashan’s money, but that was all the same in the end.
We were supposed to pass straight through here, too.
According to our original schedule, there hadn’t been any need to stop in Xi’an at all.
But before we left, Heavenly Sword True Person, the Sect Leader of Huashan, had asked us to stop by Xi’an.
Since it was Cheongpung’s hometown, we had decided to pass through while we were at it.
We had been pushing ourselves for nearly seven days and nights without eating or washing properly.
I also wanted to enjoy some hospitality and get at least one full day of rest.
I was told Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, would be waiting for us.
It had already been more than a year since I’d last seen him.
Before I left for Anhui with Jeok Cheongang, Baek Museong had said this to me.
“Contact me whenever you come to Shaanxi.
I’ll treat you properly.
Haha.”
When he promised me the full course, I’d wondered if the guy was from Busan, but apparently it hadn’t been empty talk.
At least, judging by the fact that we were meeting like this today.
“By the way, where’s Xi’an Tower?”
A passerby I’d stopped had told me we only needed to follow the main road straight ahead.
But why was the street so crowded?
I couldn’t see the end of it.
As I looked around, a finger caked in black grime pointed toward a building in the distance.
“That is Xi’an Tower.”
“Where?
Oh, you’re right.
How did you know?”
Gung Gibang, the future boss of all beggars, answered proudly.
“It is the finest place to beg.
Even the food they leave behind and throw away is fit for a sumptuous feast, and because people of high status come and go, they give plenty of alms.
Every beggar knows this place.”
So it was a Beggars’ Sect hotspot.
I shook my head and headed toward Xi’an Tower.
When we reached its enormous main entrance, wide enough for ten people to pass through at once, a guard who appeared to belong to Xi’an Tower bowed his head.
“I’m sorry, but we’re closed today.”
“...What?
Is it a day off?”
“Not exactly.
A slight problem arose during business hours.”
“Oh.”
I hadn’t expected that.
I glanced to the side and saw Cheongpung looking as though he was about to burst into tears.
Scratching my head, I spoke to the guard.
“Isn’t there any way around it?
We had an appointment today.
His name is Baek Museong.
I was told you’d know him if I gave you his name.”
“Again, I’m sorry, but at the moment— Excuse me?
Did you say Great Hero Baek Museong?”
“Yes.
Baek Museong, Huashan’s Lone Crane.”
Cheongpung called out desperately.
“Martial Nephew Baek!
Where are you, Martial Nephew Baek?
Can you hear my stomach growling?”
The guard looked back and forth between us, then flung open the tightly closed main gate.
“I’ll escort you to the private annex immediately!”
What the hell?
Why the sudden change in attitude?
Did Baek Museong stand us up?
My guess was wrong.
We followed the guard as he raced ahead almost fast enough to fly and arrived at a nearly devastated private annex.
Baek Museong was waiting for us there, sword drawn.
Wow.
This really is the full course.
This kind of shit makes me sick of being a martial artist.

chapters.title: Chapter 314
paragraphs: I stared blankly at the scene before me.
The spacious room had been reduced to a wasteland. Amid the wreckage stood two young men facing each other. No—three, if I counted the middle-aged man whose face had gone deathly pale.
What am I looking at here?
The answer came quickly.
What else? The same sight I saw practically every day.
An argument and a fight. At this point, I was starting to think they were essential virtues for any martial artist.
After taking stock of the situation, I muttered, “You’ve really laid out a full-course feast.”
Baek Museong quietly lowered his sword and gave me an awkward smile.
“You came.”
“You told me to come, so here I am. Now I already want to leave.”
“It’s been a long time. But where are the others...?”
His gaze swept over my shoulder. He couldn’t possibly be looking for Gung Gibang or Hyuk Mujin. He was obviously searching for the Martial Uncle who was the bane of his existence.
But Cheongpung and the rest of the Bermuda Triangle had vanished without a trace.
I thought they were following me quietly.
Please, just don’t cause any trouble.
I rubbed between my eyebrows. Never mind the Bermuda trio—the immediate problem was right in front of me.
“Is that what matters right now? Is causing trouble a Huashan specialty?”
“There was a minor complication.”
“You don’t need to explain. Anyone can see that.”
Suppressing a click of my tongue, I looked at the young bastard facing Baek Museong.

Sharp eyes and a shovel chin. Every young prodigy I’d met around here had been handsome or beautiful, which had left me feeling relatively deprived. But this guy was on the ugly side, so I immediately felt a certain kinship with him.
“Hello.”
They said you couldn’t spit in a smiling face.
The bastard responded to my friendly greeting.
“Get lost. A beggar like you has no place here.”
I turned to Baek Museong.
“Young Hero Baek, who the fuck is this bastard?”
“He is Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.”
“This bastard is a dragon too? Why the hell are there so many dragons?”
“He is known throughout the martial world as the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”
“He looks more like an earthworm.”
An ugly bastard with an ugly personality. That pissed me off twice as much.
At my mutter, Hyuk Sopyung’s eyebrows shot up.
“Well, look at this son of a bitch...”
“Better than being worse than a dog. And think carefully before you swing that sword. This is the greatest crisis of your life.”
Hyuk Sopyung’s hand twitched. The blade that had been inching toward me stopped and slowly lowered. He looked me up and down with blazing eyes.
“You’re no ordinary man.”
“Yep. I’m pretty extraordinary.”
“I thought you were merely a hide peddler... But then again, Huashan’s Lone Crane wouldn’t bother with someone like that.”
“Unlike you, Baek Museong gives everyone the time of day. And look at these beautiful muscles. Do you think you can build muscles like this by selling hides?”
Admittedly, I looked like a mess.

I had charged straight ahead for more than seven days and nights without stopping at an inn even once. My hair was slick with oil, and the martial uniform that had once been clean had long since become coated in dust.
The finishing touch was the wooden pack frame piled high with hides. Jeok Cheongang’s small figure was hidden inside it.
Looking shabby is one thing, but I do smell a little.
It was about time I washed.
Hyuk Sopyung glared at me as I pressed my nose to my uniform and sniffed.
“Stop fooling around and state your sect and name.”
“God, it’s always ‘sect this, sect that’ with you people. Don’t you ever get tired of it?”
“I can promise you one thing. Unless you belong to the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families, you won’t walk out of here in one piece.”
“Really?”
I made a show of shuddering.
“What am I going to do? My sect belongs to neither the Nine Sects and One Gang nor the Five Great Families. Can’t you just let me walk out anyway?”
“You should have watched your mouth. Remember that your paltry three-inch tongue has placed both you and your sect in danger.”
“My sect is actually in a bit of trouble already. There are only two of us, including me.”
“Two?”
“Yep. My Master and me. That’s it.”
A sneer tugged at Hyuk Sopyung’s lips as he turned to Baek Museong.
“To think you would waste your time on some nobody from a Third Rate sect. You must have far too much time on your hands. Wouldn’t you be better off spending it practicing your martial arts?”
“I’m not so sure. I believe there are several problems with what you just said.”
Baek Museong continued with a pleasant smile.
“First, Jin Taekyung’s sect is not Third Rate, nor is he a nobody. Second, you are one step beneath me. That has remained true from the day we first met until now.”
“What did you just say?”
“I said you are one step beneath me. Seeing you cause a drunken disturbance like this, I suspect that will remain true in the future as well.”
His lips were smiling, but his eyes were not.
There was something in Baek Museong’s gaze that had nothing to do with martial arts.
The aura—or perhaps the dignity—that belonged to him as a person.
That seemed to be part of the reason Hyuk Sopyung could only grind his teeth without daring to answer.
And people like him always try to settle things with their fists when they run out of words.
Just like now.
The tip of Hyuk Sopyung’s sword trembled. Before he could make his move, I spoke.
“I’m pretty sure I already warned you. Think carefully before you swing that sword.”
Whoosh.
Hyuk Sopyung whipped his head toward me, his eyes gleaming with murderous intent.

“I believe all things are equal, so I don’t usually split hairs over this stuff. But you should be grateful you’re a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect. If you weren’t, you’d already have been carried out of here.”
Dark Heaven was gathering like a storm cloud in the distance.
At a time like this, when the Murim needed to unite just to stand a chance, starting a dispute with the Zhongnan Sect was obviously a terrible idea.
Though it might already be a little late for that.
I already had bad blood with the Zhongnan Sect.
As Three Hands of Zhongnan—and as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
Old Master thoroughly thrashed him and sent him packing a year ago.

The Roaring Fury Swordsman wasn’t some nameless nobody rolling around in the street. He was an Elder of the Zhongnan Sect and the Senior Brother of the Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord. From what I’d heard, the fallout had been considerable.
Apparently, the Roaring Fury Swordsman had entered secluded training for some reason, while the Three Hands of Zhongnan had been slapped by their Sect Leader.
That’s already a perfectly good grudge. There’s no need to take it any further.
The smell of the oil Jeok Cheongang had poured all over the Zhongnan Sect hadn’t even faded yet. I had no desire to set it on fire.
Especially not while Jeok Cheongang was unconscious.
“So put your sword away and go quietly. Okay?”
Good job. This is how you become an adult.
It was such a calm response that I wanted to praise myself.
But Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon, disagreed.
His teeth ground together, and his eyes flashed.
“Then let’s see whether your skills can match that mouth of yours.”
Hissssss!
The sword in Hyuk Sopyung’s hand tore through the air at blinding speed.
At the same moment, a net of Sword Energy swept toward me.
It was the same martial art that the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, had unleashed a year ago.
Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.
The Zhongnan Sect’s signature technique.
Jeok Cheongang had told me that once someone reached the ultimate level of the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords, a single swing could fill heaven and earth in every direction with Sword Energy.
But...
“You know what?”
Whoosh!
Flamefire Path.
The Fire Gate Clan’s signature movement technique, passed down for hundreds of years, became a single streak of flame.
I tore through the net of Sword Energy and reached my target without hesitation. Staring into Hyuk Sopyung’s wide eyes, I whispered, “You and I are on completely different levels.”
Hiss—grab!
Hyuk Sopyung hurriedly altered his sword’s path, but I caught him by the wrist.
The Extreme Yang qi concentrated in my hand made a sizzling sound as his flesh burned.
“Gaaah!”
A single scream burst from his lips.
The sword slipped from Hyuk Sopyung’s grasp and rolled across the floor with a metallic clatter.
Before it could even hit the ground, my palm connected with his cheek.
Smack!
Once more.
Smack!
And one more time.
Smack!
Hyuk Sopyung staggered after taking three slaps without the slightest chance to resist.
Even without putting any internal energy into the blows, my physical abilities had long since surpassed human limits. His eyes were already half-unfocused, as though his soul had fled his body.
“What was it you said earlier? You wanted to see whether my skills could match my mouth?”
“Ghh... Ghhhhh...”
“Listen, you idiot. If you’re from the Zhongnan Sect, then I’m from the physical school. Next time, choose where you’re going to lie down before you stretch out your legs. Got it?”
Tap, tap.
I patted Hyuk Sopyung’s cheek. Only then did his eyes finally regain their focus.
“H-how could you overcome the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords at seven-tenths mastery so easily...?”

“You’ve only mastered seven-tenths of it? No wonder it felt so half-assed. Get it to at least nine-tenths before you come at me again. I’ve already faced it once, so the result will probably be the same, but still.”
“You’ve faced the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords at n-nine-tenths mastery?”
“I have. I even dodged it.”
“That’s impossible! Fewer than five people in our sect have reached nine-tenths mastery!”
“I’m talking about one of those five. I heard he’s one of the top three masters in Zhongnan.”
I let out a quiet laugh and continued.
“The Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il. I wonder how the old man is doing these days. He didn’t look too well when he was humiliated and sent packing last year.”
That was answer enough.

Hyuk Sopyung was a Direct Disciple of Zhongnan’s main lineage, as well as the man called the sect’s greatest prodigy. There was no way an insider wouldn’t know a rumor that had even reached outsiders.
Hyuk Sopyung’s bloodshot eyes widened, and his body began to tremble.
“Then could you be...?”

“About what I said regarding my sect—every word was true. It isn’t one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and its only members are my Master and me. I don’t know what possessed them to make the sect rules that way, but with only one successor per generation and a ban on teaching the unworthy, they’re damn strict.”
“The Fire Gate Clan...!”
“Disciples! There are two of them!”
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—you’re Jin Taekyung!”
“Jin Taekyung! That’s right!”
I yanked him closer by the collar and shouted. Hyuk Sopyung’s face turned deathly pale.
After watching his expression for a moment, I grinned and gave his crumpled collar a few brisk pats.
“You know what our Master’s temper is like, right? Let’s end this here without any hard feelings. What was the phrase? Right. Let’s bury this matter forever.”
“Strange. No answer. Maybe you’ll be able to hear me after about ten slaps.”
I slowly raised my palm.
Hyuk Sopyung flinched reflexively and clenched his teeth.
“I... understand.”
“Hm? What was that? I can’t quite hear the voice of a loser who’s only mastered seven-tenths of the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.”
“...I said I understand.”
“Good. Watch yourself on the way out. I won’t see you off.”
Crack.
The bones in Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly clenched fist creaked.
After glaring one last time at me, Baek Museong, and the middle-aged martial artist whose identity I didn’t know, he strode toward the door of the private annex.
Just as he was about to leave, Baek Museong spoke.
“I’m reminded of a boy I met at a Huashan-Zhongnan gathering ten years ago.”
“Take care, Sopyung.”
Hyuk Sopyung froze at Baek Museong’s calm voice. Then he left the private annex without another word.
Hyuk Sopyung’s presence receded into the distance.
At the same time, someone began creeping toward us.
“Come out.”
At my words, someone sucked in a startled breath.
A moment later, Cheongpung poked his head out, his cheeks puffed up like a squirrel’s.
He gulped down the food in his mouth, glanced around nervously, and bowed to Baek Museong.
“I’m really sorry about last time, Martial Nephew Baek...”
I suddenly remembered what had happened a year ago.
While Cheongpung was being forcibly escorted back to Huashan, he had beaten Baek Museong and the Three Plum Blossom Elites before escaping.
So this is a meeting between the perpetrator and the victim.
That bastard is guilty, no question.

Hiss—grab!
Hyuk Sopyung hurriedly altered his sword’s path, but I caught him by the wrist.
The Extreme Yang qi concentrated in my hand made a sizzling sound as his flesh burned.
“Gaaah!”
A single scream burst from his lips.
The sword slipped from Hyuk Sopyung’s grasp and rolled across the floor with a metallic clatter.
Before it could even hit the ground, my palm connected with his cheek.
Smack!
Once more.
Smack!
And one more time.
Smack!
Hyuk Sopyung staggered after taking three slaps without the slightest chance to resist.
Even without putting any internal energy into the blows, my physical abilities had long since surpassed human limits.
His eyes were already half-unfocused, as though his soul had fled his body.
“What was it you said earlier?
You wanted to see whether my skills could match my mouth?”
“Ghh...
Ghhhhh...”
“Listen, you idiot.
If you’re from the Zhongnan Sect, then I’m from the physical school.
Next time, choose where you’re going to lie down before you stretch out your legs.
Got it?”
Tap, tap.
I patted Hyuk Sopyung’s cheek.
Only then did his eyes finally regain their focus.
“H-how could you overcome the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords at seven-tenths mastery so easily...?”
“You’ve only mastered seven-tenths of it?
No wonder it felt so half-assed.
Get it to at least nine-tenths before you come at me again.
I’ve already faced it once, so the result will probably be the same, but still.”
“You’ve faced the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords at n-nine-tenths mastery?”
“I have.
I even dodged it.”
“That’s impossible!
Fewer than five people in our sect have reached nine-tenths mastery!”
“I’m talking about one of those five.
I heard he’s one of the top three masters in Zhongnan.”
I let out a quiet laugh and continued.
“The Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il.
I wonder how the old man is doing these days.
He didn’t look too well when he was humiliated and sent packing last year.”
That was answer enough.
Hyuk Sopyung was a Direct Disciple of Zhongnan’s main lineage, as well as the man called the sect’s greatest prodigy.
There was no way an insider wouldn’t know a rumor that had even reached outsiders.
Hyuk Sopyung’s bloodshot eyes widened, and his body began to tremble.
“Then could you be...?”
“About what I said regarding my sect—every word was true.
It isn’t one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and its only members are my Master and me.
I don’t know what possessed them to make the sect rules that way, but with only one successor per generation and a ban on teaching the unworthy, they’re damn strict.”
“The Fire Gate Clan...!”
“Disciples!
There are two of them!”
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—you’re Jin Taekyung!”
“Jin Taekyung!
That’s right!”
I yanked him closer by the collar and shouted.
Hyuk Sopyung’s face turned deathly pale.
After watching his expression for a moment, I grinned and gave his crumpled collar a few brisk pats.
“You know what our Master’s temper is like, right?
Let’s end this here without any hard feelings.
What was the phrase?
Right.
Let’s bury this matter forever.”
“Strange.
No answer.
Maybe you’ll be able to hear me after about ten slaps.”
I slowly raised my palm.
Hyuk Sopyung flinched reflexively and clenched his teeth.
“I... understand.”
“Hm?
What was that?
I can’t quite hear the voice of a loser who’s only mastered seven-tenths of the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.”
“...I said I understand.”
“Good.
Watch yourself on the way out.
I won’t see you off.”
Crack.
The bones in Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly clenched fist creaked.
After glaring one last time at me, Baek Museong, and the middle-aged martial artist whose identity I didn’t know, he strode toward the door of the private annex.
Just as he was about to leave, Baek Museong spoke.
“I’m reminded of a boy I met at a Huashan-Zhongnan gathering ten years ago.”
“Take care, Sopyung.”
Hyuk Sopyung froze at Baek Museong’s calm voice.
Then he left the private annex without another word.
Hyuk Sopyung’s presence receded into the distance.
At the same time, someone began creeping toward us.
“Come out.”
At my words, someone sucked in a startled breath.
A moment later, Cheongpung poked his head out, his cheeks puffed up like a squirrel’s.
He gulped down the food in his mouth, glanced around nervously, and bowed to Baek Museong.
“I’m really sorry about last time, Martial Nephew Baek...”
I suddenly remembered what had happened a year ago.
While Cheongpung was being forcibly escorted back to Huashan, he had beaten Baek Museong and the Three Plum Blossom Elites before escaping.
So this is a meeting between the perpetrator and the victim.
That bastard is guilty, no question.

chapters.title: Chapter 315
paragraphs: Step. Step.
The Zhongnan One Dragon, Hyuk Sopyung, walked neither quickly nor slowly.
With every step, people’s gazes and whispers followed him.
“Tut-tut. Causing a scene like that in broad daylight...”
“To think that’s the man they call his sect’s greatest young prodigy. Tells you all you need to know about the Zhongnan Sect. No wonder Huashan has always been the greatest sect in Shaanxi.”
“Why is his cheek so swollen? I heard Huashan’s Lone Crane was here. Could it be...?”
Hyuk Sopyung unconsciously rubbed his cheek.
The throbbing pain wasn’t only from the stinging gazes around him. The three slaps he had taken without being able to resist—and one man’s low voice—came vividly back to him.
I thought I told you. Think carefully before you swing that sword.
The Fire Gate Clan successor chosen by the Fire King Jeok Cheongang. A Hidden Dragon who had risen from the small stream that was Shanxi Province.
Hyuk Sopyung had already heard enough about that bastard to last him a lifetime.
But...
How can he be that strong?
He couldn’t understand it. He had become the direct Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect’s Sect Leader and studied martial arts with the sect’s full support.
Countless Peak martial arts and elixirs, even his place among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—Hyuk Sopyung had taken them all for granted.
But now, everything around him was beginning to totter.
The cold expression on the face of Xi’an Tower’s chief manager when they met at the entrance was only one sign.
“I heard you caused another disturbance.”
“A disturbance? There was a little commotion, that’s all. It was nothing serious, so let’s forget about it.”
Hyuk Sopyung was about to walk past him when the chief manager’s next words stopped him dead.
“I believe I told you last time that if this happened again, I would file a formal complaint with the Zhongnan Sect.”
“A complaint?”
Hyuk Sopyung glared at the chief manager, his eyes gleaming.
“Our Manager Song has grown quite bold.”
“Young Hero Hyuk!”
“Don’t get cocky.”
A growl slipped between Hyuk Sopyung’s clenched teeth.
“You seem awfully full of yourself just because the owner’s son joined Huashan as a lay Disciple... Do you really think the Great Zhongnan Sect is such a joke?”
“You go too far.”
Hyuk Sopyung twisted his lips at the chief manager’s stiff expression.
“You’re the ones going too far. A pack of wine sellers dares to look down on our sect? You’ve got more nerve than sense.”
“May I repeat those words to the owner exactly as you said them?”
“Don’t forget. Be sure to tell him. Then I’ll see you next time.”
Pat, pat.
Hyuk Sopyung patted the chief manager’s shoulder and walked away with a bitter smile on his lips.
Now even people like him are looking down on me.

Of course, Xi’an Tower’s owner possessed considerable influence for someone who could be called a mere businessman. He was a major player who controlled the entertainment district of Xi’an, the capital of Shaanxi Province.
But no matter how powerful someone was in the business world, before the name of the Nine Sects and One Gang, he was nothing more than a firefly before the sun.
And now Hyuk Sopyung had suffered such humiliation at the hands of a mere pleasure-house manager—not even the owner himself.
Things really are going from bad to worse.
Over the past year or two, the Zhongnan Sect’s standing had plummeted again and again.

The first shot had been fired by the Fire King Jeok Cheongang when he crushed the Roaring Fury Swordsman in front of countless witnesses. Then came the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s return from seclusion, followed by the name Huashan Divine Dragon.
How could two tigers live on the same mountain?
One had to be the strong one, and the other the weak.
The Zhongnan Sect’s role was the latter.
It won’t always be like this.
Blood trickled from Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly clenched fist.
He had expelled the last of the previous night’s alcohol from his body long ago. He was staring up at the sky with a grim expression when—
“Gasp, gasp. Senior Brother, there you are.”
“You’re... Bong-su?”
Hyuk Sopyung looked at the familiar face in surprise.
The young man was panting heavily. Like Hyuk Sopyung, he was a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect. Though they had different Masters, they belonged to the same generation.
“What brings you here when you should be at the main sect?”
The main sect stood on Mount Zhongnan, two days from Xi’an. Bong-su, Hyuk Sopyung’s Junior Brother, answered.
“I’m carrying out a mission. The entire Taeeul Sword Unit came with me.”
“A mission? The Taeeul Sword Unit too?”

The Taeeul Sword Unit was a fighting force composed of the Zhongnan Sect’s second-generation Disciples. Though they couldn’t compare to Huashan’s Plum Blossom Swordsmen, they were still an elite unit the Zhongnan Sect took great pride in.
For the Taeeul Sword Unit, who rarely even left the main sect, to come all the way here...
Hyuk Sopyung frowned in puzzlement. His Junior Brother spoke.
“I was ordered to bring you back, Senior Brother.”
“Ordered? Who’s looking for me?”
“Senior Martial Uncle is in Xi’an.”
Hyuk Sopyung’s eyes widened. There were only two people his Junior Brother, who was of the same generation as him, could call Senior Martial Uncle.
One of them, the Roaring Fury Swordsman Song Il, had shut himself away at the main sect because of the internal injury he had suffered at the Fire King’s hands. That left only one person.
But why is he in Xi’an...?
Hyuk Sopyung hurriedly pushed the question from his mind.
If his Second Martial Uncle was looking for him, he couldn’t afford to delay for even a moment. Hyuk Sopyung feared the man more than he feared his own Master, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.
And it wasn’t only Hyuk Sopyung. Every Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect felt the same way.
The anxiety on his Junior Brother’s face was proof enough.
“Senior Brother, there’s no time.”
“Take me to Senior Martial Uncle at once.”
A short while later, Hyuk Sopyung shot forward at tremendous speed using his movement technique. One question kept circling through his mind.
What on earth is going on?
One thing was certain.
If his Second Martial Uncle, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, had stepped in, this was no ordinary matter.
True Qi Guidance was a dangerous and difficult undertaking.
Even when circulating one’s qi alone, there was always a risk of qi deviation. True Qi Guidance required circulating someone else’s qi for them, so its difficulty needed no explanation.
Especially when that someone is the Fire King.
The tension was on an entirely different level from when I had performed True Qi Guidance on the Peace Guild members.
Feeling as though I were stepping onto thin ice, I began moving the Scorching Yang Qi.
Slowly. Carefully.
I repeated those two words over and over. Allowing myself no distracting thoughts, I drew in Jeok Cheongang’s immense qi.
Whoooong.
The two streams of qi met.
But there was none of the collision or resistance I had encountered with the Peace Guild members. They simply blended together naturally.
They merged and yielded to my guidance as though they had always been one—as naturally as twins reuniting after a long separation.
Because they grew from the same root.
That was right. Jeok Cheongang and I shared the same root: the Fire Gate Clan.

If someone who hadn’t learned the Fire Gate Divine Technique had rashly attempted True Qi Guidance, they might have failed to withstand Jeok Cheongang’s immense internal energy and fallen into qi deviation.
What a relief.
I had already done this several times, but it never stopped being terrifying.
With my heart in my throat, I began the True Qi Guidance in earnest.
Following the formula of the Fire Gate Divine Technique, I ceaselessly circulated the Extreme Yang qi that had now become one.
One shichen, or perhaps two.
I lost all sense of time in my concentration. The True Qi Guidance, which had seemed as though it would never end, finally came to a close when all the internal energy returned to the dantian.
Chime.
System True Qi Guidance successfully completed! - The target’s condition has improved slightly! - Your Scorching Yang Qi has increased slightly!
“Phew...”
I closed my eyes and steadied my breathing.
It wasn’t over yet. For one brief moment, I had merged with the immense qi of the Supreme Peak master known as the Fire King Jeok Cheongang and felt it as my own.
The root called the Fire Gate Clan. The trunk of the great tree that had grown from it, and its countless branches. I had clearly witnessed a glimpse of an unimaginably distant realm.
Insight came from experiences and circumstances like this.
Just like now.
I’m finally starting to see the way forward.
I could see them—the steps leading to a higher realm.
It was a small insight no one could have taught me.
Chime.

System The realm of Fire Gate Divine Technique has risen to seven stars! - You can manipulate, release, and withdraw qi more freely! - You can now perform the martial arts of the Fire Gate Clan with greater power and effectiveness! - You have acquired a large amount of EXP and Bonus Points as a reward for your enlightenment! - Level Up!
Yes. This was it.
I opened my eyes to the cheerful chime. I had climbed only a single step, but the difference was immense.
Through my newly sharpened senses, information about everything around me came flooding in.
My entire body was drenched in sweat. The impurities I had expelled reeked. And someone was struggling silently behind me.
What the fuck?
I turned my head and saw Cheongpung wrapped around Hyuk Mujin’s entire body like an anaconda, both hands clamped firmly over Mujin’s mouth and nose.
“What are you doing over there?”
Cheongpung answered brightly.
“Hyuk Mujin was about to snore, so I was stopping him!”
“Ah, well done. That bastard nearly pissed me off so badly I fell into qi deviation.”
I told that idiot Hyuk Mujin to stand guard, and he was off dreaming the Butterfly Dream.
I stared at Hyuk Mujin, whose face had turned blue as he struggled, and suddenly thought of something.
“You only need to cover his nose. Why are you covering his mouth too?”
“When I covered his nose, sounds started coming out of his mouth!”
“Oh.”
“So I covered both!”
“Hmm. Won’t he suffocate and die?”
“He can use the Turtle Breath Technique!”
“What exactly is this damn Turtle Breath Technique?”
“You hold your breath, stop your heartbeat, and lower your body temperature at the same time!”
“Sounds incredible. Is that even possible?”
“Of course. That’s what Hyuk Mujin is doing right now!”
“Mujin is?”
“Yes! His heartbeat has already stopped.”
My brain stopped working.
I stared silently at Hyuk Mujin. While we had been talking, he had stopped struggling, and his limbs now hung limp.
“Gasp! Mujin!”
“He’ll be cold soon!”
“Get your hands off him right now, you lunatic!”
“Huh? Maybe it isn’t the Turtle Breath Technique. Young Hero Hyuk? Can’t you hear me? Young Hero Hyuk?”
I didn’t know about the Turtle Breath Technique, but the Ghost Technique certainly seemed accurate.
Just before Hyuk Mujin could achieve Great Completion in the Ghost Technique, I slammed a palm into his chest.
“Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Fist!”
Thud!
With the dull impact, a harsh breath burst from Hyuk Mujin’s open mouth.
“Gahk!”
“Oh no, Mujin! My left pinky!”
“Cough, cough! C-Captain?”
“Are you all right? Can you breathe?”
“What?”
Hyuk Mujin looked around in confusion. Maybe because he had been attacked in the middle of his sleep, he didn’t seem to understand what had happened.
“What’s going on? I was just on a cloud.”
“A cloud?”
This idiot had really almost died.
I was letting out a sigh of relief when Hyuk Mujin continued.
“A man in white came over and started saying strange things. Something about a little lamb having come.”
“What kind of lamb?”
“A little lamb. Then he tried to embrace me, but there were holes this big in both his palms. I was about to cut him down without mercy when I woke up.”
Why was that person there?
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the door to our private room at Xi’an Tower slid open, and a grimy face poked inside.
Gung Gibang looked over the dejected Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, who had just returned from the dead, and finally me, still shell-shocked.
Then he muttered, “What a kennel.”
Being treated like a dog by a beggar left a bad taste in my mouth.
After barely pulling myself together, I asked Gung Gibang, “Were you out begging?”
Gung Gibang shouted indignantly, “What are you talking about? I’m on my way back from our sect’s Xi’an branch!”

The previous night, I had decided to spend a day at Xi’an Tower and recover from the fatigue of our journey. I had also asked Gung Gibang to gather information, so he must have visited the Xi’an branch for that reason.
Since beggars were scattered throughout the world, the Beggars’ Sect had branches everywhere.
In terms of sheer numbers, it was the greatest sect under heaven.
“So? Did you find anything useful? Something about the Divine Physician’s whereabouts, for example.”
“I did. Though it wasn’t about the Divine Physician.”
Gung Gibang thought for a moment before continuing.
“This information reeks to high heaven.”
“More than you?”
“Sorry. Tell me.”
Deeply offended, Gung Gibang refused to open his mouth until I had given him five silver nyang in alms.

With the dull impact, a harsh breath burst from Hyuk Mujin’s open mouth.
“Gahk!”
“Oh no, Mujin!
My left pinky!”
“Cough, cough!
C-Captain?”
“Are you all right?
Can you breathe?”
“What?”
Hyuk Mujin looked around in confusion.
Maybe because he had been attacked in the middle of his sleep, he didn’t seem to understand what had happened.
“What’s going on?
I was just on a cloud.”
“A cloud?”
This idiot had really almost died.
I was letting out a sigh of relief when Hyuk Mujin continued.
“A man in white came over and started saying strange things.
Something about a little lamb having come.”
“What kind of lamb?”
“A little lamb.
Then he tried to embrace me, but there were holes this big in both his palms.
I was about to cut him down without mercy when I woke up.”
Why was that person there?
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the door to our private room at Xi’an Tower slid open, and a grimy face poked inside.
Gung Gibang looked over the dejected Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, who had just returned from the dead, and finally me, still shell-shocked.
Then he muttered, “What a kennel.”
Being treated like a dog by a beggar left a bad taste in my mouth.
After barely pulling myself together, I asked Gung Gibang, “Were you out begging?”
Gung Gibang shouted indignantly, “What are you talking about?
I’m on my way back from our sect’s Xi’an branch!”
The previous night, I had decided to spend a day at Xi’an Tower and recover from the fatigue of our journey.
I had also asked Gung Gibang to gather information, so he must have visited the Xi’an branch for that reason.
Since beggars were scattered throughout the world, the Beggars’ Sect had branches everywhere.
In terms of sheer numbers, it was the greatest sect under heaven.
“So?
Did you find anything useful?
Something about the Divine Physician’s whereabouts, for example.”
“I did.
Though it wasn’t about the Divine Physician.”
Gung Gibang thought for a moment before continuing.
“This information reeks to high heaven.”
“More than you?”
“Sorry.
Tell me.”
Deeply offended, Gung Gibang refused to open his mouth until I had given him five silver nyang in alms.

chapters.title: Chapter 316
paragraphs: Gung Gibang carefully tucked the silver nyang into his clothes before speaking.
“It’s about the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
“The Yongbong Escort Bureau? You mean the one we ran into on the way here?”
“That’s right. Its operations are limited to Shaanxi Province now, but it was once one of the largest escort bureaus under Heaven.”
“The Yongbong Escort Bureau?”
I thought back to what I had seen two days ago.

For a mere escort bureau, they certainly had an impressive fighting force. Their Young Bureau Head, Ju Hwaran, was a skilled swordswoman worthy of her place among the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, while an escort named Song Ilseom was at least a cut above her.
Counting the old man who looked like he could have written the Donguibogam, that made three Peak masters.
That put them on par with most well-established mid-sized sects.
But compared to their glory days, when they had ranked among the top three escort bureaus under Heaven, what I had seen that day was downright shabby.
“What the hell happened to leave it in that state?”
“It started right after the Escort King passed away.”
“The Escort King? The one I know?”
“There can’t be two Escort Kings under Heaven. Great Hero Ju Gongsan—the Escort King you know—was the previous Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
Escort King Ju Gongsan.
I hadn’t known his name, but I had heard his sobriquet plenty of times. I had been around the Murim long enough by now to pick up a decent amount of general knowledge.
Besides, I had spent the past year practically joined at the hip with the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
He was a living witness to history—and occasionally an old man who reminisced about the past.
Come to think of it, that friend of mine, the Escort King, was quite something too.
He’s not your friend.
It hasn’t been that long since you tasted the Flame Divine Palm, has it?
Please tell me more. I’ll listen with rapt attention.
The story Jeok Cheongang had told me that day about the Escort King had been quite moving.

It was when the Great Faction War was at its height. By then, the Demonic Cult had seized eight provinces, including Gansu, Sichuan, and Yunnan, and was advancing into the Central Plains with a hundred thousand demonic soldiers.
When does the Escort King show up?
It hasn’t been that long since you tasted the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, has it?
Please continue. I’m begging you.

In any case, the Escort King was nothing more than a wandering escort at the time. Of course, his remarkable skill and chivalrous spirit had already earned him some renown. But with the Demonic Cult sweeping across the world, do you think the orthodox martial artists had time to care about that?
True. Strictly speaking, escorts belong more to the business world than the Murim.

The Demonic Cult needed money as well, so rather than oppressing escort bureaus and merchant groups, they chose to win them over. Given the circumstances, it wasn’t particularly strange that the Escort King of those days was in Guangdong, which was under the Demonic Cult’s control. Everything went smoothly until he met a woman who was about to give birth.
A woman about to give birth?
She carried the last seed of the Guangdong Chen Family in her womb. The family had already been wiped out for resisting the Demonic Cult more fiercely than anyone else.
They must have been found almost immediately.
The Escort King only realized the truth after he encountered a Demonic Cult pursuit squad. If he refused to hand over the woman, he would have to make an enemy of the Demonic Cult.
At the time, the Demonic Cult had already swallowed half the world after winning battle after battle, Jeok Cheongang had said.
Worse still, Guangdong Province lay tens of thousands of li from orthodox territory. It was nothing short of the Demonic Cult’s lair.
What do you think the Escort King did?
If he’d handed the woman over to the Demonic Cult, he wouldn’t have been the Escort King.
Correct. He flatly rejected their demand. His reason was simple: he had already been paid the escort fee.
On a day when the world was engulfed in war, the young escort began what might have been his final escort mission.
Tucked inside his clothes was the old jade hairpin the woman of the Guangdong Chen Family had given him as payment.
I heard it took him two whole years.
From Guangdong through Jiangxi and Hubei, all the way to Henan, where the Murim Alliance was located.
The young escort crossed half the continent while evading his pursuers. He climbed mountains, raced across fields, and swam through rivers.
No one knew how he had done it or how many dangers he had overcome, but one thing was certain.
The young escort had completed an escort mission without precedent in the history of the Murim.
When his footsteps finally reached Henan, the last seed of the Guangdong Chen Family was crying lustily in the woman’s arms, and the escort Ju Gongsan had become the Escort King.
The Martial God said that he truly deserved to be called a king. No one disagreed.
Jeok Cheongang brought up the Escort King from time to time after that.
Even Jeok Cheongang, who looked at the world with a jaundiced eye, seemed to consider the Escort King a decent man.

I heard he founded an escort bureau in his hometown of Shaanxi after the Great Faction War ended... I don’t know what became of him after that. Perhaps I should stop by someday and share a few drinks with him.
In the end, Jeok Cheongang’s wish would never come true.
According to what Gung Gibang had just told me, Escort King Ju Gongsan was already dead.
The continent sure is small.
To think the Yongbong Escort Bureau we had encountered by chance two days ago was the legacy of that very Escort King.
Noticing the interest in my eyes, Gung Gibang continued.
“Great Hero Ju Gongsan couldn’t hold out for long after the internal injuries he suffered during the Great Faction War, and passed away. It was a tragic thing.”
“Then who’s the current Bureau Head?”
“Great Hero Ju Hogun, the Junzi Sword. He’s the Escort King’s only child and Young Lady Ju Hwaran’s father.”
“Junzi Sword, huh? That sobriquet alone gives me a pretty good idea of what he’s like.”
“I’ve never met him myself, but... my Master said the man himself was a very good person.”
A single particle could change the feeling of someone’s words entirely.
Gung Gibang’s Master, the Beggars’ Sect Leader, hadn’t simply said that Ju Hogun was a good person.
He had said that Ju Hogun was good as a person.
That reeks of a sucker.
I had a feeling the Junzi Sword’s personality had played a major part in reducing the Yongbong Escort Bureau to its current state.
Sure enough, Gung Gibang read my expression and nodded.
“As you guessed. Great Hero Ju is sentimental and can’t stand by when he sees injustice, so he’s suffered tremendous losses in various ways since taking over the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
“He was in the wrong line of work from the start.”
“My Master once said that a chivalrous hero could never be a merchant.”
He was right. To be called a chivalrous hero, you had to disregard profit. To become a successful merchant, you had to pursue it more fiercely than anyone else.
An escort bureau might stand at the intersection of the Murim and the business world, but in the end, it was much closer to the latter.
One hundred points as a chivalrous hero. Zero as a merchant.
The Escort King had managed to catch two rabbits at once and build the Yongbong Escort Bureau into one of the five largest in the industry because of his fame.
But that advantage must have vanished after his death. Ju Hogun lacked the makings of a merchant, and there was no way he could make up the difference.

“Whenever a great famine struck, he would exhaust his own grain stores, then pay a premium to buy even more and give all of it away. He took in poor children and orphans, fed them, and gave them places to sleep...”
“At that point, isn’t he basically UNICEF?”
“Huh?”
“Nothing. Keep going.”

“In any case, more money went out than came in, and the Yongbong Escort Bureau gradually began to decline. Because of his ties to the previous Bureau Head, my Master advised him several times, but apparently, he refused to listen. Great Hero Ju insisted that this was his policy.”
“Wow.”
He was certainly an admirable and respectable businessman. It was just a shame he wasn’t a capable one.
Gung Gibang scratched vigorously at his back as he continued.
“What could anyone do? With a man like Great Hero Ju inheriting the escort bureau, it was bound to shrink drastically in the span of thirty years.”
“Thirty years? They say even a ruined rich family lasts three generations.”
“It would have lasted three generations easily—if Great Hero Ju hadn’t collapsed from qi deviation two years ago.”
“...What’s that supposed to mean? Is this the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s age of tribulations or something?”
“Considering all the misfortunes they’ve suffered over the past two years, you could certainly call it that.”
“Good grief. They must have been through a lot.”
For an instant, Ju Hwaran’s spirited figure flashed through my mind.
At the time, I had thought only that she was smart and pretty. As it turned out, she was a young woman carrying an entire household on her shoulders.
But...
“What exactly is this stink you keep talking about?”
Gung Gibang had started the conversation so ominously that I had listened closely, but the only foul smell around here was the stench coming off that bastard.
My fastball, aimed tight and inside, made Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin—who had been listening in silence—crane their necks forward.
“That’s right. I don’t smell anything. I want to smell the stink too!”
“Young Hero Gung, when was the last time you brushed your teeth?”
When the man who had nearly killed someone and the man who had nearly died asked in unison, Gung Gibang scowled.
“Oh, shut up with all that yapping.”
“Never mind that. Hurry up and tell us. And don’t open your mouth so wide. Seriously, when did you last brush your teeth?”
“Four months ago.”
What a filthy bastard.
I stared at him as if he were some kind of animal. Gung Gibang flinched and hurriedly spat out a name.
“Z-Zhongnan Sect.”
“Huh? Zhongnan Sect?”
“According to what our Xi’an branch uncovered, there are signs that the Zhongnan Sect was deeply involved in the downfall of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
“Good grief. Those bastards stick their noses into everything.”
So this really was information that stank.
No wonder the stench had hit me the moment I heard the words Zhongnan Sect.
For a moment, I wondered if it was because Gung Gibang had opened his mouth too wide. But judging by the conduct of every Zhongnan Sect member I had met so far, this wasn’t a rumor. It was a fact.
“They’re trying to swallow the Yongbong Escort Bureau whole, aren’t they?”
“Swallow it whole? Is it tasty?”
“Cheongpung, could you shut your mouth for a moment?”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
By now accustomed to all of this, Gung Gibang answered as if nothing had happened.

“Most likely. Zhongnan operates an escort bureau of its own, but it can’t compare to the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s position within Shaanxi. From Zhongnan’s perspective, the Yongbong Escort Bureau must be a thorn in its side, just like Huashan.”
“So they’ve been methodically bringing it down for the past two years?”
“Young Lady Ju Hwaran is certainly talented, but she has far too little experience. Being as softhearted as her father is another weakness.”
So she was smart, but naive.
Then again, from what I had heard, Ju Hwaran was only twenty-one.
At that age, she had enough on her plate just digesting everything she had learned. Adapting to real work while leading an escort bureau of that size couldn’t have been easy.
Especially with the Zhongnan Sect pulling dirty tricks behind the scenes.
Zhongnan might have been beneath Huashan, but it was still one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
The Yongbong Escort Bureau might have withstood its pressure while the Escort King was alive, but in its current state, it didn’t stand a chance.
Zhongnan would nibble away at it little by little until it finally collapsed.
“How widely known is this?”
“It’s top-secret information from the head of our Xi’an branch.”
“Top secret, huh? Then Huashan doesn’t know either?”
“Who knows? They might, or they might not. Even if they do, they could pretend otherwise and let it slide.”
“Pretend they don’t know? What’s that supposed to mean?”
Gung Gibang hesitated for a moment, then answered with a sigh.
“Because they’re both part of the Nine Sects and One Gang.”
“...What?”

“Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, is an upright and honorable man. The Sword Saint, Great Hero Mae Jonghak, is as clear as a stream, and so is Cheongpung standing here. But remember—it’s foolish to judge the whole by a single facet.”
That one sentence saw straight through me.
I was leaving today anyway. I had been planning to discreetly tip Baek Museong off.
He was someone I knew to be a good man. And he held enough standing to be called the future of Huashan.
But I had been wrong.
The future is only the future. It isn’t the present.
Once again, I realized that the Murim was more complicated than I had thought.
Even the world of ignorant, simple-looking swordsmen had rules—and a league of its own.
I guess an arm really does bend inward.
When I remained silent, Gung Gibang cautiously watched me and asked,
“What are you planning to do?”
“What do you mean, what am I going to do?”
“Are you... thinking of stepping in yourself?”
“Me?”
I considered it for a moment, then shook my head.
My encounter with the Yongbong Escort Bureau had been nothing more than chance. I had my own responsibilities.
“If I run into them before I leave, I can give them a heads-up. But that’s it.”
Now that Jeok Cheongang had collapsed, getting entangled with the Zhongnan Sect would complicate matters.
For some reason, Ju Hwaran’s face rose in my mind. I shook my head and let the thought slip away.
