chapters.title: Chapter 317
paragraphs: “Ah.”
Sunlight broke across Ju Hwaran’s long, fluttering eyelashes. Even after waking, she lay in bed for a long while, staring at the ceiling.
The night before, she and the Yongbong Escort Bureau had finally reached Xi’an.
Black Stone Stronghold, led by Heavenly Axe, had been the final obstacle on their escort mission.
They had passed through Xi’an’s safe, bustling streets and unloaded their baggage at a secluded inn. Beds, warm food, and hot bathwater had all been waiting for them.
After checking every item in the shipment, Ju Hwaran had collapsed into sleep.
At last, the end is in sight.

This place was safe. There were no bandits blocking the mountain roads, nor wandering martial artists concealing their identities and attacking in groups. Once they delivered the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng—the primary objective of this escort mission—to the Zhongnan Sect, it would all be over.
The Yongbong Escort Bureau would receive the reward its efforts deserved, and they would all return home together.
Along with thirty-three funerary urns.
Thirty-three...
Ju Hwaran’s eyes suddenly flickered faintly.
Thirty-three bone urns. Thirty-three faces. Memories of laughing and crying with them flashed before her eyes.
“Ah, I shouldn’t be doing this...”
Ju Hwaran rubbed at the corners of her eyes with her sleeve, then slapped both cheeks hard. The sharp crack brought her scattered thoughts back, if only a little.
“This is only the beginning. I have to keep my head.”
The escort mission was not over yet.
Three days remained until the deadline agreed upon with the Zhongnan Sect, and the mission would not be complete until the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng had been safely delivered.
“And then... it’ll be a new beginning.”
Muttering softly, Ju Hwaran reached inside her robes. She pulled out a tightly sealed wooden casket, checked it, then put it away again and secured it with a cord.
Just that brief exposure left a cool fragrance lingering at the tip of her nose before it faded.
Inside the casket was the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, an ancient elixir coveted by every martial artist in the Murim.
“Stay focused, Ju Hwaran. You’ve only taken the first step.”
That was when someone spoke from outside the door.
“Hwaran, are you awake?”
It was a familiar voice. Ju Hwaran straightened her clothes before answering.
“Yes, Uncle Heo. You may come in.”
“Then excuse me for a moment.”
A moment later, Chief Escort Heo Jun opened the door and entered with a bright expression.
“We’ll be able to return to the Escort Bureau sooner than expected.”
“You mean...”
“The Zhongnan Sect is waiting in Xi’an.”
“The Zhongnan Sect?”
“That’s right. And I hear the Taeeul Merciless Sword himself has come. Hahaha.”
Unlike Heo Jun, who was smiling, Ju Hwaran’s gaze sank deeply.
The Zhongnan Sect? And the Taeeul Merciless Sword came all the way to Xi’an himself?
Their return had been moved forward, so she should have been happy, just like Heo Jun.
But the more she thought about the arrogant, discourteous attitude the Zhongnan Sect had shown them until now, the more unease crept up from the depths of her heart.
“Uncle Heo, don’t you think something is strange?”
“Hm? What do you mean, strange?”
“There are still three days until the agreed-upon deadline.”
“Only three days. Even traveling slowly, it takes no more than two to get from Xi’an to Mount Zhongnan.”
“You used to say it all the time, Uncle. There are no coincidences in the Murim. It’s a place where nothing should surprise you, no matter what happens.”
“Hwaran, what are you trying to say?”
Under Heo Jun’s utterly baffled gaze, Ju Hwaran spoke gravely.

“The Zhongnan Sect has been quietly hostile toward the Yongbong Escort Bureau all this time. They must have wanted this escort mission to fail more than anyone. That’s why they deliberately imposed such difficult conditions.”
“But we accepted them. And we’ve performed admirably.”

The conditions demanded by the Zhongnan Sect had been extremely difficult. The other heads of escort bureaus who had flocked there, lured by the Zhongnan Sect’s reputation, had even shaken their heads emphatically and abandoned the commission.
If they failed to transport the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng within the specified period, the mission would be deemed a failure, and they would have to pay an astronomical penalty.
But after much deliberation, Ju Hwaran had accepted the Zhongnan Sect’s commission.
For one reason alone: to raise the Yongbong Escort Bureau to greater heights.
And we had to pay a terrible price for it.
Something that should never have happened had happened.
Information about the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng had been leaked.
Ju Hwaran was not a fool. She simply lacked experience. She possessed a sharp mind capable of considering every possibility and keeping all options open.
The suspicions she had kept buried until now were slowly taking shape. Ju Hwaran spoke quietly.
“Perhaps... perhaps the Zhongnan Sect...”
“Enough.”
Heo Jun cut her off, his face hardening.
“Stop. I know what you’re thinking, but anything beyond that is absurd. No—it’s dangerous.”
“But—”

“I know the rumors about the Zhongnan Sect. It’s also true that they’ve been keeping us in check so they can expand their own escort bureau. But what you’re suggesting, Hwaran... is dangerous speculation.”
“Uncle Heo...”
“As your uncle and as the Chief Escort of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, I’m asking you. Don’t put yourself or the bureau in danger.”
Though they shared not a drop of blood, he was an uncle who had always treated her warmly, ever since she was a child.
When he deliberately poured out those words with such a stern expression, Ju Hwaran could no longer continue speaking about the Zhongnan Sect.
“Phew.”
As Ju Hwaran let out a quiet sigh, Heo Jun gently put an arm around her shoulders.
“I’m sorry if I was too harsh.”
“No. I suppose I was being overly sensitive.”
“You had reason to be. The Zhongnan Sect did something it had never done before. Who would have expected them to send the Taeeul Merciless Sword instead of a Hall Master or Chief Steward?”
The Taeeul Merciless Sword was one of the Zhongnan Sect Leader’s two Senior Brothers.
He normally remained at the main sect and rarely showed himself in public. There was one simple reason people had remembered him for so long.
The First Sword of Zhongnan.
He was a Supreme Peak master produced by the Zhongnan Sect, a terrifying swordsman said to have mastered the ultimate principles of the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.
There had to be great significance behind a figure comparable to the Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, personally stepping forward.
That was what Ju Hwaran found most puzzling.
“Why the Taeeul Merciless Sword, of all people?”

“He must be in a hurry. Zhongnan spent a fortune acquiring the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng because of the Roaring Fury Swordsman’s Internal Injury, after all. His one and only Senior Brother ended up in that state. Imagine how he must feel.”
On the surface, it sounded reasonable.
But Ju Hwaran clearly remembered what her father, Ju Hogun, had told her years ago.
He said the man was frightening.

Her father had been so benevolent that people called him the Junzi Sword. If even Ju Hogun, who judged others generously, had described him that way, then the Taeeul Merciless Sword had to be every bit as sharp as his swordsmanship.
I can’t let my guard down until the very end.
After gathering her thoughts, Ju Hwaran asked Heo Jun about the one person still weighing on her mind.
“What about Captain Song?”
“Ah, about that...”
Heo Jun hesitated before answering.
“I had trustworthy escorts watching him discreetly day and night, but as you know, Hwaran, everyone let their guard down last night...”
“You took your eyes off him.”
“I have no excuse. It was my fault for failing to keep a closer watch.”
As Heo Jun awkwardly avoided her gaze, Ju Hwaran let out a small sigh.
Song Ilseom, whose origins were unclear and whose reputation among the public was poor, had been one of their primary subjects of surveillance.
Her suspicions of him had grown particularly strong after he met Jin Taekyung.
I told him over and over to keep a close eye on Song Ilseom.
Heo Jun was certainly a good man. He had served the Yongbong Escort Bureau for more than thirty years and had been close enough to Ju Hogun for them to address each other as brothers.
But the careless side he occasionally showed, like now, had also led to mistakes both large and small.
All I can do is hope it doesn’t happen this time.
The milk had already been spilled. In any case, the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was in her possession.
Hiding her disappointment, Ju Hwaran spoke.
“Where did the Zhongnan Sect ask us to meet?”
“At a teahouse called Tengwang Pavilion on the western edge of Xi’an. They want us there by noon.”
Tengwang Pavilion was a famous teahouse that Ju Hwaran had occasionally visited herself.
There would be plenty of witnesses, and the atmosphere was quiet, making it the perfect place to conclude an escort mission.
“We’ll leave in fifteen minutes. Please prepare.”
Baek Museong came to Xi’an Tower while we were in the middle of packing.
“Are you really leaving right away?”
“I’d like to stay a few more days too, but as you know, our schedule is a little tight.”
“That’s unfortunate. If possible, I would have liked to escort you to the main sect.”
“I’ll stop by on the way back. Give me a tour of Huashan then.”
“Haha, don’t worry. I’ll take responsibility for showing you everything properly.”
There it was again. The full-course promise.
Not that I was expecting the full course. I just hoped that when we met again, he wouldn’t be busy beating the hell out of someone like he had been this time.
Then, as I stared at Baek Museong’s face while he laughed heartily, a thought occurred to me.
Should I at least mention it? The Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect.
While I was debating, Baek Museong touched his face and asked,
“Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something on my face?”
“Young Hero Jin?”
“Oh, no. Something else just crossed my mind.”
Shit, I don’t know.
When you got right down to it, the Zhongnan Sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau were both complete strangers to me. Whatever dispute they had was theirs to resolve.
I already had more than enough problems of my own. Worrying about this too would just be sticking my nose where it didn’t belong.
This is the Murim, after all.
I muttered inwardly as I seated Jeok Cheongang on the pack frame. Then I picked up the furs and began piling them over him one by one.
Even as I worked, I couldn’t understand why Ju Hwaran kept coming to mind.
Song Ilseom, whom I had only glimpsed in passing, came to mind along with her.
Now that I think about it, he was a suspicious bastard. He stank even worse than Gung Gibang.
After learning about the relationship between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect, I found myself wondering who that bastard really was.
His Level was a staggering 110. At that level, he could probably strip one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes clean to the bone.
He had looked to be in his early to mid-thirties at most, but... who was he, and which sect did he belong to?
Could he be an assassin sent by the Zhongnan Sect? No, that’s probably going too far.
Had he simply fallen for Ju Hwaran’s beauty and decided to stay?

No. If that were the case, there would have been no reason for him to hide his true abilities. Was this one of those stories where the protagonist hides his power? Did some loser hiding his power look cooler when he rescued her?
Ju Hwaran. We only exchanged a few words, but she seemed like a good person. She had a refreshingly direct way of speaking too.
She also possessed extraordinary martial talent, having reached the Peak realm at her age.
And then there was... right. The dimples that appeared when she smiled were pretty. So were her half-moon eyes.
Come to think of it, she looked like a cat.
Cats had always been my favorite animals.
“Um, Captain?”
“Hm? Yeah?”
I turned and saw Hyuk Mujin staring at me strangely.
And not just him. Gung Gibang, Cheongpung, and even Baek Museong were all looking at me the same way.
“What? Why is everyone staring at me?”
“Well, the thing is...”
Hyuk Mujin cautiously pointed at the pack frame.
“In my humble opinion, Great Hero Jeok is going to suffocate at this rate.”
“Gasp!”
I hurriedly flung aside the furs that had piled up like a mountain.
Jeok Cheongang, who had nearly gone to meet that person while still in a coma, was breathing faintly.
“Oh, Benefactor! You’re just like me!”
“Did you just insult me?”
“Ah. No, no. That isn’t what I meant...”
Ignoring Cheongpung as he instantly drooped, I began piling the furs back on. Jeok Cheongang’s slight frame quickly disappeared beneath them.
Only after making sure enough air could pass through did I hoist the pack frame onto my back.
“All right. If everyone’s ready, let’s get going.”
We stepped outside amid Xi’an Tower’s lavish hospitality.
The bustling streets of Xi’an were packed with people. Over the din, Baek Museong spoke.
“I’d like to see you off, but you won’t allow it, will you?”
“We’ll be seeing each other again later anyway.”
“Haha. I knew you’d say that. Then I’ll be off. Stay well, Martial Uncle Cheongpung.”
“Take care, Martial Nephew Baek!”
In the end, I hadn’t even brought it up.
Good. This was fine.
Just as I was about to turn away, alone in my lingering unease amid the warm farewells, I overheard someone speaking.
“Did you hear? The Taeeul Merciless Sword of the Zhongnan Sect is in Xi’an.”
“What? The Taeeul Merciless Sword? Why on earth would he come here?”
“How should I know? Someone saw him heading toward Tengwang Pavilion in the west. Apparently, he’s meeting with the Yongbong Escort Bureau... but I can’t say for sure.”
The whispering voices slowly faded into the distance.
I asked Cheongpung,
“Cheongpung.”
“Yes, Benefactor.”
“Have you ever had tea?”
“Yes! I have!”
“No, you haven’t tried tea yet.”
If I said you hadn’t, then you hadn’t.

chapters.title: Chapter 318
paragraphs: “Astringent.”
The old man muttered as he savored his Tieguanyin.
His broad shoulders belied his age, and his snow-white beard hung all the way to his navel, giving him the appearance of an immortal.
He would have looked the part, too, if not for the old sword propped beside him.
“I-I’m sorry, Senior. I haven’t reached my father’s level yet...”
“It’s a shame, but it can’t be helped. When the owner changes, it’s only natural for the tea to taste different. You may go.”
The teahouse owner, who had been bowing repeatedly, vanished as though he had been waiting for those very words.
The old man watched him leave, then ran a hand over his teacup.
“The three of us martial brothers used to stop by this place from time to time. That was more than thirty years ago. Your Master wasn’t the Sect Leader back then, either.”
“I see.”
Hyuk Sopyung answered from across the table.
He had kept his mouth shut for more than half an hour while the old man performed his tea ceremony, and his voice was cracked like a drought-stricken rice paddy.
“Would you like a cup?”
The old man’s gentle voice contained not the slightest hint of coercion.
But when the old man before him offered something, it had to be accepted. Hyuk Sopyung knew that, as did the thirty members of the Taeeul Sword Unit stationed throughout the teahouse.
“I would be honored, Senior Martial Uncle.”
The old man picked up the jade-colored teapot and tilted it over the empty cup Hyuk Sopyung held out respectfully.
Trickle.
The tea slowly began to fill the cup.
At the same time, Hyuk Sopyung’s expression changed drastically.
“What is it?”
“I... It’s nothing.”
His words notwithstanding, Hyuk Sopyung was clearly struggling. His hand trembled, and his face flushed so red it seemed ready to burst.
It was only tea, yet every drop that struck the cup bore down on him with terrifying pressure.
What the hell...?

It was an enormous amount of internal energy. An overwhelming force that even Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy, could not withstand despite receiving every elixir available without restraint.
He drew up all the internal energy in his body and poured it into the teacup, but he reached his limit almost immediately.
Tap. Crack.
The instant the last drop fell, a hairline crack spread through the cup in Hyuk Sopyung’s hand, and tea spilled over the rim.
That was when the old man’s gaze darkened.
He was Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
“How old are you this year?”
“...I have reached thirty.”
“When did you last see this old man?”
“Ten years ago.”
“Yes, that’s right. The Huashan-Zhongnan gathering. That was where we last met.”
The Huashan-Zhongnan gathering. Or the Zhongnan-Huashan gathering.
Huashan and Zhongnan—the dragon and tiger crouched in Shaanxi Province—held a gathering once every ten years where their young prodigies competed against one another.
Its official purpose was to foster friendship and exchange through duels, but everyone knew it was really a competition between the two sects.
“I remember now. I watched with my own eyes as that bastard Baek Museong toyed with you.”
Hyuk Sopyung’s eyelids trembled.
How could he forget? The defeat he had suffered that day. The merciless gaze of The First Sword of Zhongnan, who had sought him out the moment he returned to the main sect.
“At your age, this old man had already mastered eight-tenths of the Taeeul Divine Technique. What about you?”
“...I apologize.”
“Ten years is enough time for mountains and rivers to change. Yet you remain exactly where you were.”
The same goes for you, Senior Martial Uncle.
Hyuk Sopyung fought desperately to hold back the words rising in his throat.
Surely you haven’t forgotten everything you did to me that day.
Talent without effort could never bloom.
Hyuk Sopyung loved martial arts. That was why he had been called the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest prodigy. He had devoted himself to martial arts and swung his sword through blood and sweat.
But he had not slowly fallen apart simply because Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong, defeated him in front of everyone.
“I already know you’ve been disgracing our sect’s name. I hear you’ve made quite a name for yourself in Xi’an.”
“Senior Martial Uncle...”
“This old man is speaking. Shut your mouth.”
Hwangbo Eom’s formerly dispassionate voice had turned colder than eternal ice.
“Watching all of you has been quite the farce. From top to bottom, every last one of you is splattering mud across the Zhongnan Sect’s signboard.”
By the top, he meant the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il. By the bottom, he meant Hyuk Sopyung.

Even though his only Senior Brother was laid up with an Internal Injury, Hwangbo Eom continued to spew venom at him. Hyuk Sopyung and the disciples of the Taeeul Sword Unit realized once again that the merciless part of his epithet—
Taeeul Merciless Sword.
—did not apply only to his enemies.
“Your Master, who led the Zhongnan Sect into this sorry state, is just as pathetic. Why our Master ever handed the position of Sect Leader to someone like him...”
That was when Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly pressed lips finally parted.
“You go too far.”
“What did you say?”
Whoosh.
A gust swept over Hyuk Sopyung’s entire body.
No—it was not wind.
It was a powerful wave of qi flowing from the Taeeul Merciless Sword, a Supreme Peak master produced by Zhongnan.
“I must be going deaf in my old age. Say that again.”
But Hyuk Sopyung did not yield, even beneath the suffocating pressure.
“Your words... ngh. Go too far.”
Though the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord had never shown him warmth or affection, he was still Hyuk Sopyung’s one and only Master. And more than that—
“He is the Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect. You are a Disciple of Zhongnan, just as this junior is. Show the Sect Leader the respect he is due.”
“Respect for the Sect Leader?”
A sharp gleam flashed through Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.
There had been a time when no one stood closer to the position of Zhongnan Sect Leader than he did.
He had a Senior Brother and Junior Brother under the same Master, but neither had been a true rival. Neither could match his martial prowess or his ruthlessness.
The Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect should have been Hwangbo Eom. It was only natural.
“And what could a nobody like you possibly know to dare...!”
Hwangbo Eom was about to roar when he abruptly closed his mouth.
He had noticed Hyuk Sopyung’s unwavering gaze. He had also sensed the strange current passing among the Zhongnan disciples of the Taeeul Sword Unit.
These bastards.
Hwangbo Eom’s gaze turned cold. At the same time, the powerful aura pouring from his body slowly subsided.
His lips moved beneath his snow-white beard.
“The Sect Leader of the Great Zhongnan Sect...”
Hwangbo Eom lifted his still more than half-full teacup and drained it. Deep furrows appeared between his wrinkled brows.
“Still astringent. With a new owner, neither the flavor nor the fragrance is what it used to be.”

“The Great Zhongnan Sect? What a laughable thing to say. Zhongnan today is nothing more than a castle in the air. While you were lost in despair and wasting your days on drinking, women, and gambling, this old man was working to restore our sect.”
“What do you mean...?”
Confusion colored Hyuk Sopyung’s voice.
Hadn’t Hwangbo Eom shut himself away at the main sect? Even when his Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman, returned with a serious Internal Injury, he had not shown his face even once.
Then how...?
Hyuk Sopyung’s thoughts were cut short when a group entered the teahouse.
At their head was a young woman whose mere presence seemed to brighten her surroundings.
“I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”
Ju Hwaran, the Dagger Hidden Flower.
At her bold greeting, the corners of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth curled upward.
“Good. Did you bring the item I requested?”
He stroked his thick beard, his eyes flashing with an unreadable light.
“By the way, who’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword?”
Speed Beggar answered gruffly.
“Who else would the Taeeul Merciless Sword be? He’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”
“Gibang. Aren’t you curious which is stronger—the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms at five-tenths power or the Flame Divine Palm at seven-tenths?”

“...The Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom. He’s the Junior Brother of the Roaring Fury Swordsman, Song Il, and the Senior Brother of the current Zhongnan Sect Leader, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.”
As expected of a walking encyclopedia of the Murim. I hadn’t brought him along for moments like this, but he was useful in all sorts of ways.
Except for the smell.
I muttered inwardly as I kept walking.
We were on our way to a teahouse called Tengwang Pavilion. Gung Gibang walked beside me, looking deeply displeased.
“I’ve been thinking about this, and I don’t think it’s a good idea.”
“Why?”
“This is bigger than I expected. And it isn’t just anyone—it’s the Taeeul Merciless Sword. At least you can reason with the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord, but that man...”
Gung Gibang couldn’t finish his sentence and shook his head repeatedly.
“Why? How bad is he? Have you met him before?”
“Once, while I was with my Master. That was enough to make me never want to see him again.”
Judging by Gung Gibang’s reaction, Hwangbo Eom must have made one hell of a first impression.
He shuddered with a disgusted expression, then gave me a sidelong glance.
“You don’t need to ask me. No one knows a household better than its neighbor.”
At the end of Gung Gibang’s gaze was Baek Museong, who had been walking silently without saying a word.
The face that usually wore a relaxed smile had long since hardened like stone.
Okay. I get the picture.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword.
As you spent time in the Murim, you started noticing a few interesting things. One of them was martial epithets.
An epithet contained a piece of the person it belonged to. Sometimes it told you what weapon they favored. Other times, it revealed their personality.
In Hwangbo Eom’s case, it did both.
Merciless. That word alone tells me more or less what I need to know.
I’d bet Hyuk Mujin’s wrist that he wasn’t some genial neighborhood grandpa who chuckled all day. If that wasn’t enough, I’d throw in his ankle too.
Gung Gibang spoke anxiously.
“It’s not too late to turn back.”
“Hm? Turn back from what?”
“Interfering in matters between sects is likely to cause trouble. Even more so when the other party is the Taeeul Merciless Sword of the Zhongnan Sect.”
“So?”
“What do you mean, ‘so’? I’m telling you to forget this nonsense and go to Sichuan!”
I blinked innocently.
“What the hell are you talking about?”
“Huh?”
“Who’s interfering? We’re just going to drink some tea. Isn’t that right, Cheongpung?”
Cheongpung, who was chewing the candied sweets I had bought to keep him quiet, answered enthusiastically.
“Yes! We’re going to drink tea!”
Gung Gibang stared at him incredulously.
“Didn’t you say earlier that you’d already had tea?”
“Uh... Well...”
No wonder his answer had sounded so evasive.
Cheongpung had already polished off the sweets in the blink of an eye. He sucked on his fingers and looked back and forth between Gung Gibang and me.
His eyes dripped with longing as they swept across a street stall overflowing with snacks.
“Cheongpung, you’ve never had tea before. Right?”
As I spoke, I spread one hand wide and waved it over Gung Gibang’s shoulder. Five more candied sweets were added to Cheongpung’s share, and he nodded eagerly.
“That’s right! I’ve never had tea before! My butt’s itching to get to the teahouse!”
“You heard him.”
His will to fight shattered, Gung Gibang tore at his matted hair.
“Damn it. If Master beats me with the Dog-Beating Staff later, I’m telling him this was all your fault.”
“Go ahead. My Master is the Fire King.”
“You miserable bastard. You’re worse than a dog.”
“Stop whining and keep walking. What about you, Mujin? Got a problem?”
Hyuk Mujin looked at me hopefully.
“Am I allowed to say so?”
“Sure. If you want to die.”
“All right. We’re almost there.”
The weathered signboard bearing the name Tengwang Pavilion drew steadily closer.
I strode onward until I finally stopped before the teahouse door.
Well, this is no joke.

The Taeeul Merciless Sword. The greatest swordsman Zhongnan could boast of. I could feel the aura of a Supreme Peak master beyond the door, along with the presence of dozens of people carrying considerable qi.
The pack frame on my shoulders suddenly felt heavier.
“Old Master, don’t worry. No matter what happens, I’ll protect you.”
“Nothing will happen,” I muttered softly, then threw open the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 319
paragraphs: “I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”
Ju Hwaran gave a crisp, formal clasped-hands salute.
The Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom, truly lived up to his reputation. Merely meeting his gaze made her chest tighten and left her struggling to breathe.
The First Sword of Zhongnan...
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families—the fifteen pillars supporting the Murim of today.
The man before her was the greatest master of the Zhongnan Sect, one of those fifteen powers. The immense weight of his name pressed down on her.
But it’s all right.
She had completed an escort mission everyone had agreed was impossible.
That was why she could stand tall even if the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord himself had come instead of the Taeeul Merciless Sword.
“Well? Did you bring the item I requested?”
“Of course.”

As she answered, Ju Hwaran took the wooden casket containing the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng from inside her robes. Straw rope was wound tightly around the entire casket, and a few small words had been written on its knot.
Shandong Seongsu Jang Family.
Hwangbo Eom checked the writing and nodded.
“No mistake. It bears the seal of the Seongsu Jang Family.”
People said that if Sichuan had the Tang Family, then Shandong had the Seongsu Jang Family.
That was how renowned the Seongsu Jang Family was for its medical arts. Unlike the Sichuan Tang Clan, a Murim great family, it was a prestigious medical family with its roots in medicine.
The Zhongnan Sect had purchased the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng through that very family and entrusted its transportation to the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
“The Pill Physician, the current Family Head of the Seongsu Jang Family, personally placed the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng inside and signed the casket.”
“Oh? The Pill Physician himself?”
“Yes. Several witnesses, myself included, watched the entire process.”
“You’re remarkably thorough for someone your age.”
Hwangbo Eom stroked his white beard with wrinkled fingers.
“This old man has heard that the Junzi Sword’s daughter is a gifted young woman. Thank you for handling such a difficult assignment so reliably.”
“Our Yongbong Escort Bureau does not tolerate even the slightest mistake on an escort mission.”
“That must be why you’re called the best in Shaanxi. Our sect operates an Escort Bureau as well, but it cannot compare with yours. Ha ha ha.”
Ju Hwaran’s heart pounded.
Was it because Hwangbo Eom had praised her?
No. It had nothing to do with his praise. Something else was constricting her chest, and she knew the name of that feeling.
Anxiety.
Something is wrong.
It was an intuition bordering on foresight. But before Ju Hwaran could even begin to trace its source, Hwangbo Eom spoke.
“Well, only the final procedure remains.”
They would inspect the requested item, then each leave their signature to certify that the handover was complete.
After a simple procedure that would take less than the time needed to drink a cup of tea, the four-month escort mission that had cost them so dearly would finally come to an end.
That was how it was supposed to happen.
...But would it really?
A chill unlike anything she had ever felt crept up her spine.
Hwangbo Eom’s voice pierced her frozen ears.
“What are you waiting for? Show me the item.”
Ju Hwaran slowly raised her head.
His voice was kind and gentle, yet the old man’s pitch-black eyes gleamed with a strange light.
She barely managed to force the words past her red lips.
“...Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“Open the casket. With your own hands.”
Ju Hwaran realized it then—the source of her anxiety, and that she had nowhere left to retreat.
In the end, only one choice remained.
Rustle.

Her slender, trembling fingers began to untie the knot. The wooden casket she had kept close to her heart for the past four months suddenly felt alien, as though she were seeing it for the first time.
No. No, that can’t be. I’m certain. There’s no way...
And then—
Click.
At last, the wooden casket opened, revealing what lay inside. A pure fragrance, straight roots, and a frost-covered, snow-white body.
It was unmistakably snow ginseng. Yet everyone who saw it held their breath, their eyes widening.
Hwangbo Eom’s gentle voice rang through the suffocating silence.
“How amusing.”
He crooked one wrinkled finger, releasing a powerful stream of internal energy.
The snow ginseng floated into the air through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space as he continued.
“A Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng... Is this old man seeing things because his strength has waned?”
It was obvious who the question was meant for.
Every gaze turned in the same direction. The horrified Chief Escort Heo Jun and Song Ilseom, who had been standing at a slant as though he weren’t there, were no exception.
At the end of those dozens of gazes stood Ju Hwaran, her face pale and her eyes closed.
It’s over.
The moment she saw the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng inside the casket, she had shut her eyes, unable to face the sight.
Something that could not and should not have happened had happened.
I saw it myself. I even kept it in my possession.
Where had everything gone wrong?
The past few months flashed through the darkness before her eyes like scenes from a dream.
She had staked the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s very survival on this mission.
The Zhongnan Sect had offered an enormous sum for completing it. But if they failed, the Bureau would have to pay ten times that amount as a penalty.
And now that double-edged sword had plunged into the hearts of both Ju Hwaran and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
“I won’t ask how this happened. I have no interest in whatever extraordinary circumstances caused the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng to turn into a Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng. However...”
Hwangbo Eom swept a look of feigned regret over Ju Hwaran and the other members of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
“We will have to receive compensation for this matter.”

“Our sect has already paid the Seongsu Jang Family one hundred thousand silver nyang for the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng. And if the Yongbong Escort Bureau successfully completed the mission, we agreed to pay an escort fee of ten thousand silver nyang—one-tenth of the cargo’s value.”
The value of the lost Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, plus the tenfold penalty the Yongbong Escort Bureau owed for failing to fulfill the contract.
Together, they amounted to the astronomical sum of two hundred thousand silver nyang. It was an amount they could cover only by selling off most of what the Yongbong Escort Bureau owned.
Blood ran from Ju Hwaran’s lips as the realization struck her, and Chief Escort Heo Jun’s face went black.
“G-Great Hero Hwangbo, that is...!”
“Two hundred thousand silver nyang. I will permit no compromise.”
The escorts who had accompanied Ju Hwaran groaned in despair.
Every one of them except Song Ilseom.
Though the Escort Bureau where he had worked for nearly ten years now faced a desperate crisis, he showed no reaction. Only the corner of his mouth twitched once.
Hwangbo Eom caught the movement out of the corner of his eye, then held out a full cup of tea to Ju Hwaran.
“Have a cup. When the mind is troubled, nothing is better than a warm cup of tea.”
Ju Hwaran’s long, tightly shut eyelashes trembled. Slowly, she opened her eyes and stared at Hwangbo Eom.
“Is this... Is this Zhongnan’s way?”
“I’m afraid I don’t know what you mean.”
Hwangbo Eom laughed softly and raised his own teacup to his lips.
As expected, the tea was astringent. The young owner who had inherited the teahouse from his family was still inexperienced.
And yet, for some reason, the aroma and flavor lingering in Hwangbo Eom’s mouth now were incomparable to what he had tasted a moment ago.
“Very good. I feel as though I’ve gone back thirty years.”
“What’s wrong? Drink before it gets cold.”
Ju Hwaran silently bit her lip.
She had been completely outmaneuvered. Even after taking every precaution, she had still fallen into the trap.

For the past two years, she had led the Escort Bureau in place of her father, the Junzi Sword, Ju Hogun. She had endured all kinds of mistakes and failures, both large and small, but never had she faced anything as hopeless as this.
Can I rise again like before?
She had stumbled before, but she had never stayed down. Yet two hundred thousand silver nyang was enough to crush the Yongbong Escort Bureau out of existence.
We can pay the penalty.
It was possible.

They would have to sell every field and parcel of land owned by the Yongbong Escort Bureau for a pittance, then send away the hundreds of caravan porters, escorts, and Escort Captains whose wages they could no longer afford.
And once that entire process was over, nothing would remain of the Yongbong Escort Bureau but an empty shell.
Is it really over? Just like this?
Hwangbo Eom watched Ju Hwaran with amusement.
He had long heard that the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau was quite capable.
But to him, she was still nothing more than a naive greenhorn.
Heh. How pitiful.
Just as Hwangbo Eom chuckled inwardly—
“Hmm?”
His gaze suddenly turned toward the door of the teahouse. Several people’s qi was drawing closer.
This is...
The qi was so powerful that even Hwangbo Eom, a Supreme Peak master, could not easily ignore it.
A vast reserve of internal energy comparable to that of an Elder from the Nine Sects and One Gang steadily approached, then stopped directly outside the teahouse.
Could it be Huashan?
Hwangbo Eom’s prediction was proven spectacularly wrong the next moment.
Creaaak.
“Oh, I was just in the mood for some tea, and look at that! A teahouse, right when I needed one.”
A broad-shouldered young man opened the door and strode in at the head of the group.
Hwangbo Eom’s eyes darkened as he looked at Jin Taekyung.
Even at a glance, it was an unusual sight.
Dozens of swordsmen stood throughout the room, and the air hung heavy.
Ju Hwaran—or rather, the Yongbong Escort Bureau?
The question had barely crossed my mind when I spotted them.
On top of a table surrounded by people, slender fingers trembled faintly.
I had only met her once, but I could tell who she was just from her fingers. Funny how that worked.
Were her hands pretty?
As I scratched the back of my head, everyone’s gaze flew toward me.
A middle-aged man who appeared to be the owner of the teahouse hurried over, bowing repeatedly.
“Sir, I’m sorry, but we’re completely full right now...”
“There’s a seat over there.”
“That seat isn’t in use.”
“Then I’ll drink standing up.”
At that moment, a martial artist who appeared to be a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect approached with measured steps.
“Are you a martial artist?”
“No, I’m fat.”
The martial artist looked me up and down as if he were staring at a complete lunatic.
“I don’t know who you are or where you come from, but an important person is here right now. You would do well to leave.”
“I’m an important son in my own family too, so why should I? There’s plenty of room anyway.”
“...You’re being troublesome. I am a Disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect. You should understand by now, so leave.”
“Why do you keep ordering me around? I just want to sit down and have some tea.”
Cheongpung, who had been fidgeting behind me, shouted excitedly.
“Benefactor! Candied sweets too!”
“Candied sweets? Hey, Mujin. Does this teahouse sell those too?”
“Are you seriously saying that right now?”
The Zhongnan Sect disciple looked at us as if to say, What the hell is wrong with these guys? Then he spotted someone, and his face stiffened.
“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”
Maybe it was because this was Huashan’s home ground, but quite a few people here recognized Baek Museong.
In any case, the Zhongnan Disciple’s involuntary shout had an immediate effect. Unlike when we first entered, everyone was looking at us now.
Two gazes stood out from the rest.
I waved at one of them.
“Oh, we meet again.”
“...Young Hero Jin?”
Ju Hwaran stared at me with her pale face and wide, round eyes.
Across from her sat an old man with a long white beard.
I gave Ju Hwaran a small smile, then gazed at the old man.
“Is there some problem between you and Young Lady Ju?”
The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—stroked his beard and laughed.
“An interesting fellow has appeared.”

chapters.title: Chapter 320
paragraphs: The old man had the bearing of an immortal. I had heard he was nearly eighty, yet as befitted a Supreme Peak master with profound internal energy, his clear, refined face bore not a single age spot, and his back was perfectly straight.
And then there were his eyes.
Their dark gleam was enough to make anyone uncomfortable the moment they met his gaze. The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—spoke.
“An interesting fellow has appeared.”
I met his stare and answered.
“I hear that pretty often.”
“You have plenty of nerve too.”
“That’s also true.”
The corners of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth rose.
“You must know who this old man is. Enough of your pointless wordplay.”
“Who are you?”
“What?”
“We’ve never met before. How am I supposed to know who you are or where you’re from? You have to introduce yourself. That’s basic etiquette.”
Startled gasps came from all around at my nonchalant reply.
“Y-Young Hero Jin.”
Ju Hwaran and the others from the Yongbong Escort Bureau gaped at me, while the Zhongnan Sect disciples, realizing what was happening, reached for their sword hilts as one.
“How dare you behave so insolently!”
“Show some respect at once!”
Hwangbo Eom raised a hand and calmed them.
Normally, this was the point when someone would start foaming at the mouth and check their blood pressure as it shot through the roof.
But Hwangbo Eom was clearly different.
“So that’s how it is.”
He studied me with a faint smile, then slowly turned his head.
His gaze passed over me, Cheongpung, and Hyuk Mujin before settling on the other two.
“You do not know this old man? The pillar of Huashan and the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect must have told you already. A joke carried too far becomes unpleasant.”
Baek Museong and Gung Gibang flinched, then stepped forward and offered clasped-hands salutes.
“I am Baek Museong, a humble junior of the Murim. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“I-I am Gung Gibang of the Beggars’ Sect...”
“Enough.”
Hwangbo Eom waved them off, his robe sleeve fluttering, and turned his gaze back to me.
“I believe I have indulged a child’s tantrum long enough. Is that still not enough for you?”
He really was no ordinary old man.
He was a completely different breed from his Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
Both his martial arts and his temperament were a cut above.
He’s a tricky one.
Still, this was more or less what I had expected.
Without letting my thoughts show, I shrugged calmly.
“No, that’s enough. Great Hero Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”
“You’re certainly bold. Why not claim you failed to recognize me?”
“Because it looks better to admit it cleanly.”
“Hahaha! What an insolent brat.”
Hwangbo Eom burst into hearty laughter. He sounded both intrigued by me and utterly dumbfounded.
The Zhongnan Sect disciples under his command, however, seemed to find the situation not merely absurd but insulting.
It would have been one thing if I genuinely had not known who he was.
But I had known and only pretended otherwise.
Hwangbo Eom’s standing within the Zhongnan Sect must have been too high for them to simply laugh it off.
“You bastard!”
Was it called the Taeeul Sword Unit?
It started when a middle-aged man who appeared to be the eldest of the Zhongnan Sect disciples shouted and drew his sword.
Clang-clang-clang!
Thirty well-maintained swords pointed toward me. As disciples of the Zhongnan Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, every one of them was at least a First Rate master.
Of course...
They’re hopelessly weak.
At this level, they posed no threat to me whatsoever.
First Rate? Peak? It made no difference.
In my eyes, they were nothing more than thirty men with swords.
I am strong.
Might Makes Right.
One of the absolute laws governing the Murim.
Before I knew it, I had become strong enough to remain at ease under that law. That was why I could stride forward without hesitation.
“Since fate brought us together, would you mind if I joined you?”
I addressed Hwangbo Eom, ignoring the thirty blades surrounding me. The middle-aged swordsman leading them flushed red.
“H-How dare you, you insolent bastard!”
“Bangjajeon is so damn good.”
“Taeeul Sword Unit, hear my command! Seize this bastard—”
That was when Hwangbo Eom, who had been silently watching me, finally spoke.
“Join us... Very well.”
Everyone stared at him in surprise.
“S-Senior Martial Uncle?”
“Put away your swords.”
“B-But that bastard—”
“Do you intend to defy this old man’s command?”
At his icy voice, the middle-aged swordsman bit his lip and lowered his sword.
As the weapons that had brightly illuminated the inside of the teahouse disappeared, nothing remained to block my way.
“Thank you. All that glare was getting hard on the eyes.”
Scrape. Thump.
I passed the people standing rigid with shock and dropped into the seat beside Ju Hwaran. Seeing how pale she was, I gave her a slight smile.
“Long time no—well, not really. It’s been two days. How have you been?”
“Young Hero Jin...”
“You don’t have to answer. I was only being polite. Honestly, Young Lady Ju, judging by your expression, you don’t look like you’ve been doing very well.”
“That’s not what I meant. How did you even—?”
“I happened to be passing by and stopped in by chance. Cheongpung here insisted on having a cup of tea. Of course, that was also a coincidence.”
Unlike Baek Museong, Gung Gibang, and Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung—whose duodenum was apparently made entirely of liver—sat down beside me without hesitation and pouted.
“Benefactor, when are the candied sweets coming?”
“Wait just a little longer. I’ll pile them into a whole mountain for you.”
“Wow! A mountain of sweets!”
Cheongpung looked ecstatic, as though a mountain of candied sweets had appeared right before his eyes.
Ju Hwaran, on the other hand, looked as though a mountain had collapsed on top of her.
Of course, most of that was probably because of Hwangbo Eom sitting across from her.
He looked back and forth between Cheongpung and me with an odd gleam in his eyes, then spoke.
“You have quite the nerve. Almost recklessly so.”
“It used to be small. But after going through one thing and another, it suddenly grew a lot.”
“This and that, you say. I suppose the Shaolin Bloodshed would do that.”
“Why so surprised?”
Hwangbo Eom curled his lips into a smile and continued.
“I have heard all about the rumor that the Fire King took a Hidden Dragon under his wing. I also heard that you left the Murim Alliance seven days and nights ago.”
What a slippery old man.
He had known from the start.
Unlike Ju Hwaran, who had merely guessed our identities two days ago, he already knew everything.
How?
This operation had been carried out quickly and in secret, yet he knew everything as if he could see the palm of his hand.
Did the Zhongnan Sect Leader, who should still be at the Murim Alliance, send a messenger pigeon?
Then could he also know about Old Master’s condition...?
Just as the thought crossed my mind, Hwangbo Eom’s gaze flicked toward the pack frame I had entrusted to Baek Museong before sitting down.
Then he casually tossed out a remark.
“Though I never expected the Fire King’s heir to be dressed like a leather merchant.”
Was he pretending not to know, or did he genuinely have no idea?
His expression gave nothing away.

Jeok Cheongang was currently in a state resembling suspended animation. His heartbeat, breathing, and every other bodily function had slowed to the extreme, making his presence extraordinarily difficult to detect.
It was similar to the Turtle Breath Technique Cheongpung had mentioned before.
And with all those hides piled over him, even a Supreme Peak master would have trouble noticing him.
Keeping him warm was not the only reason we had covered him with so many hides.
They concealed his appearance, muffled every sound, and hid his presence so no one would discover he was there.
“What is it?”
“Nothing. Anyway, I’m thirsty.”
I hurriedly redirected Hwangbo Eom’s attention. Without another word, he picked up the teapot and held a cup out to me.
“Take it.”
“Don’t mind if I do.”
Pour.
Hwangbo Eom was no pushover.
I felt the profound internal energy carried through the stream of tea and clicked my tongue inwardly.
So this is Zhongnan’s greatest master.
The tea fell in a slow, graceful arc, yet the force within it was heavy and powerful enough to shatter a boulder.
Still, it’s not as strong as Old Master’s.
Jeok Cheongang had a mischievous streak and had played all sorts of tricks on me. What Hwangbo Eom was doing now was no different.
I had broken more than one or two cups this way.
Besides, Jeok Cheongang stood foremost among the Ten Kings, an absolute master sometimes compared even to the Three Saints.
This much is nothing.
When I did not so much as blink, Hwangbo Eom’s eyebrow twitched. At the same time, the internal energy carried by the tea grew even stronger.
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“Hm?”
“The tea’s about to overflow.”
“You can stop pouring now.”
Just as I had said, the cup was already full. I lifted the perfectly smooth cup, not a single hairline crack on its surface, and emptied it in one gulp.
“Ahh. That hit the spot.”
“You seem fond of tea.”
“Not really. Anyway, allow me to pour you a cup this time.”
I reached out, and the teapot glided through the air into my hand.
It was the art martial artists called Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.

I possessed nearly two jiazi’s worth of internal energy and insight that had reached the brink of the Peak realm. I did not use the technique often because it consumed so much internal energy, but I could perform it whenever I wished.
I need to put on at least this much of a show.
Old Master had once said in passing:

“There are idiots everywhere in the Murim. You have to show those bastards something flashy before they’ll listen. Look at this old man. All I did was beat the Demonic Cult bastards because they pissed me off, and they still call me a king.”
King Cheongang indeed. Spoken like a man who had turned the Murim upside down by racking up a thousand kills all by himself.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space isn’t quite on that level, but it’s still an impressive technique.
Sure enough, the onlookers’ eyes widened.
“He used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space so easily...”
“Good heavens.”
Few people could use Seizing an Object Through Empty Space as casually as I had. Especially at my age.
But I did not stop there. I drew up my internal energy.
I circulated the Fire Gate Divine Technique to seven-tenths, and Extreme Yang energy seeped into both my hands.
Fwoosh!
Heat burst forth, and the tea inside the pot began to boil violently. I calmly filled Hwangbo Eom’s cup and said,
“The tea had gone a little cold. Since you’re going to drink it anyway, wouldn’t it be better warm? The weather has been cold lately, and the older you get, the more careful you have to be.”
Hwangbo Eom’s face stiffened.
Heating tea with internal energy would not have been particularly difficult for him either. There was a technique called Samadhi True Fire, after all.
But the Fire Gate Divine Technique was renowned as the greatest divine technique under heaven when it came to controlling Scorching Yang Qi.
No matter how powerful a Supreme Peak master Hwangbo Eom was, he could not match the Fire Gate Divine Technique.
And... No. It was too soon to jump to that conclusion.
I cut off the thought before it could go any further and offered him the cup.
“Please, drink.”
“Ahem.”
“Here comes the tea! Chug, chug, chug-chug!”
“...I shall drink it properly.”
“Look at my internal organs! I’ve suffered internal injuries!”
Hwangbo Eom glared at me, then drained the cup.
When he set it down, his gaze had changed considerably from when he had regarded me as a mere youngster.
“Your martial arts are quite impressive.”
I smiled and waved a hand.
“Oh, no. Not at all.”
“Do you intend to deceive this old man’s eyes?”
“No. I meant my martial arts aren’t merely ‘quite impressive.’ They’re extremely impressive.”
“Your arrogance knows no—”
“Oh, and for the record, my Master said that. The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. You know him, right?”
Now I was the only one smiling.
Not a trace of amusement remained on Hwangbo Eom’s face.
After a brief silence, he abruptly asked,
“What are you plotting?”
“Pardon?”
“Your insolence reaches the heavens. I have heard enough nonsense about this being a coincidence. Tell me the truth.”
“You’re refreshingly direct. In that case, sure.”
A faint smile touched my lips as I continued.
“I was just passing by when I happened to wonder what kind of dirty trick the Zhongnan Sect was trying to pull, so I came to take a look.”
At those words, the eyes of Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, turned cold.

sentences.text: The old man had the bearing of an immortal.
I had heard he was nearly eighty, yet as befitted a Supreme Peak master with profound internal energy, his clear, refined face bore not a single age spot, and his back was perfectly straight.
And then there were his eyes.
Their dark gleam was enough to make anyone uncomfortable the moment they met his gaze.
The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—spoke.
“An interesting fellow has appeared.”
I met his stare and answered.
“I hear that pretty often.”
“You have plenty of nerve too.”
“That’s also true.”
The corners of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth rose.
“You must know who this old man is.
Enough of your pointless wordplay.”
“Who are you?”
“What?”
“We’ve never met before.
How am I supposed to know who you are or where you’re from?
You have to introduce yourself.
That’s basic etiquette.”
Startled gasps came from all around at my nonchalant reply.
“Y-Young Hero Jin.”
Ju Hwaran and the others from the Yongbong Escort Bureau gaped at me, while the Zhongnan Sect disciples, realizing what was happening, reached for their sword hilts as one.
“How dare you behave so insolently!”
“Show some respect at once!”
Hwangbo Eom raised a hand and calmed them.
Normally, this was the point when someone would start foaming at the mouth and check their blood pressure as it shot through the roof.
But Hwangbo Eom was clearly different.
“So that’s how it is.”
He studied me with a faint smile, then slowly turned his head.
His gaze passed over me, Cheongpung, and Hyuk Mujin before settling on the other two.
“You do not know this old man?
The pillar of Huashan and the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect must have told you already.
A joke carried too far becomes unpleasant.”
Baek Museong and Gung Gibang flinched, then stepped forward and offered clasped-hands salutes.
“I am Baek Museong, a humble junior of the Murim.
I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“I-I am Gung Gibang of the Beggars’ Sect...”
“Enough.”
Hwangbo Eom waved them off, his robe sleeve fluttering, and turned his gaze back to me.
“I believe I have indulged a child’s tantrum long enough.
Is that still not enough for you?”
He really was no ordinary old man.
He was a completely different breed from his Senior Brother, the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
Both his martial arts and his temperament were a cut above.
He’s a tricky one.
Still, this was more or less what I had expected.
Without letting my thoughts show, I shrugged calmly.
“No, that’s enough.
Great Hero Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”
“You’re certainly bold.
Why not claim you failed to recognize me?”
“Because it looks better to admit it cleanly.”
“Hahaha!
What an insolent brat.”
Hwangbo Eom burst into hearty laughter.
He sounded both intrigued by me and utterly dumbfounded.
The Zhongnan Sect disciples under his command, however, seemed to find the situation not merely absurd but insulting.
It would have been one thing if I genuinely had not known who he was.
But I had known and only pretended otherwise.
Hwangbo Eom’s standing within the Zhongnan Sect must have been too high for them to simply laugh it off.
“You bastard!”
Was it called the Taeeul Sword Unit?
It started when a middle-aged man who appeared to be the eldest of the Zhongnan Sect disciples shouted and drew his sword.
Clang-clang-clang!
Thirty well-maintained swords pointed toward me.
As disciples of the Zhongnan Sect, one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, every one of them was at least a First Rate master.
Of course...
They’re hopelessly weak.
At this level, they posed no threat to me whatsoever.
First Rate?
Peak?
It made no difference.
In my eyes, they were nothing more than thirty men with swords.
I am strong.
Might Makes Right.
One of the absolute laws governing the Murim.
Before I knew it, I had become strong enough to remain at ease under that law.
That was why I could stride forward without hesitation.
“Since fate brought us together, would you mind if I joined you?”
I addressed Hwangbo Eom, ignoring the thirty blades surrounding me.
The middle-aged swordsman leading them flushed red.
“H-How dare you, you insolent bastard!”
“Bangjajeon is so damn good.”
“Taeeul Sword Unit, hear my command!
Seize this bastard—”
That was when Hwangbo Eom, who had been silently watching me, finally spoke.
“Join us...
Very well.”
Everyone stared at him in surprise.
“S-Senior Martial Uncle?”
“Put away your swords.”
“B-But that bastard—”
“Do you intend to defy this old man’s command?”
At his icy voice, the middle-aged swordsman bit his lip and lowered his sword.
As the weapons that had brightly illuminated the inside of the teahouse disappeared, nothing remained to block my way.
“Thank you.
All that glare was getting hard on the eyes.”
Scrape.
Thump.
I passed the people standing rigid with shock and dropped into the seat beside Ju Hwaran.
Seeing how pale she was, I gave her a slight smile.
“Long time no—well, not really.
It’s been two days.
How have you been?”
“Young Hero Jin...”
“You don’t have to answer.
I was only being polite.
Honestly, Young Lady Ju, judging by your expression, you don’t look like you’ve been doing very well.”
“That’s not what I meant.
How did you even—?”
“I happened to be passing by and stopped in by chance.
Cheongpung here insisted on having a cup of tea.
Of course, that was also a coincidence.”
Unlike Baek Museong, Gung Gibang, and Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung—whose duodenum was apparently made entirely of liver—sat down beside me without hesitation and pouted.
“Benefactor, when are the candied sweets coming?”
“Wait just a little longer.
I’ll pile them into a whole mountain for you.”
“Wow!
A mountain of sweets!”
Cheongpung looked ecstatic, as though a mountain of candied sweets had appeared right before his eyes.
Ju Hwaran, on the other hand, looked as though a mountain had collapsed on top of her.
Of course, most of that was probably because of Hwangbo Eom sitting across from her.
He looked back and forth between Cheongpung and me with an odd gleam in his eyes, then spoke.
“You have quite the nerve.
Almost recklessly so.”
“It used to be small.
But after going through one thing and another, it suddenly grew a lot.”
“This and that, you say.
I suppose the Shaolin Bloodshed would do that.”
“Why so surprised?”
Hwangbo Eom curled his lips into a smile and continued.
“I have heard all about the rumor that the Fire King took a Hidden Dragon under his wing.
I also heard that you left the Murim Alliance seven days and nights ago.”
What a slippery old man.
He had known from the start.
Unlike Ju Hwaran, who had merely guessed our identities two days ago, he already knew everything.
How?
This operation had been carried out quickly and in secret, yet he knew everything as if he could see the palm of his hand.
Did the Zhongnan Sect Leader, who should still be at the Murim Alliance, send a messenger pigeon?
Then could he also know about Old Master’s condition...?
Just as the thought crossed my mind, Hwangbo Eom’s gaze flicked toward the pack frame I had entrusted to Baek Museong before sitting down.
Then he casually tossed out a remark.
“Though I never expected the Fire King’s heir to be dressed like a leather merchant.”
Was he pretending not to know, or did he genuinely have no idea?
His expression gave nothing away.
Jeok Cheongang was currently in a state resembling suspended animation.
His heartbeat, breathing, and every other bodily function had slowed to the extreme, making his presence extraordinarily difficult to detect.
It was similar to the Turtle Breath Technique Cheongpung had mentioned before.
And with all those hides piled over him, even a Supreme Peak master would have trouble noticing him.
Keeping him warm was not the only reason we had covered him with so many hides.
They concealed his appearance, muffled every sound, and hid his presence so no one would discover he was there.
“What is it?”
“Nothing.
Anyway, I’m thirsty.”
I hurriedly redirected Hwangbo Eom’s attention.
Without another word, he picked up the teapot and held a cup out to me.
“Take it.”
“Don’t mind if I do.”
Pour.
Hwangbo Eom was no pushover.
I felt the profound internal energy carried through the stream of tea and clicked my tongue inwardly.
So this is Zhongnan’s greatest master.
The tea fell in a slow, graceful arc, yet the force within it was heavy and powerful enough to shatter a boulder.
Still, it’s not as strong as Old Master’s.
Jeok Cheongang had a mischievous streak and had played all sorts of tricks on me.
What Hwangbo Eom was doing now was no different.
I had broken more than one or two cups this way.
Besides, Jeok Cheongang stood foremost among the Ten Kings, an absolute master sometimes compared even to the Three Saints.
This much is nothing.
When I did not so much as blink, Hwangbo Eom’s eyebrow twitched.
At the same time, the internal energy carried by the tea grew even stronger.
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“Hm?”

I lifted the perfectly smooth cup, not a single hairline crack on its surface, and emptied it in one gulp.

That hit the spot.”
