chapters.title: Chapter 321
paragraphs: “What... did you just say?”
Hwangbo Eom’s voice was stretched so taut it seemed ready to snap.
The snow-white beard that had made him look like an immortal bristled, and his eyes hardened as he stared at me.
I answered with a mild smile.
“Didn’t I just tell you? I came to see what kind of dirty trick you were pulling. By. Chance.”
At that moment, blue sparks flew from Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.
“Hah!”
With his thunderous roar, an immense wave of qi erupted from him.
The aura of a Supreme Peak master made the table—or rather, the ground itself—pitch like a ship caught in a storm.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The violent tremors threw the entire teahouse into chaos. Dozens of pieces of teaware shattered with a deafening crash, spraying tea in every direction.
The proprietor, who had been nervously watching from a corner, let out a shriek and collapsed to the floor.
I instantly raised my sleeve to shield Ju Hwaran’s face from the flying tea, then clicked my tongue.
“Someone your age shouldn’t be causing a scene in another person’s shop. Not with other people around.”
“How dare you...”
The pressure radiating from Hwangbo Eom intensified.

This was the aura of none other than The First Sword of Zhongnan. Even the swordsmen of the Taeeul Sword Unit arrayed around him like guards flinched as though burned and stumbled backward. The members of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, Ju Hwaran included, went deathly pale.
“Hngh!”
“Gasp!”
No matter how talented a young prodigy might be, the gulf between them and Hwangbo Eom was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
Baek Museong, known as a pillar of Huashan, and Gung Gibang, Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect and its hundred thousand members, fared little better than Ju Hwaran.
Even counting everyone present, only about three people still looked unaffected.
One was me, of course.
“Benefactor, when are the candied sweets coming out?”
Another was Cheongpung, who cared only about his candied sweets, to hell with the Taeeul Merciless Sword or anything else.
And the last was...
“Hmm.”
Song Ilseom, the fierce-eyed escort.
He gave a quiet grunt under the weight of Hwangbo Eom’s aura. When our eyes met, he frowned and turned away.
I don’t like you either, asshole.
From the moment I first saw him, Song Ilseom had stunk of something suspicious in more ways than one.
It would not take long to find out whether that impression of mine was mistaken or based on fact.
“Maybe it’s because no one opened a window, but the air feels awfully stuffy.”
I spoke calmly and drew up my internal energy. The hundred years of internal energy coiled within my dantian spread between the tables like an invisible curtain.
Freed from the crushing pressure, Ju Hwaran finally released the breath she had been holding.
“Young Lady Ju, are you all right?”
“Yes, yes.”
Still gasping, Ju Hwaran clutched my sleeve.
“Thank you, Young Hero Jin. But this...”
“Enough.”
A single word from Hwangbo Eom cut her off.
The immortal had transformed into a Fiend. He glared at me, his gaze brimming with killing intent.
“The arrogance of a young whelp like you pierces the heavens.”
“I’m pretty good at piercing things. I use a spear.”
“Do you even understand what you’re doing?”
“Of course.”
I leaned lazily against the hard back of my chair and continued.
“I’m rescuing innocent people who fell into a trap someone laid for them. Purely because I happened to be passing by, of course.”
“A trap. I presume that ‘someone’ refers to our sect.”
“Well, you’re free to think whatever you like.”
The fury in Hwangbo Eom’s eyes subsided. In its place, an unmistakable sneer spread across his lips.
“You seem unaware that a man must answer for his words.”
“Judging by the fact that I came here, I’d say I’m well aware of that.”
“Boy, you have insulted the Great Zhongnan Sect with baseless accusations you cannot prove. Do you wish to make us your enemy?”
“It’s funny to hear orthodox Murim companions talk about friend and foe. Are you perhaps from an unorthodox faction?”
“You insolent whelp!”
“I already heard what happened between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and your sect. That’s why I came.”
I picked up the snow ginseng rolling across the table.
The thing in my hand was certainly an excellent elixir. Yet the name displayed through Item Appraisal had not changed.
Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.
I already knew that the item Zhongnan Sect had commissioned the Yongbong Escort Bureau to transport was Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.
It was a peerless elixir said to grant a full jiazi of internal energy instantly upon consumption.
Murim practitioners would risk their lives to possess such a rare treasure, and its value was whatever price the seller cared to name.
According to the information Gung Gibang had gathered, the Yongbong Escort Bureau had staked its survival on this escort mission.
Unless Ju Hwaran was a complete fool, there was no way she would have thrown such precious cargo into a wagon and left it unattended.
Then where had the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng gone? And why had it been replaced with Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, an elixir far inferior to it?
It was obvious.
It could only mean that either the Zhongnan Sect or Hwangbo Eom personally had meddled with it.
On top of that, the Zhongnan Sect had been deeply involved in the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s decline for the past two years.
The Xi’an branch of the Beggars’ Sect, whose information network was said to rival the Lower District Sect’s for the finest under heaven, had already pieced together most of what had happened.
This was supposed to be the finishing blow.
The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was the final strike meant to bring down the cornered Yongbong Escort Bureau.
They had dangled bait too tempting to resist, then dug an inescapable trap beneath it. The result was unfolding before my eyes.
But...
“You know, living in this world has taught me something. Even when everything looks finished, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw the whole thing into disarray.”
Hwangbo Eom regarded my muttering with contempt.
“A brat who still reeks of his mother’s milk does nothing but wag his tongue. Has becoming the Fire King’s Disciple blinded you to your place, you country bumpkin from Shanxi?”
“I’m still young, so there’s no need to worry about my eyesight. You’re the one who should be concerned about failing vision, Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“How should I tear apart that wicked mouth of yours?”

“I don’t know whether my mouth is wicked, but I do know Zhongnan’s specialty. You can’t utter a word when someone stronger than you shows up. Was it a year ago? Your Senior Brother gave me an advance lesson.”
I still remembered it clearly.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had invoked Zhongnan’s name to pressure the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I even remembered the sight of him being driven away without managing a single proper word after the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, appeared.
I pressed my lips together and looked at Hyuk Sopyung, who sat beside Hwangbo Eom.
“And yesterday, I had a review session.”
Hwangbo Eom was a perceptive old man.
Realizing what had happened, he clicked his tongue and muttered, “...Our sect is crawling with worms.”
“Still, aren’t harmful pests better than venomous insects? From my point of view, getting drunk and causing a scene is much more exemplary than ruining a perfectly good escort bureau.”
“You dare call this old man venomous? Hah. Hahaha!”
Contrary to my expectations, I could no longer sense the slightest agitation from Hwangbo Eom.
He looked down on everyone present, myself included, like a hawk high above that was ready to swoop down and seize its prey.
“Boy, do you understand what it means to make an enemy of the Great Zhongnan Sect—and of this old man?”
His wrinkled hand pressed against the table. The spilled tea slowly rose, took the form of an arrow, and pointed straight between my brows.
“If this old man so much as wishes it, today will be the day of your funeral.”
That’s what you think.
I opened my mouth.
“Well, from either your perspective or mine, that doesn’t sound like a particularly good choice.”

“That is why you remain alive. This old man will personally punish you for today’s offense in due time. If you do not wish to die like a dog, withdraw. This is a matter between our sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
Just as I was about to respond, a hand tugged at my sleeve.
At the same time, a trembling woman’s voice, carried on internal energy, pierced my ears.
—Young Hero Jin...
Two days ago, Ju Hwaran’s eyes had been clear and spotless. Now they swirled with conflicting emotions.
Fear and anger at what was happening. Relief at my arrival, and worry for my safety.
I knew exactly what she was thinking and what she wanted to say.

—I’m grateful that you’re thinking of us, but he’s right. This is an affair between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect. If you get involved any further, you’ll put yourself in danger as well.
Looking into Ju Hwaran’s eyes suddenly brought back a memory from a year ago.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had threatened to seal the gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan for an absurd reason. What would have happened that day if Jeok Cheongang had not appeared?
Orthodox faction? What a load of fucking bullshit.
The righteousness of the powerful was not the same as the righteousness of the weak.
I did not believe everyone in the orthodox Murim was evil. At the same time, I did not believe they were all good.
Even Shaolin Temple surely had people with wicked hearts, and I believed there were good people even within the Demonic Cult, that supposed den of fiends and monsters.
Orthodox, unorthodox, demonic. Good and evil existed in all three.
It isn’t about the sect. It’s about the person.
In the end, the individual was what mattered. And the old man before me was one of the biggest fucking bastards under heaven.
I took a deep breath, then spoke to Ju Hwaran aloud rather than using Sound Transmission.
“Young Lady Ju.”
“Y-Young Hero Jin?”

“You’re right. This is an affair between the Zhongnan Sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau. If I stick my nose into it, all I’ll get is a loss. No matter how powerful the Jin Family of Taiyuan is, we’re still nowhere near enough to stand before the name of the Zhongnan Sect.”
Ju Hwaran’s eyelids fluttered with surprise, then lowered.
I could feel her sinking into resignation.
But I was not finished.
“I kept thinking the same thing on the way here. Wondering whether this was really the right choice, or whether I should pretend I knew nothing and keep walking.”
“Young Hero Jin, you can stop. Please, that’s enough.”
“No.”
I shook my head.
“At first, I thought I was doing this because your face kept coming to mind. But...”
I turned and found Hwangbo Eom watching me with an amused smile.
The Zhongnan Sect was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and Hwangbo Eom was its elder and most powerful martial artist.
His martial arts were higher and his personality more meticulous, but Hwangbo Eom was still the same kind of person as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
I stared straight at this second Roaring Fury Swordsman and opened my mouth.
“It felt like fucking bullshit.”
Even without seeing it, I could feel the energy in the room stirring.
I continued with a sigh.

“‘Upright.’ That’s why you’re called the orthodox faction. But there’s nothing upright about this, is there? If you’re going to act like this, use the jeong from Choco Pie instead. Why the fuck would you use the jeong that means ‘upright’?”
Never once in my life had I thought of myself as a good person.
I had become a Hunter for money, and in the Murim, I had even considered abandoning someone to save my own life.
I was a murky gray. Nothing more, nothing less.
Yet now, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
“Maybe I was pretty white after all. Why else would I go this far?”
“You insolent little—!”
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”
I smiled at Hwangbo Eom as he prepared to roar.
“I told you earlier, didn’t I? Even when everything seems over, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw it all into disarray.”
I slowly reached out and tapped the empty air.
No one else could see it, but I could.
Hwangbo Eom’s dominoes were tumbling one after another.
“I’m not even your grandson, Great Hero Hwangbo. Why else would I spend this long talking to an eighty-year-old grandfather?”
For an instant, Hwangbo Eom looked dumbfounded. Then his face twisted violently.
He had sensed it too—the presences of several people rapidly approaching the teahouse.
“You bastard. What the hell are you plotting?”
“You’re the one who pulled a trick. I...”
I turned my head and finished.
“I made a plan.”
That was the moment the teahouse’s doors opened and about a dozen people came streaming inside.
First came five beggars carrying a mountain of bamboo slips in their arms. They were the Xi’an Branch Leader of the Beggars’ Sect and his subordinates.
At the head of the other group stood a woman I knew well.
“Congratulations on your promotion. It’s been a while.”
“Oh, my Young Master. A congratulatory greeting after an entire year? How prompt of you.”
Wolhwa, Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi branch, playfully arched one pretty eyebrow.

sentences.text: “What... did you just say?”
Hwangbo Eom’s voice was stretched so taut it seemed ready to snap.
The snow-white beard that had made him look like an immortal bristled, and his eyes hardened as he stared at me.
I answered with a mild smile.
“Didn’t I just tell you?
I came to see what kind of dirty trick you were pulling.
By.
Chance.”
At that moment, blue sparks flew from Hwangbo Eom’s eyes.
“Hah!”
With his thunderous roar, an immense wave of qi erupted from him.
The aura of a Supreme Peak master made the table—or rather, the ground itself—pitch like a ship caught in a storm.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The violent tremors threw the entire teahouse into chaos.
Dozens of pieces of teaware shattered with a deafening crash, spraying tea in every direction.
The proprietor, who had been nervously watching from a corner, let out a shriek and collapsed to the floor.
I instantly raised my sleeve to shield Ju Hwaran’s face from the flying tea, then clicked my tongue.
“Someone your age shouldn’t be causing a scene in another person’s shop.
Not with other people around.”
“How dare you...”
The pressure radiating from Hwangbo Eom intensified.
This was the aura of none other than The First Sword of Zhongnan.
Even the swordsmen of the Taeeul Sword Unit arrayed around him like guards flinched as though burned and stumbled backward.
The members of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, Ju Hwaran included, went deathly pale.
“Hngh!”
“Gasp!”
No matter how talented a young prodigy might be, the gulf between them and Hwangbo Eom was as vast as the distance between heaven and earth.
Baek Museong, known as a pillar of Huashan, and Gung Gibang, Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect and its hundred thousand members, fared little better than Ju Hwaran.
Even counting everyone present, only about three people still looked unaffected.
One was me, of course.
“Benefactor, when are the candied sweets coming out?”
Another was Cheongpung, who cared only about his candied sweets, to hell with the Taeeul Merciless Sword or anything else.
And the last was...
“Hmm.”
Song Ilseom, the fierce-eyed escort.
He gave a quiet grunt under the weight of Hwangbo Eom’s aura.
When our eyes met, he frowned and turned away.
I don’t like you either, asshole.
From the moment I first saw him, Song Ilseom had stunk of something suspicious in more ways than one.
It would not take long to find out whether that impression of mine was mistaken or based on fact.
“Maybe it’s because no one opened a window, but the air feels awfully stuffy.”
I spoke calmly and drew up my internal energy.
The hundred years of internal energy coiled within my dantian spread between the tables like an invisible curtain.
Freed from the crushing pressure, Ju Hwaran finally released the breath she had been holding.
“Young Lady Ju, are you all right?”
“Yes, yes.”
Still gasping, Ju Hwaran clutched my sleeve.
“Thank you, Young Hero Jin.
But this...”
“Enough.”
A single word from Hwangbo Eom cut her off.
The immortal had transformed into a Fiend.
He glared at me, his gaze brimming with killing intent.
“The arrogance of a young whelp like you pierces the heavens.”
“I’m pretty good at piercing things.
I use a spear.”
“Do you even understand what you’re doing?”
“Of course.”
I leaned lazily against the hard back of my chair and continued.
“I’m rescuing innocent people who fell into a trap someone laid for them.
Purely because I happened to be passing by, of course.”
“A trap.
I presume that ‘someone’ refers to our sect.”
“Well, you’re free to think whatever you like.”
The fury in Hwangbo Eom’s eyes subsided.
In its place, an unmistakable sneer spread across his lips.
“You seem unaware that a man must answer for his words.”
“Judging by the fact that I came here, I’d say I’m well aware of that.”
“Boy, you have insulted the Great Zhongnan Sect with baseless accusations you cannot prove.
Do you wish to make us your enemy?”
“It’s funny to hear orthodox Murim companions talk about friend and foe.
Are you perhaps from an unorthodox faction?”
“You insolent whelp!”
“I already heard what happened between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and your sect.
That’s why I came.”
I picked up the snow ginseng rolling across the table.
The thing in my hand was certainly an excellent elixir.
Yet the name displayed through Item Appraisal had not changed.
Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.
I already knew that the item Zhongnan Sect had commissioned the Yongbong Escort Bureau to transport was Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.
It was a peerless elixir said to grant a full jiazi of internal energy instantly upon consumption.
Murim practitioners would risk their lives to possess such a rare treasure, and its value was whatever price the seller cared to name.
According to the information Gung Gibang had gathered, the Yongbong Escort Bureau had staked its survival on this escort mission.
Unless Ju Hwaran was a complete fool, there was no way she would have thrown such precious cargo into a wagon and left it unattended.
Then where had the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng gone?
And why had it been replaced with Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, an elixir far inferior to it?
It was obvious.
It could only mean that either the Zhongnan Sect or Hwangbo Eom personally had meddled with it.
On top of that, the Zhongnan Sect had been deeply involved in the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s decline for the past two years.
The Xi’an branch of the Beggars’ Sect, whose information network was said to rival the Lower District Sect’s for the finest under heaven, had already pieced together most of what had happened.
This was supposed to be the finishing blow.
The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was the final strike meant to bring down the cornered Yongbong Escort Bureau.
They had dangled bait too tempting to resist, then dug an inescapable trap beneath it.
The result was unfolding before my eyes.
But...
“You know, living in this world has taught me something.
Even when everything looks finished, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw the whole thing into disarray.”
Hwangbo Eom regarded my muttering with contempt.
“A brat who still reeks of his mother’s milk does nothing but wag his tongue.
Has becoming the Fire King’s Disciple blinded you to your place, you country bumpkin from Shanxi?”
“I’m still young, so there’s no need to worry about my eyesight.
You’re the one who should be concerned about failing vision, Great Hero Hwangbo.”
“How should I tear apart that wicked mouth of yours?”
“I don’t know whether my mouth is wicked, but I do know Zhongnan’s specialty.
You can’t utter a word when someone stronger than you shows up.
Was it a year ago?
Your Senior Brother gave me an advance lesson.”
I still remembered it clearly.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had invoked Zhongnan’s name to pressure the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I even remembered the sight of him being driven away without managing a single proper word after the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, appeared.
I pressed my lips together and looked at Hyuk Sopyung, who sat beside Hwangbo Eom.
“And yesterday, I had a review session.”
Hwangbo Eom was a perceptive old man.
Realizing what had happened, he clicked his tongue and muttered, “...Our sect is crawling with worms.”
“Still, aren’t harmful pests better than venomous insects?
From my point of view, getting drunk and causing a scene is much more exemplary than ruining a perfectly good escort bureau.”
“You dare call this old man venomous?
Hah.
Hahaha!”
Contrary to my expectations, I could no longer sense the slightest agitation from Hwangbo Eom.
He looked down on everyone present, myself included, like a hawk high above that was ready to swoop down and seize its prey.
“Boy, do you understand what it means to make an enemy of the Great Zhongnan Sect—and of this old man?”
His wrinkled hand pressed against the table.
The spilled tea slowly rose, took the form of an arrow, and pointed straight between my brows.
“If this old man so much as wishes it, today will be the day of your funeral.”
That’s what you think.
I opened my mouth.
“Well, from either your perspective or mine, that doesn’t sound like a particularly good choice.”
“That is why you remain alive.
This old man will personally punish you for today’s offense in due time.
If you do not wish to die like a dog, withdraw.
This is a matter between our sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
Just as I was about to respond, a hand tugged at my sleeve.
At the same time, a trembling woman’s voice, carried on internal energy, pierced my ears.
—Young Hero Jin...
Two days ago, Ju Hwaran’s eyes had been clear and spotless.
Now they swirled with conflicting emotions.
Fear and anger at what was happening.
Relief at my arrival, and worry for my safety.
I knew exactly what she was thinking and what she wanted to say.
—I’m grateful that you’re thinking of us, but he’s right.
This is an affair between the Yongbong Escort Bureau and the Zhongnan Sect.
If you get involved any further, you’ll put yourself in danger as well.
Looking into Ju Hwaran’s eyes suddenly brought back a memory from a year ago.
The Roaring Fury Swordsman had threatened to seal the gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan for an absurd reason.
What would have happened that day if Jeok Cheongang had not appeared?
Orthodox faction?
What a load of fucking bullshit.
The righteousness of the powerful was not the same as the righteousness of the weak.
I did not believe everyone in the orthodox Murim was evil.
At the same time, I did not believe they were all good.
Even Shaolin Temple surely had people with wicked hearts, and I believed there were good people even within the Demonic Cult, that supposed den of fiends and monsters.
Orthodox, unorthodox, demonic.
Good and evil existed in all three.
It isn’t about the sect.
It’s about the person.
In the end, the individual was what mattered.
And the old man before me was one of the biggest fucking bastards under heaven.
I took a deep breath, then spoke to Ju Hwaran aloud rather than using Sound Transmission.
“Young Lady Ju.”
“Y-Young Hero Jin?”
“You’re right.
This is an affair between the Zhongnan Sect and the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
If I stick my nose into it, all I’ll get is a loss.
No matter how powerful the Jin Family of Taiyuan is, we’re still nowhere near enough to stand before the name of the Zhongnan Sect.”
Ju Hwaran’s eyelids fluttered with surprise, then lowered.
I could feel her sinking into resignation.
But I was not finished.
“I kept thinking the same thing on the way here.
Wondering whether this was really the right choice, or whether I should pretend I knew nothing and keep walking.”
“Young Hero Jin, you can stop.
Please, that’s enough.”
“No.”
I shook my head.
“At first, I thought I was doing this because your face kept coming to mind.
But...”
I turned and found Hwangbo Eom watching me with an amused smile.
The Zhongnan Sect was one of the Nine Sects and One Gang, and Hwangbo Eom was its elder and most powerful martial artist.
His martial arts were higher and his personality more meticulous, but Hwangbo Eom was still the same kind of person as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
I stared straight at this second Roaring Fury Swordsman and opened my mouth.
“It felt like fucking bullshit.”
Even without seeing it, I could feel the energy in the room stirring.
I continued with a sigh.
“‘Upright.’ That’s why you’re called the orthodox faction.
But there’s nothing upright about this, is there?
If you’re going to act like this, use the jeong from Choco Pie instead.
Why the fuck would you use the jeong that means ‘upright’?”
Never once in my life had I thought of myself as a good person.
I had become a Hunter for money, and in the Murim, I had even considered abandoning someone to save my own life.
I was a murky gray.
Nothing more, nothing less.
Yet now, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
“Maybe I was pretty white after all.
Why else would I go this far?”
“You insolent little—!”
“Great Hero Hwangbo.”
I smiled at Hwangbo Eom as he prepared to roar.
“I told you earlier, didn’t I?
Even when everything seems over, something unexpected can suddenly pop up and throw it all into disarray.”
I slowly reached out and tapped the empty air.
No one else could see it, but I could.
Hwangbo Eom’s dominoes were tumbling one after another.
“I’m not even your grandson, Great Hero Hwangbo.
Why else would I spend this long talking to an eighty-year-old grandfather?”
For an instant, Hwangbo Eom looked dumbfounded.
Then his face twisted violently.
He had sensed it too—the presences of several people rapidly approaching the teahouse.
“You bastard.
What the hell are you plotting?”
“You’re the one who pulled a trick.
I turned my head and finished.
“I made a plan.”
That was the moment the teahouse’s doors opened and about a dozen people came streaming inside.
First came five beggars carrying a mountain of bamboo slips in their arms.
They were the Xi’an Branch Leader of the Beggars’ Sect and his subordinates.
At the head of the other group stood a woman I knew well.
“Congratulations on your promotion.
It’s been a while.”
“Oh, my Young Master.
A congratulatory greeting after an entire year?
How prompt of you.”
Wolhwa, Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi branch, playfully arched one pretty eyebrow.

chapters.title: Chapter 322
paragraphs: Wolhwa seemed even more beautiful than she had been a year ago.
Dressed in dazzling clothes and wearing an alluring smile, she approached with the grace of a peacock and placed a hand on my shoulder.
“Our Young Master Jin. You’ve gotten even more dashing since I last saw you.”
At least this part of her hadn’t changed.
I let out a quiet laugh and pushed her hand away.
“You haven’t changed a bit.”
“I’m hurt. After a whole year, is that all you have to say?”
“Hmm. I suppose you’ve gotten a little prettier, too.”
“It feels like I had to fish for that compliment myself, but... fine. You pass. Dropping everything and rushing over here was worth it after all.”
As Wolhwa flashed me one of her signature eye-smiles, a young beggar in shabby clothes approached from beside her with a sour expression.
The cord at his waist, marking him as a disciple of the Beggars’ Sect, was tied into three knots.
In other words, he was a three-knot Disciple.
“I’m the Heukgeol Beggar, head of the Beggars’ Sect’s Xi’an branch.”
“Yes, I’m from the Jin Family of Taiyuan—”
“I already know. You’re as strapping as I’d heard. With a face like that, you could easily earn dozens of silver nyang a day begging. Have you ever considered joining the Beggars’ Sect?”
“Well, forget it if you’re not interested. In any case, it seems someone who should be here is missing.”
Huff, huff.
Heukgeol Beggar blew hard through his nose as he looked around. The moment he spotted his target, he shouted.
“Gung Gibang! You son of a bitch!”
When did that bastard get over there?
Gung Gibang was already crouched beneath a table some distance away. He gave us an awkward smile.
“Oh, look. My old friend of twenty years, Big Nose, is here. What brings you here?”
“I told you not to call me Big Nose! And what brings me here? You miserable bastard! I warned you over and over to make sure this didn’t happen, but you went and did it anyway...!”
Heukgeol Beggar furiously shook the wooden slip in his hand.

Beneath the message telling him to gather the necessary information and come to Tengwang Pavilion, eight yellow hairs had been attached. They had apparently been plucked from some stray dog passing through the neighborhood.
Anyone else would have wondered what the hairs were supposed to mean, but according to Gung Gibang, they were the mark of an eight-knot disciple of the Beggars’ Sect.
In other words, the mark of the Successor Beggar.
“Ahem. I told you, I couldn’t help it.”
“Damn it. If the Law Beggar comes looking for you over this, remember that it’s all your fault.”
“Now, now. You have a lot to say for a mere three-knot Disciple. You should be attending to the Successor Beggar instead.”
“You’re no Successor Beggar. You’re a successor mutt.”
Despite his words, Heukgeol Beggar reached out and pulled away a chair so Gung Gibang could climb out more easily.
Judging from their conversation, the two had been close friends since their days as young beggars.
Even better. This should go smoothly.
For someone else, however, it would be very bad news.
I turned my head and found Hwangbo Eom’s face twisted with displeasure. The corners of my mouth rose of their own accord.
“If this is your first time meeting, you should at least exchange greetings. Both of them do very important work here in Shaanxi Province.”
The Zhongnan Sect could not compare to Huashan, but its position in Shaanxi Province was by no means insignificant.
There was no way Hwangbo Eom did not know the branch leaders of the Beggars’ Sect and the Lower District Sect. I had only added that last part to sour his mood.

Just as I had expected, Hwangbo Eom already knew who they were. He bit his lip. His fingers twitched as though he wanted nothing more than to draw the sword propped beside the table and start swinging.
Go ahead. Draw it.
But Hwangbo Eom was not nearly as easy to provoke as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
The sly old man’s eyes slowly turned cold.
“What the hell are you doing?”
The answer came from behind me.
“I know, right? My heart is already pounding with anticipation over what our Young Master Jin might do next.”
Hwangbo Eom glared sharply at Wolhwa, who had spoken without warning.
“This is not a matter for the Lower District Sect. I do not know why you came here, but... it would be best for you to withdraw now.”
“Great Hero Hwangbo, I’m sorry, but I don’t think I can do that.”
Wolhwa continued with a radiant smile.
“I’ve already accepted a commission. Of course, the client is Young Master Jin, standing right here. Isn’t that right?”
“Oh, absolutely. Did you receive the silver nyang retainer I sent through the attendant?”
“Of course I did. But one silver nyang is terribly stingy. I’ll collect a generous fee from you later, so be prepared.”
I had no idea how much she intended to fleece me for, but that was a problem for later.
Hwangbo Eom silently glared at Wolhwa and me as we chatted amiably. His next target was Heukgeol Beggar.
“And what does the Beggars’ Sect intend to do?”
“Great Hero Hwangbo, this is quite a predicament.”
Heukgeol Beggar scratched his lice-ridden head and bowed deeply.
“I’m sorry, but it’s not a matter I can do anything about.”
“Is that the will of the Beggars’ Sect?”
Heukgeol Beggar bent at the waist in alarm.
“What? Oh, heavens, no. How could a mere three-knot Disciple like me presume to speak for the Beggars’ Sect?”
“Then withdraw, unless you wish to make an enemy of our sect.”
“Well, the thing is, we have sect rules on our side, too. That might be difficult.”
“You call that an excuse?”
“It isn’t an excuse. It’s the truth. Isn’t that right? No, wouldn’t you say so, Successor Beggar?”
Gung Gibang avoided Hwangbo Eom’s gaze and nodded.
“Well, yes.”
“This old man went easy on you because you were a young prodigy of the Beggars’ Sect, but you’ve gone too far...”
Hwangbo Eom looked back and forth between the two, then shouted like a thunderclap.
“Enough excuses! Beggars’ Sect, will you get the hell out of here already?”
Boom!
With a furious roar, Hwangbo Eom slammed his palm into the center of the table.
A low rumble rolled through the room. Unable to withstand his profound internal energy, the table was punched clean through, leaving a hole shaped like his palm.
And then...
“Well now.”
“This is something.”
At that moment, the atmosphere around the bowing Gung Gibang and Heukgeol Beggar changed.
The two men looked at each other’s grime-covered faces and let out quiet laughs.
“Hey, Gibang. I guess we really are beggars. Even here, people treat us like beggars.”
“Tell me about it. I’m in a lousy mood today, too. Should we just call every beggar in Shaanxi Province?”
“As the branch leader, that’s my job. If we gathered only the ones in Xi’an, we’d still have about a thousand.”

“That’s not your call, three-knot. I’m an eight-knot—the one and only eight-knot disciple in the Beggars’ Sect! If the Successor Beggar calls, they’ll come running even from the neighboring province.”
“Shaanxi will become a den of beggars. At that point, wouldn’t it be looting rather than begging?”
“Now, now, what do you mean, looting? I hear there’s a great deal of food on Mount Zhongnan... While we’re at it, let’s wipe out every edible thing there.”
It wasn’t Alibaba and the Forty Thieves.
It was Gung Gibang and ten thousand beggars.
I already knew that the Beggars’ Sect was a great sect with a hundred thousand disciples, but hearing them talk about it made me want to piss myself.
At the very least, they’d be a swarm of locusts.

If ten thousand beggars swept over Mount Zhongnan, it would become a desert within a month. The complete annihilation of the mountain wildlife would be a given, and they would strip away every edible blade of grass and shred of bark.
“Y-you bastards, what kind of nonsense are you spouting...?”
Hwangbo Eom’s wrinkled hand trembled.
“Do you think this old man would stand by and watch such a thing happen? I will personally demand that the Gang Leader punish both of you!”
“Do as you wish. My Master will beat me within an inch of my life, but surely he won’t kill his only Disciple. However...”
Gung Gibang was no longer the man who had been inching backward, trying to escape. His voice had settled low, deeper than a swamp.

“As the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, I have issued an order to the Xi’an branch. And only two people under heaven can rescind an order from the Successor Beggar: the Dragon-Head Gang Leader, who commands our hundred thousand disciples, and the Law Beggar, who enforces the sect rules.”
“My Master, the Dragon-Head Gang Leader, has told me again and again: we may not have homes, but does that mean we have no pride? Great Hero Hwangbo, you have insulted a beggar’s pride.”
A veteran beggar, all right.
It wasn’t easy to look that cool and that pathetic at the same time, but he pulled it off effortlessly.
Maybe he really is good at begging.
With a voice brimming with tragic grandeur and words that made him sound utterly pitiable, Gung Gibang dominated the room before turning to Heukgeol Beggar.
“You brought everything I listed in the letter, right?”
“How could I fail to, when it was the Successor Beggar’s order?”
At Heukgeol Beggar’s gesture, the Beggars’ Sect disciples from the Xi’an branch who had been waiting behind him began neatly stacking the bamboo slips they had brought.
There were a full hundred of them.
But that was not all.
“What are you all waiting for? It’s time to get to work.”
At the sound of Wolhwa’s alluring voice, the Lower District Sect members who had been standing quietly nearby placed bundles of paper beside the bamboo slips.
There were nearly as many bundles as there were bamboo slips.
The sight before him made Hwangbo Eom’s face go rigid.
“Wh-what is all this?”
I gazed fondly at the bamboo slips and sheets of paper.
“Nothing comes to mind? For example... the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s unending run of bad luck over the past two years.”

“Let’s swim upstream like salmon and retrace the past. And while we’re at it, let’s find out how the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng that had been on its way here without a problem managed to vanish without a trace.”
The energies of two people thrashed with the vigor of salmon fighting upstream.
One was Hwangbo Eom, overwhelmed by confusion.
The other was Ju Hwaran.
Her luminous eyes, frozen cold without a trace of anger or excitement, turned toward Hwangbo Eom.
“So that’s what happened after all.”
“Did you know?”
“How could I not? I suspected it all along, but I had no choice but to let it happen.”
“Because we were up against one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.”
Her voice drifted weakly into the empty air.

For the past two years, the Zhongnan Sect had manipulated the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s failures from the shadows. Someone who did not know the circumstances might say that she had brought down the Escort Bureau in a mere two years, but that would be wrong.
The Yongbong Escort Bureau had already been a listing ship, and Ju Hwaran had become its captain before she was even twenty.
It was thanks to her ability that the bureau had held firm until now, despite the threat of the enormous monster known as the Zhongnan Sect.
But now... everything would be different.
“You’ve been through a lot.”
At my brief words, Ju Hwaran bit her lip tightly.
And what she chose was not tears, but a smile.
“Thank you, Young Hero Jin. But I’ll hear that after this escort mission is over.”
She was right.
Just as Ju Hwaran had said, the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s escort mission was not over yet.
I gave Heukgeol Beggar and Wolhwa a small nod.
“Let’s begin.”
Hwangbo Eom suddenly wondered.
What is happening?
Everything had been proceeding smoothly. He had taken each step carefully over the past two years, and all that remained was to bring it to a close.
There had been a time when he thought so.
He truly had.

“Last summer, the Yongbong Escort Bureau suffered a loss of one thousand silver nyang when its deal with the Geumo Merchant Guild fell through. A man named Hwang Cheolsim secretly intervened in the process. According to what our sect uncovered, he was a lay disciple of Zhongnan, and...”
The voices reaching Hwangbo Eom’s ears felt distant and unfamiliar.
Most of the information uncovered by the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect was true.
By cross-checking their findings, they had confirmed the facts more thoroughly and uncovered new incidents. One lead grew into the next without end, like the stem of a plant.
This is impossible.
Hwangbo Eom stood frozen like a statue, repeating the same thought over and over.
Then one person entered his field of vision.
The corners of his mouth were raised. His clear eyes seemed capable of seeing straight through the human heart.
Jin Taekyung was laughing at him.
It’s all that bastard’s fault. If only he hadn’t been there, if only...!
People said that Taeeul Merciless Sword Hwangbo Eom was different from his two martial brothers.
But they were wrong.
At this very moment, Hwangbo Eom’s mind was being bleached white by rage.
The cold, poisonous heart that had occupied that space was gone. In its place was something even worse—a murderous intent that filled him to the brim.
“You bastard—!”
Shiiing!
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
The scabbard flew into Hwangbo Eom’s grasp, and a silver line burst from it.

Despite his words, Heukgeol Beggar reached out and pulled away a chair so Gung Gibang could climb out more easily.
Judging from their conversation, the two had been close friends since their days as young beggars.
Even better.
This should go smoothly.
For someone else, however, it would be very bad news.
I turned my head and found Hwangbo Eom’s face twisted with displeasure.
The corners of my mouth rose of their own accord.
“If this is your first time meeting, you should at least exchange greetings.
Both of them do very important work here in Shaanxi Province.”
The Zhongnan Sect could not compare to Huashan, but its position in Shaanxi Province was by no means insignificant.
There was no way Hwangbo Eom did not know the branch leaders of the Beggars’ Sect and the Lower District Sect.
I had only added that last part to sour his mood.
Just as I had expected, Hwangbo Eom already knew who they were.
He bit his lip.
His fingers twitched as though he wanted nothing more than to draw the sword propped beside the table and start swinging.
Go ahead.
Draw it.
But Hwangbo Eom was not nearly as easy to provoke as the Roaring Fury Swordsman.
The sly old man’s eyes slowly turned cold.
“What the hell are you doing?”
The answer came from behind me.
“I know, right?
My heart is already pounding with anticipation over what our Young Master Jin might do next.”
Hwangbo Eom glared sharply at Wolhwa, who had spoken without warning.
“This is not a matter for the Lower District Sect.
I do not know why you came here, but... it would be best for you to withdraw now.”
“Great Hero Hwangbo, I’m sorry, but I don’t think I can do that.”
Wolhwa continued with a radiant smile.
“I’ve already accepted a commission.
Of course, the client is Young Master Jin, standing right here.
Isn’t that right?”
“Oh, absolutely.
Did you receive the silver nyang retainer I sent through the attendant?”
“Of course I did.
But one silver nyang is terribly stingy.
I’ll collect a generous fee from you later, so be prepared.”
I had no idea how much she intended to fleece me for, but that was a problem for later.
Hwangbo Eom silently glared at Wolhwa and me as we chatted amiably.
His next target was Heukgeol Beggar.
“And what does the Beggars’ Sect intend to do?”
“Great Hero Hwangbo, this is quite a predicament.”
Heukgeol Beggar scratched his lice-ridden head and bowed deeply.
“I’m sorry, but it’s not a matter I can do anything about.”
“Is that the will of the Beggars’ Sect?”
Heukgeol Beggar bent at the waist in alarm.
“What?
Oh, heavens, no.
How could a mere three-knot Disciple like me presume to speak for the Beggars’ Sect?”
“Then withdraw, unless you wish to make an enemy of our sect.”
“Well, the thing is, we have sect rules on our side, too.
That might be difficult.”
“You call that an excuse?”
“It isn’t an excuse.
It’s the truth.
Isn’t that right?
No, wouldn’t you say so, Successor Beggar?”
Gung Gibang avoided Hwangbo Eom’s gaze and nodded.
“Well, yes.”
“This old man went easy on you because you were a young prodigy of the Beggars’ Sect, but you’ve gone too far...”
Hwangbo Eom looked back and forth between the two, then shouted like a thunderclap.
“Enough excuses!
Beggars’ Sect, will you get the hell out of here already?”
Boom!
With a furious roar, Hwangbo Eom slammed his palm into the center of the table.
A low rumble rolled through the room.
Unable to withstand his profound internal energy, the table was punched clean through, leaving a hole shaped like his palm.
And then...
“Well now.”
“This is something.”
At that moment, the atmosphere around the bowing Gung Gibang and Heukgeol Beggar changed.
The two men looked at each other’s grime-covered faces and let out quiet laughs.
“Hey, Gibang.
I guess we really are beggars.
Even here, people treat us like beggars.”
“Tell me about it.
I’m in a lousy mood today, too.
Should we just call every beggar in Shaanxi Province?”
“As the branch leader, that’s my job.
If we gathered only the ones in Xi’an, we’d still have about a thousand.”
“That’s not your call, three-knot.
I’m an eight-knot—the one and only eight-knot disciple in the Beggars’ Sect!
If the Successor Beggar calls, they’ll come running even from the neighboring province.”
“Shaanxi will become a den of beggars.
At that point, wouldn’t it be looting rather than begging?”
“Now, now, what do you mean, looting?
I hear there’s a great deal of food on Mount Zhongnan...
While we’re at it, let’s wipe out every edible thing there.”
It wasn’t Alibaba and the Forty Thieves.
It was Gung Gibang and ten thousand beggars.
I already knew that the Beggars’ Sect was a great sect with a hundred thousand disciples, but hearing them talk about it made me want to piss myself.
At the very least, they’d be a swarm of locusts.
If ten thousand beggars swept over Mount Zhongnan, it would become a desert within a month.
The complete annihilation of the mountain wildlife would be a given, and they would strip away every edible blade of grass and shred of bark.
“Y-you bastards, what kind of nonsense are you spouting...?”
Hwangbo Eom’s wrinkled hand trembled.
“Do you think this old man would stand by and watch such a thing happen?
I will personally demand that the Gang Leader punish both of you!”
“Do as you wish.
My Master will beat me within an inch of my life, but surely he won’t kill his only Disciple.
However...”
Gung Gibang was no longer the man who had been inching backward, trying to escape.
His voice had settled low, deeper than a swamp.
“As the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, I have issued an order to the Xi’an branch.

And only two people under heaven can rescind an order from the Successor Beggar: the Dragon-Head Gang Leader, who commands our hundred thousand disciples, and the Law Beggar, who enforces the sect rules.”
“My Master, the Dragon-Head Gang Leader, has told me again and again: we may not have homes, but does that mean we have no pride?
Great Hero Hwangbo, you have insulted a beggar’s pride.”
A veteran beggar, all right.
It wasn’t easy to look that cool and that pathetic at the same time, but he pulled it off effortlessly.
Maybe he really is good at begging.
With a voice brimming with tragic grandeur and words that made him sound utterly pitiable, Gung Gibang dominated the room before turning to Heukgeol Beggar.
“You brought everything I listed in the letter, right?”
“How could I fail to, when it was the Successor Beggar’s order?”
At Heukgeol Beggar’s gesture, the Beggars’ Sect disciples from the Xi’an branch who had been waiting behind him began neatly stacking the bamboo slips they had brought.
There were a full hundred of them.
But that was not all.
“What are you all waiting for?
It’s time to get to work.”
At the sound of Wolhwa’s alluring voice, the Lower District Sect members who had been standing quietly nearby placed bundles of paper beside the bamboo slips.
There were nearly as many bundles as there were bamboo slips.
The sight before him made Hwangbo Eom’s face go rigid.
“Wh-what is all this?”
I gazed fondly at the bamboo slips and sheets of paper.
“Nothing comes to mind?
For example... the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s unending run of bad luck over the past two years.”
“Let’s swim upstream like salmon and retrace the past.
And while we’re at it, let’s find out how the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng that had been on its way here without a problem managed to vanish without a trace.”
The energies of two people thrashed with the vigor of salmon fighting upstream.
One was Hwangbo Eom, overwhelmed by confusion.
The other was Ju Hwaran.
Her luminous eyes, frozen cold without a trace of anger or excitement, turned toward Hwangbo Eom.
“So that’s what happened after all.”
“Did you know?”
“How could I not?
I suspected it all along, but I had no choice but to let it happen.”
“Because we were up against one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.”
Her voice drifted weakly into the empty air.
For the past two years, the Zhongnan Sect had manipulated the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s failures from the shadows.
Someone who did not know the circumstances might say that she had brought down the Escort Bureau in a mere two years, but that would be wrong.
The Yongbong Escort Bureau had already been a listing ship, and Ju Hwaran had become its captain before she was even twenty.
It was thanks to her ability that the bureau had held firm until now, despite the threat of the enormous monster known as the Zhongnan Sect.
But now... everything would be different.
“You’ve been through a lot.”
At my brief words, Ju Hwaran bit her lip tightly.
And what she chose was not tears, but a smile.
“Thank you, Young Hero Jin.
But I’ll hear that after this escort mission is over.”
She was right.
Just as Ju Hwaran had said, the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s escort mission was not over yet.
I gave Heukgeol Beggar and Wolhwa a small nod.
“Let’s begin.”
Hwangbo Eom suddenly wondered.
What is happening?
Everything had been proceeding smoothly.
He had taken each step carefully over the past two years, and all that remained was to bring it to a close.
There had been a time when he thought so.
He truly had.
“Last summer, the Yongbong Escort Bureau suffered a loss of one thousand silver nyang when its deal with the Geumo Merchant Guild fell through.
A man named Hwang Cheolsim secretly intervened in the process.
According to what our sect uncovered, he was a lay disciple of Zhongnan, and...”
The voices reaching Hwangbo Eom’s ears felt distant and unfamiliar.
Most of the information uncovered by the Lower District Sect and the Beggars’ Sect was true.
By cross-checking their findings, they had confirmed the facts more thoroughly and uncovered new incidents.
One lead grew into the next without end, like the stem of a plant.
This is impossible.
Hwangbo Eom stood frozen like a statue, repeating the same thought over and over.
Then one person entered his field of vision.
The corners of his mouth were raised.
His clear eyes seemed capable of seeing straight through the human heart.
Jin Taekyung was laughing at him.
It’s all that bastard’s fault.
If only he hadn’t been there, if only...!
People said that Taeeul Merciless Sword Hwangbo Eom was different from his two martial brothers.
But they were wrong.
At this very moment, Hwangbo Eom’s mind was being bleached white by rage.
The cold, poisonous heart that had occupied that space was gone.
In its place was something even worse—a murderous intent that filled him to the brim.
“You bastard—!”
Shiiing!
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
The scabbard flew into Hwangbo Eom’s grasp, and a silver line burst from it.

chapters.title: Chapter 323
paragraphs: It all happened in an instant.
The qi permeating the air surged, and the sword propped against the table flew into one man’s waiting hand.
And then...
Shuaaaak!
A dazzling streak of light filled my vision. The strike was impossibly fast and precise.
The blue qi crystallized around the blade and scattered a brilliant radiance. I already knew another name for that light.
Sword Force.
A power granted only to those who had stepped into the Supreme Peak realm. Stronger than anything else in the world, it was falling straight toward the crown of my head.
At this rate, I’ll die. No question about it.
But...
This isn’t nearly enough.
In a world slowed to a crawl, I moved—and the Sword Force split the air.
Shlick! Kraaash!
Everything was cleaved apart. The table, the chairs, even the floor of the teahouse that must have stood there for countless years.
The gale unleashed by the Sword Force swept through the room. Screams and thunderous crashes swallowed everything. Beyond them, I saw the old man’s eyes stretched wide.
“H-how did you...”
I gently pushed Ju Hwaran, whom I had pulled into my arms, to the side and answered.
“How did I dodge it? I saw it coming, so I dodged.”
“People say the Supreme Peak realm—and Sword Force—belong to a realm beyond humanity.”
Unconcealed shock spread across Hwangbo Eom’s wrinkled face.
“Th-then could it be that you...!”
“Who knows?”
I answered with a faint smile. By now, thunder must have been crashing through Hwangbo Eom’s head.
Of course, I had not gained the enlightenment required to reach the Supreme Peak realm.
To be precise, it wasn’t my martial arts but my physical abilities themselves that had reached a realm beyond humanity.
What should I even call this?
A Supreme Peak master—physically?
There was no doubt that I was a new kind of Supreme Peak master, one without precedent in the history of the Murim.
I shrugged.
“It’s nothing special. I tried it, and it worked.”
Hwangbo Eom shouted, his eyes bloodshot.
“I refuse to believe this! How can a brat like you have reached such a realm?”
“I find it hard to believe, too. Who swings a sword in a place like this? Are you out of your mind?”
“That...”
Hwangbo Eom’s eyes stiffened as they swept across the room.
Fortunately, his strike had been aimed precisely at me, so no one else had been injured. Even so, every face around us showed shock and fury.

“You went on about the orthodox faction and the Great Zhongnan Sect, but the second you lost your temper, you became no better than a fiend. Why not rename yourselves the Zhong-Bastard Sect while you’re at it?”
“You—!”
Hwangbo Eom’s hand trembled around the sword hilt. His conflicted gaze swept over the room before turning cold.
“Disciples of the Zhongnan Sect, heed my command.”
“Y-yes, Martial Uncle!”
The thirty members of the Taeeul Sword Unit, frozen like statues by the sudden turn of events, jolted back to their senses.
They hurriedly cupped their hands, and Hwangbo Eom’s command fell over their heads.
“Seal the entrances immediately. No one is to leave this place.”
“S-Senior Martial Uncle!”
“B-but...”
“What are you waiting for? Do you intend to disobey this old man’s command?”
As Hwangbo Eom’s roar left the Taeeul Sword Unit hesitating, a quiet voice pierced everyone’s ears.
“Yes. I do.”
Hwangbo Eom’s face filled with fury when he recognized the speaker.
“Hyuk Sopyung. How dare you...”
I knew the young man. Hyuk Sopyung, the Zhongnan One Dragon.
He stared at Hwangbo Eom with an indescribably complicated look in his eyes.
“Please stop. This is the first and last time I will beg you.”
“What did you say?”
“The way you’re acting right now, Senior Martial Uncle... Isn’t this beneath a disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect?”
“Shut your mouth!”
Kraaash!
Another gale swept through the room, and Hyuk Sopyung’s body slid backward.
But his gaze did not waver.
Hwangbo Eom looked back and forth between Hyuk Sopyung and the thirty hesitant members of the Taeeul Sword Unit, then bit down hard on his lip.
“You little...”
The next moment, he pulled a small copper tablet from inside his robes and threw it at Hyuk Sopyung’s feet.
“This is our sect’s Sect Leader’s Command Token, entrusted to this old man by your Master. Do you still intend to refuse?”
The Sect Leader’s Command Token was a powerful symbol of the authority held by the leader of a sect.
Hyuk Sopyung’s eyelids trembled when he recognized his Master’s copper tablet.
“Senior Martial Uncle, you truly haven’t changed.”
“Choose. Expulsion or obedience.”
“Expulsion...”
Hyuk Sopyung’s regretful gaze settled on Ju Hwaran and me.
Then he gave a bitter smile, prostrated himself before the copper tablet, and slammed his forehead against the floor.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
“Disciple Hyuk Sopyung obeys the Sect Leader’s Command Token!”
His cry sounded as if he were vomiting blood. Blood streamed down his split forehead.
Hyuk Sopyung rose with a blank expression, as if he felt no pain at all, and blocked the entrance to the teahouse. The thirty members of the Taeeul Sword Unit followed suit.
I clicked my tongue as I watched it all unfold.
“At this point, you haven’t just crossed the line—you erased it altogether. Are you sure you can deal with the consequences?”
Major figures from Huashan, the Beggars’ Sect, and the Lower District Sect were all gathered here. No matter how powerful the Zhongnan Sect was, the fallout from today would be fierce.
But Hwangbo Eom had already lost his mind. His eyes held nothing but rage.
“They will come to no harm. All except you.”
“Ah. So you’ll deal with me first and clean up afterward?”
“Yes. At last, I can tear that mouth of yours apart.”
“Why are you so desperate to tear it apart, old man? The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Fire Gate Clan aren’t exactly a pair of pushover nobodies.”
“The Fire Gate Clan?”
A sneer formed at the corner of Hwangbo Eom’s mouth.
The next moment, a line of Sound Transmission pierced my ear.
—The young tiger is in danger, yet the great tiger shows no sign of waking.
—Did you think this old man wouldn’t know, you foolish child? I already knew the Fire King’s illness was grave.
A secret known to only a handful of people had leaked out.
My face stiffened before I could stop it. Hwangbo Eom’s smile deepened when he saw my reaction.
—The Fire King Jeok Cheongang, and you. I have had more than enough of you both. This might be a good opportunity to settle my bad blood with the Fire Gate Clan once and for all.
Settle his bad blood?
Hwangbo Eom’s words left me momentarily dazed.
Does he mean what I think he means?
My tangled thoughts vanished in an instant. Only one remained.
“Sorry, but can I ask everyone for one favor?”
I could feel their gazes even without looking.
Baek Museong and Cheongpung. Gung Gibang and Heukgeol Beggar. Wolhwa and Hyuk Mujin. And finally, Ju Hwaran.
Everyone in the room was looking at me.
Then a voice so dry that I could hardly believe it belonged to me slipped between my lips.
“Block the entrance. Don’t let anyone get out.”
Hwangbo Eom had been the first to block the door, but I would be the one to decide when it opened and closed.
“Taeeul Merciless Sword Hwangbo Eom.”
I let out a quiet sigh. Extreme Yang qi boiled up from my dantian and flowed from me as white steam.
“You... said something you never should have.”
He should never have brought up Jeok Cheongang over something as trivial as this.
He truly shouldn’t have.
Starting now, he would pay the price for saying what should never have been said.
“Come at me, you fucking old bastard.”
In time split into smaller and smaller instants, Hwangbo Eom and I rushed toward each other.
Kraaaaaash!
Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.
A dense and powerful net of Sword Energy covered heaven and earth in every direction.
The sword forms came without pause, on a completely different level from those of the Roaring Fury Swordsman I had faced a year ago or Hyuk Sopyung the day before.
Shishishishishik!
They were blindingly fast and destructive. Even a glancing blow would split flesh and bone and bring death.
I can’t dodge this. There’s no way.
At least, it would have been true if I were the me from a year ago.
The saying wipe your eyes and look again came to mind—a phrase for progress so astonishing that you had to rub your eyes and take another look.
Even that fell short of describing me.
Through endless days of brutal training, I had grown stronger. No, it would not be wrong to call it evolution.
Heaven is truly heartless. How can someone like you even exist?
Jeok Cheongang’s face, filled with helpless disbelief, appeared over the net of Sword Energy.
I laughed quietly and swept my spear, White Flame, upward.
Shraaaak!
The Extreme Yang qi coating White Flame’s spearhead tore through the net.
A fish would have fled through the gap in the torn net, but I was no fish.
I was a shark.
The fisherman who had cast the net had clearly overlooked that fact.
The old fisherman’s wrinkled face filled with shock.
“You—!”
I did not answer.
I bent my knees and lowered my waist. The spear in my hand curved smoothly like a dragon’s tail.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Fwoooosh! Boom!
The blue-burning spear and sword collided. A deafening crash rang out as an immense shock wave erupted.
Had Hwangbo Eom been trying to conserve his strength?
If so, he had made a terrible mistake. No matter how severely it drained his internal energy, he should have used Sword Force.
“Hup!”
His eyes opened wide.
The old man staggered before my strength, which had entered the realm beyond humanity, and the innate ferocity of my martial art.
“Wh-what kind of martial art is this...?”
The founder of the Fire Gate Clan had been called the greatest martial artist under heaven in his era.
He created the Fire Gate Divine Technique and made it the root of the clan. The sixteen Sect Leaders who followed became different branches growing from that same root.
The Fire Dragon Divine Spear was no different.
Created by the fifth Sect Leader, the spear art was supremely destructive and fierce. Its movements truly resembled those of a fire dragon.
And...
This is only the beginning.
Whoooosh!
I held nothing back.
I thrust, slashed, swept, and struck.
Whenever the blue flames ran wild, thunderous crashes like the sky splitting apart shook heaven and earth.
After the tail come the claws.
No one under heaven had ever seen a dragon fight.
But while learning the Fire Dragon Divine Spear, I had found myself wondering.
If a fire dragon really swung its claws, wouldn’t it look exactly like this?
Gooooong.
Extreme Yang qi coiled around the tip of my spear.
The tea spilled across the floor during Hwangbo Eom’s earlier rampage had long since evaporated. The jade-colored tea set glowed red-hot, as if it were back inside the kiln where it had been fired.
Sensing that something was wrong, Hwangbo Eom shouted like a thunderbolt.
“You bastard!”
He was already nearing eighty.
But to someone who had entered the Supreme Peak realm, age was nothing more than a number.
His formidable internal energy and the Zhongnan Sect’s ultimate techniques, honed for more than a jiazi, poured down like beams of light.
Swoooosh!
If the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords were a net, this was a harpoon meant to finish its prey.
As his sword slashed toward my chest at incredible speed, scattering dozens of afterimages, one martial art flashed through my mind.
Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword.
One of the Zhongnan Sect’s most celebrated ultimate sword techniques.
Jeok Cheongang had described the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword as a sword art of extreme speed.
Then he had added one more thing.
Maybe this old man is going senile. Why do I get the feeling you’ll be faster than the sword?
If Jeok Cheongang woke up, I wanted to tell him he had been right.
And that the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts had shattered the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword.
Heavenly Strike.
The fire dragon swung its claws.
The strike descended from the sky, erasing the afterimages created by the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword as it fell like a bolt of lightning.
Kraaaaaash!
A pillar of hellfire erupted.
