A dead man could feel neither.
He would do anything if it meant surviving this place and seeing tomorrow’s sun.
“Urgh.
Hwaran...”
Heo Jun groaned in pain.
Ju Hwaran’s flexible sword had passed straight through his right shoulder, and the hand gripping its hilt trembled faintly.
“Then at least make an excuse.
Tell me why you did it.
Why you had no other choice.”
If excuses would have raised his chances of survival even slightly, Heo Jun would already have offered every one he could invent.
But he knew Ju Hwaran too well.
The fact that she had swung her sword meant she was already certain.
A clumsy excuse now would only hasten his death.
He had to beg without reservation and appeal subtly to her emotions.
“It was all this foolish uncle’s fault.
I have nothing else to say.”
Heo Jun let his head droop and reddened his eyes.
The effect was immediate.
He felt the strength behind her sword weaken and continued.
“I am ashamed to admit that I once accepted a bribe.
Then, after my hyung suddenly collapsed, the Zhongnan Sect used it as leverage to approach me, and I...
I was afraid I would be cast out.
I didn’t want to leave the Escort Bureau I had devoted my entire life to, and I trusted the Zhongnan Sect when they promised they wouldn’t hurt you.”
“I intended to cooperate only once—just once—but by then, I had already stepped into a swamp I could never escape.”
“Is all of that true?”
“How could I lie to you?”
Despite his claim, Heo Jun’s entire story contained only one truth.
He had accepted a bribe.
He had been the one to approach the Zhongnan Sect after Junzi Sword collapsed, concealing his identity as he did so.
Their secret relationship had continued for two years.
I only have to get through this moment.
Just this moment!
Tears streamed down his face.
They held no remorse—only terror of death and a desperate desire to survive.
“Please forgive me...!”
The onlookers shook their heads at his desperate plea.
More than a few escorts turned away, unable to bear the sight.
Ju Hwaran did not.
She stared at Heo Jun, biting her lip, then abruptly asked, “How did you steal the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng?
I never let it out of my sight for even a moment.”
“Th-that...”
“Tell me the truth.”
“...I mixed a mind-clouding drug into the food.
Everyone was exhausted, so a small dose was enough.”
The mind-clouding drug was a narcotic that clouded the mind and induced sleep.
Its effects had been undeniable.
Even Ju Hwaran, a Peak master, had fallen into a deep sleep, mistaking the drug’s effects for the exhaustion of the journey.
“So that was why you were outside my room that night.”
“I had to conceal my presence even as I left.
That bastard—no, Captain Song—remained awake until dawn despite taking the drug.”
Song Ilseom, leaning against the wall with his arms folded, muttered expressionlessly.
“So that was a mind-clouding drug.
No wonder I felt unusually tired that day.
Use something better next time—assuming you have a next time.”
What a goddamn bastard.
Heo Jun barely swallowed the curse rising to his lips and looked at Ju Hwaran.
“Hwangbo Eom, that old man, threatened me.
He said that unless I switched the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, he would kill me and my family and wipe out the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
I only wanted to protect everyone!”
“Then you made the wrong choice.”
“You’re right.
I even went to my hyung’s sickbed once and confessed everything in tears.
But... but I couldn’t undo my mistake.”
“Your mistake?”
Ju Hwaran’s eyes trembled at the mention of her father, but only for an instant.
Then she gave a small shake of her head.
“No.
You’re wrong.
It wasn’t a mistake.
It was a choice, Uncle.”
“Hwaran...!”
“My father often told me that every choice carries responsibility.
Though he failed to make the family business he inherited prosper, he never once regretted the choices he made.”
Heo Jun suddenly realized that the conflict and uncertainty he had seen in Ju Hwaran’s eyes were fading.
It can’t be.
No.
It could not be.
This could not be happening!
Tears and cold sweat streamed down Heo Jun’s cheeks.
He desperately raised his voice.
“Give me one chance!
Just one last chance!
I’m your father’s one and only sworn younger brother, and your uncle, aren’t I?
Hwaran, for the sake of the bond we’ve shared, please!”
“The bond we’ve shared, you say?”
“Yes!
I shared thirty years of hardship and joy with my hyung.
If your father were here—if it were him—he would not take my life so easily!”
“Uncle Heo.
No—Chief Escort Heo Jun.”
Heo Jun stopped pounding his head against the floor and looked up blankly.
His niece’s eyes met his.
They were eyes he had never seen before—cold and utterly devoid of hesitation.
“You’re right.
If my father were here, he would have forgiven you.
But...”
Her low voice continued toward the frozen Heo Jun.
“I am not Junzi Sword Ju Hogun.
I am Dagger Hidden Flower Ju Hwaran.”
The next instant, silver sword light filled Heo Jun’s vision.
Swish!
Slice!

chapters.title: Chapter 328
paragraphs: “Guh... ghk.”
Blood gushed from Heo Jun’s slashed throat.
He thrashed and clutched at his neck, but it was already too late.
Ju Hwaran’s single sword strike had been fast and precise. It had accomplished its purpose without a single mistake.
“Grrk...”
It was the death rattle of a dying man.
What had he wanted to say? This is unfair? Spare me? Or perhaps, I’ll curse you even in death?
Heo Jun’s lips, which had been opening and closing as blood rattled in his throat, suddenly froze.
The strength drained from his flailing limbs. His eyes, fixed on Ju Hwaran and clouded with countless emotions, lost their light.
Haaa...
His final breath in this world dispersed into the air.
Heo Jun—the sworn brother of Junzi Sword Ju Hogun and the Chief Escort who had served the Yongbong Escort Bureau for thirty years—died just like that.
At the hands of the niece who had once followed him as though he were family.
“...Uncle Heo.”
The words slipped quietly from Ju Hwaran’s lips. From behind, she looked strangely desolate.
She gazed down at Heo Jun’s lifeless body for a moment, then slowly turned around.
Her obsidian eyes passed over the escorts of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and settled on the outsiders.
One person at a time. Finally, she looked at me, then offered everyone a formal martial salute.
“I, Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau, have been discourteous before my seniors in the martial world.”
Pain often made people mature. I hoped this ordeal had helped her grow.
It’s a relief that she seems calmer than I expected, but...
There was an awkward edge to the air.
Just as I was thinking that, something pressed down hard on my foot.
I looked down and saw an ornate danghye.
As far as I knew, there was only one person here who would wear something like that.
When I gave her a questioning look, Wolhwa glanced pointedly to either side.
Only then did I notice everyone staring at me.
At some point, they had all split off to either side and were now looking straight at me.
At the end of the path they had opened stood Ju Hwaran, still holding her salute.
...What is this?
Was there something on my face?
As I stood there flustered, Wolhwa whispered so softly that I could barely hear her.
“Young Master Jin, say something.”
“Pardon?”
“Young Lady Ju greeted us. You need to respond on everyone’s behalf.”
“Why do I have to do it?”
“Hurry. Young Lady Ju will grow old waiting.”
Well, she had aged about ten seconds in the meantime.

I had no idea why I had to speak when Huashan’s leading candidate for Sect Leader, the Beggar Prince, and the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi Branch Leader were all standing right there, but I gave an awkward bow anyway.
“There’s no need to call it discourteous. And I’m not a senior in the martial world, so you can treat me casually.”
“How could I do that?”
Ju Hwaran raised her head and spoke calmly.

“Great Hero Jin and the other seniors are Benefactors of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. Without your help, we would have suffered a terrible ordeal... and we would never have been able to punish the traitor.”
A trace of bitterness crossed her face as she added those final words.
Perhaps she noticed it herself, because her voice grew firmer.
“I will repay the debt we owe you today without fail.”

I couldn’t exactly claim it had been nothing. The help provided by me and the other sects had certainly been substantial. From the perspective of Ju Hwaran and the Yongbong Escort Bureau, even a hundred bows wouldn’t have been enough.
Still, being called Great Hero is a little much.
Even Young Hero made me cringe, and now the title had evolved to the next stage.
Feeling as though I ought to grow a beard, I changed the subject.
“Repay the others, not me. More importantly, what are you going to do now?”
“We’ll recover the body first and return to the bureau. There’s a lot to take care of.”
“You must be incredibly busy.”
Ju Hwaran was managing the bureau in place of her unconscious father.
Dealing with the aftermath of the long escort mission alone would fill her days, and after one outrageous incident after another, even ten bodies wouldn’t be enough to handle everything.
Ju Hwaran nodded.
“Even so, we have enough time to host Great Hero Jin and his companions.”
“You have enough time? That’s a relief... Huh?”
“You and your companions are Benefactors who saved me and everyone under my care. I cannot send you away without offering you proper hospitality.”
“Um, Young Lady Ju, the thing is...”
“Are you perhaps very busy?”
I was busy. Extremely busy.
Jeok Cheongang had a treatment window of six months at minimum and eight at most.
Within that time, I had to scour the vast land of Sichuan for the mysterious person known as the Divine Physician.
It took us a week to get from Henan to Shaanxi. Reaching Sichuan will take at least another week, no matter how fast we travel.
And that was assuming I used my movement technique to the fullest.
Everything about the Divine Physician was shrouded in mystery. No one could predict how long it would take to find him.
That was why spending even a single day in Xi’an had already made me anxious.
And it’s already late in the day.
The sun had passed its zenith long ago. Our entanglement with the Zhongnan Sect had cost us a considerable amount of time, so I needed to start running as though my feet were on fire.
And yet...
“No, I’m not busy.”
My mouth opened of its own accord, and that ridiculous answer slipped out.
What had just happened? That was the exact opposite of what I had meant to say.
As I stood there dazed, Ju Hwaran cautiously asked,
“Great Hero Jin, are you really all right? If you have something urgent to attend to, we can postpone it until later.”
Thank you. Thank you so much for saying that first.
Sharp and perceptive as ever. She had scratched exactly where it itched, and I answered without hesitation.
“No matter how urgent it is, can’t I share one meal with you?”
“Right...”
“I was already hungry after exerting myself so much. This works out perfectly. Let’s go.”
Am I a fucking idiot? Seriously?
I needed to go to Sichuan. Why the hell was I going to the Yongbong Escort Bureau?
But by the time I came to my senses, I had already hoisted the pack frame onto my back.
Just as I heaved an inward sigh, I noticed someone who had remained completely detached from everything going on around him.
When I stared at him, he spoke first.
“What? Do you have something to say?”
This was the first time casual speech from someone I had just met sounded so natural.
Since he had dropped the formalities first, that made things easier for me too.
“I was just wondering if you weren’t coming.”
“I have no reason to.”
“Then make one.”
“I know you have plenty of time to spare, so let’s have a conversation.”
“A conversation?”
“Yeah. A conversation.”
Song Ilseom raised an eyebrow at me, then pushed himself upright from where he had been leaning.
It was early spring. The blazing sun disappeared behind the western mountains less than two shichen after we arrived at the Yongbong Escort Bureau.
Oil lamps illuminated the reception room, where a magnificent feast had been laid out across the table. Cheongpung and Gung Gibang stared wide-eyed as they crammed food into their mouths.
“Mmph. Benefactor. This is delicious. Mmph-mmph-mmph.”
“...Eat as much as you want. Preferably don’t talk.”
The food did look delicious.
At least until Cheongpung went out of his way to show me what was in his mouth.
“Gobble, gobble. This Escort Bureau sure knows how to cook. Young Bureau Head, could you give the extra food to the members of our sect as well?”
Gung Gibang really was a beggar to the bone.
As he continued his meat-centered massacre, Ju Hwaran nodded.
“Of course. Tell them they can come whenever they’re hungry.”
“Oh, whenever they’re hungry?”
“...Not quite that much.”
If every Beggars’ Sect disciple in Shaanxi Province descended on the place, all four hundred thousand silver nyang of the compensation would disappear into food costs.
Gung Gibang grinned, baring his yellow teeth.
“Don’t worry. I’ll make sure to explain it so you have nothing to worry about.”
Hyuk Mujin, who was at least eating normally, whispered,
“The way he says that makes me even more worried.”
“You said it.”
At this rate, the Yongbong Escort Bureau might go under because of the Beggars’ Sect instead of the Zhongnan Sect.
I was resolving to give him a warning when Ju Hwaran spoke to me.
“It’s a shame the others didn’t come.”
“Yeah. The food is good, too.”
The others in our group—Baek Museong, Heukgeol Beggar, and Wolhwa—had all declined the invitation.
I wasn’t sure why, but the two men might have changed their answers after Wolhwa gave them a long, pointed stare.
In any case...
“For someone who likes the food, you aren’t eating very much.”
“No, it’s delicious. Look. I’ve already finished two bowls of rice.”
“That’s strange. Why does it seem as though you’ve barely eaten?”
“It’s all relative. Look at them. They’re waging the Great Faction War against the food.”
Schlurp, schlurp!
Gobble, gobble!
Chomp, chomp, chomp!
Ju Hwaran nodded as though she had attained enlightenment.
“Ah.”
“Mujin and I are the normal ones. The person who’s actually eating very little is over there.”
Song Ilseom replied in his usual blunt tone.
“I’ve been saying this for ten years, but the food here is too salty. Spicy and salty dishes overstimulate the senses and weigh down the body.”
“That reminds me of someone. If she were here, she’d beat you to death with a ladle.”
“Who are you talking about?”
“Someone I know. One hit from her and you’ll scream whether you mean to or not. She’s beaten the hell out of me over the years, and strangely enough, I’ve never managed to dodge her once.”
“Great Hero Jin, is that true?”
“You?”
Ju Hwaran asked back in surprise, and Song Ilseom’s eyes flashed.
“If even you, the man who defeated the Taeeul Merciless Sword, say so... she must be an extraordinary master indeed. Can you tell me her name and epithet?”
“Kim Jeonghee. Her epithet is Lady.”
“Hmm. I’ve never heard of her.”
Of course he hadn’t. She was my mother.
Without showing anything on my face, I continued in a solemn tone.
“In any case, she always said you had to eat all kinds of food without being picky if you wanted to grow big—no, strong.”
“Hmm.”
“So stop whining about the side dishes and fucking eat.”
Song Ilseom pondered this with a serious expression, then picked up his chopsticks and began eating the side dishes.
The more I watched him, the stranger his personality seemed.
He’s strange, but he doesn’t seem dangerous.
A few shichen earlier, I had briefly suspected Song Ilseom of being something very bad indeed.
It had been a reasonable suspicion. He was an exceptional Peak master who had concealed his strength for ten years, and I had already encountered a similar case in Shanxi Province.
Dark Heaven.
The Head Elder and the Five Gates of Shanxi had lain low for decades. Perhaps that was why Song Ilseom’s behavior had reminded me of them.
But the longer I spoke with him, the more my suspicion faded, leaving only curiosity behind.
What the hell is this guy?
His blunt manner of speaking and behavior. He seemed rough to the point of being crude, yet there was a peculiar air of refinement in his appearance and various other aspects of him.
Perhaps that was why his casual speech sounded so natural.
Well, this is something.
I stared at Song Ilseom.
He chewed the side dishes thoroughly, his face twisted into an exaggerated grimace. After swallowing, he spoke.
“That look again. What is it?”
“I was just thinking about your identity.”
“Are you that curious?”
“Yeah. Very.”
Talking with this guy was like driving down a wide-open highway. That was why it felt so comfortable.
Before long, everyone else—including Ju Hwaran—had pricked up their ears and fixed their eyes on Song Ilseom’s mouth.
Apparently displeased by the attention, he raised an eyebrow.
“There’s nothing special about it. I stayed at the Yongbong Escort Bureau because of a connection to the previous generation.”
“A connection to the previous generation?”
“To be precise, my father received a great kindness from them.”
Huh? Wait a second. That sounded familiar, but I couldn’t quite place it.
I turned and found Ju Hwaran staring wide-eyed at Song Ilseom.
This was clearly the first time she had heard the story in ten years.
“May I ask your father’s name?”
“Song Pyosan.”
“Song Pyosan... I’ve never heard that name.”
“That’s hardly surprising. It happened almost fifty years ago.”
Almost fifty years ago? Was he talking about the Great Faction War?
Before we could ask, Song Ilseom continued as though it were nothing important.

“The Guangdong Chen Family was a clan forgotten long ago. My grandmother was saved with the help of Escort King Ju Gongsan, but she feared the greedy martial artists and had her child carry on her surname. It was a wise decision.”
I felt completely blindsided. Ju Hwaran stared at Song Ilseom with trembling eyes.
“Then could you be...?”
Instead of answering, Song Ilseom drew a faded jade hairpin from his robes and held it out.
It was the only escort fee a young escort surnamed Ju had received from a heavily pregnant woman more than fifty years ago.

But the longer I spoke with him, the more my suspicion faded, leaving only curiosity behind.
What the hell is this guy?
His blunt manner of speaking and behavior.
He seemed rough to the point of being crude, yet there was a peculiar air of refinement in his appearance and various other aspects of him.
Perhaps that was why his casual speech sounded so natural.
Well, this is something.
I stared at Song Ilseom.
He chewed the side dishes thoroughly, his face twisted into an exaggerated grimace.
After swallowing, he spoke.
“That look again.
What is it?”
“I was just thinking about your identity.”
“Are you that curious?”
“Yeah.
Very.”
Talking with this guy was like driving down a wide-open highway.
That was why it felt so comfortable.
Before long, everyone else—including Ju Hwaran—had pricked up their ears and fixed their eyes on Song Ilseom’s mouth.
Apparently displeased by the attention, he raised an eyebrow.
“There’s nothing special about it.
I stayed at the Yongbong Escort Bureau because of a connection to the previous generation.”
“A connection to the previous generation?”
“To be precise, my father received a great kindness from them.”
Huh?
Wait a second.
That sounded familiar, but I couldn’t quite place it.
I turned and found Ju Hwaran staring wide-eyed at Song Ilseom.
This was clearly the first time she had heard the story in ten years.
“May I ask your father’s name?”
“Song Pyosan.”
“Song Pyosan...
I’ve never heard that name.”
“That’s hardly surprising.
It happened almost fifty years ago.”
Almost fifty years ago?
Was he talking about the Great Faction War?
Before we could ask, Song Ilseom continued as though it were nothing important.
“The Guangdong Chen Family was a clan forgotten long ago.
My grandmother was saved with the help of Escort King Ju Gongsan, but she feared the greedy martial artists and had her child carry on her surname.
It was a wise decision.”
I felt completely blindsided.
Ju Hwaran stared at Song Ilseom with trembling eyes.
“Then could you be...?”
Instead of answering, Song Ilseom drew a faded jade hairpin from his robes and held it out.
It was the only escort fee a young escort surnamed Ju had received from a heavily pregnant woman more than fifty years ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 329
paragraphs: When Song Ilseom’s identity was revealed, everyone was astonished.

Hyuk Mujin had admired the Murim even before becoming part of the Taiyuan Jin Family, so of course he knew the stories about him. Even Cheongpung pretended to know him, claiming that the Sword Saint had told him about Song Ilseom.
“Mmph-mmph. Grandpa said the Escort King was a good man. Gulp. That’s what he said.”
“...I know. Just swallow before you talk. Please.”
“Okay! Mmph-mmph.”
If even Cheongpung knew the story, the other two went without saying.
Ju Hwaran, the Escort King’s granddaughter, was staring at the jade hairpin with trembling eyes, while Gung Gibang was so excited that he sprayed the contents of his mouth in every direction.
“Th-the Guangdong Chen Family!”
Tududududuk!
Song Ilseom knocked away a dozen or so grains of rice with his chopsticks and replied.
“As I said, the Guangdong Chen Family ceased to exist long ago. By the way, can you do something about all that flying out of your mouth?”
“My Master also told me about the Escort King’s Ten-Thousand-Mile Escorts. But to think the child from that story was you!”
“Did you listen with your nose? That child was my father. And stop spitting everywhere. It’s disgusting.”
Swish! Tududududuk!
Wow. He knocked away every single one.
After whipping his chopsticks through the air like lightning yet again, Song Ilseom asked me, “Is this beggar really the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect?”
“He is, even if he doesn’t look like it. Why?”
“A Rain of Ten Thousand Flowers keeps pouring from his mouth. I wondered if he might be a disciple of the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Hmm. Probably not.”
While we were talking, Ju Hwaran finally spoke, her gaze still fixed on the jade hairpin.
“My father told me about it. He said my grandfather wondered what had become of the Guangdong Chen Family until the very end, but he was never able to find them...”
“My grandmother carried that regret with her as well. She had to flee with my father, who was still a baby, without leaving so much as a letter.”
“Why did they suddenly disappear?”
“Because it was dangerous. The Guangdong Chen Family’s martial arts were all lost when the family estate burned to the ground, but apparently no one believed it.”
“But if they were within the territory of the orthodox factions...”

“Greed does not discriminate between members of orthodox factions and practitioners of demonic, heterodox arts. Some of those seeking the Guangdong Chen Family’s Peak martial arts were people even the Escort King’s name couldn’t deter.”
A time of chaos.
Those words gave me some idea of what the mother and child must have endured back then.
In chaotic times, the rules binding people together crumble. Everyone gives in to their instincts, and morality inevitably fades.
The mother had fled to protect her child from the greed of others, without telling anyone.
“My grandmother was an ordinary woman who couldn’t have stood against even a Third Rate swordsman, but she was wiser than ten Peak masters combined.”
After a brief silence, Song Ilseom added, “Of course, even she couldn’t escape birth, aging, sickness, and death.”
“Then...”
“She died of an illness when I was ten. As she gave me this jade hairpin, she told me everything that had happened. It was an astonishing story—the first I had ever heard of it.”
Despite his blunt demeanor, Song Ilseom was surprisingly good at telling a story.
The one thing I had been curious about was what had happened to his parents. But once I heard that he had wandered the streets after his grandmother’s death, there was no need to ask.
Unfortunately, both of them had clearly died young.
As soon as one question disappeared, another took its place.
“Then how did you develop that level of skill? Didn’t you say the Guangdong Chen Family’s martial arts were lost as well?”
Song Ilseom’s answer was simple.
“On the battlefield.”
“Did you live as a wandering martial artist?”
“I had no talent for begging. More people beat me because they disliked my face and expression than tossed me an iron coin.”
Gung Gibang, who had been listening quietly, nodded with deep sympathy.

“There’s a proper way to beg. The most important thing for a beggar is a face and expression that inspire pity, but when you’re as handsome as Song Ilseom or me, even earning a few coins is difficult. I went hungry plenty of days myself.”
Song Ilseom’s expression hardened.
“Successor Beggar, I find that remark deeply offensive. I’d appreciate it if you stopped insulting me.”
“Why? Did you ever see my face when I was young? I’m telling you, without the slightest exaggeration, I was handsome enough to make Song Yu weep.”
“Song Yu would weep?”
Song Ilseom stared intently at Gung Gibang’s face, which looked like something out of a Picasso masterpiece.
“With that face, he might. If you run into me at night, stay far away. If I suddenly came face-to-face with you, I might cut you by mistake.”
Looking as though he was debating whether to cut him down right then and there, Song Ilseom continued his story.

“In any case, I was hopeless at begging and couldn’t find any decent work. After going hungry for more than three days, the sky started turning yellow. I decided becoming a sword boy would be better than starving to death.”
“A sword boy? The kind who carries someone’s sword?”
“That’s right.”
“Isn’t that something rich people hire? They can’t be bothered carrying their own swords, so they make someone else do it.”
“Do you think rich people would hire some beggar brat who crawled in from who knows where?”
“Fair point.”
“Surprisingly, wandering martial artists hire the most sword boys. They make them handle every odd job imaginable, then use them as meat shields when things get dangerous.”
I thought it sounded like a sweet gig, but it turned out to be a part-time job straight out of the Hell Continent.
“It wasn’t a particularly comfortable or pleasant experience.”
Song Ilseom calmly recounted his past.
Most days, he waited on wandering martial artists while enduring constant abuse and violence. When arrows rained down, he went out to retrieve weapons.
When the wandering martial artist abandoned him and fled because he was too busy saving his own life, Song Ilseom experienced nothing short of hell.

“I hid among piles of corpses for four days. When I barely made it out alive and went looking for the wandering martial artist, the first thing he did was search for the sword he had entrusted to me.”
“Wow. What a crazy bastard.”
“Fortunately, the two swords I was carrying were unharmed. Even while fleeing, I refused to let go of them.”
“...Wow. You really are a crazy bastard.”

“I wasn’t as crazy as he was. He started spouting nonsense about how he had originally entrusted me with three swords, then told me to get the hell out of there if I didn’t want to die like a dog. Of course, he didn’t give me a single coin for the year I had worked for him.”
Song Ilseom brushed back the hair that had fallen over his forehead and muttered, “That pissed me off.”
Naturally, instead of filing a complaint with the labor authorities, he chose a faster solution.
“There happened to be two swords. I picked one up. It was heavy.”
“You won.”
“I killed him.”
Song Ilseom casually corrected me as he twirled his chopsticks.
“It wasn’t difficult. I’d watched his martial arts every day, and they were predictable. I dodged ten times and stabbed once, as if we’d rehearsed the whole exchange. Then he fell.”
Gulp.
Hyuk Mujin swallowed nervously and asked,
“How old were you then?”
“Twelve? Thirteen? I don’t remember exactly, but it was around then.”
“Th-then your opponent...”
“He was a lousy Third Rate wandering martial artist. If he’d been First Rate, do you think I’d have been crazy enough to take him on?”
No, I think a kid who hadn’t even graduated from elementary school attacking a martial artist was already insane.
What was I doing at that age?
Who knew? I was probably running around picking my nose or something.
This guy’s a gifted bastard too.
Countless martial sects and families existed throughout the world.
If the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the first tier, there naturally had to be a second tier.
According to something Jeok Cheongang had mentioned in passing, the Guangdong Chen Family had belonged to that second tier.
Blood will tell, huh?
To reach that level without any of his family’s secret martial arts...
Just as I was marveling at the thought that Song Ilseom really was something special, Gung Gibang, who had been silent for a while, suddenly stared at him in shock.
“Could you be the Soul-Chasing Guest?”
“That’s what they called me ten years ago. By the way, is your mouth a bottomless jar? How the hell are you still spitting out rice after all this time?”
“Hah. I never imagined the famous Soul-Chasing Guest would be a young man around my age.”
The Soul-Chasing Guest. That was apparently Song Ilseom’s former epithet.
He must have been almost as famous as he was skilled, because Ju Hwaran’s eyes widened as well.
“You’re the Soul-Chasing Guest who won a hundred life-and-death duels?”
“One hundred and two, to be exact. It’s all hollow fame, so there’s no need to make a fuss. There are already two people here younger and more impressive than me.”
Cheongpung, who had somehow finished off most of the food, grinned.
“No, you’re still amazing, Young Hero Song.”
I nodded.
“Yeah, he’s strong. Weaker than me, though.”
“...Are you two making fun of me?”
Cheongpung slurped down something that looked like cinnamon punch and answered, “No teasin’ you!”
“He says he isn’t teasing you.”
At my helpful translation, Song Ilseom’s gaze shifted toward me.
“What about you?”
“I am teasing you.”
“...Got any booze? I feel like having a drink for the first time in a while.”
The meal, which had begun in the early evening, didn’t end until close to midnight.
Ignoring the fine liquor, Song Ilseom had downed cup after cup of strong liquor and now had his head planted on the table. Ju Hwaran, who had been sipping hers, had flushed cheeks as well.
And then...
It really is time to go.
When I rose, Gung Gibang used his internal energy to purge the alcohol from his body, while Hyuk Mujin hoisted Cheongpung onto his back. Cheongpung was already completely wasted and snoring softly.
“We’ve imposed on you, Young Lady Ju.”
“You’re leaving already?”
“I’d like to stay longer, but I don’t think I can this time.”
“Is that so?”
Her drunken eyes curved like half-moons.
Her steps were light, almost as if she were dancing, and deep dimples showed in her cheeks. Apparently, drinking made her laugh.
“Would you like to take a walk?”
“Pardon?”
“Let’s go for a walk. The flowers in the garden have just bloomed.”
“Oh. Congratulations. They must be pretty.”
She burst out laughing.
Before I could ask what was so funny, Ju Hwaran giggled and stepped outside.
I followed her without thinking, then stopped short and turned around.
“You two aren’t coming?”
“...Is he even human?”
“Lower than a beggar. Beggarly bastard. Worse than a beggar.”
“What the hell? Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s how I feel.”
“That’s how I feel.”
“Come on. Young Lady Ju said the flowers have bloomed in the garden. We can look around together and leave right afterward. The timing will be perfect—”
The sighs of Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin cut me off.
The two men shook their heads with expressions of utter horror, then spoke in turn.
“I need to take a dump. Where’s the latrine?”
“Me too. We’ll take turns going back and forth, so take your time looking around.”
“...Uh. Sure.”
What’s wrong with those two? Do their stomachs hurt that badly? Their faces look downright demonic today.
I must be imagining the contempt and fury in their eyes.
I hurried outside and began walking through the garden beside Ju Hwaran, who was waiting for me.
“Great Hero Jin is... how should I put it? You’re a very interesting person.”
“Am I?”
“Yes. You can be a little exasperating sometimes, but... well, in a way, that’s one of your strengths too.”
What is this? Is she insulting me indirectly?
At my bewildered expression, the smile on Ju Hwaran’s lips deepened.
“I don’t remember the last time I laughed out loud. It must have been more than half a year ago.”
“Hmm? Didn’t you laugh last time too? When we passed Black Stone Mountain?”
“Oh. Did I?”
“Maybe you just don’t remember. That makes twice in three days.”
“I wonder. Is that really it?”
Ju Hwaran murmured dreamily, then suddenly pointed at the sky.
“Great Hero Jin, do you see that?”
“Of course. It’s a full moon.”
“The moon is especially bright tonight.”
“Did you know why the moon is bright, Young Lady Ju? It’s because it reflects light from the sun.”
“Pardon?”
“No, I’m serious. It’s not some ridiculous story. It’s a famous result of scientific research... No, I heard it from a scholar. Where was it? That’s right, somewhere around the imperial palace.”
Another quiet laugh slipped from her lips.
“No, it really is true...”
“All right. I’ll believe you. By the way, Great Hero Jin.”
“Yes?”
“This.”
To me, still feeling wronged, Ju Hwaran suddenly held something out.
A solid, elongated wooden case. One I had already seen at the teahouse.
“Could this be...?”
“That’s right. Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.”
“It’s a small gift compared to what you’ve done for us, but would you accept it? It would put my heart at ease, at least a little.”
I silently looked back and forth between Ju Hwaran and the wooden case.
Should I refuse? Should I accept it? Should I refuse...
After several rounds of agonizing, I finally nodded.
“I’ll accept it gratefully. Thank you.”
Ju Hwaran beamed.
Her smile was brighter than the moon hanging in the sky.
We walked for about fifteen minutes, chatting about nothing in particular, until the flowers lining both sides of the path gradually began to thin.
Ju Hwaran’s steps slowed as well.
“Great Hero Jin.”
“Yes, Young Lady Ju?”
“Do you think I can do well?”
Her sudden voice sounded raw and desolate.
Perhaps this was why she had drunk.
But there were days like that. Days when nothing could hold your emotions back. Moments when everything you had struggled to suppress finally surged over the brim.
“Do you really think I can do well?”
I spoke.
“It’s okay if you can’t.”
It’s okay. I understand how you feel. Stay strong.

Sometimes, every word of comfort sounded hollow. Of course she wasn’t okay. Someone standing a step removed could never fully understand what the person suffering was going through, and being told to stay strong didn’t suddenly give you strength.
I didn’t offer Ju Hwaran some clumsy consolation today because she was already suffering enough.
“You’re only human too, Young Lady Ju. It’s okay if you don’t do well. You don’t have to force yourself to be strong.”
She only had to keep going as she had, following the current wherever it carried her.
One step at a time, at her own pace rather than someone else’s.
“Wouldn’t that be enough?”
Ju Hwaran looked up at me, tears clinging to her eyes.
Then they curved like half-moons.
Thump!
I kicked off the ground.
The scenery receded, and the earth blurred past beneath me.
The voices of Ju Hwaran and the people of the Yongbong Escort Bureau gradually faded before cutting off entirely.
Only then did the two guys who had been watching me warily speak.
“Young Lady Ju’s eyes looked swollen earlier...”
“Do you think she cried? No. No way. She couldn’t have.”
They noticed that carefully even in the dark.
When I didn’t answer, Hyuk Mujin pointed at the bulge beneath my clothes.
“But what’s that?”
“Oh, this?”
I forgot to put it in my Inventory.
I let out a quiet laugh as someone’s lie came to mind.
“Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.”
“Whaaat?”
“Huh?”

Their faces look downright demonic today.
I must be imagining the contempt and fury in their eyes.
I hurried outside and began walking through the garden beside Ju Hwaran, who was waiting for me.
“Great Hero Jin is... how should I put it?
You’re a very interesting person.”
“Am I?”
“Yes.
You can be a little exasperating sometimes, but... well, in a way, that’s one of your strengths too.”
What is this?
Is she insulting me indirectly?
At my bewildered expression, the smile on Ju Hwaran’s lips deepened.
“I don’t remember the last time I laughed out loud.
It must have been more than half a year ago.”
“Hmm?
Didn’t you laugh last time too?
When we passed Black Stone Mountain?”
“Oh.
Did I?”
“Maybe you just don’t remember.
That makes twice in three days.”
“I wonder.
Is that really it?”
Ju Hwaran murmured dreamily, then suddenly pointed at the sky.
“Great Hero Jin, do you see that?”
“Of course.
It’s a full moon.”
“The moon is especially bright tonight.”
“Did you know why the moon is bright, Young Lady Ju?
It’s because it reflects light from the sun.”
“Pardon?”
“No, I’m serious.
It’s not some ridiculous story.
It’s a famous result of scientific research...
No, I heard it from a scholar.
Where was it?
That’s right, somewhere around the imperial palace.”
Another quiet laugh slipped from her lips.
“No, it really is true...”
“All right.
I’ll believe you.
By the way, Great Hero Jin.”
“Yes?”
“This.”
To me, still feeling wronged, Ju Hwaran suddenly held something out.
A solid, elongated wooden case.
One I had already seen at the teahouse.
“Could this be...?”
“That’s right.
Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng.”
“It’s a small gift compared to what you’ve done for us, but would you accept it?
It would put my heart at ease, at least a little.”
I silently looked back and forth between Ju Hwaran and the wooden case.
Should I refuse?
Should I accept it?
Should I refuse...
After several rounds of agonizing, I finally nodded.
“I’ll accept it gratefully.
Thank you.”
Ju Hwaran beamed.
Her smile was brighter than the moon hanging in the sky.
We walked for about fifteen minutes, chatting about nothing in particular, until the flowers lining both sides of the path gradually began to thin.
Ju Hwaran’s steps slowed as well.
“Great Hero Jin.”
“Yes, Young Lady Ju?”
“Do you think I can do well?”
Her sudden voice sounded raw and desolate.
Perhaps this was why she had drunk.
But there were days like that.
Days when nothing could hold your emotions back.
Moments when everything you had struggled to suppress finally surged over the brim.
“Do you really think I can do well?”
I spoke.
“It’s okay if you can’t.”
It’s okay.
I understand how you feel.
Stay strong.
Sometimes, every word of comfort sounded hollow.
Of course she wasn’t okay.
Someone standing a step removed could never fully understand what the person suffering was going through, and being told to stay strong didn’t suddenly give you strength.
I didn’t offer Ju Hwaran some clumsy consolation today because she was already suffering enough.
“You’re only human too, Young Lady Ju.
It’s okay if you don’t do well.
You don’t have to force yourself to be strong.”
She only had to keep going as she had, following the current wherever it carried her.
One step at a time, at her own pace rather than someone else’s.
“Wouldn’t that be enough?”
Ju Hwaran looked up at me, tears clinging to her eyes.
Then they curved like half-moons.
Thump!
I kicked off the ground.
The scenery receded, and the earth blurred past beneath me.
The voices of Ju Hwaran and the people of the Yongbong Escort Bureau gradually faded before cutting off entirely.
Only then did the two guys who had been watching me warily speak.
“Young Lady Ju’s eyes looked swollen earlier...”
“Do you think she cried?
No.
No way.
She couldn’t have.”
They noticed that carefully even in the dark.
When I didn’t answer, Hyuk Mujin pointed at the bulge beneath my clothes.
“But what’s that?”
“Oh, this?”
I forgot to put it in my Inventory.
I let out a quiet laugh as someone’s lie came to mind.
“Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.”
“Whaaat?”
“Huh?”

chapters.title: Chapter 330
paragraphs: Around midnight.
The four figures leaving the Yongbong Escort Bureau vanished in the blink of an eye.
The members of the bureau who had come to see them off shivered in the cold wind, but Ju Hwaran stood perfectly still.
As if someone might return if she waited just a little longer.
It was then that she heard a voice from the darkness.
“They’re gone.”
Startled by the voice’s soundless arrival, the escorts parted to either side. Ju Hwaran, however, remained composed.
“Yes. They’ve left.”
“Are you disappointed?”
“I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t.”
“It can’t be helped. Those who leave, leave. Those who stay, stay. That’s the way of things.”
“The way of things...”
Ju Hwaran murmured the words, then slowly turned around.
“Which are you, Captain Song?”
“Me?”
Song Ilseom gave a quiet laugh and conspicuously swung the travel pack slung over his shoulder.
“Which do you think?”
“Is that why you pretended to pass out drunk?”
“It’s been ten years. I’d say I’ve done my duty by now...but is that still not enough?”
“No.”
“It isn’t enough. You still haven’t done your duty.”
Song Ilseom’s brow furrowed at Ju Hwaran’s unhesitating answer.
“Still not enough? Even after I protected the Yongbong Escort Bureau—and you—for ten years?”
“Can that compare to the debt of gratitude owed for my grandfather’s lifesaving deed?”
Song Ilseom raised his voice and stepped forward. The nearby escorts flinched and gripped their sword hilts.

They had not heard the hidden truth of his origins. To them, Song Ilseom was still someone to be wary of. The other two escort captains who made up the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts with him were openly hostile.
“Lower your voice. It’ll be better for your health.”
“We don’t know what the Young Bureau Head thinks, but we’re not convinced. No matter how we look at it, there’s something suspicious about you.”
The two escort captains blocked Song Ilseom’s path with grim expressions.
“Enough. Step aside.”
At Ju Hwaran’s calm voice, the two escort captains stammered.
“Y-Young Bureau Head.”
“But this man hasn’t completely cleared himself of suspicion yet—!”
“I said step aside. I have something important to discuss with him. Everyone return to your posts and take care of the remaining work.”
“Y-yes, ma’am.”
Their mouths worked as if they still had more to say, but the two escort captains finally nodded and slowly withdrew with the other escorts.
Song Ilseom watched them leave, then clicked his tongue at Ju Hwaran.
“I can’t tell whether they’re loyal or stupid. After all that’s happened, they still can’t tell friend from foe.”
“Your premise is wrong.”
“What?”
“They’re neither loyal nor stupid, despite what you think.”
A question flashed through Song Ilseom’s mind.
Could it be?
The insight came in an instant.
He was a born fighter and a martial artist through and through, but that did not mean he was stupid.
Once he grasped the situation, Song Ilseom muttered, “What a damned mess.”
Ju Hwaran nodded.
“They deliberately sabotaged escort missions and contracts, siphoned off funds amid the confusion, and carefully doctored the ledgers. There’s no way Uncle Heo did all of that alone.”
“Just how far does this conspiracy reach?”
“We’ll have to determine the exact number and identities from here on...but at the very least, those two must be included.”
Ju Hwaran’s gaze swept over the retreating backs of the two escort captains before settling on Song Ilseom.
“I’m going to root them out completely.”
“Why didn’t you reveal it right there after the Chief Escort was killed?”
“The confusion would only have grown worse. Besides, if I can’t accomplish even this with my own strength, I have no right to become the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau.”
“Are you confident?”
Ju Hwaran stared silently at Song Ilseom.
“How about putting away that travel pack and taking it out again a year from now?”
“You want to use me to root them out?”
“Captain Song, right now I need a blade sharp enough to cut down anyone. As it happens, the perfect person is standing right in front of me.”
“I refuse. And stop calling me Captain.”
“Then how about hiring the Soul-Chasing Guest?”
“What?”
Ju Hwaran shrugged.
“The renowned Soul-Chasing Guest won’t come cheap...but given our past connection, perhaps you’ll offer me a discount?”
“So I’m supposed to repay that lifesaving debt this way?”
“If that were my intention, I would have asked for something much greater.”
“A moment ago, you said I still hadn’t done my duty in return for the Escort King’s lifesaving grace.”
“That was because too many people were watching. My grandfather said it himself. He was merely one person saving another.”
“Ha!”
Song Ilseom could no longer hold back his laughter.
He remembered what Junzi Sword Ju Hogun had said ten years ago to the young man who had come to him carrying a faded jade hairpin.
“Though a generation passed before we met, you came to find us in the end. That is enough. Don’t let the ties of the previous generation bind you. Live your own life.”
“Pardon?”
“My father told me that what he had done was simply save another person. I feel the same way. And...thank you for growing into such a fine young man.”
It had been a shock.

From childhood onward, Song Ilseom’s life had been one continuous struggle. His parents had died young, and when his only source of support—his grandmother—passed away as well, he had been forced to make his way alone, without anyone’s help.
He had stolen weapons from piles of corpses, cut down wandering martial artists who tried to rob him of his rightful pay, and proven himself through countless life-and-death duels.
I thought he would ask me for something.
To Song Ilseom, who had lived as a wandering martial artist, that was only natural.
If Ju Hogun had wanted someone eliminated, Song Ilseom would have willingly done it. It would have left a bad taste in his mouth, but killing was what he had always done.
It would have been just one more among the countless requests he had completed.
But Ju Hogun had been different.
He was the first “adult” Song Ilseom had met since becoming an orphan with no one in the world.
Perhaps that was why the words had slipped out before he could think.
“Ten years.”
“Hmm?”
“I’ll leave after ten years. Though all I know is how to kill, I’ll protect you and your child no matter what happens. Just as the Escort King did several decades ago.”
Song Ilseom had kept his oath.

He became an escort of the Yongbong Escort Bureau and faithfully followed orders. While he remained at the bureau, he followed the Chief’s daughter like a shadow and protected her at her father’s request.
As the years passed and the child grew into a beautiful young woman, strange rumors began circulating about the two of them, but he paid them no mind.
Whether the Chief collapsed or the Escort Bureau fell apart, Song Ilseom silently remained in place.
I’m only doing my duty.
Song Ilseom opened his tightly shut eyes and abruptly spoke to Ju Hwaran, who had been watching him.
“I’m leaving in a month.”
“If you discover the identities of the traitors, I’ll lead the way and weed them out. A month will be enough.”
Seeing Ju Hwaran’s expression, Song Ilseom spoke bluntly.
“Don’t make that face. I’m only going to Xianyang to pick up an elixir and bring it back.”
“An elixir?”
“That’s right. It should be able to cure the Chief’s illness. The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was too potent and might have done more harm than good, but this elixir should definitely work.”
“H-how did you obtain an elixir like that...?”
“Enough. I’m tired of talking, so don’t ask any more questions.”
Song Ilseom waved a hand.

He had managed to secure the elixir after more than two years of searching. It was not a legendary treasure like the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, but nothing else was better suited to restoring the Chief after his qi deviation.
It had cost him every last coin of the enormous fortune he had earned as the Soul-Chasing Guest, but money could always be earned again.
“Do you know something?”
Song Ilseom continued in a quiet voice.
“There’s nothing harder than saving a person’s life. What you took for granted...was the hardest thing in the world for me.”
Song Ilseom had made his living by killing people.
It was only after joining the Yongbong Escort Bureau that he began protecting someone instead.
“Captain Song...”
Ju Hwaran stared at him with glistening eyes, but when she saw his furrowed brow, she hastily corrected herself.
“Ah, Great Hero Song.”
“How long are you going to keep getting that wrong?”
“I’m sorry. I was so surprised that it slipped out...”
“Then why don’t you create a position while you’re at it?”
“Pardon?”
“I don’t want to be Chief Escort. I’m terrible at escort missions, and I’d have to manage people.”
“P-pardon?”
“Guard Hall Master. Yes, that will do.”
While Ju Hwaran was still stammering, Song Ilseom turned and walked away.
Not toward the gate and the darkness beyond it, but toward his own quarters.
“I shouldn’t have packed my bag.”
As she watched Song Ilseom’s back recede with those quiet words trailing behind him, dimples appeared beside Ju Hwaran’s mouth.
Whoosh!

Sails stretched taut and sterns sliced through the current as the swift ships raced forward like the wind. Bare-chested, bronze-skinned men hauled on ropes and pulled at the oars. At least fifty men could be seen on the deck of each ship.
With five swift ships in all, their force numbered nearly three hundred.
“Faster! Faster!”
“You louts! How can you call yourselves members of the Water Dragon Stronghold when you’re that slow?”
The Water Dragon Stronghold was a major river stronghold belonging to the Yangtze River Channel League.
Its members proudly called themselves the heroes of the Yangtze, but ordinary people had a rather less flattering name for them.
“River bandits! They’re river bandits!”
“Why the hell are those bastards here?”
The shipmaster who spotted the five fast ships promptly collapsed into his seat.
These were no ragtag thugs. They were the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There was no outrunning their swift ships, and fighting them was out of the question.
This day has gone completely to hell.
No. There was only one way to get through this quietly, at least.
Looking utterly dejected, the shipmaster called over the youngest sailor passing by.
“Hey!”
“Yes, shipmaster.”
“Tell the passengers to pay up.”
“Pardon?”
“Collect the money! They have to pay the toll, don’t they?”

The fact that they belonged to the Yangtze River Channel League was both unfortunate and fortunate. Once they were caught, there was no way to escape, but they did not simply swing their swords without reason.
The Yangtze River Channel League claimed this set them apart from the common river-bandit rabble found everywhere under heaven, but one pack of bastards was much the same as another.
“Phew... I’ve really lost today’s business.”
The shipmaster was heaving sigh after sigh when someone tapped him on the shoulder.
“Excuse me.”
“Gah! You startled me! Who are you?”
“I’m a passenger.”
“I know that.”
The shipmaster studied the young man who had appeared out of nowhere. Judging by the sword at his waist, he seemed to be a martial artist, but...
He looks kind of dopey. That mouth of his sticks out, too. Bet he never shuts up.
Third Rate martial artists were a dime a dozen.
It wasn’t as if he had never dealt with one or two of them before. The shipmaster sighed and opened his mouth.
“What do you want? If this is about the money, I’ve got nothing to say. Go back to your seat. Don’t try anything stupid and end up crossing the Sanzu River.”
The young man watched the swift ships drawing rapidly closer.
“Are they river bandits?”
“Can’t you tell by looking? They’re from the Water Dragon Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League. There isn’t a soul in Sichuan who doesn’t know them.”
“The Yangtze River Channel League...”
“Running won’t help. You’ll never escape those swift ships. Once they spot you, it’s over. Completely over!”
“That ship must be pretty fast.”
“What kind of question is—”
The shipmaster was about to snap at him when he sucked in a breath and clamped his mouth shut.
A shadow had risen behind the young man, a full head taller than him.
The giant had shaggy hair, and a great mound of hides rose high atop the pack frame on his back.
He stared blankly at the shipmaster, then spoke to the young man.
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Let’s take that ship.”
The shipmaster wondered if he had heard correctly.

paragraphs: Ship-Fire Boy. A child who lights the fires aboard a ship.
The term meant a boatman. It was also the sobriquet of one particular man.
“Stronghold Lord.”
At his subordinate’s call, the man sitting cross-legged in the center of the cabin opened his eyes.
A crystalline gleam flashed in them. His skin was bronze and his body muscular, befitting a hardened river man. His bulging temples marked him as a Peak master who had reached a considerable realm.
“What is it?”
A deep, resonant voice emerged between his dry lips. His subordinate answered with the utmost respect.
“There’s a vessel fifty zhang away.”
“A vessel? Brothers from our alliance?”
“No.”
Then there was only one possibility.
On the mighty Yangtze, there were only those who robbed and those who were robbed.
“How many?”
“A little over fifty. It doesn’t appear to be a merchant ship, either.”
“I see.”
“What should we do?”
“Deal with it quietly. Don’t cause a commotion.”
With that, the man closed his eyes again.
A warship sent by the imperial court might have warranted his personal attention. This matter was far too trivial.
As always, his subordinates would carry out his orders.
Interrupting my meditation over something so insignificant.
The man let go of his irritation and sank back into contemplation.
It had already been more than ten years since he reached the Peak realm. Now, however, an invisible wall stood in his path.
He had tried consuming stolen elixirs and even smoking opium, which was said to reveal sights one had never experienced before. All of it had been a waste of time.
This is going to be difficult at this rate.
Water Dragon Stronghold was one of the ten largest strongholds in the Yangtze River Channel League.
Thanks to its location in Sichuan, through which vast quantities of goods passed, it was known as one of the most lucrative strongholds in the alliance.
But the man had only just entered his forties, and his ambitions were greater still.
Alliance Leader.
His goal was to become the master of the Yangtze River Channel League—and, with it, the king of the Yangtze.
Anyone unaware of his circumstances might scoff at such a preposterous ambition, but the man possessed both the ability and the background to make it possible.
The proof was that he had become lord of Water Dragon Stronghold more than ten years ago, when he was barely past thirty.
“Whooo...”
The man drew a long breath. As he drew in and circulated the natural qi permeating the air, his sharpened senses gathered information from his surroundings.
The damp smell of water. The swift ship gradually slowing beneath him. Even the shouts and laughter of his subordinates.
“Hahaha! Running into us means you bastards have the worst luck imaginable. Who owns this ship?”
“I-I do, sir.”
“You launched your ship without permission from us heroes. I assume you’re prepared for the consequences?”
“I-I’ve committed a crime worthy of death by failing to recognize the heroes of the Yangtze. This isn’t much, but please accept it as a token of my sincerity...”
Wham! Crash!
A blow landed, and someone went sprawling. The man’s brow furrowed at the shrill screams that followed.
I told them not to make a commotion.
No martial artist enjoyed having his training interrupted. His men might be rough and ignorant, but he had not expected them to be incapable of following such a simple order.
The man’s eyes snapped open. He was about to spring to his feet when—
Boom! Crack! Thud! Th-th-th-thump!
A savage barrage of noise erupted, and then everything fell silent.
It seems to be over.
Somewhat mollified, the man closed his eyes again.
Or he would have, if not for the question that suddenly crossed his mind.
But...why is it so quiet?
Step. Step. Step.
Low, resonant footsteps approached the cabin.
At last, someone stopped directly outside the door and spoke through a yawn.
“What are you doing? Aren’t you coming out?”
An unfamiliar voice. He had never heard it before.
Alarm bells rang in the man’s mind.
An enemy!
Everything happened in an instant.
The man shot to his feet and streaked toward the door like a beam of light.
His fist, carrying enough power to smash apart a massive sailing ship, shattered the thick wooden door and hurtled toward the enemy beyond it.
And then—
Kraaaang!
A deafening boom and its aftershock rocked the swift ship.
The man stared wide-eyed at his enemy.
More precisely, at the palm that had stopped his fist.
A seething voice escaped between his clenched teeth.
“Who are you?”
“Me?”
The young man answered with a faint smile.
“The owner of this ship.”
Flames poured from the eyes of the man known as the Ship-Fire Boy, Mu Song.
“How dare a little pup like you... I’ll show you the sky.”
I kicked the leg of the middle-aged man sprawled flat on his back across the deck.
“How long are you going to keep staring at the sky? Get up. Quickly.”
Focus returned to his hazy eyes. The middle-aged man propped up his upper body and stared at me with a dazed expression.
“H-how did you defeat the Ship-Breaking Fist so easily...?”
“Wait. Ship-Breaking Fist?”
Right. Now I remembered.
I had definitely seen that martial art somewhere before, but the memory had been so hazy that I couldn’t place it.
Intrigued, I looked the middle-aged man up and down.
“What’s your relationship with Cheol Soo?”
“Cheol... Soo? Who are you talking about?”
“You know. Cheol Soo. Cheol Soo...”
Gung Gibang quietly cut in.
“The Iron-Water Divine Dragon.”
“Right. The Iron-Water Divine Dragon. When I met him at the Star-Array Grand Banquet, he kept going on about the Ship-Breaking Fist too.”
If I remembered correctly, it had been during the first preliminary round.
He had spouted some bullshit about how I should consider it an honor to witness the Ship-Breaking Fist, so I had smashed a cliff apart with the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
I heard he forfeited right afterward and went straight home.
It had happened only a month ago here in the Murim, but after everything I had been through, it felt like the distant past.
In any case, the middle-aged man before me had learned the same martial art as the Iron-Water Divine Dragon. He was also a Peak master, a cut above Cheol Soo in skill.
After blinking at me like a goldfish, he stammered in a trembling voice.
“W-were you acquainted with my youngest?”
“Your youngest?”
“The Cheol Soo you mentioned is the youngest of us three martial brothers. He’s the third Disciple, and I’m the second.”
Huh. I had heard that before too.
People had gone on endlessly about the Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s Master.
“Then, could it be...?”
The middle-aged man nodded.
“That’s right. My Master is the man known as the Seafaring King.”
“Jang Bogo!”
“No, it’s nothing. I was just talking to myself.”
“But why are you suddenly being so polite...?”
“Of course I should be polite. You’re my Senior in the martial world and a hero of the Yangtze River Channel League. Please, feel free to speak casually to me.”
To be honest, the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance both looked like criminal organizations full of social misfits to me.
But...
If he’s the Seafaring King’s Disciple, that changes things.
The Seafaring King would hardly be pleased to hear that I had beaten his Disciple black and blue to steal his swift ship.
At least with the Green Forest Alliance’s Heavenly Axe, I had been fully justified, so they couldn’t complain. In this case, though, it would be better to smooth things over.
I helped the bewildered middle-aged man to his feet and brushed the dust from his clothes.
“Look how dirty your clothes got. What a disaster. You’ll have to get them dry-cleaned.”
“W-why are you suddenly acting like this?”

“I told you to speak casually with me. There was an unfortunate incident because of a minor misunderstanding on my part, but if I’d known you belonged to the renowned Yangtze River Channel League, I would have settled everything amicably through conversation. You understand, right?”
“...Really?”
“Of course. Do I look like the sort of ill-bred junior who would lie to his Senior?”
The middle-aged man stared at me for a moment, then cautiously shifted his gaze upward.
I followed his eyes and saw a flag rising high above the fast ship.
The words emblazoned across it were large enough to read from a hundred meters away.
Yangtze River Channel League.
I finally spoke in a grave voice.
“I’m illiterate. I can’t read.”
Yeah. I knew he wouldn’t buy it.
I clenched my fist and looked at the middle-aged man.
“Let’s just settle this amicably.”
“...Very well.”
Whoooosh.
The swift ship sliced powerfully through the water. Cheongpung, who had been sitting at the bow enjoying the wind, came racing over and began chattering excitedly.
“Benefactor! It’s so refreshing!”
“Of course it is. It’s still early spring.”
“There are so many fish too!”
“There should be. It’s a river.”
“There are so many people on the ship over there, and they’re getting beaten so much!”
“Of course they’re getting beaten—wait, what?”
What had I just heard?
As I doubted my ears, Cheongpung answered with an innocent smile.
“Every time the captain swings that huge oar, their skin tears and blood sprays everywhere!”
It seemed Mu Song had lined up his subordinates and was beating them one after another with an oar.
They had mistakenly attacked a passenger ship and suffered a tremendous humiliation, so I supposed it was understandable.
“Pretend you didn’t see anything. You saw nothing.”
“Can I ask him to let me hit one of them just once?”
“No. Please don’t.”
Ignoring the surrounding sailors, who were staring at Cheongpung as if wondering whether he was even human, I turned to Gung Gibang.
“Hey, if you knew, you should’ve told me beforehand.”
“Am I some kind of fortune-teller? How am I supposed to know who’s stationed at every single stronghold?”
Gung Gibang stared at me incredulously, then muttered under his breath.
“The crazy bastard is the one who charged in after seeing the Yangtze River Channel League’s flag. Bit late to complain now.”
“Hey, I can hear you.”
“You were supposed to. You don’t fucking listen even when I tell you something. What the hell do you expect me to do?”
“Damn, you’ve gotten awfully bold. What do you think of this insubordination, Mujin?”
Hyuk Mujin answered.
“Uweeeeeegh!”
“...Your seasickness is pretty bad. Get some rest.”
For someone who was supposedly a Supreme First Rate master, he was still in terrible shape.
Cheongpung watched Hyuk Mujin cling to the railing and dry-heave again and again, then twisted enviously from side to side.
“I want to get seasick too. I’ve never tried it before.”
Lucky you. So many things you still want to experience.
Maybe it was because I was on a boat, but today I was experiencing the power of the Bermuda Triangle all over again.
Am I going to end up adrift on the Yangtze?
As that thought crossed my mind, the hulking Mu Song landed on the deck using a light, elusive movement technique completely at odds with his massive build.
He tossed the blood-soaked oar to a subordinate and approached me.
“Are you uncomfortable anywhere?”
“Ah, yes. I’m comfortable, Senior.”
Mu Song glanced at Hyuk Mujin, who was still dry-heaving.
“That fellow doesn’t look very comfortable.”
“That’s all right. I’m comfortable.”
“Is there a problem?”
“No, no. In any case, you’re headed to Chengdu?”
“Yes. How long will it take?”
“We’re currently at Guang’an, which could be considered the entrance to Sichuan. At this speed, three days. If we catch a favorable wind, two days will be more than enough.”
That was about the same speed as traveling with a movement technique, perhaps even a little faster.
An ordinary vessel would have taken much longer, but this was one of the swift ships for which the Yangtze River Channel League was renowned.
I sincerely clasped my hands in a respectful salute.
“Thank you.”
“Nonsense. It’s no great trouble.”
Mu Song was being so cooperative because he had learned who our group was.
I was the Disciple of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang. Gung Gibang was the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect. Cheongpung had inherited the true transmission of the Sword Saint, Mae Jonghak.
And finally, the great Jin Family of Taiyuan’s...
Ah, let’s leave that last one out.
“In any case, Chengdu is close, so rest comfortably while you wait. This Mu Song has the rivers flowing through Sichuan firmly under his control.”
“Wow. That’s impressive, Senior.”
“Without my orders, no one dares do anything foolish on the Yangtze. Hahahaha!”
At that exact moment, faint cries drifted over from far away.
“Aaaah!”
“Kill them all and take everything!”
I muttered as the distant screams reached us.
“They seem pretty good at doing foolish things...”
Mu Song’s face flushed bright red.
“How dare anyone run wild on the Yangtze!”

chapters.title: Chapter 332
paragraphs: “Who dares run wild on the Yangtze?”
Not that I expected an answer from all the way over there.
Letting Mu Song’s shout go in one ear and out the other, I circulated my internal energy and sharpened my eyesight.
The distance was easily over two hundred zhang. But my vision had improved enough that you could call me a human eagle, allowing me to take in the entire scene at a glance.
That’s...
River bandits.
Two ships far larger than the swift ship we were riding had surrounded one tiny boat. Black specks that looked like arrows and harpoons flew toward it without pause.
Then I spotted the flags fluttering from the bandits’ ships, and my gaze naturally shifted toward Mu Song.
“I don’t know what kind of scum they are, but they picked the wrong target. You there! Immediately deal with those rootless bastards... What’s wrong?”
“Uh, Senior. I’m not quite sure how to put this.”
“What?”
“That unaffiliated rabble looks like they belong to the Yangtze River Channel League.”
After a brief silence, Mu Song roared, “That’s impossible!”
“No, it’s entirely possible. Their flag says ‘Yangtze River Channel League’ in very bold lettering.”
“Didn’t you say you were illiterate a moment ago?”
Was he a river bandit or a razor? He was surprisingly sharp.
Instead of panicking, I hardened my expression.
“I’m a fast learner. Besides, is that really important right now? Every moment counts! We need to punish those lawless thugs disrupting order on the Yangtze!”
Mu Song looked as if he wanted to punish me first, but he wholeheartedly agreed with my point.
“Exactly. In this day and age, how dare they commit murder on the Yangtze... I’ll kill every last one of them with a single palm strike!”

It was a little depressing to hear that from a river-bandit chief, but according to something Gung Gibang had casually told me, Mu Song belonged to the moderate faction within the Yangtze River Channel League.
His philosophy was that taking people’s money was enough. Why take their lives too?
He was still taking their money.

Come to think of it, they were all much the same. Still, in a Murim where people drew their swords at the slightest provocation, he really was conscientious for a top-tier river bandit—especially one who was a Disciple of the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League.
“Raise the red flag!”
At Mu Song’s booming command, the five swift ships raised the red flags that signaled battle and surged forward.
Whoooooosh!
The sails swelled taut in a timely gust of wind. Built for maximum speed, the swift ships sliced through the current and devoured the distance between us.
The two-hundred-zhang gap shrank by half in an instant. Among the river bandits preparing for close-quarters battle, urgent shouts rang out.
“S-swift ships!”
“Mu Song of Water Dragon Stronghold is here! Everyone, retreat!”
But Mu Song was not about to let them escape.
Barely fifty zhang now separated us from the enemy. A fierce light flashed in his eyes as he glared at the bandits scrambling back to their ships.
“Let’s at least see what you bastards look like!”
Grinding his teeth, Mu Song snatched up a massive harpoon, kicked off the stern, and leaped into the air.
Boom!
The sturdy wooden deck splintered, and the Yangtze swallowed Mu Song’s body as it arced through the air.
Isn’t that dangerous?
Mistaking the Yangtze for some valley stream in Gangwon Province would be a serious mistake.
Although this was a branch of the Yangtze that split away from the main channel, it was as wide and deep as the sea, and the current was viciously rough.
Even Hyuk Mujin, who had been dry-heaving, asked with a pale face, “Shouldn’t we rescue him—uweeegh!”
“Gibang, pat that bastard on the back.”
“I’m not his nanny...”
Of course he wasn’t. Who would hire a beggar as a nanny?
Despite his grumbling, Gung Gibang pounded Hyuk Mujin on the back.

“There’s a limit to ignorance. Do you think a river bandit chief would jump into the Yangtze without learning water-based martial arts? Especially a Disciple of the Seafaring King, who no one can match in the water?”
“Oh, right.”
“I don’t know who those bastards are, but they’ve tangled with the wrong man. There’ll be a string of funerals today. Tsk, tsk.”
Gung Gibang’s prediction was accurate.
A few seconds later, Mu Song surfaced more than ten zhang ahead of the swift ship.
Spla-aaash!
Every time his massive body traced a supple curve like a wave, he shot forward like a water-skier. My jaw dropped.
“Unbelievable!”
He was even faster than the swift ship.
The sight of Mu Song charging toward the enemy vessel like a fish-man made my own blood boil.
“Since it’s come to this, I’m going too!”
Gung Gibang shrieked, “Going where?”
“Uweeegh!”
“Benefactor, me too!”
“Get lost, all of you! The Grand Line is calling me! The Yangtze is calling me!”
Breaking free of the Bermuda Triangle, I raced across the deck and launched myself from the bow with all my strength.
Boom! Craaack!
The bow shattered under the force. Weightlessness swept over me as the wind slammed into my face.
Whoooooosh!
“Freedom! Freedom!”
I became a bird.
Then I lost momentum and began to fall.
“Senior!”
“Gasp!”
Tap!
I landed lightly on the back of a passing fish-man.
Angle, speed, distance, landing point. This result was only possible because I had calculated everything perfectly.
“Whew. Per-fect.”
“What part of that was perfect!”
Mu Song roared at his unexpected passenger, but what could he do? I was already aboard.
I glared at the river bandits frantically turning their ships around.
“Let’s go!”
“Damn it! Since it’s come to this, we’ll charge straight into the ship!”
“That’s my Senior!”
“We’ll settle this when this is over!”

“Yaaaargh!”

Powerful qi gathered at the tips of both weapons.
Whoooooosh!

Kwaaang! Rumble-rumble-rumble!
A thunderous roar erupted with an enormous shock wave.
“Mujin.”
At my solemn voice, Hyuk Mujin finally stopped retching and answered with a pale face.
“Yes?”
“I think I was born to be a river bandit.”
“What kind of nonsense is that?”
“Do you want to hear yourself wail?”
“I misspoke because I’m not feeling well. Now that I think about it, the role suits you perfectly.”
“Right?”
“Yes. I can still vividly see you recklessly—no, courageously—smashing straight through that ship.”
“What a rush.”
I nodded smugly and gazed at the slowly sinking ship.
On one side, Mu Song’s men had divided themselves among the small ferryboats carried aboard the swift ships and were pulling floundering river bandits from the water.
On the other ship, the river bandits hung their heads as they were transferred to the swift ships one after another, bound together with ropes.
One ship sunk. The other captured.
An excellent result for my first naval battle.
Originally, I had planned to sink both ships. But the river bandits lost their will to fight as soon as they saw the ship carrying their comrades sink, and they surrendered.
Of course, surrender did not lead to a particularly happy ending.
“How dare scum like you tarnish the name of the Yangtze River Channel League?”
Moderate or not, Mu Song was still a martial artist who had no qualms about killing and a river bandit who had spent his life on the unforgiving Yangtze.
Once he snapped, there was no stopping him.
“Throw them to the fish.”
The tightly bound river bandits opened their eyes wide.
“T-this can’t be happening!”
“Stronghold Lord! Please, anything but that!”
Mu Song answered them with an icy stare.
“Stronghold Lord? You belong to a different stronghold. Why would I be your Stronghold Lord? And don’t worry. Your chief will be joining you soon, so you won’t be lonely.”
“We were wrong! Please, just this once...!”

“If you were willing to invade Water Dragon Stronghold’s territory and do something like this, you should have been prepared for the consequences. Do you know why I had my men pull you out of the water? So I could punish you with my own hands.”
Mu Song jerked his chin, and his subordinates stepped forward and dragged the river bandits away.
The river bandits screamed as death closed in, but their limbs were already bound. One splash after another rang out as they sank beneath the surface.
Cheongpung bit his lip, his face pale, as more than fifty river bandits were drowned alive before his eyes.
No wonder.
Someone who was afraid even of blood could hardly endure a sight like this.
Despite myself, I grew concerned and spoke to him quietly.
“Close your eyes. I’ll tell you when it’s over.”
“No, Benefactor. I’m fine.”
“They may deserve to die, but you’re still watching people die. It might be hard to look at.”
“No.”
“Hm?”
Cheongpung’s eyes twitched.
“I’m just... trying to get used to it.”
Get used to it? I had never expected to hear something like that from Cheongpung.
Cheongpung was kind by nature, and unlike other young men his age, he had not been tainted by the ways of the world.
Perhaps that was why he feared blood and had always avoided killing. But now, I sensed a steely resolve within him.
Was it the battle with the Blood Lord at Mount Song? Did it begin then?
His first encounter with the fear and terror of death must have awakened something inside him.
Part of me was proud of him. Another part felt bitter.
It can’t be helped. This is the Murim.
That was right. This was the Murim—and the storm clouds of war were gathering.
He could not remain an innocent mountain youth forever in a place like this.
If this helped him grow... maybe it was for the best.
Cheongpung fought to keep his eyes from closing. At last, he let out a sigh of relief.
The river bandits had finally been dealt with.
But it was not over yet.
“Hwang Tae-gu. Now it’s your turn.”
Mu Song’s low voice rang across the deck.
Unlike the other river bandits, a man in his fifties had been forced to his knees before Mu Song, tightly bound in chains.
Hwang Tae-gu was the mastermind behind this attack.
Gung Gibang muttered as he watched him.
“I was wondering why Mu Song was here. So that’s what happened.”
“What do you mean?”
“Even the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families have their factions. Imagine how bad it must be in a band of river bandits like the Yangtze River Channel League.”
“So this Hwang Tae-gu lost a factional struggle?”
“He was famous for being greedy and violent. Just a few years ago, he lorded over the Yangtze in Sichuan... There’s no doubt Mu Song pushed him out.”
So the loser of an internal power struggle had gone rogue and finally gotten himself caught?
As I considered that, Hwang Tae-gu opened his mouth.
“I have nothing to say to some ignorant young punk. Kill me.”
“You’ll get your wish whether you say anything or not. But why did you do this?”
“Heh heh. What a stupid question. I’m a river bandit. What’s wrong with a river bandit killing and taking what he wants?”
“There’s no reasoning with you. I should have killed you long ago.”
Mu Song’s face hardened, and he raised his harpoon.
“Would Great Hero Mu Song, the Ship-Fire Boy, please wait a moment?”
A voice suddenly rang out, piercing the ears of everyone present.
