chapters.title: Chapter 333
paragraphs: “Great Hero Mu Song, the Ship-Fire Boy, could you wait a moment?”
I wanted to give the owner of that voice a standing ovation.
Think about it. Who could say something like that in a situation like this?
Especially when the person they were addressing was a river-bandit chief who had thrown around fifty river bandits to the fish in five minutes.
But who was it?
Judging by the way he called Mu Song a Great Hero, he obviously isn’t in this line of work.
Mu Song’s subordinates called him Stronghold Lord or Chief, so that ruled them out. None of my companions, myself included, had said a word, so that ruled us out too.
That left...
The passengers who were attacked by the river bandits.
Everyone else had clearly reached the same conclusion.

My companions and I—even the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold. Every head turned in the same direction, toward the twenty passengers who had moved onto the swift ship when Hwang Tae-gu’s attack left their boat listing.
“Who is it? Step forward.”
At Mu Song’s fierce glare, his harpoon hanging low in one hand, his subordinates hurriedly cleared a path. A lone figure stood at the end of it.
“It was me.”
I had guessed as much from the voice, but he was quite young. No, he looked almost boyish.
Twenty at most, if I’m being generous?
Boy suited him better than young man. Flustered by everyone’s attention, he hesitated, then awkwardly clasped his hands together.
“I-I’m Mungyeong.”
“Mungyeong?”
Mu Song frowned.
“Never heard the name. And from the look of you, you aren’t a martial artist.”
Mu Song had a good eye.
The boy, Mungyeong, had the aura of an ordinary commoner. Nothing more, nothing less.
Mungyeong swallowed nervously under our scrutiny and answered,
“T-That’s right. I’m merely a medical apprentice still in training. I have no connection to the Murim.”
“A medical apprentice? Then how do you know me?”
“How could I not know of the righteous boatman on the Yangtze in Sichuan who keeps such a strict rein on bloodshed?”
Now that was some serious flattery.
Mu Song’s mouth twitched as he went from a river-bandit chief who controlled Sichuan’s waterways and shook down travelers to a righteous boatman in the blink of an eye.
“Hmm. Is that so?”
“Wealth comes and goes, but a man has only one life. Those who know how many lives were lost on the Yangtze until just a few years ago call you the Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness.”
“Ahem. There’s no need to go that far. Being called the Hero of the Yangtze is enough for me.”
What a load of horseshit...
Mu Song was reasonably sensible, but he was still a river bandit. Keeping his thuggery within reasonable bounds didn’t make him a model citizen.
But the young medical apprentice seemed to see things differently.
“My parents died tragically on the Yangtze more than ten years ago. If Great Hero Mu Song hadn’t saved me, I would have met the same fate.”
“Oh, dear. That’s unfortunate. But if it was more than ten years ago...”
“That’s right.”
Mungyeong continued in a trembling voice.
“The man kneeling before you is my parents’ killer.”
“Good heavens.”
The river bandits and passengers who had been listening intently let out low groans. Mu Song nodded as if he understood and spoke.
“Now I understand why you asked me to stop. Though it goes against the League regulations, I understand how you feel. I’ll give you the chance.”
“You mean you’ll let me decide whether he lives or dies?”
“Of course.”
But Mungyeong’s answer defied everyone’s expectations—including mine.
“Then... please let him live.”
Mu Song had been about to hand Mungyeong the harpoon he was holding. Even Hwang Tae-gu, who had already closed his eyes as though resigned to everything, snapped them open and stared at Mungyeong.
“W-What did you say?”
When Mu Song asked again in confusion, Mungyeong bowed at the waist.

“I desperately wish to avenge my parents, but I am a medical apprentice. How can one who deals in life bring about death? I beg you to cripple his martial arts and punish him according to strict law, so that he can never commit evil again.”

“If we do as you ask, he’ll be taken to League headquarters. He deserves to die, but with all the connections he’s made over the years, he may manage to save his life. Wouldn’t it be better to take your revenge with your own hands, right here?”

“I have no connection to the Murim, but I have often heard that, for a martial artist, losing one’s martial arts is the same as death. I may not have killed him, but would that not be as good as killing him? And...”
Mungyeong gazed at Hwang Tae-gu with clear eyes.
“This is not about personal revenge, but the greater good. If the Yangtze River Channel League punishes him itself, would that not serve as a warning to others who commit such slaughter?”
Not a trace of trembling remained in the boy’s resolute voice. His words held a conviction that made those listening nod along.
Exclamations rose from the crowd.
“Well, I’ll be. That young fellow is something else.”
“If it were me, I’d have shoved that harpoon straight into his chest.”
“He’s remarkable in more ways than one. He’ll make a fine physician.”
Mu Song also seemed deeply impressed by Mungyeong’s well-reasoned argument. He nodded admiringly and stepped in front of Hwang Tae-gu.
“If your ears work, you heard him. What do you think?”
“I-I’ll survive, and I’ll tear every one of you apart!”
The killing intent flashing in Hwang Tae-gu’s eyes did not last long.
Thud!
“Guh!”
Mu Song’s toe drove into the spot beneath Hwang Tae-gu’s navel—the place known as the dantian.
Mu Song looked down coldly at Hwang Tae-gu, who toppled backward, vomiting blood.
“Go ahead and survive, then. See if you can carry out your threat. With your dantian shattered, though, you’ll hardly be alive even if you live.”
With a sharp crack of displaced air, Mu Song’s foot lashed out and struck Hwang Tae-gu’s dantian again.
Whooooom! Crack!
“Guh! N-No!”
By the time Hwang Tae-gu’s scream echoed hollowly across the deck, everything was already over.
Ssshhh.
I can feel it.
Qi streamed from his twitching seven apertures and scattered into the air.
When a cup holding water breaks, the water spills out. The moment his qi-sea acupoint was destroyed, the internal energy stored in his dantian disappeared.
“You bastards! I swear I’ll—!”
The Peak master who had once commanded countless ships and ruled the Yangtze in Sichuan no longer existed.
Hwang Tae-gu was now nothing more than a powerless man in his fifties. He kept shouting until Mu Song silenced him with a Pressure-Point Strike, leaving his entire body rigid.
“What a noisy bastard. Throw him somewhere out of the way. We’ll escort him to League headquarters later.”
“Yes.”
A bald, copper-skinned river bandit who looked like Diglett hoisted Hwang Tae-gu onto his back and disappeared. For the moment, the matter was settled.
Mu Song scratched the back of his head and looked around at the crowd.
“Well, this is awkward. I’ve shown you all an ugly sight. I offer my sincere apologies to everyone who suffered through this incident.”
So a good bandit defeated a bad bandit?
In any case, the commoners whose lives had been saved by Water Dragon Stronghold bowed repeatedly.
“Oh, no, not at all. Without the Heroes of the Yangtze, we would have been done for.”
“We don’t know how we could ever repay this debt...”
“Perhaps the Primordial Heavenly Venerable was watching over us. Not a single person died, so you needn’t worry.”
Huh? Not one person died?
At those words, I looked over the passengers.
It’s true.
There were injured people here and there, but no corpses.
Mu Song and I had arrived before the battle turned into a full-scale melee, but the river bandits had definitely fired arrows and harpoons at them from a distance.
How had a mere twenty commoners all survived?
It didn’t take long for me to get my answer.
“If that young medical apprentice hadn’t been here, we might all have died.”
“Indeed. How could anyone remain so calm in a situation like that? He’s truly remarkable.”
The conversation I overheard went like this.
When the passengers spotted the approaching river bandits and panicked, Mungyeong stepped forward. He had them tear up the deck and use the planks as shields, then ordered them to break the mast.
Tearing up the deck is one thing, but breaking the mast?
An ordinary person would have thought first of rowing for their life and escaping. Mungyeong had done the opposite.
He broke the sails and left the boat’s fate to the violent current of the Yangtze, which heaved and rolled like a whirlpool.
And it worked.
I knew roughly how naval battles worked.
After firing from a distance, the usual tactic was to close in and ram the other ship, or hook it with ropes and board it for close combat.
But if the target had completely lost the ability to steer and was spinning and pitching wildly, finding an opening wouldn’t be easy. That was how Mungyeong had bought them time.
Well, look at this guy.
Then there was his decision regarding Hwang Tae-gu. This was no ordinary clever boy.
Perhaps he felt my gaze. Mungyeong, who had been smiling awkwardly at all the praise directed his way, flinched.
“Y-Young Hero. Did you need something from me?”
“What would I need? Judging by your age, you could be my little brother. I was just looking at you because you did something impressive.”
“Th-That’s too much praise.”
“From what I heard, that was pretty bold. How did you come up with it?”
“Although I’m training to become a medical apprentice now, before my parents passed away, I used to read all kinds of miscellaneous books.”
“Miscellaneous books?”
“Yes. Believe it or not, my family comes from a humble military household. My grandfather was also a military officer who received a stipend from the court.”
He was trying to hide both his faint wariness of a stranger and a quiet sense of pride.
Seen this way, he wasn’t much different from any other boy his age.
But something about him didn’t sit right.
I studied Mungyeong carefully and muttered inwardly.
Skill, activate Qi Sense.
Ding.
Along with the familiar chime, information about him rose into the air.
System Lv. 6 Mungyeong
“I guessed wrong.”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing. Stay healthy, eat well, and grow up strong.”
“Y-Yes...”
Clicking my tongue inwardly, I turned away from the bewildered Mungyeong.
Mu Song, who had been watching, spoke to me quietly.
“What was that about?”
“Nothing important. I just took a personal interest in him.”
“Junior, do you happen to have a taste for men?”
You fucking bastard...
When he saw my expression, Mu Song cleared his throat and changed the subject.
“Ahem. In any case, we should continue on our way. The current is rough, but the wind is favorable, so we should reach Xi’an soon.”
“What about the others? Their original boat was listing too.”
“The others? Ah, my men will take them somewhere safe.”
Mu Song chuckled and added,
“Of course, we’ll accept a small token of their appreciation.”
Saving their lives, then shaking them down for money. Was that clever or stupid?
I was briefly struck speechless by this novel form of creative economics when—
“W-Wait a moment.”
“Hm?”
It was Mungyeong. Glancing around nervously, he fidgeted with his fingers before speaking.
“Um, did you say you were going to Xi’an?”
“That’s right. Why?”
Mungyeong gasped, then spilled out his words in a rush.

“The thing is, I happen to be on my way to Xi’an too. If you would give me a ride just this once, I’ll repay this kindness even beyond the grave, remember it to my very bones, and even if this body dies and dies, dies a thousand times over and turns to white bones, I will never forget—”
What is this?
I let out a long sigh at the Jeong Mong-ju villain.
“Fine. Get on.”
“Thank you!”
As Mungyeong hurried off to gather his luggage, Mu Song muttered under his breath,
“Wait, this is my ship...”
Yeah. No.

sentences.text: “Great Hero Mu Song, the Ship-Fire Boy, could you wait a moment?”
I wanted to give the owner of that voice a standing ovation.
Think about it.
Who could say something like that in a situation like this?
Especially when the person they were addressing was a river-bandit chief who had thrown around fifty river bandits to the fish in five minutes.
But who was it?
Judging by the way he called Mu Song a Great Hero, he obviously isn’t in this line of work.
Mu Song’s subordinates called him Stronghold Lord or Chief, so that ruled them out.
None of my companions, myself included, had said a word, so that ruled us out too.
That left...
The passengers who were attacked by the river bandits.
Everyone else had clearly reached the same conclusion.
My companions and I—even the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold.
Every head turned in the same direction, toward the twenty passengers who had moved onto the swift ship when Hwang Tae-gu’s attack left their boat listing.
“Who is it?
Step forward.”
At Mu Song’s fierce glare, his harpoon hanging low in one hand, his subordinates hurriedly cleared a path.
A lone figure stood at the end of it.
“It was me.”
I had guessed as much from the voice, but he was quite young.
No, he looked almost boyish.
Twenty at most, if I’m being generous?
Boy suited him better than young man.
Flustered by everyone’s attention, he hesitated, then awkwardly clasped his hands together.
“I-I’m Mungyeong.”
“Mungyeong?”
Mu Song frowned.
“Never heard the name.
And from the look of you, you aren’t a martial artist.”
Mu Song had a good eye.
The boy, Mungyeong, had the aura of an ordinary commoner.
Nothing more, nothing less.
Mungyeong swallowed nervously under our scrutiny and answered,
“T-That’s right.
I’m merely a medical apprentice still in training.
I have no connection to the Murim.”
“A medical apprentice?
Then how do you know me?”
“How could I not know of the righteous boatman on the Yangtze in Sichuan who keeps such a strict rein on bloodshed?”
Now that was some serious flattery.
Mu Song’s mouth twitched as he went from a river-bandit chief who controlled Sichuan’s waterways and shook down travelers to a righteous boatman in the blink of an eye.
“Hmm.
Is that so?”
“Wealth comes and goes, but a man has only one life.
Those who know how many lives were lost on the Yangtze until just a few years ago call you the Great Hero of Benevolence and Righteousness.”
“Ahem.
There’s no need to go that far.
Being called the Hero of the Yangtze is enough for me.”
What a load of horseshit...
Mu Song was reasonably sensible, but he was still a river bandit.
Keeping his thuggery within reasonable bounds didn’t make him a model citizen.
But the young medical apprentice seemed to see things differently.
“My parents died tragically on the Yangtze more than ten years ago.
If Great Hero Mu Song hadn’t saved me, I would have met the same fate.”
“Oh, dear.
That’s unfortunate.
But if it was more than ten years ago...”
“That’s right.”
Mungyeong continued in a trembling voice.
“The man kneeling before you is my parents’ killer.”
“Good heavens.”
The river bandits and passengers who had been listening intently let out low groans.
Mu Song nodded as if he understood and spoke.
“Now I understand why you asked me to stop.
Though it goes against the League regulations, I understand how you feel.
I’ll give you the chance.”
“You mean you’ll let me decide whether he lives or dies?”
“Of course.”
But Mungyeong’s answer defied everyone’s expectations—including mine.
“Then... please let him live.”
Mu Song had been about to hand Mungyeong the harpoon he was holding.
Even Hwang Tae-gu, who had already closed his eyes as though resigned to everything, snapped them open and stared at Mungyeong.
“W-What did you say?”
When Mu Song asked again in confusion, Mungyeong bowed at the waist.
“I desperately wish to avenge my parents, but I am a medical apprentice.
How can one who deals in life bring about death?
I beg you to cripple his martial arts and punish him according to strict law, so that he can never commit evil again.”
“If we do as you ask, he’ll be taken to League headquarters.
He deserves to die, but with all the connections he’s made over the years, he may manage to save his life.
Wouldn’t it be better to take your revenge with your own hands, right here?”
“I have no connection to the Murim, but I have often heard that, for a martial artist, losing one’s martial arts is the same as death.
I may not have killed him, but would that not be as good as killing him?
And...”
Mungyeong gazed at Hwang Tae-gu with clear eyes.
“This is not about personal revenge, but the greater good.
If the Yangtze River Channel League punishes him itself, would that not serve as a warning to others who commit such slaughter?”
Not a trace of trembling remained in the boy’s resolute voice.
His words held a conviction that made those listening nod along.
Exclamations rose from the crowd.
“Well, I’ll be.
That young fellow is something else.”
“If it were me, I’d have shoved that harpoon straight into his chest.”
“He’s remarkable in more ways than one.
He’ll make a fine physician.”
Mu Song also seemed deeply impressed by Mungyeong’s well-reasoned argument.
He nodded admiringly and stepped in front of Hwang Tae-gu.
“If your ears work, you heard him.
What do you think?”
“I-I’ll survive, and I’ll tear every one of you apart!”
The killing intent flashing in Hwang Tae-gu’s eyes did not last long.
Thud!
“Guh!”
Mu Song’s toe drove into the spot beneath Hwang Tae-gu’s navel—the place known as the dantian.
Mu Song looked down coldly at Hwang Tae-gu, who toppled backward, vomiting blood.
“Go ahead and survive, then.
See if you can carry out your threat.
With your dantian shattered, though, you’ll hardly be alive even if you live.”
With a sharp crack of displaced air, Mu Song’s foot lashed out and struck Hwang Tae-gu’s dantian again.
Whooooom!
Crack!
“Guh!
N-No!”
By the time Hwang Tae-gu’s scream echoed hollowly across the deck, everything was already over.
Ssshhh.
I can feel it.
Qi streamed from his twitching seven apertures and scattered into the air.
When a cup holding water breaks, the water spills out.
The moment his qi-sea acupoint was destroyed, the internal energy stored in his dantian disappeared.
“You bastards!
I swear I’ll—!”
The Peak master who had once commanded countless ships and ruled the Yangtze in Sichuan no longer existed.
Hwang Tae-gu was now nothing more than a powerless man in his fifties.
He kept shouting until Mu Song silenced him with a Pressure-Point Strike, leaving his entire body rigid.
“What a noisy bastard.
Throw him somewhere out of the way.
We’ll escort him to League headquarters later.”
“Yes.”
A bald, copper-skinned river bandit who looked like Diglett hoisted Hwang Tae-gu onto his back and disappeared.
For the moment, the matter was settled.
Mu Song scratched the back of his head and looked around at the crowd.
“Well, this is awkward.
I’ve shown you all an ugly sight.
I offer my sincere apologies to everyone who suffered through this incident.”
So a good bandit defeated a bad bandit?
In any case, the commoners whose lives had been saved by Water Dragon Stronghold bowed repeatedly.
“Oh, no, not at all.
Without the Heroes of the Yangtze, we would have been done for.”
“We don’t know how we could ever repay this debt...”
“Perhaps the Primordial Heavenly Venerable was watching over us.
Not a single person died, so you needn’t worry.”
Huh?
Not one person died?
At those words, I looked over the passengers.
It’s true.
There were injured people here and there, but no corpses.
Mu Song and I had arrived before the battle turned into a full-scale melee, but the river bandits had definitely fired arrows and harpoons at them from a distance.
How had a mere twenty commoners all survived?
It didn’t take long for me to get my answer.
“If that young medical apprentice hadn’t been here, we might all have died.”
“Indeed.
How could anyone remain so calm in a situation like that?
He’s truly remarkable.”
The conversation I overheard went like this.
When the passengers spotted the approaching river bandits and panicked, Mungyeong stepped forward.
He had them tear up the deck and use the planks as shields, then ordered them to break the mast.
Tearing up the deck is one thing, but breaking the mast?
An ordinary person would have thought first of rowing for their life and escaping.
Mungyeong had done the opposite.
He broke the sails and left the boat’s fate to the violent current of the Yangtze, which heaved and rolled like a whirlpool.
And it worked.
I knew roughly how naval battles worked.
After firing from a distance, the usual tactic was to close in and ram the other ship, or hook it with ropes and board it for close combat.
But if the target had completely lost the ability to steer and was spinning and pitching wildly, finding an opening wouldn’t be easy.
That was how Mungyeong had bought them time.

chapters.title: Chapter 334
paragraphs: Time flowed like a river.
It was a common, well-worn metaphor, but that was exactly how my three days aboard the swift ship passed.
Thanks to this ship, we cut down our travel time by quite a bit.

True to the name Yangtze River Channel League, Mu Song and the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold were all outstanding sailors. They knew the lower reaches of the Yangtze, which ran throughout Sichuan, as well as the palms of their hands.
“We’ll be there soon, Old Master.”
I gazed at Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled face as I murmured.
Only a few weeks had passed, but his already small, thin body was gradually weakening.
It was something I realized every time I used True Qi Guidance to bolster his qi, as I had today.
Recovery is impossible. For now, the best I can do is slow the decline.
He had only lasted this long because he was a Supreme Peak master with profound internal energy.
And... our sole hope lay with one person whose medical skills had reached a godly realm.
The Divine Physician.
A mysterious figure whose face, name, age, and even gender were unknown.
The Divine Physician first became known more than forty years ago, though, so I figured they had to be over sixty.
I’ll find the Divine Physician no matter what... and wake you up.
So please, hold on a little longer.
Just as I added those words too softly for anyone else to hear, light footsteps approached. A murmured conversation drifted through the gap in the cabin door.
“Stop, stop, stop. Move, and I’ll cut you.”
“Gasp! Please don’t! You know me.”
“I do. But not even a rat gets past me. That includes some brat who came rolling in from who knows where. You could be an assassin, for all I know.”
“An assassin? I’m a medical apprentice! How could you say something so outrageous?”
“Then what brings you here?”
“G-Great Hero Mu Song asked me to deliver a message.”
“Impossible. Unless you can get past Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, no one can—!”
Bang! Thud!
Mungyeong’s jaw dropped as the Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan struck his head on the corner of the door and collapsed.
“He’s dead.”
“He’s not dead.”
“B-But a blow like that must have caused serious damage to his head...”
“Enough. What did Senior Mu Song tell you?”
The boy stared back and forth between Hyuk Mujin and me in terror before answering.
“H-He said we’re almost there, so you should get ready.”
“Oh, really? All right. Gather your things too.”
“I’m already packed.”
Mungyeong had little luggage.
He pulled his acupuncture and moxibustion supplies from the small bundle clutched to his chest, examined Hyuk Mujin, then sighed in relief.
“Fortunately, his head didn’t split open.”
“That’s because it’s made of rock.”
“Martial artists really are something else...”
“Oh? Getting cheeky, are we?”
“Gasp! I misspoke!”
I pretended I was about to rap him on the head, and Mungyeong flinched.
A quiet laugh escaped me.
“I’m kidding, you idiot.”
“You startled me.”
Traveling aboard a swift ship that sailed day and night was surprisingly grueling.
Whenever I finished circulating my internal energy and contemplating martial arts, I wandered the deck for some fresh air. Every time I did, I saw Mungyeong.
He was always checking on everyone else’s condition.
He was a good kid. Apparently, he was also quite skilled. Even the river bandits who had been skeptical of him at first often approached him shyly for treatment.
And after talking with him a few times, he seems pretty cheerful too.
Contrary to the mature first impression he had given me, Mungyeong had a lively, boyish side.
Once someone told him who we were, he seemed to take an interest in the Murim and started asking all sorts of questions.
“Young Master Jin, you’re the Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King? Wow!”
“I’ve heard all about Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint. Young Master Cheong must be incredible too.”
“Wow! The Beggars’ Sect! The Successor Beggar!”
“You’re the Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad? Ah, yes...”
In any case, Mungyeong had naturally blended into our group over those three short days.
Once we reach Chengdu, this will probably be the last time we sit across from each other and talk.
Once we reached Chengdu, our paths would naturally diverge.
I grabbed Mungyeong by the shoulder as he rose onto his toes and peeked over mine.
“Ow! That hurts!”
“What are you so curious about that you’re craning your neck like that?”
“Nothing. I just thought I saw someone’s foot through the gap in the door.”
The boy had sharp eyes. I had hurriedly covered Jeok Cheongang with leather, but Mungyeong had somehow spotted the exposed part.
Still, I answered casually without betraying any panic.
“You imagined it.”
“I don’t think I did...”
“Mungyeong.”
“Yes?”
“Do you really want to see what’s inside?”
He swallowed hard at my ominous tone and began backing away.
“W-Why are you acting like this?”
“I asked you a question. Do you want to see it?”
“No. No, I don’t!”
“Why not? Come inside and take a look. It’ll be fun.”
“Eek!”
Thump! Bang!
Mungyeong stepped on Hyuk Mujin as he backed away, fell over, then scrambled to his feet and fled.
Hyuk Mujin, whose back had been stepped on in the confusion, opened his eyes.
“H-Huh? I could’ve sworn I was just talking to Mungyeong.”
He looked around in bewilderment, then his face stiffened with shock.
“I didn’t even see him strike! He must be an assassin who has reached the Peak realm!”
Smack!
“Argh! Why did you hit me?”
“Stop talking nonsense and gather your things. We’re almost there.”
After giving Hyuk Mujin a satisfying whack on the back of the head, I returned to the cabin, moved Jeok Cheongang onto the pack frame, and stepped out onto the deck.
A giant standing at the stern of the slowing swift ship turned and greeted me.
“Oh, Junior.”
“Yeah, Senior.”
“...Is it just me, or have your answers gotten shorter?”
“It’s entirely your imagination. My voice is naturally a little quiet.”
Mu Song, the giant, stared at me with a dubious expression before calling over one of his subordinates and giving an order.
“Lower the blue flag and raise the white one.”
“Yes, Stronghold Lord.”
It might have sounded like some sort of blue-flag, white-flag game, but this was Water Dragon Stronghold’s signaling system. Apparently, it meant they had no intention of causing trouble.
“This may be an impertinent question, but are river bandits really allowed this close to such a busy area?”
“It is an impertinent question, but I’ll answer it anyway. Yes.”
“How?”
“Can you see it?”
Mu Song pointed toward the slowly approaching pier.
Tall wooden buildings stood packed closely together. Commoners passing by merely glanced at the swift ship before continuing on their way, while a few watched with curiosity.
We might have been far from the city center, but Chengdu was the capital and heart of Sichuan Province. Yet that was the extent of their reaction.
“Well? They all look used to us, don’t they?”
“They do. It’s strange how little attention they’re paying us.”
“It wasn’t always like this. Hwang Tae-gu, that son of a bitch, caused all kinds of trouble before I came along.”
Mu Song ground his teeth before continuing.
“I went through hell trying to change people’s opinion of us. Thanks to that, the authorities turn a blind eye to us now—to a point.”
“The authorities? You mean officials of the Great Nation?”

“That’s right. Dealing with us must have been a nuisance for them too. Formally requesting a fleet from the imperial court would have been burdensome, but staying on high alert every time they encountered us would have worn everyone down. So we reached a compromise.”
“What kind of compromise?”
“I’m different from Hwang Tae-gu. Only a complete idiot kills powerless commoners every time he gets the chance. It’s like killing our own customers with our own hands.”
“Of course, I refrain from killing because I dislike bloodshed. Not because of money.”
That wasn’t very convincing.
No matter how I looked at it, the only reason Mu Song didn’t kill people seemed to be money.
What a money-mad river bandit.
I couldn’t deny that Mu Song had a talent for shaking people down.
In any case, unlike Hwang Tae-gu, who robbed and killed indiscriminately, the moderate Mu Song had tried negotiating with the authorities and demonstrated considerable skill in doing so.
“Our range of activity has widened a little, while the authorities have received fewer petitions over people being killed by river bandits. Isn’t that a benefit to both sides?”
“Even so, they let you come this far?”
“Not officially, of course. Ah, here they come now.”
At the end of his gaze was a massive warship equipped with cannons.
Once the ships drew close enough that even people without martial arts could recognize one another, a middle-aged man in full armor suddenly stuck his head out from the stern.
“Who goes there?”
“General, it’s me! I’ve come to put a few people ashore.”
“People? Who?”
“My juniors. I’ll personally vouch for them.”
A river-bandit chief vouching for us. Yeah, that would go over well.
The official called back heartily.
“By all means!”
Fuck, it actually worked.
Mu Song suddenly pulled something from his robe and hurled it.
“Catch!”
The official snatched the bundle out of the air after it sailed toward him in a long arc, then grinned.
“You don’t have to do this every time. Thank you. I’ll buy you a proper drink next time.”
“Sure, let’s do that. How is the City Lord?”
“He had a son nine days ago.”
“Oh, what wonderful news. I’ll be sure to attend the doljabi.”
“Of course. The City Lord will be delighted.”
“Take care, then.”
“I wish you martial fortune, Stronghold Lord!”
For fuck’s sake. The country’s in fine shape.
After their cordial exchange, the warship turned back the way it had come, and the swift ship glided leisurely toward the pier.
“No need to drop anchor, right?”
“Huh? Oh, right.”
“Are you shocked? That’s how the world works. Still, you finally look like a young prodigy your age.”
Fair enough. Worse things happened in the real world, so what was the big deal?
I gave Mu Song, who was laughing heartily, a respectful clasped-fist salute.
“Thank you for your help, Senior. We had a comfortable journey thanks to you.”
“This was nothing. Hardly worth calling help. Just say the word. I am Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song!”
“Ah, truly the greatest Senior! You’ve turned the Yangtze upside down!”
“Ha ha ha!”
I grinned along with Mu Song as he roared with laughter.
“Then I’ll ask for your help again on our way back.”
“Senior?”
Mu Song stared at me, his eyes trembling.
“I’ll... send my subordinates.”
“Thank you!”
Yangtze taxi. What a steal.
Was it just my imagination, or was the swift ship moving much faster than usual?
I watched it cut frantically through the water as though fleeing a sea monster, then turned around.
The Bermuda Triangle and a beaming young medical apprentice stood there.
“Thanks to you, we arrived quickly. Thank you.”
“The men who rowed and steered did all the work, so why are you thanking me? I don’t know where you’re going or what for, but stay healthy.”
We had only spent a few days together, but I thought we had formed a pretty good bond.
He was usually innocent and carefree, yet surprisingly thoughtful. It was admirable how well he had endured the pain of losing his parents at such a young age.
I sincerely hoped he would become a fine physician.
“I don’t have a parting gift, but use this for travel expenses.”
I took out a few silver nyang and pressed them into his hand. Mungyeong stared at me in surprise.
“Y-Young Master, this is...”
“It’s fine. Think of it as allowance from your hyung.”
“But it’s too much.”
“Then pay me back later. Once you become a physician who can put Hua Tuo—or rather, the Divine Physician—to shame, come find me at the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Divine Physician...?”
“That’s right. If you’re going to do it, you might as well become the best.”
Mungyeong blinked, looking back and forth between me and the silver nyang in his hand. A faint smile touched his lips.
“Yes. I will.”
“Good. I’m leaving now. Take care.”
After the Bermuda Triangle and I exchanged farewells with Mungyeong, we turned to leave.
Hyuk Mujin, who had suffered through prolonged seasickness, quietly came up beside me and spoke.
“Captain, I’m exhausted. Can’t we rest for half a day before leaving?”
“No. It’s only another half day, so rest when we get there.”
“That’s only half a day if we use a movement technique. And I heard the people of the Sichuan Tang Clan are terrifying... We’ll have to be careful even when we breathe.”
“Then don’t rest. Die.”
“Is that any way to speak to your right-hand man?”
“What? I can’t hear you. My left pinky is mumbling something.”
Just as Hyuk Mujin’s lips jutted out a mile—
“Um, did you say you were going all the way to the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
We slowly turned our heads.
Mungyeong stood there, his eyes sparkling like morning stars.

“The thing is, I happen to be on my way to the Sichuan Tang Clan too. If you would allow me to accompany you, I would never forget this kindness even if this body died and died, then died ten thousand deaths more, until whether my soul existed or not—”
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
“I get it. Shut up and follow us.”
Fuck. Now it’s the Bermuda Quadrilateral.

“Stop, stop, stop.
Move, and I’ll cut you.”
“Gasp!
Please don’t!
You know me.”
“I do.
But not even a rat gets past me.
That includes some brat who came rolling in from who knows where.
You could be an assassin, for all I know.”
“An assassin?
I’m a medical apprentice!
How could you say something so outrageous?”
“Then what brings you here?”
“G-Great Hero Mu Song asked me to deliver a message.”
“Impossible.
Unless you can get past Hyuk Mujin, Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, no one can—!”
Bang!
Thud!
Mungyeong’s jaw dropped as the Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan struck his head on the corner of the door and collapsed.
“He’s dead.”
“He’s not dead.”
“B-But a blow like that must have caused serious damage to his head...”
“Enough.
What did Senior Mu Song tell you?”
The boy stared back and forth between Hyuk Mujin and me in terror before answering.
“H-He said we’re almost there, so you should get ready.”
“Oh, really?
All right.
Gather your things too.”
“I’m already packed.”
Mungyeong had little luggage.
He pulled his acupuncture and moxibustion supplies from the small bundle clutched to his chest, examined Hyuk Mujin, then sighed in relief.
“Fortunately, his head didn’t split open.”
“That’s because it’s made of rock.”
“Martial artists really are something else...”
“Oh?
Getting cheeky, are we?”
“Gasp!
I misspoke!”
I pretended I was about to rap him on the head, and Mungyeong flinched.
A quiet laugh escaped me.
“I’m kidding, you idiot.”
“You startled me.”
Traveling aboard a swift ship that sailed day and night was surprisingly grueling.
Whenever I finished circulating my internal energy and contemplating martial arts, I wandered the deck for some fresh air.
Every time I did, I saw Mungyeong.
He was always checking on everyone else’s condition.
He was a good kid.
Apparently, he was also quite skilled.
Even the river bandits who had been skeptical of him at first often approached him shyly for treatment.
And after talking with him a few times, he seems pretty cheerful too.
Contrary to the mature first impression he had given me, Mungyeong had a lively, boyish side.
Once someone told him who we were, he seemed to take an interest in the Murim and started asking all sorts of questions.
“Young Master Jin, you’re the Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King?
Wow!”
“I’ve heard all about Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.
Young Master Cheong must be incredible too.”
“Wow!
The Beggars’ Sect!
The Successor Beggar!”
“You’re the Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad?
Ah, yes...”
In any case, Mungyeong had naturally blended into our group over those three short days.
Once we reach Chengdu, this will probably be the last time we sit across from each other and talk.
Once we reached Chengdu, our paths would naturally diverge.
I grabbed Mungyeong by the shoulder as he rose onto his toes and peeked over mine.
“Ow!
That hurts!”
“What are you so curious about that you’re craning your neck like that?”
“Nothing.
I just thought I saw someone’s foot through the gap in the door.”
The boy had sharp eyes.
I had hurriedly covered Jeok Cheongang with leather, but Mungyeong had somehow spotted the exposed part.
Still, I answered casually without betraying any panic.
“You imagined it.”
“I don’t think I did...”
“Mungyeong.”
“Yes?”
“Do you really want to see what’s inside?”
He swallowed hard at my ominous tone and began backing away.
“W-Why are you acting like this?”
“I asked you a question.
Do you want to see it?”
“No.
No, I don’t!”
“Why not?
Come inside and take a look.
It’ll be fun.”
“Eek!”
Thump!
Bang!
Mungyeong stepped on Hyuk Mujin as he backed away, fell over, then scrambled to his feet and fled.
Hyuk Mujin, whose back had been stepped on in the confusion, opened his eyes.
“H-Huh?
I could’ve sworn I was just talking to Mungyeong.”
He looked around in bewilderment, then his face stiffened with shock.
“I didn’t even see him strike!
He must be an assassin who has reached the Peak realm!”
Smack!
“Argh!
Why did you hit me?”
“Stop talking nonsense and gather your things.
We’re almost there.”
After giving Hyuk Mujin a satisfying whack on the back of the head, I returned to the cabin, moved Jeok Cheongang onto the pack frame, and stepped out onto the deck.
A giant standing at the stern of the slowing swift ship turned and greeted me.
“Oh, Junior.”
“Yeah, Senior.”
“...Is it just me, or have your answers gotten shorter?”
“It’s entirely your imagination.
My voice is naturally a little quiet.”
Mu Song, the giant, stared at me with a dubious expression before calling over one of his subordinates and giving an order.
“Lower the blue flag and raise the white one.”
“Yes, Stronghold Lord.”
It might have sounded like some sort of blue-flag, white-flag game, but this was Water Dragon Stronghold’s signaling system.
Apparently, it meant they had no intention of causing trouble.
“This may be an impertinent question, but are river bandits really allowed this close to such a busy area?”
“It is an impertinent question, but I’ll answer it anyway.
Yes.”
“How?”
“Can you see it?”
Mu Song pointed toward the slowly approaching pier.
Tall wooden buildings stood packed closely together.
Commoners passing by merely glanced at the swift ship before continuing on their way, while a few watched with curiosity.
We might have been far from the city center, but Chengdu was the capital and heart of Sichuan Province.
Yet that was the extent of their reaction.
“Well?
They all look used to us, don’t they?”
“They do.
It’s strange how little attention they’re paying us.”
“It wasn’t always like this.
Hwang Tae-gu, that son of a bitch, caused all kinds of trouble before I came along.”
Mu Song ground his teeth before continuing.
“I went through hell trying to change people’s opinion of us.
Thanks to that, the authorities turn a blind eye to us now—to a point.”
“The authorities?
You mean officials of the Great Nation?”
“That’s right.
Dealing with us must have been a nuisance for them too.
Formally requesting a fleet from the imperial court would have been burdensome, but staying on high alert every time they encountered us would have worn everyone down.
So we reached a compromise.”
“What kind of compromise?”
“I’m different from Hwang Tae-gu.
Only a complete idiot kills powerless commoners every time he gets the chance.
It’s like killing our own customers with our own hands.”
“Of course, I refrain from killing because I dislike bloodshed.
Not because of money.”
That wasn’t very convincing.
No matter how I looked at it, the only reason Mu Song didn’t kill people seemed to be money.
What a money-mad river bandit.
I couldn’t deny that Mu Song had a talent for shaking people down.
In any case, unlike Hwang Tae-gu, who robbed and killed indiscriminately, the moderate Mu Song had tried negotiating with the authorities and demonstrated considerable skill in doing so.
“Our range of activity has widened a little, while the authorities have received fewer petitions over people being killed by river bandits.
Isn’t that a benefit to both sides?”
“Even so, they let you come this far?”
“Not officially, of course.
Ah, here they come now.”
At the end of his gaze was a massive warship equipped with cannons.
Once the ships drew close enough that even people without martial arts could recognize one another, a middle-aged man in full armor suddenly stuck his head out from the stern.
“Who goes there?”
“General, it’s me!
I’ve come to put a few people ashore.”
“People?
Who?”
“My juniors.
I’ll personally vouch for them.”
A river-bandit chief vouching for us.
Yeah, that would go over well.
The official called back heartily.
“By all means!”
Fuck, it actually worked.
Mu Song suddenly pulled something from his robe and hurled it.
“Catch!”
The official snatched the bundle out of the air after it sailed toward him in a long arc, then grinned.
“You don’t have to do this every time.
Thank you.
I’ll buy you a proper drink next time.”
“Sure, let’s do that.
How is the City Lord?”
“He had a son nine days ago.”
“Oh, what wonderful news.
I’ll be sure to attend the doljabi.”
“Of course.
The City Lord will be delighted.”
“Take care, then.”
“I wish you martial fortune, Stronghold Lord!”
For fuck’s sake.
The country’s in fine shape.
After their cordial exchange, the warship turned back the way it had come, and the swift ship glided leisurely toward the pier.
“No need to drop anchor, right?”
“Huh?
Oh, right.”
“Are you shocked?
That’s how the world works.
Still, you finally look like a young prodigy your age.”
Fair enough.
Worse things happened in the real world, so what was the big deal?
I gave Mu Song, who was laughing heartily, a respectful clasped-fist salute.
“Thank you for your help, Senior.
We had a comfortable journey thanks to you.”
“This was nothing.
Hardly worth calling help.
Just say the word.
I am Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song!”
“Ah, truly the greatest Senior!
You’ve turned the Yangtze upside down!”
“Ha ha ha!”
I grinned along with Mu Song as he roared with laughter.
“Then I’ll ask for your help again on our way back.”
“Senior?”
Mu Song stared at me, his eyes trembling.
“I’ll... send my subordinates.”
“Thank you!”
Yangtze taxi.
What a steal.
Was it just my imagination, or was the swift ship moving much faster than usual?
I watched it cut frantically through the water as though fleeing a sea monster, then turned around.
The Bermuda Triangle and a beaming young medical apprentice stood there.
“Thanks to you, we arrived quickly.
Thank you.”
“The men who rowed and steered did all the work, so why are you thanking me?
I don’t know where you’re going or what for, but stay healthy.”
We had only spent a few days together, but I thought we had formed a pretty good bond.
He was usually innocent and carefree, yet surprisingly thoughtful.
It was admirable how well he had endured the pain of losing his parents at such a young age.
I sincerely hoped he would become a fine physician.
“I don’t have a parting gift, but use this for travel expenses.”
I took out a few silver nyang and pressed them into his hand.
Mungyeong stared at me in surprise.
“Y-Young Master, this is...”
“It’s fine.
Think of it as allowance from your hyung.”
“But it’s too much.”
“Then pay me back later.
Once you become a physician who can put Hua Tuo—or rather, the Divine Physician—to shame, come find me at the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“The Divine Physician...?”
“That’s right.
If you’re going to do it, you might as well become the best.”
Mungyeong blinked, looking back and forth between me and the silver nyang in his hand.
A faint smile touched his lips.
“Yes.
I will.”
“Good.
I’m leaving now.
Take care.”
After the Bermuda Triangle and I exchanged farewells with Mungyeong, we turned to leave.
Hyuk Mujin, who had suffered through prolonged seasickness, quietly came up beside me and spoke.
“Captain, I’m exhausted.
Can’t we rest for half a day before leaving?”
“No.
It’s only another half day, so rest when we get there.”
“That’s only half a day if we use a movement technique.
And I heard the people of the Sichuan Tang Clan are terrifying...
We’ll have to be careful even when we breathe.”
“Then don’t rest.
Die.”
“Is that any way to speak to your right-hand man?”
“What?
I can’t hear you.
My left pinky is mumbling something.”
Just as Hyuk Mujin’s lips jutted out a mile—
“Um, did you say you were going all the way to the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
We slowly turned our heads.
Mungyeong stood there, his eyes sparkling like morning stars.
“The thing is, I happen to be on my way to the Sichuan Tang Clan too.
If you would allow me to accompany you, I would never forget this kindness even if this body died and died, then died ten thousand deaths more, until whether my soul existed or not—”
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
“I get it.
Shut up and follow us.”
Fuck.
Now it’s the Bermuda Quadrilateral.

chapters.title: Chapter 335
paragraphs: Like Sichuan Province in the real world, Sichuan in this world boasted a vast territory.
Shanxi, Henan, and Shaanxi. You had to combine all three provinces for their total area to rival Sichuan’s. That was how enormous it was.
The continent really is something.
With land this vast, it wasn’t all that strange for three tigers to coexist in a single province.
The Emei Sect and Qingcheng Sect, both counted among the Nine Sects and One Gang. And...
Finally, the Sichuan Tang Clan. Or the Tang Family.
One of the three tigers crouching in Sichuan, it was also the closest to Chengdu, making it the perfect first destination.
If we can get the cooperation of all three factions and bring the Beggars’ Sect into the picture, things should go much more smoothly.
As I was thinking this, Gung Gibang, who had been following a step behind me, pointed ahead.
“We’re almost there. The Sichuan Tang Clan.”
He was right. A wide basin stretched out before us, with a towering stone wall rising from it.
We were still too far away to judge its exact height, but it looked well over ten meters tall.
“What the hell? Why did they build a fortress?”
“History taught them a lesson.”
“History?”

“They suffered terribly during the Great Faction War. When the Demonic Cult occupied Sichuan, many members of the Tang Family were killed, and even Tang Family Hill, the clan’s main base, was burned to the ground.”
“Their home base got completely wrecked.”

“It wasn’t that one-sided. As they retreated, they released all kinds of deadly poisons, so the Demonic Cult bastards who charged in without knowing what they were walking into died in droves too. Do you know the Sichuan Tang Clan’s motto?”
“Uh... ‘The North Remembers’?”
“...What the hell are you talking about?”
“You know nothing, Gung Snow.”
Gung Gibang looked at me as though he were staring at a madman before opening his mouth.
“Repay kindness twofold. Repay grudges ten thousandfold.”
“Damn, that’s intense.”
“It was. The demonic, heterodox bastards who sided with the Demonic Cult during the occupation of Sichuan died shitting and pissing through all seven apertures.”
“Poisoning?”

“Poisoning, assassination, and even sending out pursuit squads to hunt them down independently. They died in all sorts of ways. A few may have survived through sheer luck, but they probably weren’t really living even if they were alive.”
Understandable.

Could that person walking toward me be an assassin sent by the Tang Clan? Had they perhaps poisoned the teacup? Trapped in a prison created by psychological pressure, they would have suffered from nervous exhaustion for the rest of their life.
They probably spent their days trembling in a corner with a sword in one hand and a silver spoon in the other.

“When it comes to poison and hidden weapons, the Sichuan Tang Clan is number one under heaven. No one can match how closed-off and relentless they are. Did you see anyone from the Sichuan Tang Clan at the Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
Thinking back, I couldn’t remember seeing a single one.

Even factions that hadn’t sent their young prodigies to compete in the Star-Array Grand Banquet, such as the Namgung Family, had sent important figures. But I hadn’t heard of anyone coming from the Sichuan Tang Clan.
“I don’t think so.”
“Right? There wasn’t anyone?”
“No. There really wasn’t.”
“That’s the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
They do whatever the fuck they want. No brakes.
I could feel it. The more I listened, the more uneasy I became.
What if they turn us down flat?
I had even brought a letter from the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak to request their cooperation, but I couldn’t shake the feeling that something might go wrong.
I was suppressing those thoughts and using my movement technique when Gung Gibang suddenly spoke.
“We should walk from here.”
“Do we really have to?”
“They probably won’t appreciate us approaching at high speed.”
“They might.”
Gung Gibang pointed at a massive boulder a few paces ahead.
Written across it in blood-red letters were the words:
Anyone who approaches without permission will pay a blood debt.
“Let’s walk. I’ve been wanting to walk for a while now.”
“Hey, sometimes you need to look around at the scenery and gaze up at the sky. That’s what living is all about.”
Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin, and I stopped using our movement techniques.
One person did not.
With a fierce gust of wind, a figure shot straight toward the front gate.
Whoooosh!
“Hellooo!”
“Cheongpung, you crazy bastard!”
“I’m Cheongpung!”
Cheongpung hurtled forward, waving energetically, with a boy of similar build riding on his back.
Cheongpung spoke to Mungyeong, who was swaying pitifully in every direction.
“Medical apprentice, say hello!”
“H-Hello!”
Please don’t.
Don’t make him do weird things. And don’t do them just because he tells you to.
I lunged forward to grab Cheongpung by the scruff of his neck, but the Sichuan Tang Clan’s response came faster.
Whoooosh! Boom!
A massive spear as tall as a grown man hurtled down from atop the stone wall. It buried itself directly in front of Cheongpung’s foot, its shaft quivering.
Then, in the next instant—
“Who goes there?”
Clatter-clatter-clatter!
Dozens of crossbows appeared atop the wall along with the shout, which carried powerful internal energy.
Between the countless arrowheads glittering in the sunlight, a middle-aged man with his eyes wide open shouted at us again.
“Outsiders, identify yourselves!”
Cheongpung answered.
“Hello! I’m Cheongpung!”
“I-I am Mungyeong. P-please show mercy and lower your weapons, and I shall repay this grace even if this body dies and dies, then dies a hundred times over, until— Mmph!”
Stop it, you trolls!
I hurriedly clamped my hands over Cheongpung’s and Mungyeong’s mouths, then bowed repeatedly toward the wall.
“I’m sorry. I’m sorry. The kids don’t know any better. My name is Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
The middle-aged man thought for a moment, then his eyes widened slightly.
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—the Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King?”
“Yes. That’s me.”
I jerked my chin toward Gung Gibang, who had arrived a beat later, and continued.
“This is the Oseong-and-Haneum villain—no, the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar, Gung Gibang.”
“The Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang and the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar...”
His tone and expression remained suspicious, but the middle-aged man’s wariness eased considerably.
When he crooked a finger, the crossbows aimed at us lowered toward the ground.
“What brings you to our family?”
“I’d like to meet the Family Head.”
“The Family Head?”
“Yes. It’s important.”
The middle-aged man frowned, apparently displeased with my answer, but this wasn’t something we could announce to the whole neighborhood.
The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was no fool. There was a reason he had written the letter himself and entrusted us to deliver it in person instead of sending a messenger pigeon.
“The Family Head has many matters to handle right now. Our family is not accepting any outsiders whatsoever. Leave and return another time.”
“You only need to deliver a message.”
“Impossible. The Family Head himself gave me these orders. And if your business were truly that important, you should have contacted us in advance.”
Why is he being so damn firm? I didn’t plan for this.
Gung Gibang seemed to be thinking the same thing. He whispered in a voice as small as an ant.
“Something’s strange. Even for a closed-off place like the Sichuan Tang Clan, this is too much...”
I agreed. Pointing crossbows at us without warning and maintaining this level of vigilance were things one would expect only in wartime.
What a warm welcome.

Still, we had come to ask for their cooperation. I couldn’t simply complain. If we wanted to meet the Family Head, it seemed we would have to show at least half our hand, even if we didn’t reveal everything.
Can’t be helped.
After a brief hesitation, I stared straight at the middle-aged man.
“I brought a letter from Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
“Please allow me to meet the Family Head.”
The effect was immediate. The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was an idol to martial artists and a giant among giants who might become the Alliance Leader of the New Murim Alliance.
He was in a completely different league from greenhorns like us, who had only made names for ourselves within the past year or two.
“...Hmm. Wait here a moment.”
The middle-aged man let out a groan and disappeared from the top of the stone wall. He returned a short while later.
His first words were practically a foregone conclusion.
“The Family Head has granted permission.”
The moment he finished speaking—
Grrrrrrr.
The enormous iron gate slowly opened its jaws with a grinding groan.
Not long after passing through the iron gate, I realized my earlier suspicion had been correct.
Something happened. There’s no doubt about it.
The people who appeared to be members of the Sichuan Tang Clan were proof enough. Their guarded movements, tense eyes, and overall atmosphere said it all.
The sense that something was wrong grew even stronger after we left the Outer Hall and entered the Inner Hall.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Craftsmen hammered away at something without pause. Martial artists dressed in uniforms walked around in pairs, while crates loaded with weapons and hidden weapons were carried from place to place.
At the sight, Gung Gibang and I exchanged Sound Transmission.
— Hey, am I the only one getting a bad feeling?
— I feel it too. It looks like they’re preparing for battle.
— Could they have found some demonic fiend? Maybe one of the men who set fire to the Sichuan Tang Clan during the Great Faction War.
— I don’t know. For now, we should keep our mouths shut and pretend we don’t know anything.
I had already been planning to do that. If they had intended to tell us, they would have done so by now.
The real problem was that only I had heard the Sound Transmission.
“Wow! I’ve never seen anything like this before! Are you preparing for a war or something?”
For a moment, I thought the world had stopped.
The craftsmen and martial artists around us froze in place and silently stared at us.
Hundreds of gazes pierced my entire body like hidden weapons.
What sin did I commit in my past life to get tangled up with a bastard like Cheongpung?
One second. Two seconds. Three seconds.
Is this the Hyperbolic Time Chamber?
By the time my mouth had dried out like the sand around the Sphinx’s front paws, the middle-aged man guiding us spoke to the others.
“What are you doing? Get back to work.”
Only then did the world begin moving again.
The middle-aged man glanced at the people returning to their tasks, then casually tossed a remark our way.
“You all look tight-lipped. I like that.”
On the surface, it sounded like a compliment.
So why did it sound like a warning to keep our mouths shut if we wanted to live long, healthy lives?
Why else? Because that’s exactly what he meant, damn it.
Maybe it was because of the Tang Clan’s association with poison and hidden weapons.
The middle-aged man and the other members of the Tang Family were clearly a step below me in skill, yet they all gave off an unmistakably dangerous scent.
“Hold your breath. That’s poison mist. It smells awful.”
“...Oh. Yes.”
So that was the dangerous smell?
I glared at the blue-haired bastard, who was still looking around with a bright expression, and continued walking behind the middle-aged man.
After walking for some time, we passed through five gates and finally stopped in front of the sixth.
“You cannot bring weapons into the Family Head’s Hall.”
Following the middle-aged man’s instructions, we handed over all our weapons. Afterward, the martial artists guarding the hall searched us as well.
They’re incredibly strict.
At that moment, one of the guards patting me down in search of hidden weapons suddenly flinched and shouted.
“There’s a hidden weapon here!”
“That’s not a hidden weapon. It’s my thing.”
“Pardon?”
“It’s mine. You know... that.”
What kind of humiliation play is this?
I would rather pull out a poisoned hidden weapon than take that out in the Family Head’s Hall. It would be a much easier way to die.
I reluctantly gave him permission to see for himself, and the middle-aged man’s eyes widened.
“You’re quite impressive.”
“...Could you just let me through without saying anything?”
“I understand. But you really are impressive.”
“Oh, please.”
Reading the sincerity in my plea, he was about to order the guards to let us pass when he suddenly frowned.
“I nearly forgot. You there, stay behind.”
Oh, right. He was here.
The “you” the middle-aged man was referring to was Mungyeong.
“I hear you’re a medical apprentice who came to our family to obtain a prescription.”
Having been dragged this far before he even knew what was happening, Mungyeong answered in a trembling voice.
“Y-Yes.”
“Under normal circumstances, it would be out of the question... but you were fortunate enough to fall in with the right group. I’ll assign someone to guide you, so go take care of your business.”
“Th-Thank you.”
Mungyeong bowed deeply before disappearing with one of the martial artists. The middle-aged man took the lead and beckoned to us.
“Let us go inside.”
Twenty steps made of blue stone.
And at the top, a single door.
“Uncle, it’s me.”
An elderly voice answered the middle-aged man.
“Come in.”
