I had even brought a letter from the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak to request their cooperation, but I couldn’t shake the feeling that something might go wrong.
I was suppressing those thoughts and using my movement technique when Gung Gibang suddenly spoke.
“We should walk from here.”
“Do we really have to?”
“They probably won’t appreciate us approaching at high speed.”
“They might.”
Gung Gibang pointed at a massive boulder a few paces ahead.
Written across it in blood-red letters were the words:
Anyone who approaches without permission will pay a blood debt.
“Let’s walk.
I’ve been wanting to walk for a while now.”
“Hey, sometimes you need to look around at the scenery and gaze up at the sky.
That’s what living is all about.”
Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin, and I stopped using our movement techniques.
One person did not.
With a fierce gust of wind, a figure shot straight toward the front gate.
Whoooosh!
“Hellooo!”
“Cheongpung, you crazy bastard!”
“I’m Cheongpung!”
Cheongpung hurtled forward, waving energetically, with a boy of similar build riding on his back.
Cheongpung spoke to Mungyeong, who was swaying pitifully in every direction.
“Medical apprentice, say hello!”
“H-Hello!”
Please don’t.
Don’t make him do weird things.
And don’t do them just because he tells you to.
I lunged forward to grab Cheongpung by the scruff of his neck, but the Sichuan Tang Clan’s response came faster.
Whoooosh!
Boom!
A massive spear as tall as a grown man hurtled down from atop the stone wall.
It buried itself directly in front of Cheongpung’s foot, its shaft quivering.
Then, in the next instant—
“Who goes there?”
Clatter-clatter-clatter!
Dozens of crossbows appeared atop the wall along with the shout, which carried powerful internal energy.
Between the countless arrowheads glittering in the sunlight, a middle-aged man with his eyes wide open shouted at us again.
“Outsiders, identify yourselves!”
Cheongpung answered.
“Hello!
I’m Cheongpung!”
“I-I am Mungyeong.
P-please show mercy and lower your weapons, and I shall repay this grace even if this body dies and dies, then dies a hundred times over, until— Mmph!”
Stop it, you trolls!
I hurriedly clamped my hands over Cheongpung’s and Mungyeong’s mouths, then bowed repeatedly toward the wall.
“I’m sorry.
I’m sorry.
The kids don’t know any better.
My name is Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
The middle-aged man thought for a moment, then his eyes widened slightly.
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi—the Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King?”
“Yes.
That’s me.”
I jerked my chin toward Gung Gibang, who had arrived a beat later, and continued.
“This is the Oseong-and-Haneum villain—no, the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar, Gung Gibang.”
“The Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang and the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar...”
His tone and expression remained suspicious, but the middle-aged man’s wariness eased considerably.
When he crooked a finger, the crossbows aimed at us lowered toward the ground.
“What brings you to our family?”
“I’d like to meet the Family Head.”
“The Family Head?”
“Yes.
It’s important.”
The middle-aged man frowned, apparently displeased with my answer, but this wasn’t something we could announce to the whole neighborhood.
The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was no fool.
There was a reason he had written the letter himself and entrusted us to deliver it in person instead of sending a messenger pigeon.
“The Family Head has many matters to handle right now.
Our family is not accepting any outsiders whatsoever.
Leave and return another time.”
“You only need to deliver a message.”
“Impossible.
The Family Head himself gave me these orders.
And if your business were truly that important, you should have contacted us in advance.”
Why is he being so damn firm?
I didn’t plan for this.
Gung Gibang seemed to be thinking the same thing.
He whispered in a voice as small as an ant.
“Something’s strange.
Even for a closed-off place like the Sichuan Tang Clan, this is too much...”
I agreed.
Pointing crossbows at us without warning and maintaining this level of vigilance were things one would expect only in wartime.
What a warm welcome.
Still, we had come to ask for their cooperation.
I couldn’t simply complain.
If we wanted to meet the Family Head, it seemed we would have to show at least half our hand, even if we didn’t reveal everything.
Can’t be helped.
After a brief hesitation, I stared straight at the middle-aged man.
“I brought a letter from Great Hero Mae Jonghak, the Sword Saint.”
“Please allow me to meet the Family Head.”
The effect was immediate.
The Sword Saint Mae Jonghak was an idol to martial artists and a giant among giants who might become the Alliance Leader of the New Murim Alliance.
He was in a completely different league from greenhorns like us, who had only made names for ourselves within the past year or two.
Wait here a moment.”
The middle-aged man let out a groan and disappeared from the top of the stone wall.
He returned a short while later.
His first words were practically a foregone conclusion.
“The Family Head has granted permission.”
The moment he finished speaking—
Grrrrrrr.
The enormous iron gate slowly opened its jaws with a grinding groan.
Not long after passing through the iron gate, I realized my earlier suspicion had been correct.
Something happened.
There’s no doubt about it.
The people who appeared to be members of the Sichuan Tang Clan were proof enough.
Their guarded movements, tense eyes, and overall atmosphere said it all.
The sense that something was wrong grew even stronger after we left the Outer Hall and entered the Inner Hall.
Clang!
Clang!
Clang!
Craftsmen hammered away at something without pause.
Martial artists dressed in uniforms walked around in pairs, while crates loaded with weapons and hidden weapons were carried from place to place.
At the sight, Gung Gibang and I exchanged Sound Transmission.
— Hey, am I the only one getting a bad feeling?
— I feel it too.
It looks like they’re preparing for battle.
— Could they have found some demonic fiend?
Maybe one of the men who set fire to the Sichuan Tang Clan during the Great Faction War.
— I don’t know.
For now, we should keep our mouths shut and pretend we don’t know anything.
I had already been planning to do that.
If they had intended to tell us, they would have done so by now.
The real problem was that only I had heard the Sound Transmission.
“Wow!
I’ve never seen anything like this before!
Are you preparing for a war or something?”
For a moment, I thought the world had stopped.
The craftsmen and martial artists around us froze in place and silently stared at us.
Hundreds of gazes pierced my entire body like hidden weapons.
What sin did I commit in my past life to get tangled up with a bastard like Cheongpung?
One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Is this the Hyperbolic Time Chamber?
By the time my mouth had dried out like the sand around the Sphinx’s front paws, the middle-aged man guiding us spoke to the others.
“What are you doing?
Get back to work.”
Only then did the world begin moving again.
The middle-aged man glanced at the people returning to their tasks, then casually tossed a remark our way.
“You all look tight-lipped.
I like that.”
On the surface, it sounded like a compliment.
So why did it sound like a warning to keep our mouths shut if we wanted to live long, healthy lives?
Why else?
Because that’s exactly what he meant, damn it.
Maybe it was because of the Tang Clan’s association with poison and hidden weapons.
The middle-aged man and the other members of the Tang Family were clearly a step below me in skill, yet they all gave off an unmistakably dangerous scent.
“Hold your breath.
That’s poison mist.
It smells awful.”
Yes.”
So that was the dangerous smell?
I glared at the blue-haired bastard, who was still looking around with a bright expression, and continued walking behind the middle-aged man.
After walking for some time, we passed through five gates and finally stopped in front of the sixth.
“You cannot bring weapons into the Family Head’s Hall.”
Following the middle-aged man’s instructions, we handed over all our weapons.
Afterward, the martial artists guarding the hall searched us as well.
They’re incredibly strict.
At that moment, one of the guards patting me down in search of hidden weapons suddenly flinched and shouted.
“There’s a hidden weapon here!”
“That’s not a hidden weapon.
It’s my thing.”
“Pardon?”
“It’s mine.
You know... that.”
What kind of humiliation play is this?
I would rather pull out a poisoned hidden weapon than take that out in the Family Head’s Hall.
It would be a much easier way to die.
I reluctantly gave him permission to see for himself, and the middle-aged man’s eyes widened.
“You’re quite impressive.”
“...Could you just let me through without saying anything?”
“I understand.
But you really are impressive.”
“Oh, please.”
Reading the sincerity in my plea, he was about to order the guards to let us pass when he suddenly frowned.
“I nearly forgot.
You there, stay behind.”
Oh, right.
He was here.
The “you” the middle-aged man was referring to was Mungyeong.
“I hear you’re a medical apprentice who came to our family to obtain a prescription.”
Having been dragged this far before he even knew what was happening, Mungyeong answered in a trembling voice.
“Y-Yes.”
“Under normal circumstances, it would be out of the question... but you were fortunate enough to fall in with the right group.
I’ll assign someone to guide you, so go take care of your business.”
“Th-Thank you.”
Mungyeong bowed deeply before disappearing with one of the martial artists.
The middle-aged man took the lead and beckoned to us.
“Let us go inside.”
Twenty steps made of blue stone.
And at the top, a single door.
“Uncle, it’s me.”
An elderly voice answered the middle-aged man.
“Come in.”

chapters.title: Chapter 336
paragraphs: An old tree.
That was the first thing that came to mind when I saw the old man.
Inside the dark pavilion, partitioned off by cloth on all four sides, he stood alone with his back to us. He looked like an ancient tree that had lost every trace of life.
If he hadn’t slowly turned around the next moment, I might have thought he had already taken root in the floor.
“I see...”
Green light swirled in his eyes.
The old man—Tang Sadok, the Myriad-Poison Asura—continued in a voice that hissed like a snake.
“You brought a letter?”
The middle-aged man answered.
“Yes, Uncle. Great Hero Mae Jonghak sent—”
“Did I ask you?”
“This is no place for you. Leave.”
Realizing his mistake, the middle-aged man bowed silently and left the pavilion.
After coldly dismissing his own nephew with a few words, Tang Sadok leaned back in a leather chair.
Would you look at the presence on this old man.
The problem was, it was a villain’s presence.
From my first impression alone, I could have believed he belonged to the Demonic Cult rather than the orthodox faction.
I stepped forward beneath Tang Sadok’s gaze.
“I am Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It is an honor to meet you, Great Hero Tang Sadok.”
Tang Sadok answered with an unreadable expression.
“I have heard that Senior Jeok took a Disciple in his later years. I also know of his ties to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Oh, really?”
That was a good sign.
Tang Sadok stroked his chin in thought, then abruptly spoke.
“His name was... Yes, the Blade of Flowers, Jin Baekyang. Now I remember.”
Good sign, my ass. That name pops up every time I’m about to forget it.
The Head Elder really must have been something in his day.
Then again, it made sense. He had been a Peak master who distinguished himself during the Great Faction War. It was hardly strange that he had formed friendships with other masters during that time.
He even said he’d met the Fire King once or twice.
Thanks to that, when I first met Jeok Cheongang, I got nailed with a Flame Divine Palm before I could explain the situation.
Tang Sadok stared at me and asked,
“How has Jin Baekyang been?”
“Well, you see...”
Before answering, I glanced around, ready to dodge in case a poisonous snake suddenly sprang out or a hidden weapon came flying at me.
“He passed away.”
“What?”
Yeah, I knew this was coming.
Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open, and I hurried to continue.
“It was an unfortunate accident. There were circumstances, of course. If you give me a little time, I can explain everything and clear up any misunderstandings—”
“No need.”
“Excuse me?”
“He was an obnoxious bastard. Every time people fawned over him and called him a Great Hero or a chivalrous knight, it soured my mood.”
“No martial artist dies without a reason. Once he is dead, that is the end of it.”
I was relieved that this had gone more smoothly than expected, but the old man’s personality was practically toxic.
Wasn’t he basically saying he was glad the obnoxious bastard was dead?
His personality is practically on Dark Heaven’s level.
Whether or not he sensed the suspicion taking root in my mind, Tang Sadok waved a hand irritably.
“Enough about the dead. Let us get to the point. Great Hero Mae Jonghak sent this old man a letter?”
“Yes. It’ll be faster if you read it yourself.”
I pretended to rummage through my robes and summoned the Sword Saint’s handwritten letter from my Inventory.
Tang Sadok took the letter and read it. The furrows between his brows deepened until a furious roar finally burst from his throat.
“Those goddamn bastards!”
Whoooom!
The pavilion shuddered beneath the force of his profound internal energy.
His green robes billowed as his fury erupted, and he ground out each word as though chewing it up and spitting it out.
“Is everything written here true?”
“Yes. It happened exactly as the letter says.”
The Sword Saint’s letter clearly summarized the events in Henan and asked Tang Sadok to provide every possible assistance in finding the Divine Physician to treat Jeok Cheongang.
“To think Senior Jeok’s condition is so grave...”
“Actually, there’s something I’d like to ask before we begin searching for the Divine Physician.”
The Sichuan Tang Clan was renowned throughout the martial world for its poisons and hidden weapons, but every member of the family was also a skilled physician.
And one among them stood at the very pinnacle.
I looked straight at Tang Sadok and asked,
“Could I meet the Grand Family Head?”
Poison King Tang Taesang.
A Supreme Peak master who had been called the greatest under heaven when it came to poisons and hidden weapons, even before the Great Faction War.
After dominating an entire era, he had passed the position of Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan to his only child twenty years ago and disappeared from public view.
That child was the old man standing before me now—Tang Sadok.
“We have no idea how many days it might take to find the Divine Physician. If the Poison King could examine my Master before then...”
“Enough.”
Tang Sadok cut me off, his face rigid.
“Impossible. That is this old man’s answer.”
My heart sank at the unexpected response.
Poison King Tang Taesang might not have appeared in public for many years, but Tang Sadok clearly knew where he was.
Impossible. Tang Sadok knew, yet he was still refusing to help.
My voice trembled despite myself.
“W-Why?”
“I cannot say.”
“You cannot say?”
“Instead, I will assign several people to guide you. If you go to Qingcheng and Emei, they will gladly help you.”
What did I just hear?
This shock was several times greater than the first.
Tang Sadok’s words meant the Sichuan Tang Clan would not help us with this matter.
Well, it wasn’t as though they were offering no help whatsoever.
A few guides to take us to the Qingcheng Sect and Emei Sect.
That was it.
That was all the help we could expect from the Sichuan Tang Clan.
The back of my head tingled as though someone had clubbed me with an iron rod. Something hot surged up from deep within my chest.
“Is that all?”
“What more did you expect?”
“We need to find the Divine Physician!”
“That is your problem, not mine or our family’s. The fact that you brought a letter from Great Hero Mae Jonghak changes nothing. It was a request, and this old man refused it. That is all.”
The words lodged in my throat.
Everything Tang Sadok said was true. To him and the Sichuan Tang Clan, helping us was a choice, not an obligation.
Right. Of course it was.
Once I finally accepted the truth I had kept desperately denying, bitter disappointment and anger welled up inside me.
As I stood there at a loss for words, someone stepped forward with the sweet scent of snacks.
“I am Cheongpung of Huashan. It is an honor to meet you.”
So he had this side to him too.
Wearing an expression I had never seen before and speaking in an unfamiliar tone, Cheongpung offered a clasped-fist salute and continued.
“I do not know why you are refusing, Family Head, but if you help us, I will never forget this kindness.”

“I know you are Great Hero Mae Jonghak’s Disciple. One must be cautious when forming ties of gratitude and grudges in the martial world. Stop meddling in matters that do not concern you and step back.”
“I’m not meddling.”
“Then what are you doing?”
Cheongpung answered with a clear, unwavering gaze.
“My grandfather called it human compassion.”
Tang Sadok regarded Cheongpung with a complicated expression, then shook his head.
“Even if Great Hero Mae Jonghak came here and asked me himself, this old man’s answer would remain the same.”
Cheongpung, Gung Gibang, and Hyuk Mujin all started to speak at once, but I cut in first.
“What’s the reason?”
“The reason?”
“Even a stray mutt passing by knows how powerful the Sichuan Tang Clan is. So why the hell are you refusing?”
“And what will you do if I do not wish to tell you?”
“What will I do?”
I stared into Tang Sadok’s green eyes and answered,
“Then the ties of gratitude and grudges you mentioned will form between me and the Sichuan Tang Clan. And I should warn you—they won’t be the pleasant kind.”
“Hah. What a fearless brat.”
“Normally, I check where I’m lying before I stretch out my legs, but in this case, I’m in a bit—well, a lot—of a hurry.”
Jeok Cheongang had half a year left at most.
Even the greatest martial sects under heaven and the Imperial Court had failed to find the Divine Physician.
If Jeok Cheongang died because he could not receive treatment in time... If he died because the Sichuan Tang Clan had refused to help...
“Then I don’t know what I might do.”
When I finished speaking, suffocating silence descended upon the pavilion.
Tang Sadok studied me for a long time, his gaze deep and unfathomable. At last, his lips parted.
“I regret what happened to Senior Jeok.”
“If you’re sorry, why not help us?”
“This old man would like to. But what can I do? Our family does not have the strength to spare right now.”
No strength to spare?
The moment I heard those words, the scenes I had witnessed on the way here flashed through my mind.
An atmosphere so tense it bordered on murderous. Artisans working without rest. Weapons constantly being carried from one place to another.
“What the hell is going on?”
“Going on?”
Step.
Tang Sadok took a step toward me.
Perhaps it was due to the poison arts he had cultivated, but his green eyes gleamed more eerily than ever. Within them burned anger and grief.
“It has already happened. All that remains now is for our family to marshal its full strength and slaughter every last culprit involved.”
That was it.
That was why the Sichuan Tang Clan could not help us now.
That was why Tang Sadok had been so reluctant to explain himself, even after a green brat like me challenged him to his face.
That was why this took priority over finding the Divine Physician and saving the Fire King’s life—and why he had flatly refused to let me meet Poison King Tang Taesang.
“Don’t tell me...”
Perhaps he saw the realization on my face.
Tang Sadok met my wide-eyed stare and spoke in a voice thick with killing intent.
“By the time we received the news, it was already too late. Not one of his limbs had been left intact.”
Those words turned my suspicion into certainty.
Poison King Tang Taesang was dead.
“Hmm.”
The middle-aged man was of average height, with a round face and the sort of ordinary appearance one might see anywhere.
Leaning against the wall of a pitch-black cave, he carefully examined his forearm and muttered.
“This won’t do. The poison is vicious.”
He clicked his tongue softly.
He had done everything he could, but the best he had managed was to force all the poison into one arm.
“Poison King... He was fierce. More than I expected.”
Poison King Tang Taesang.
The expression on his face when he finally breathed his last was still vivid in the middle-aged man’s mind.
But the result left the middle-aged man in a difficult position.
He had succeeded in eliminating the Supreme Peak master known as the Poison King, yet failed to accomplish the more important task.
Not that I ever expected it to be easy.
With that thought, the middle-aged man abruptly brought the edge of his hand down on his left forearm.
A dazzling flash burst forth, and the severed forearm fell to the ground.
Schhk! Ssssss!
Poison-laden blood splattered across the cave, melting everything it touched. Acrid toxic smoke billowed into the air.
The small creatures watching the middle-aged man from hidden crevices died the instant the smoke reached them, never knowing what had happened.
Eek... Eeeek...
Listening to the bats’ dying shrieks, the middle-aged man walked out of the cave and grinned up at the blazing sunlight.
It was impossible to believe that smile belonged to a man who had just cut off his own arm.

“Then the ties of gratitude and grudges you mentioned will form between me and the Sichuan Tang Clan.
And I should warn you—they won’t be the pleasant kind.”
“Hah.
What a fearless brat.”
“Normally, I check where I’m lying before I stretch out my legs, but in this case, I’m in a bit—well, a lot—of a hurry.”
Jeok Cheongang had half a year left at most.
Even the greatest martial sects under heaven and the Imperial Court had failed to find the Divine Physician.
If Jeok Cheongang died because he could not receive treatment in time...
If he died because the Sichuan Tang Clan had refused to help...
“Then I don’t know what I might do.”
When I finished speaking, suffocating silence descended upon the pavilion.
Tang Sadok studied me for a long time, his gaze deep and unfathomable.
At last, his lips parted.
“I regret what happened to Senior Jeok.”
“If you’re sorry, why not help us?”
“This old man would like to.
But what can I do?
Our family does not have the strength to spare right now.”
No strength to spare?
The moment I heard those words, the scenes I had witnessed on the way here flashed through my mind.
An atmosphere so tense it bordered on murderous.
Artisans working without rest.
Weapons constantly being carried from one place to another.
“What the hell is going on?”
“Going on?”
Step.
Tang Sadok took a step toward me.
Perhaps it was due to the poison arts he had cultivated, but his green eyes gleamed more eerily than ever.
Within them burned anger and grief.
“It has already happened.
All that remains now is for our family to marshal its full strength and slaughter every last culprit involved.”
That was it.
That was why the Sichuan Tang Clan could not help us now.
That was why Tang Sadok had been so reluctant to explain himself, even after a green brat like me challenged him to his face.
That was why this took priority over finding the Divine Physician and saving the Fire King’s life—and why he had flatly refused to let me meet Poison King Tang Taesang.
“Don’t tell me...”
Perhaps he saw the realization on my face.
Tang Sadok met my wide-eyed stare and spoke in a voice thick with killing intent.
“By the time we received the news, it was already too late.
Not one of his limbs had been left intact.”
Those words turned my suspicion into certainty.
Poison King Tang Taesang was dead.
“Hmm.”
The middle-aged man was of average height, with a round face and the sort of ordinary appearance one might see anywhere.
Leaning against the wall of a pitch-black cave, he carefully examined his forearm and muttered.
“This won’t do.
The poison is vicious.”
He clicked his tongue softly.
He had done everything he could, but the best he had managed was to force all the poison into one arm.
“Poison King...
He was fierce.
More than I expected.”
Poison King Tang Taesang.
The expression on his face when he finally breathed his last was still vivid in the middle-aged man’s mind.
But the result left the middle-aged man in a difficult position.
He had succeeded in eliminating the Supreme Peak master known as the Poison King, yet failed to accomplish the more important task.
Not that I ever expected it to be easy.
With that thought, the middle-aged man abruptly brought the edge of his hand down on his left forearm.
A dazzling flash burst forth, and the severed forearm fell to the ground.
Schhk!
Ssssss!
Poison-laden blood splattered across the cave, melting everything it touched.
Acrid toxic smoke billowed into the air.
The small creatures watching the middle-aged man from hidden crevices died the instant the smoke reached them, never knowing what had happened.
Eek...
Eeeek...
Listening to the bats’ dying shrieks, the middle-aged man walked out of the cave and grinned up at the blazing sunlight.
It was impossible to believe that smile belonged to a man who had just cut off his own arm.

chapters.title: Chapter 337
paragraphs: Inside the vast, chilly pavilion, a draft squeezed through the gaps around the windows, making the oil lamp on the windowsill flicker. An old man’s face slowly appeared over the wavering flame.
Eyes suffused with green light and a body as withered as an ancient tree.
The old man’s name was Tang Sadok. His alias was the Myriad-Poison Asura.
He was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, one of the Five Great Families under heaven—and a son who had recently lost his father.
Whoooosh.
The cold wind beating against the closed window seemed to carry the voice I had heard several shichen ago.
By the time I heard the news, it was already too late. Not one of his limbs had been left intact.
The One God, the Three Saints, and the Ten Kings.
The heroes who had once saved the world from the hundred thousand forces of the Demonic Path had long since become white-haired old men.
Some had grown old or sick and died. Some had vanished after seeking peace. Others had handed their successors the responsibility and stepped down.
Poison King Tang Taesang had also left to find his own path.
There is a place called Meishan two days from here. My father often spoke of its beautiful mountains.
More than twenty years ago, it had only been natural for the Poison King to head for Meishan after stepping down as Family Head.
It must have been the final resting place chosen by an old martial artist who had spent his entire life weathering the turbulent currents of Murim.
He did not welcome visitors. We had no choice but to send someone to check on him every once in a while.
And that had become a scar that would never fade.
Several days ago, an unbelievable urgent report had arrived.
When Tang Sadok rushed there in a panic, he found the aftermath of a battle that had shaken heaven and earth—and the Poison King’s corpse.
“My father’s body had been... severely mutilated. They were unmistakable signs of torture.”
I did not know why the culprit had tortured the Poison King.
But Poison King Tang Taesang, a Supreme Peak master who had dominated an entire era, had died that way. At the hands of an unknown figure whose name and face remained a mystery.
Furious beyond measure, Tang Sadok had personally led his clansmen in combing the surrounding area, but it was already too late.
I will find that bastard and kill him. I’ll tear his limbs apart and scatter them across the Nine Provinces, then let the blood from his body flow into the Four Seas and Five Lakes.
What could anyone say to Tang Sadok as he raged, radiating suffocating killing intent? I understood his anger and resolve well enough.
He and the Sichuan Tang Clan would never stop until they found the culprit and killed him. Naturally, they could not help us find the Divine Physician.
“Poison King Tang Taesang is dead. The Poison King himself...”
A massive tectonic shift was taking place. And it was happening right beside us.
Just as I murmured those words while staring at the oil lamp, an urgent voice came from behind me.
“Watch your mouth. Do you have any idea what’ll happen if you say something like that in the middle of the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
It was not difficult to tell who the voice belonged to. I had sensed the three of them approaching long ago.
Without turning my head, I answered, “You’re back.”
“Not ‘you’re back.’ I said watch your mouth. Your mouth!”
“It’s fine. There’s no one nearby.”
“I’m saying we should be careful. Being around you scares the life out of me.”
Gung Gibang sighed and dropped into a chair. Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin entered behind him and each claimed a seat.
“Where did you go?”
Gung Gibang answered curtly.
“The Chengdu branch of the Beggars’ Sect.”
“Mungyeong went with you?”

“Of course not. He’s holed up in the pavilion the Tang Clan provided for him. When I saw him earlier, he was so absorbed in a medicinal prescription that he didn’t even notice someone had come in. He’ll probably stay the night and leave with us tomorrow.”
“So? Did you find anything out?”
“No. It was a waste of time. I casually probed the branch leader about the Sichuan Tang Clan, but he didn’t know much either.”

That was understandable. From what I had heard, the Poison King’s residence lay deep in a remote mountain valley that no one ever visited. Only a member of Tang Sadok’s household would secretly stop by every once in a while.
Besides, the Sichuan Tang Clan deliberately covered everything up...
Tang Sadok wanted his family to take revenge on its own.
Considering the power possessed by the Sichuan Tang Clan, a great Murim family, and the character they had displayed, their independent course of action was not strange at all.
“He did find it a little suspicious. Apparently, the Sichuan Tang Clan recently sent people to request some information they needed.”
“They’ve already caught the scent. Did you tell him?”
Gung Gibang hesitated for a moment before speaking.

“Although Great Hero Tang Sadok ordered everyone to remain silent... I’m the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect. I told the branch leader the truth and instructed him to keep an eye on anyone suspicious.”
“What about Cheongpung?”
Amid the serious atmosphere, Cheongpung was struggling mightily to suppress a yawn.
“I sent a messenger eagle to my grandfather, just as my Benefactor instructed.”
Gung Gibang nodded and added, “The message will reach him within seven days at the latest.”
“Good. Well done.”
I thought we had taken the bare minimum of precautions.
Tang Sadok would be furious if he found out, but this was something I had to do.
“Um, Captain.”
“Hmm?”
Hyuk Mujin glanced around cautiously before speaking.
“May I ask you something?”
“If I say no, will you refrain from asking?”
“No. You know I can’t stand not knowing something.”
I was already so troubled that I could die from it, and this idiot was unbelievable.
For a moment, I considered giving him a good, satisfying smack for the first time in a while, but held myself back.
“What is it?”
“Why are you clenching your fist? That’s scary.”
“Stop stalling and ask, you bastard.”
Hyuk Mujin eyed my fist warily and whispered, “Who’s the culprit?”
“The culprit?”
“Yes. The culprit who killed and even tortured Great Hero Tang Taesang, the Poison King.”
“Well, well. The culprit.”
Smack!
“Argh! Why did you hit me?”
“If I, knew, would I, be here, doing this? Huh?”
Smack! Smack! Smack! Smack!
I pummeled the back of his head without holding back. It was wonderfully cathartic.
“Ugh... If you didn’t know, you could’ve just said so. Why...”
“Because you’re spouting nonsense and pissing me off.”
“Th-that’s...”
Gung Gibang looked contemptuously at Hyuk Mujin as he thrashed around, clutching his head.
“Tsk, tsk. Even a stray yellow dog is wiser than you. How would anyone know who that heinous bastard is or where he came from?”
Hyuk Mujin wiped away a stray tear and muttered, “You spread a mat beside that stray yellow dog and beg in the street.”
“What did you say?!”
“Why? Am I wrong?”
“How dare you insult our Sect!”
“They say you should call a spade a spade. Don’t misunderstand—I only look down on you, Young Hero Gung.”
Cheongpung burst out laughing and clapped.
“Wow! Benefactor! Young Hero Hyuk said he looks down on Young Hero Gung!”
“Don’t laugh! Stop him, you lunatic Cheongpung!”
Hyuk Mujin had gotten much better with his words.
I held back Gung Gibang, who looked ready to explode after that brutal dose of truth.
“Both of you, calm down.”
That did not seem sufficient, so I added one more thing.
“Unless you want me to beat you to death.”
That was better.
I let out a deep sigh as I watched them glower and huff at each other.
“Who knows what kind of bastard the culprit is? If we knew, the Sichuan Tang Clan would’ve caught and killed him already.”
Still glaring, Hyuk Mujin said, “I know that. I mean, do you have any guesses?”
“Think before you ask. Think, you foolish bastard.”

“But when did we become close enough for you to keep speaking informally to me? Does being the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar give you the right to look down on the Vice Squad Leader of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan’s Jin Dragon Squad? Don’t you agree, Captain?”
...Actually, given the difference between them, it did seem reasonable for him to look down on Mujin.
When I did not answer, Hyuk Mujin’s eyes narrowed.
I subtly changed the subject.
“Well, Murim is crawling with suspicious bastards. There are the Dark Heaven and Demonic Cult bastards, for starters.”
“Hmph! Do you think they’re the only possibilities?”
Gung Gibang snorted harshly and picked up the thread.
“The Sichuan Tang Clan has devoted all its strength to eliminating demonic, heterodox arts. It could have been someone with a personal grudge.”
I stared in disgust at the booger stuck to the bridge of Gung Gibang’s nose.
“Weren’t those demonic and heterodox bastards wiped out already?”

“No matter how thoroughly you sweep a courtyard, some sand always remains. The world is vast. Do you really think there was nowhere for them to hide? Some survived to the bitter end despite the relentless pursuit.”
That was a valid point.
And if they had survived being hunted by the orthodox faction that ruled Murim, every last one of them had to be an incredible master.
Like the Yin-Yang Twin Freaks I fought at Shaolin.
Who could have imagined that two Supreme Peak fiends believed to be dead would appear at Shaolin?
Murim was a place where countless chains of gratitude and grudges became tangled together. No matter what happened or where, nothing was truly surprising.
And there was the torture.
There were two reasons to torture someone.
Either you hated them enough to make them suffer before killing them, or there was something you wanted them to tell you.
I did not know the culprit’s purpose, but one thing was certain.
...One seriously dangerous bastard has appeared.
And he was someone I did not want to encounter, even by chance.

My current realm was at the very edge of Peak. I had not yet attained enlightenment, but with the power I had obtained through the System, I could hold my own against someone who had just entered Supreme Peak.
Hwangbo Eom, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, was a perfect example.

But an opponent beyond that level would be difficult. In fact, if I had not gained a small insight during my battle with Hwangbo Eom, I might have been forced to kneel before his Taeeul Formless Sword.
And if my opponent was powerful enough to kill the Poison King, who had ranked among the five strongest of the Ten Kings...
As I am now, defeat would be certain.
As much as it pained me, I had no choice but to accept that reality.
While I was quietly lost in thought, Gung Gibang suddenly spoke as if something had just occurred to him.
“Come to think of it, the culprit could be an assassin.”
“A killer? An assassin?”
“Are there other kinds of assassins?”
I frowned.
“You think those bastards are that skilled?”
“You don’t know what you’re talking about. According to my Master, the Valley Master of Moonshadow Assassination Valley has killed no fewer than three Supreme Peak masters.”
“...An assassin killed three Supreme Peak masters?”
“Without a doubt. I heard it threw the entire Murim into an uproar.”
“Then is that Valley Master or whatever the greatest assassin under heaven?”
Gung Gibang looked at me as though I were the most insane person alive.
“What are you talking about? The greatest assassin under heaven has never changed.”
“Oh.”
I had momentarily forgotten.
The Sword Saint. The Bow Saint. And finally, the man known as the Slaughter Saint.
When I first heard the name, I thought he was called the Slaughter Saint simply because he’d killed so many people.
As it turned out, being an assassin was his actual profession.

According to Jeok Cheongang, he had taken more lives than anyone could count. He killed people from the orthodox, demonic, and heterodox factions alike, so fairly and impartially that he had even been branded an enemy of all Murim.
That was until the Great Faction War.
He had killed so many demonic fiends that people had no choice but to issue an amnesty decree for the man who had once been an enemy of all Murim—and give him the alias Slaughter Saint.
“Of course, there’s no way the Slaughter Saint killed Great Hero Tang Taesang, but the Sichuan Tang Clan is probably considering the possibility that an assassin did it.”
“It’s unfortunate, but they’ll deal with it themselves.”
Whoever the culprit was, I had only one goal: find the Divine Physician and save Jeok Cheongang.
It was unfortunate that we could not receive help from the Sichuan Tang Clan, but Qingcheng and Emei still remained.
Which meant...
“Young Hero Gung, did you pull that booger out in advance so you could eat it as a late-night snack?”
“What did you say?!”
“Wahahaha! Benefactor! Young Hero Gung is going to eat his booger as a late-night snack!”
...No, seriously. What the hell was wrong with these bastards?
Unable to take it any longer, I overturned the table.
“Get the hell out! We have to leave early tomorrow, so go get some damn sleep!”
I unleashed a lion’s roar and chased the Bermuda Triangle away, then dropped back into my chair.
I stared blankly at the flickering oil lamp before murmuring, “Inventory open. Summon.”
Tap.
A small jade-colored shard appeared in my palm.
When I turned over the Divine Physician’s Token, faint writing appeared.
The finest Chinese gallnuts come from Sichuan.
Chinese gallnut, my ass. They should’ve written down the damn home address.

What the hell was wrong with these bastards?
Unable to take it any longer, I overturned the table.
“Get the hell out!
We have to leave early tomorrow, so go get some damn sleep!”
I unleashed a lion’s roar and chased the Bermuda Triangle away, then dropped back into my chair.
I stared blankly at the flickering oil lamp before murmuring, “Inventory open.
Summon.”
Tap.
A small jade-colored shard appeared in my palm.
When I turned over the Divine Physician’s Token, faint writing appeared.
The finest Chinese gallnuts come from Sichuan.
Chinese gallnut, my ass.
They should’ve written down the damn home address.

chapters.title: Chapter 338
paragraphs: That night, my mind was so full of worries that I never made it to bed. All I could do was watch the sun come up.
My body isn’t tired, but my mind is.
Looking back, I had been through every kind of upheaval imaginable over the past few months.
If I hadn’t kept my body and mind clear by circulating my qi, I might have developed stress-induced hair loss.
I had considered crossing over to reality for a while to rest, but a crazy skeleton mage was running wild over there.
Come to think of it, that place is in Sichuan too.
Was some kind of curse following me?
No wonder Shu was the first kingdom to fall in Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
Feeling vaguely uneasy, I left the pavilion with the pack frame on my back. The Bermuda Triangle was already outside waiting for me.
“Oh? The booger’s gone. Did you really eat it as a late-night snack?”
“Stop! I said stop!”
“Benefactor! Benefactor! Gung Gibang ate that booger last night!”
“I did not!”
Ugh. I wanted to beat every last one of them to death.
If this were a novel and I were the author, I would find some way to kill those bastards.
But when did anything in this world ever go the way I wanted? I was shaking my head when—
“Huff, huff. I’m sorry I’m late!”
Right. There was that guy too.
Mungyeong came running up, panting heavily.
“Huff... I-I stayed up late reading medicinal prescriptions, and...”
I didn’t even have to look. I could see the whole thing in virtual reality: he had clearly pushed himself too hard in his burning enthusiasm for learning, then overslept.
I waved off Mungyeong as he anxiously watched my expression.
“It’s fine. I just came out too. By the way, you’ve picked up quite a bit of luggage overnight.”
“Oh, this?”
Mungyeong smiled brightly and patted his bulging travel bag.
“They gave me copies of some precious medicinal prescriptions and plenty of medicinal herbs, and—and... Anyway, they gave me all sorts of things!”
“Good. Congratulations.”
“Hehe.”
That kid was absolutely thrilled.
Then again, to a novice medical apprentice like Mungyeong, all of this was practically a fortuitous encounter.
The Sichuan Tang Clan wasn’t the kind of place that opened its doors to anyone who knocked, much less freely handed over medicinal prescriptions.
It was a great Murim family as well as a renowned medical family. Everything Mungyeong had gained here would be a tremendous asset to him in the future.
“Good. You should be able to take something away from this, at least.”
“Huh?”
“Never mind.”
“Did things not go well for you?”
“Yeah. There’s someone who absolutely has to be treated, but... circumstances are making it difficult.”
We were still talking when the middle-aged man we had met the day before approached with several subordinates.
“Everyone’s here. Follow me.”
We followed him. The atmosphere and behavior of the people we passed seemed even more tense than yesterday, but there were far fewer martial artists around.
It’s begun.
Large numbers of martial artists must have left to hunt down the culprit.
No, the hunt had probably begun before we even arrived. Tang Sadok had lost his father. There was no way he would have spent several days sitting around in a daze.
After walking while lost in thought, we soon reached the iron gate.
As the gate slowly opened, the middle-aged man abruptly spoke.
“Uncle—no, the Family Head asked me to deliver a message.”
“What did he say?”
“Once his revenge is complete, our family will help you with all its strength.”
Mungyeong looked confused, but everyone else, myself included, offered a clasped-fist salute.
“May you achieve what you seek.”
“And you as well.”
A faint smile crossed the middle-aged man’s cold face.
We hadn’t received any practical assistance, but this was a decent enough farewell.
Now it was time to say goodbye to one more person.
“It’s been fun.”
Mungyeong nodded as though he understood.
“You’re leaving again.”
“Yeah. We have a lot of places to stop by.”
“If I may ask, where are you going...?”
“Qingcheng. Then Emei.”
Mungyeong’s eyes widened.

“Oh! Mount Qingcheng and Mount Emei, two of the most famous mountains under heaven! You don’t mean the sacred sites of Daoism and Buddhism, where all manner of exotic flowers and mystical herbs are said to be hidden?”
“...Uh, I think those are the ones.”
“I can’t believe it! You’re going somewhere that wonderful!”
What was this? Déjà vu?
I felt as if I had been seeing this same scene a lot lately. Just as a strange sense of foreboding sent a chill down my spine, Mungyeong let out a soft sigh.
“It’s a shame, but I can’t go with you this time. I have to return to my master.”
“Nice one, Master!”
“I mean, that’s too bad.”
“Riiight.”
“I mean it, you punk.”
Mungyeong gave me a suspicious look, then bowed deeply.
“Thank you for everything. Thanks to all you Young Masters, I survived and had so many wonderful experiences.”
“There’s no need to thank me. Stay healthy, study hard, and focus on becoming a great physician.”
Mungyeong’s eyes sparkled.
“Like the Divine Physician?”
“Exactly. Like the Divine Physician.”
“Yes, Young Master! I’ll engrave your words on my heart and never forget them!”
A quiet laugh escaped me at his spirited answer.
“Take care, then.”
“Goodbye! We have to meet again someday!”
If fate brought us together again, we would meet one way or another.
I waved to Mungyeong, then turned resolutely toward the west.
“Come on. Let’s go to Qingcheng.”
I was just about to take my first determined step when—
“Young Hero Jin Taekyung?”
“Hm?”
I looked back and saw the Bermuda Triangle standing there blankly beside two unfamiliar men.
They were the guides the Sichuan Tang Clan had assigned to us.
“What is it?”
“Um, well...”
“That’s not the right direction. The road is blocked if you go that way.”
The guides Tang Sadok had assigned us proved to be a stroke of genius.

Unusually for members of the Tang Clan, they specialized in gathering and cultivating medicinal and poisonous herbs rather than martial arts. Perhaps because of that, they knew the land of Sichuan like the backs of their hands.
“We go this way from here, right?”
“No. That way is faster.”
“But according to the map, this seems to be the right way.”
“What’s written on a map isn’t always the answer. That’s especially true of old maps.”
“The Sichuan Tang Clan gave me this one.”
“I drew that map twenty years ago.”
“Let’s go.”
Well, if the mapmaker said it was the wrong way, then it was the wrong way.
After that, I simply went wherever they told me and stopped whenever they told me. Of course, I wasn’t just following them around doing nothing.
“Wait. Can’t we just jump across here?”
“Huh? This is a cliff.”
“If we jump straight to the cliff on the other side, we’ll get there in no time.”
“You’ll die in no time too. The gap is nearly twenty zhang wide. How could you possibly—”
“Come on, let’s give it a try.”
Boom! Whoooosh! Tap-tap!
“See? It works.”
“...It actually works.”
“All right, cross one at a time!”
“...Are you talking to us?”
“Oh.”
“Could you jump back over and carry us across?”
“Can do. Easily.”
I was willing to do anything if it would save time.
Combine Made-in-Sichuan navigation with monstrous physical abilities that far exceeded human limits, and wherever I went became a road.
“My goodness... This is impossible. It only took half a day to get from Chengdu to Mount Qingcheng. The journey normally takes three days.”
“Impossible is nothing.”
I tossed out a famous line I had picked up from television as we entered Mount Qingcheng.

After revealing our identities to the disciples of the Qingcheng Sect, we were escorted to Shangqing Palace, where the sect decided all matters great and small. There, we met another Supreme Peak master: the Sect Leader of the Qingcheng Sect, Cheongpung the Ancient Sword.
“I’m Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Wow, hello! I’m Cheongpung! I’ve never met anyone with a name so similar to mine before. It’s so nice to meet you!”
“Please shut up... And Cheongpung the Ancient Sword isn’t his name. It’s his alias.”

The Elders of the Qingcheng Sect stared at us as if they had never seen such lunatics in their lives, but their Sect Leader, Cheongpung the Ancient Sword, proved far more straightforward than I had expected.
After reading the letter I handed him, he chuckled like a friendly old man from the neighborhood.
“We should help one another. Besides, Great Hero Mae Jonghak personally asked this favor of us.”
That evening, the residents at the foot of Mount Qingcheng were thrown into an uproar.
Daoists from the Qingcheng Sect, whom they were lucky to see even a few times a year, came streaming down the mountain in a long procession.
There were hundreds of them. Among their number were the Qingcheng Seventy-Two Swordsmen, all First Rate masters, as well as two Elders.
“Our Sect Leader Senior Brother ordered us to do our utmost to help Young Hero Jin find the Divine Physician.”
“Junior Brother and I have been nothing but old men gathering dust for years, but we’ll gladly step forward for something like this. Ho ho.”
Thank you. Overwhelming thanks...
Honestly, I couldn’t help getting a little choked up.
We might all belong to the orthodox faction, but an entire sect had rolled up its sleeves to save Jeok Cheongang.
“I will repay the Qingcheng Sect for this help.”
“I’ll hear that again after we find the Divine Physician.”
“And this isn’t all. We’ve also sent messenger pigeons to our lay disciples, so we should receive good news soon.”
Although the Qingcheng Sect did not possess the same standing as Huashan or Shaolin, it was still a massive, prestigious sect—large enough to be called one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
The vast web of connections it had formed through its lay disciples would be an enormous help.
“Thank you. Truly, thank you.”
“A man shouldn’t bend his back so readily. We’re merely doing what we ought to do, so pay it no mind.”
“That’s right. Too much gratitude is unsightly. Enough with the formalities. Tell us where we should begin looking.”
I rubbed at the corners of my reddened eyes and answered.
“Everywhere.”
“Huh?”
“What?”
“All of Sichuan...”
After a brief silence, quiet mutters slipped from the lips of the two old Daoists who looked like immortals.
“Goddamn it...”
“How are we supposed to find him...?”
Leaving behind the two Daoists, who had begun succumbing to the woes of the secular world less than fifteen minutes after descending the mountain, I set off toward our next destination.
“Benefactor! Are we going to Mount Emei now?”
“No. Gung and Mujin will handle the Emei Sect.”
We had two guides, and there were already plenty of people in our group. There was no need for everyone to travel in one huge crowd.
There was no telling where Cheongpung might run off to, so I would keep him with me. By now, Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin were probably running as fast as they could toward the Emei Sect.
Just then, one of the guides asked curiously,
“Then where are you going?”
“To the authorities.”
“The authorities? You mean you’re going to a government office?”
“Yes.”
“Young Hero Jin, I don’t know what connections you have with the authorities, but this isn’t something you can accomplish by mobilizing a few constables.”
“Right.”
“Then why...?”
I spoke to the guide, who shook his head as though he could not understand me at all.
“But wouldn’t it be a different story with hundreds or thousands of people?”
“H-Hundreds or thousands? Are you perhaps acquainted with the Sichuan City Lord?”
“No.”
I grinned and continued.
“I’m friends with a king.”
“Pardon?”
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.
He was the one and only younger brother of the emperor of the Great Nation that ruled the world, a noble imperial Prince—and a huge fan of mine.

chapters.title: Chapter 339
paragraphs: Early morning.
Nestled in the arms of his favorite concubine, the City Lord of Sichuan Province asked groggily, “Who is it? Who’s here to see me?”
Confronted with his superior’s naked body first thing in the morning, the Captain of the Guards hurriedly lowered his gaze.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and a man named Cheongpung of Huashan request an audience.”
“Huashan?”
The name was fairly familiar.
Though he had been born into a powerful aristocratic family and lived a life entirely removed from Murim, even the City Lord of Sichuan had heard of Huashan more than once.
“Huashan... Isn’t that one of those Ten Great Sects or whatever they’re called?”
“More precisely, they are known as the Nine Sects and One Gang. Huashan is a prestigious sect renowned throughout Murim.”
“They’re still nothing but ruffians. Calling men who swing swords in broad daylight without so much as an identification plaque a prestigious sect... Tsk, tsk.”
The Captain of the Guards had once roamed the martial world himself. He had plenty to say, but antagonizing the City Lord would not be wise.
The City Lord clicked his tongue at the silent captain, then suddenly spoke again.
“Wait. The Jin Family of Taiyuan sounds rather familiar too.”

“It is an emerging sect that unified the Murim of Shanxi two years ago and has now made its name known throughout the Central Plains. Of course, if we are speaking only of the family’s history, it is old enough to rival the Nine Sects and One Gang...”
“No, that’s not what I mean. I’ve definitely heard the name plenty of times... Ah!”
After frowning in thought for a moment, the City Lord slapped his knee with a cry of realization.
“That’s right. The Jin Family Escort Bureau!”
“The Jin Family Escort Bureau...”
Only then did the Captain of the Guards recall what he had momentarily forgotten.

Come to think of it, it had not been that long ago. Three or four months at most. The sight of wagons laden with riches rolling in one after another had stretched the City Lord’s smile from ear to ear.
“But weren’t they the Jin Family Trading Company?”
“The Jin Family Escort Bureau and the Jin Family Trading Company. Both belong to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, if I remember correctly. Yes, it’s all coming back to me.”

The Jin Family of Taiyuan had entered the world of commerce in earnest by opening new trade routes through the northern tribes. Before long, its name had begun spreading throughout the Central Plains.
“So, what have they brought this time?”
The Captain of the Guards hesitated beneath the City Lord’s expectant gaze.
“Well... they appear to have come empty-handed.”
“What?”
“However, the young man named Jin Taekyung is a direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and a young prodigy who has earned great fame in Murim...”
“Enough of that martial-world nonsense.”
The City Lord was already scowling.
Born into an aristocratic family, he had noble pride ingrained in his very bones.

If the Jin Family Trading Company had come bearing bribes, he would have welcomed them with open arms. But some young brat claiming to be the direct descendant of a frontier martial family and requesting a private audience at the crack of dawn was another matter entirely.
No need to hear him out. He’s obviously here to ask for some filthy favor. This is why you shouldn’t accept things from lowborn people so readily.
Having already decided they were unwelcome guests, the City Lord pulled the blanket up to his chin.
“Damn it. I finally got a good night’s sleep, and now my mood is ruined.”
At that moment, his favorite concubine stirred awake and asked in a seductive voice, “My lord, what has you so upset?”
“Some young brat showed up at the crack of dawn. You remember the Jin Family Trading Company that came by a few months ago, don’t you, Aehyang?”
“Oh my. Yes, yes. Of course I do.”
“He says he’s a direct descendant of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, a pack of martial-world ruffians from Shanxi.”
“And?”
“What do you mean, ‘and’? He’s obviously here to ask for some dirty favor, so I should throw him out immediately. How dare he...”
“My lord.”
“What is it?”
“Why don’t you meet him just this once?”
“W-What?”
“He might have brought another nice gift. Like this pretty necklace I’m wearing.”
The City Lord’s heart melted at his concubine’s coy smile.
Just as she said, many of the items the Jin Family Trading Company had brought last time had been rare treasures.
The various pieces of jewelry and ornaments said to have been made by the northern tribes were mysterious yet exquisitely crafted. His concubine wore them constantly and never took them off.
“It’s my request. Won’t you grant it? Please?”
Favorite concubine launches three seconds of pleading gaze!
It was super effective!
The City Lord of Sichuan frantically waved to the Captain of the Guards.
“Bring them in. Quickly!”
“Yes. Shall I escort them to the reception room?”
“What reception room? I’ll only be seeing their faces for a moment. Bring them here.”
“What are you waiting for? Hurry up and bring in those martial-world ruffians.”
The Captain of the Guards bowed with a sour expression and left the room. The City Lord thrust out his protruding belly and put on airs for his concubine.
“I’m only agreeing to meet them as a special favor because you asked.”
“Thank you, my lord. But I heard those martial-world ruffians are terribly rough... Aehyang is scared.”
“What? Scared?”

The City Lord burst into hearty laughter, then declared in a deliberately stern voice, “Ho! I govern an entire city by the command of His Imperial Majesty himself. Are you saying you fear a few common street thugs?”
“Oh my. My lord, you’re so wonderful!”
The City Lord embraced the concubine nestled against him and smiled contentedly.
“Don’t worry about a thing. The moment those bastards enter, I’ll force them to their knees so they cannot even look at you.”
“Th-That’s...!”
Patter-patter-patter—thud!
The naked City Lord bolted out of bed, threw himself flat on the floor, and cried out, “I-I behold the token of His Highness Prince Shangshan!”
Good grief. Did he cook a locomotive smokestack rare and eat it?
His reaction was so extreme that even I was momentarily taken aback.
All I had done was take that out and show it to him.
Was it really that powerful?
I looked down at the gold plaque in my hand.
It had been about a year ago, if I remembered correctly. I had even held a private autograph session for Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, and received this Item as a Quest completion Reward.

System Item Window Prince Shangshan’s Token Type: Treasure Grade: None Restriction: Jin Taekyung Description: A token imbued with the authority of Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, the emperor’s only younger brother and an imperial prince. The clouds and dragon engraved into its surface symbolize the imperial family, and it is also of immense artistic value. Special Note: Can be used only once.
I never expected to use something I had shoved into my Inventory and forgotten about like this.
I had known the imperial family wielded enormous authority in this world, but the City Lord’s reaction exceeded even my expectations.
It’s a shame I can only use it once.
Still, I couldn’t complain.
I decided to give Prince Shangshan even better fan service from now on.
Next time I see him, I’ll give him a rare collectible and even throw in a free hug.
When I remained silent, the City Lord cautiously raised his upper body.
At first, he had looked at Cheongpung and me as though we were street thugs. Now his eyes were trembling as though an earthquake had struck.
Wobble, wobble.
No, seriously. That did not need to be shaking too.
At my disgusted glare, the City Lord hurriedly covered his lower body.
“Th-There’s a reason for this...”
There probably was.
Spring flowers were beginning to bloom outside, but the smell of chestnut blossoms was overpowering in here.
I picked up a blanket lying nearby and tossed it to him.
“Th-Thank you.”
“Don’t mention it.”
If anything, I was the grateful one. Looking at a naked middle-aged man who appeared thirty-five weeks pregnant was torture in itself.
Beside me, Cheongpung stared at the City Lord’s bulging belly with keen interest and whispered, “Benefactor. Do you think it’s a boy or a girl?”
“Men can’t give birth.”
“Gasp!”
Still, he had come a long way. Just a year ago, he had firmly believed in the theory that cranes delivered babies by rocket express.
I addressed the City Lord, who had covered his lower body with the blanket and was watching me nervously.
“Neither of us gains anything by dragging this out, so I’ll get straight to the point. We came to ask you for a favor.”
“T-The messenger of His Highness Prince Shangshan need only speak. I will help to the fullest extent of my power.”
“I’m looking for someone. First, how many people can you mobilize?”

The City Lord hesitated before answering uncertainly, “W-Well, I’m not sure. Excluding the forces needed to defend against invasions by the border tribes, I believe I could mobilize several thousand.”
Several thousand government troops alone. If we added the constables from the local offices, the number would be even higher.
That was excellent news.
I smiled broadly, grabbed the City Lord by the shoulder, and pulled him to his feet.
“Then let’s start by searching everywhere around Chengdu. The first condition is that the person must be a physician.”
“A physician? The person you’re looking for is a physician?”
“Yes. People call him the Divine Physician.”
“Gasp! The Divine Physician? You mean that Divine Physician?”
“Why? Are you losing your nerve? If you do a good job, I could put in a good word for you with His Highness Prince Shangshan.”
After thinking for a moment, the City Lord of Sichuan cried out in a trembling voice, “I will devote myself to completing the mission!”
Wobble, wobble.
No, everything else was fine, but he really needed to stop that from shaking too.
The reputation I had heard about the City Lord of Sichuan was the worst imaginable.

He was known as an incompetent official who had claimed his current position through his family’s influence. His hobby was gobbling up bribes wherever he could get them, and his specialty was wine, women, and gambling—or so everyone said.
But he’s the City Lord.
That was what mattered most. Just as I had borrowed the authority of Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, the City Lord possessed the authority and power of the most powerful man in Sichuan.
“The City Lord of Sichuan, Won Gyun, commands this! Let every official in Sichuan carry out my orders without fail!”
Hearing his name had made me trust him considerably less, but a City Lord was still a City Lord.

Courier horses bearing official documents raced to every corner of Sichuan, and notices seeking the Divine Physician were posted throughout the marketplaces. Naturally, an enormous reward was offered to anyone who provided information.
“A thousand silver nyang! As expected of an acquaintance of His Highness Prince Shangshan, you are truly generous!”
Won Gyun’s admiring gaze did not last long.
“What are you talking about? You’re paying for all of it.”
“...What?”
“Do I look like someone who carries around a thousand silver nyang?”
“N-No, but even so, that’s an enormous sum.”
“Then put it on credit. I’ll mention it to His Highness Prince Shangshan later and ask him to reimburse you.”
“No! I’ll pay it myself!”
“By squeezing the lifeblood out of the common people? Or by squeezing the fat out of your own belly?”
“Even if I have to spend my personal fortune, I will pay it myself!”
“Wow. Our City Lord is so cool!”
An enormous reward capable of changing a person’s life several times over, along with a huge number of people mobilized for the search.
But even that was not enough.
If the Divine Physician could be found with this much, the imperial court wouldn’t have given up.
Who was the Divine Physician?
He was an unknown figure whom the imperial court had failed to find even after spreading a proclamation throughout the world in the emperor’s name.
People like that generally preferred to avoid notice.
“Let the government troops handle the marketplaces and busy districts. We’ll search every scenic mountain and stream.”
“I agree.”
“I should’ve just stayed at Qingcheng...”
The hundreds of Disciples who had descended the mountain with the two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect were perfect for the task.
Three days after the government and Murim joined hands and began an unprecedented full-scale search, they finally arrived.
“Captain...”
The moment I saw the exhaustion written across Hyuk Mujin’s face and Gung Gibang standing beside him in grim silence, I understood.
Something went wrong.
I could not rejoice even though the men I had been waiting for had finally arrived. One look was enough to tell me they had not brought the news we had hoped for.
I walked forward without a word. Passing Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang, I stopped before the person behind them.
“I’m Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
She was a middle-aged nun. Her closely shaven head and pallid complexion immediately caught my eye.
She was the Emei Sect’s only reinforcement.
No. She looked more like the survivor of a routed army.
“Th-This humble nun’s Dharma name is Myoryeong... Cough.”
Drops of blood trickled down her chin.
An internal injury.
I caught her as she staggered. Looking into the eyes of Venerable Myoryeong, which seemed ready to fade away at any moment, I asked forcefully, “What on earth... happened?”

Confronted with his superior’s naked body first thing in the morning, the Captain of the Guards hurriedly lowered his gaze.

This is why you shouldn’t accept things from lowborn people so readily.

He’s obviously here to ask for some dirty favor, so I should throw him out immediately.
How dare he...”
“My lord.”

Just as she said, many of the items the Jin Family Trading Company had brought last time had been rare treasures.
