chapters.title: Chapter 340
paragraphs: The middle-aged nun, Venerable Myoryeong, struggled to speak, her face pallid.
“The Venerable Nun... has entered nirvana.”
The moment I heard those words, my fist clenched on its own, and something deep in my chest sank with a heavy thud.
The two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect, who had rushed over after sensing the ominous mood, stared wide-eyed and shouted.
“Venerable Myoryeong, what do you mean? The Venerable Nun has entered nirvana?”
“That’s impossible! It can’t be!”
I already knew whom they meant by the Venerable Nun.
She, too, was one of the masters of the previous generation who remained vividly etched in Jeok Cheongang’s memories.
She was remarkably forthright. She stopped at nothing against her enemies, and her martial arts were outstanding. There were even times when she surpassed Hong Dao, that lazy bald monk.
During the Great Faction War, the Demonic Cult had feared her as the Blood Rakshasa, while the Murim of the Central Plains had bestowed upon her the sobriquet Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
Even as the years passed and the heroes of the past vanished one by one, she remained on Mount Emei and held her ground.
She was the Emei Sect’s sole Supreme Peak master and its respected Sect Leader.
And now the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was dead.
First the Poison King, and now the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
What a damned mess.
I finally spoke the words that had been hovering on the tip of my tongue.
“Who killed her?”
Venerable Myoryeong, Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin, and the two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect.
Five pairs of eyes turned toward me at once. All five held surprise, though not for the same reason.
“The culprit?”
“D-Do you mean someone murdered the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun...?”

The two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect could not continue and fell silent. They had only belatedly realized what they had failed to notice in their shock at the news: Venerable Myoryeong’s current condition.
Venerable Myoryeong’s clothes were caked with dried, dark-red blood, and her complexion had turned a deathly blue.
She stared at me with wide eyes, then lowered her head.
“As expected, Young Hero Jin already knew.”
As expected?
At my questioning look, Gung Gibang nodded gravely.
“We had no choice. The man who murdered the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun...”
“He’s the same person as the culprit behind what happened at the Sichuan Tang Clan, or at least connected to him. I think so too.”
The Elders, realizing there was something they did not know, asked in urgent voices,
“You knew about the killer? Has something happened to the Sichuan Tang Clan as well?”
“Tell us everything. Quickly!”
There was no hiding it now.
Perhaps this had been inevitable from the moment the Poison King was murdered.
I drew a deep breath and spoke.
“A few days ago, Great Hero Tang Taesang, the Poison King, passed away. More precisely, someone murdered him.”
“The Family Head, Great Hero Tang Sadok—the Myriad-Poison Asura—declared that he would have his revenge. By now, he should be pursuing the culprit with the members of his household.”
But the Poison King had not been the only victim.
Leaving the stunned Elders behind me, I looked straight at Venerable Myoryeong.
“What happened?”
“It was a middle-aged man. He was missing one arm.”
“A one-armed man?”
“Yes. He was...”
A trembling voice escaped Venerable Myoryeong’s lips.
“He was a fiend incarnate.”
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Fierce wind tore past us, and the surrounding scenery blurred with every stride.
The nun in my arms was astonishingly light, and the qi I could feel through our bodies was perilously faint.
She made it all the way here in this condition...
Venerable Myoryeong had not even finished telling us what had happened before vomiting a basinful of blood and losing consciousness.
Following close behind me, Gung Gibang spoke with a grim expression.
“How bad are her injuries?”
“Serious. I poured internal energy into her to bolster her vitality for now, but... it won’t be enough.”
Gung Gibang let out a quiet groan.
“She wasn’t this bad when we first set out. Venerable Myoryeong insisted she could endure the journey.”
“You should’ve stopped her anyway, you bastard.”
“...There was no stopping her. I’m sorry.”
My lips moved, but I pressed them shut without speaking.
I knew. Even if I had gone instead of Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin, I could not have stopped Venerable Myoryeong.
Even as she vomited blood, the voice she had forced out still rang vividly in my ears.
“The Sect Leader and all three Elders... That fiend killed them all. I—we couldn’t chase him as he walked away smiling.”
She said the fiend had descended upon Mount Emei, the sacred mountain of Buddhism, only three days ago.
The demon had climbed the mountain like any other pilgrim and sought out the residence where the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun lived. Three Elders happened to be there at the time.
Then a battle that shook heaven and earth erupted. A mountain peak collapsed, and Mount Emei itself trembled.
What Venerable Myoryeong had witnessed after recognizing the disaster and rushing there from the nearest location was four dead nuns and a single demon.
“Don’t look at me like that. My art of killing was simply stronger than Emei’s Dharma.”
“H-How could you do such a thing? Do you truly not fear Heaven?”
“How laughable. The Buddha and Heaven you speak of are all lies and illusions. I will show you that I have another Heaven.”
That was the last thing he said.
The killer struck Venerable Myoryeong with a palm and disappeared. Then, while the Emei Sect was consumed by grief and rage, two young men arrived.
After Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin told her that members of the Qingcheng Sect were nearby, she ignored everyone’s attempts to stop her and descended Mount Emei.
“Please help us. Please! No matter what, we must stop that fiend... Cough!”
Remembering Venerable Myoryeong crying out until the moment she lost consciousness made me clench my teeth.
Just what kind of bastard was he...?

A one-armed, middle-aged man. A master with enough terrifying martial prowess to single-handedly kill the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun, a Supreme Peak master of the previous generation, along with three Elders.
What was his purpose? Why had he done such a thing? And was he the same man who had murdered Tang Taesang, the Poison King?
What if he wasn’t?
The moment my thoughts reached that point, a chill ran down my spine, and my heart began pounding violently.
If the two incidents had been committed by different people... it was only a matter of time before Sichuan became a land of death.
Just as my previously effortless steps began to grow heavy, the two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect spoke.
“I think we should part ways here.”
“I’m sorry, but circumstances leave us no other choice.”
It was only natural for them to worry about their own sect.
First the Sichuan Tang Clan, and now the Emei Sect. Anyone with a brain could guess that the Qingcheng Sect might be next.
“There’s no need to apologize. I would have done the same.”
“Thank you for understanding.”
“Are you going straight to Mount Qingcheng?”
The older of the two Elders shook his head.
“I will lead some of our Disciples to assist the Emei Sect. My Junior Brother will return to the main sect with the remaining Disciples. What about you?”
“Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries are worse than I thought. I intend to find a physician first, then contact the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
With so many of their members away, the Sichuan Tang Clan and the Qingcheng Sect had both been left virtually undefended. They needed to be warned, just in case.
The Elder, whose own sect was in the same position, understood that perfectly well.
“For now, focus on treating Venerable Myoryeong. We will send someone to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Thank you.”
“Think nothing of it. May fortune favor your martial path.”
“And yours.”
We exchanged martial salutes and split into three groups.
The two Elders led their respective groups of Disciples north and east, leaving only four people, including me.
Ah. Jeok Cheongang and Venerable Myoryeong were here too.
We had come all the way to Sichuan to heal one patient, but instead of finding the Divine Physician, we had gained another.
What is this, some kind of hidden-camera prank?
Fuck, as if.
I heaved an inward sigh and was about to start walking again when—
Step. Step.
Light footsteps came up the dirt path, accompanied by cheerful humming. A boy climbing the mountain trail finally spotted us and opened his eyes wide.
“Huh? Wha—?”
It was a familiar face. The boy’s name was Mungyeong.
I was glad to see him again after only a few days, but before that feeling could fully surface, another thought flashed through my mind.
“Mungyeong.”
“What brings everyone here...? Huh?”
“You’re a medical apprentice, right?”
I still remembered him treating people on the deck of the swift ship.
I did not know exactly what treatment he had provided, but according to the river bandits, he was quite skilled.
“Yeees. I am, but...”
Mungyeong answered with a bewildered expression, then looked at Venerable Myoryeong in my arms. No further explanation was necessary.
He pulled a wooden case of acupuncture and moxibustion tools from the travel bag in his arms and strode toward us.
“First... let me examine the patient.”
Swish.
It took Mungyeong only moments to check her pulse and insert the needles.
Yet despite handling the entire process with effortless fluidity, a shadow hung over his face.
“...How is she?”
I did not need to ask to know the answer would not be good.
Sure enough, Mungyeong quietly shook his head.
“Not good. Not at all.”
“You managed to give her some basic treatment, right?”
“Yes.”
I let out a sigh of relief.
It might have been unkind, but I had never expected much from Mungyeong in the first place. He was young and had only been studying medicine for a short time.
Basic treatment was all I had wanted from him.
“You did well. That’s enough for now. If we get to Chengdu as quickly as possible and find a way...”
“Will that really be enough?”
“What?”
“In one month, her flesh will begin to rot. In four months, her bones will melt away.”
“Hold on. What the hell are you talking about...?”
But Mungyeong continued in the same quiet voice.
“After half a year of horrific pain, she will look like a living corpse. She might survive a year at most. Once her organs begin to rot, she will finally stop breathing.”
“...What?”

“Even if you take her to Chengdu, you won’t find any suitable treatment. The physicians available among the common people can only handle women’s ailments of the sort suffered by high officials and nobles. And the Sichuan Tang Clan...”
Two things shocked me.
First, that Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries were so severe.
Second, the unfamiliar sight of Mungyeong calmly describing something so horrifying.

“I heard rumors all over the marketplace that the Tang Clan’s martial artists had headed west. It will take them several days at least to return. By then, it will be too late. How long ago was she injured?”
Hyuk Mujin answered haltingly.
“Th-Three days. A little over three days, I think.”
“Three days...”
Mungyeong let out a quiet groan, then continued in a heavy voice.
“The Black Hand Seal is a terrifying evil technique. Once seven days and nights have passed, there will be no turning back.”
Grab!
That was as far as he got.
My patience snapped. Unable to hold back any longer, I seized him by the collar.
“You... How the hell do you know that?”
A teenage medical apprentice had just named an evil technique no one else present had ever heard of.
The Mungyeong I knew could never have possessed such knowledge.
“Tell me. Now.”
Mungyeong swallowed hard at my chilling aura before answering,
“My Master... My Master told me everything.”
“Your Master?”
“Y-Yes. Yes... Cough!”
A flash of realization streaked through my mind.
The strength drained from the hand gripping his collar.
A murmur like a groan slipped from my lips.
“The Divine Physician...?”

sentences.text: The middle-aged nun, Venerable Myoryeong, struggled to speak, her face pallid.
“The Venerable Nun... has entered nirvana.”
The moment I heard those words, my fist clenched on its own, and something deep in my chest sank with a heavy thud.
The two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect, who had rushed over after sensing the ominous mood, stared wide-eyed and shouted.
“Venerable Myoryeong, what do you mean?
The Venerable Nun has entered nirvana?”
“That’s impossible!
It can’t be!”
I already knew whom they meant by the Venerable Nun.
She, too, was one of the masters of the previous generation who remained vividly etched in Jeok Cheongang’s memories.
She was remarkably forthright.
She stopped at nothing against her enemies, and her martial arts were outstanding.
There were even times when she surpassed Hong Dao, that lazy bald monk.
During the Great Faction War, the Demonic Cult had feared her as the Blood Rakshasa, while the Murim of the Central Plains had bestowed upon her the sobriquet Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
Even as the years passed and the heroes of the past vanished one by one, she remained on Mount Emei and held her ground.
She was the Emei Sect’s sole Supreme Peak master and its respected Sect Leader.
And now the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was dead.
First the Poison King, and now the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
What a damned mess.
I finally spoke the words that had been hovering on the tip of my tongue.
“Who killed her?”
Venerable Myoryeong, Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin, and the two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect.
Five pairs of eyes turned toward me at once.
All five held surprise, though not for the same reason.
“The culprit?”
“D-Do you mean someone murdered the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun...?”
The two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect could not continue and fell silent.
They had only belatedly realized what they had failed to notice in their shock at the news: Venerable Myoryeong’s current condition.
Venerable Myoryeong’s clothes were caked with dried, dark-red blood, and her complexion had turned a deathly blue.
She stared at me with wide eyes, then lowered her head.
“As expected, Young Hero Jin already knew.”
As expected?
At my questioning look, Gung Gibang nodded gravely.
“We had no choice.
The man who murdered the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun...”
“He’s the same person as the culprit behind what happened at the Sichuan Tang Clan, or at least connected to him.
I think so too.”
The Elders, realizing there was something they did not know, asked in urgent voices,
“You knew about the killer?
Has something happened to the Sichuan Tang Clan as well?”
“Tell us everything.
Quickly!”
There was no hiding it now.
Perhaps this had been inevitable from the moment the Poison King was murdered.
I drew a deep breath and spoke.
“A few days ago, Great Hero Tang Taesang, the Poison King, passed away.
More precisely, someone murdered him.”
“The Family Head, Great Hero Tang Sadok—the Myriad-Poison Asura—declared that he would have his revenge.
By now, he should be pursuing the culprit with the members of his household.”
But the Poison King had not been the only victim.
Leaving the stunned Elders behind me, I looked straight at Venerable Myoryeong.
“What happened?”
“It was a middle-aged man.
He was missing one arm.”
“A one-armed man?”
“Yes.
He was...”
A trembling voice escaped Venerable Myoryeong’s lips.
“He was a fiend incarnate.”
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Fierce wind tore past us, and the surrounding scenery blurred with every stride.
The nun in my arms was astonishingly light, and the qi I could feel through our bodies was perilously faint.
She made it all the way here in this condition...
Venerable Myoryeong had not even finished telling us what had happened before vomiting a basinful of blood and losing consciousness.
Following close behind me, Gung Gibang spoke with a grim expression.
“How bad are her injuries?”
“Serious.
I poured internal energy into her to bolster her vitality for now, but... it won’t be enough.”
Gung Gibang let out a quiet groan.
“She wasn’t this bad when we first set out.
Venerable Myoryeong insisted she could endure the journey.”
“You should’ve stopped her anyway, you bastard.”
“...There was no stopping her.
I’m sorry.”
My lips moved, but I pressed them shut without speaking.
I knew.
Even if I had gone instead of Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin, I could not have stopped Venerable Myoryeong.
Even as she vomited blood, the voice she had forced out still rang vividly in my ears.
“The Sect Leader and all three Elders...
That fiend killed them all.
I—we couldn’t chase him as he walked away smiling.”
She said the fiend had descended upon Mount Emei, the sacred mountain of Buddhism, only three days ago.
The demon had climbed the mountain like any other pilgrim and sought out the residence where the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun lived.
Three Elders happened to be there at the time.
Then a battle that shook heaven and earth erupted.
A mountain peak collapsed, and Mount Emei itself trembled.
What Venerable Myoryeong had witnessed after recognizing the disaster and rushing there from the nearest location was four dead nuns and a single demon.
“Don’t look at me like that.
My art of killing was simply stronger than Emei’s Dharma.”
“H-How could you do such a thing?
Do you truly not fear Heaven?”
“How laughable.
The Buddha and Heaven you speak of are all lies and illusions.
I will show you that I have another Heaven.”
That was the last thing he said.
The killer struck Venerable Myoryeong with a palm and disappeared.
Then, while the Emei Sect was consumed by grief and rage, two young men arrived.
After Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin told her that members of the Qingcheng Sect were nearby, she ignored everyone’s attempts to stop her and descended Mount Emei.
“Please help us.
Please!
No matter what, we must stop that fiend...
Cough!”
Remembering Venerable Myoryeong crying out until the moment she lost consciousness made me clench my teeth.
Just what kind of bastard was he...?
A one-armed, middle-aged man.
A master with enough terrifying martial prowess to single-handedly kill the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun, a Supreme Peak master of the previous generation, along with three Elders.
What was his purpose?
Why had he done such a thing?
And was he the same man who had murdered Tang Taesang, the Poison King?
What if he wasn’t?
The moment my thoughts reached that point, a chill ran down my spine, and my heart began pounding violently.
If the two incidents had been committed by different people... it was only a matter of time before Sichuan became a land of death.
Just as my previously effortless steps began to grow heavy, the two Elders of the Qingcheng Sect spoke.
“I think we should part ways here.”
“I’m sorry, but circumstances leave us no other choice.”
It was only natural for them to worry about their own sect.
First the Sichuan Tang Clan, and now the Emei Sect.
Anyone with a brain could guess that the Qingcheng Sect might be next.
“There’s no need to apologize.
I would have done the same.”
“Thank you for understanding.”
“Are you going straight to Mount Qingcheng?”
The older of the two Elders shook his head.
“I will lead some of our Disciples to assist the Emei Sect.
My Junior Brother will return to the main sect with the remaining Disciples.
What about you?”
“Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries are worse than I thought.
I intend to find a physician first, then contact the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
With so many of their members away, the Sichuan Tang Clan and the Qingcheng Sect had both been left virtually undefended.
They needed to be warned, just in case.
The Elder, whose own sect was in the same position, understood that perfectly well.

“Thank you.”

May fortune favor your martial path.”

chapters.title: Chapter 341
paragraphs: A conversation I’d had with Mungyeong several days ago flashed through my mind.
Thank you for everything.
Forget the thanks. Just focus on becoming a great physician.
Like the Divine Physician?
Yes, like the Divine Physician.
And then there was the last thing he had said almost in passing.
It’s a shame we can’t go together this time. I have to return to my Master.
How had I not realized it?

Looking back, Mungyeong had been unusual from the very beginning. He had shown incredible resourcefulness when the river bandits threatened his life, composure far beyond his years, and remarkable medical skill.
That’s not all.

The boy had nearly sunk to the bottom of the Yangtze because of the river bandits, yet he had brazenly hitched a ride aboard the swift ship and then visited the Sichuan Tang Clan—infamous throughout Murim for their vicious tempers—just to get a prescription.
Mungyeong had casually done things that even martial artists with Botox injected into their livers might have shied away from.
And on top of that, the things he just said and did...
I had no idea what kind of martial art the Black Hand Seal was or how powerful it might be.
But I knew one thing for certain.
“The Divine Physician. You’re the Divine Physician’s Disciple.”
The others stared wide-eyed at Mungyeong after hearing the joy and deflation mingled in my words.
A suffocating silence descended over us, and Mungyeong shrank back.
“I-I’m sorry. But I couldn’t tell you.”
“Why not?”
I regretted asking the moment the words left my mouth. The Divine Physician had spent his entire life hiding his identity. Of course his Disciple had kept silent.
If Venerable Myoryeong’s life had not been hanging by a thread, Mungyeong almost certainly would never have revealed his Master’s identity.
“Where is the Divine Physician—or rather, where is your Master?”
Mungyeong hesitated, then bit his lip tightly.
“But before that, could you promise me one thing?”
“I’ll keep the secret. Absolutely.”
With that firm answer, I pulled something from inside my robe and held it out.
Lately, I had been taking it out of my Inventory and examining it whenever I had a spare moment.
The finest Chinese gallnuts come from Sichuan.
Mungyeong’s eyes widened when he saw the faint writing on the jade-colored porcelain shard.
“This is...”
“Do you recognize it?”
“Yes. It’s unmistakably my Master’s handwriting.”
Mungyeong examined the Divine Physician’s Token from every angle, apparently fascinated, then let out a small exclamation.
“Come to think of it, my Master once told me that a very long time ago, he left a token with a famous physician and told him to come to Sichuan. But how did you come to possess it, Young Master...?”
“The famous physician gave it to me directly. There’s a patient whom no one but the Divine Physician can treat.”
I continued emphatically.
“There’s someone I have to save.”
“I don’t know who that person is, but... you hold them very dear, Young Master.”
Someone dear to me.
Yes. I supposed that was true. Jeok Cheongang was precious to me. He had given me everything he had, and now it was my turn to protect him.
“Yes. That’s right.”
Mungyeong smiled faintly and nodded.
“Come with me. I’ll take you to my Master.”
Crunch. Crunch.
The snow crunched beneath our feet with every step.
I looked around. Bare branches covered in frost. Thick white snow blanketing everything in sight.
It doesn’t get any less incredible.
Outside, it was early spring, and new shoots were beginning to emerge. But the place we were walking through looked like the depths of winter after a heavy snowfall.
So this is a Mystic Gate Formation...

Mungyeong had led us to the very same mountain we had searched with the Qingcheng Sect. But when we reached a certain point, he strained to move several rocks, and an entirely new path and landscape unfolded before us.
It was unlike anything we had ever seen. Every last one of us had stood there with our mouths hanging open.
Mungyeong told us that the formation had been installed by the Master of Strange Illusions.
According to Gung Gibang, who had sprayed spit everywhere as he explained, the Master of Strange Illusions had been known as the greatest formation master under heaven in the distant past.

I had no idea what sort of connection he had shared with the Divine Physician, but he had installed something like this. We had nearly wandered around for ages despite being right on top of the place.
No wonder nobody could find him.
What good was it to deploy top-tier Murim artists and countless government troops?
If they had searched each mountain one by one using ordinary methods, even half a century would not have been enough, let alone six months.
“Wow! Woooow!”

Cheongpung, who had been running several steps ahead of us like a puppy let loose in a snowy field, cried out in delight. I was about to scold him when the scenery changed completely the very next moment, and my mouth fell open too.
“...Whoa. What the hell is this?”
The world had changed again in the space of a few steps.
The snow-white depths of winter had given way to spring in full bloom.
Everything around us was green, and nameless flowers were in full bloom. Hyuk Mujin approached with a dazed expression and asked,
“Captain. Am I seeing things?”
“I don’t know, Mujin.”
Even Gung Gibang, the most experienced in Murim among us, stood there with his mouth hanging open.
“Good heavens... Hk! Ptooey, ptooey! What is this?”
“Butterflies?”
Oh, they really were butterflies. And not just one or two.
Every color imaginable.
Hundreds of butterflies resting throughout the flower field took flight at once. It was a spectacular sight.
Whoooosh.
Where had the wind suddenly come from? And where was the bright sunlight pouring in from?
Every single thing I saw felt like one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
The pyramids have nothing on this.
There was a place where the seasons changed after only a few steps, so what were the pyramids compared to that? Some Egyptian logistics officer probably just ran his workers ragged building them.
All the pharaoh had to do was put on a solemn face and say, “This pharaoh is disappointed in you,” a few times, and they would be hauling stones while getting whipped.
But this place...
This was on an entirely different level.
“Young Master Jin?”
“Huh? Oh, yeah.”
“We’re almost there. We only have to cross that hill.”
We hurriedly came to our senses and followed Mungyeong again.
Once we crossed the low hill covered in green grass, a small thatched hut came into view, standing alone on a flat stretch of land.
And...
He was there.
“Master!”

At Mungyeong’s shout, an old man planting something in the vegetable garden before the hut straightened his bent back. His beard was as white as the snow we had seen along the way. His eyes were clear and framed by deep wrinkles.
When he noticed us, the corners of his eyes curved gently.
“Some honored guests have arrived.”
We had finally found him.
The Divine Physician.
It was a long while before we properly spoke with the Divine Physician.
After examining Venerable Myoryeong, the Divine Physician had Mungyeong carry her into the hut. The two of them did not emerge again until a shichen later.
“It has been a long time since anyone came to visit.”
The Divine Physician’s sudden voice was like a cool spring breeze. I had been pacing around the hut and hurriedly bowed.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan pays his respects to the Divine Physician.”
“Dong Feng.”
“Pardon?”
“That is my name. The title Divine Physician is too grand for me, so please call me Old Man Dong.”
How could I call the greatest physician under heaven Old Man Dong, as if he were some old man Kim at a neighborhood real estate office?
I was young enough to be his grandson, too.
But when I met the Divine Physician’s benevolent gaze, I had no choice but to quietly comply.
“Yes. I will, Old Man Dong.”
“Thank you, Young Master Jin.”
The Divine Physician smiled gently, then exchanged greetings with everyone else, one by one.
He remained courteous even toward those of us who were far younger than him, and he never once seemed hurried.
“Hello! I’m Cheongpung!”
He did not even lose his smile in front of the local lunatic.
“Heh heh. You’re a very energetic person. My name is Dong Feng. You may call me Old Man Dong, just like the others.”
“But my grandfather told me I have to show respect to my elders.”
“Your grandfather gave you an excellent lesson. But if our hearts are at ease with each other, what harm is there? Just think of me as a friend who happens to be a little older than you.”
“A friend?”
“That’s right. A friend.”
Cheongpung smiled brightly.
“Then let’s get along, Old Man Dong!”
“Heh heh. Heh heh heh!”
He’s laughing?
Was he some kind of Murim Joker? The type who laughed when he was angry and laughed when he was dumbfounded?
“Old Man Dong, have you ever tried candy?”
“I like sweets. I used to enjoy candied hawthorn skewers, too.”
“Hey, me too!”

The setting looked like a healing movie, but the conversation was pure horror thriller. In the end, Gung Gibang’s face went deathly pale. He clamped both hands over Cheongpung’s mouth and slowly backed away.
The Divine Physician laughed heartily at the sight, then turned to Mungyeong.
“You have brought some interesting people.”
Mungyeong bowed deeply.
“I’m sorry, Master. I brought them without your permission.”
“No, no. Heaven brings people together through fate. This, too, must be the natural order. Wouldn’t you agree?”
His last question was directed at me. I nodded and held out the Divine Physician’s Token I had prepared in advance.
“This is...”
“This is a token you left behind long ago, Divine Physician—or rather, Old Man Dong. The Luoyang Strange Physician gave it to me and told me to seek you out.”
“I did?”
“Pardon?”
No way. Had he forgotten about it?
The Divine Physician tilted his head. Only after Mungyeong reminded him again did he let out a small exclamation.
“Ah, yes. I remember now. It happened so long ago that it had slipped my mind.”
“Whew. For a moment, I thought you’d forgotten completely.”
“In any case, if you possess this token... that must mean something has happened that requires this old man’s aid.”
“Yes, that’s right.”
“Is it about the nun you brought here? If so, there is no need to worry too much. She has already made it past the immediate crisis.”
The Divine Physician looked toward the hut where Venerable Myoryeong lay and continued.
“It will not be an easy road, but... once the rest of her treatment is complete, sufficient rest should allow her to make a full recovery.”
It was the best news I had heard in a long time. Not only had Venerable Myoryeong escaped the brink of death, but the Divine Physician truly possessed medical skill worthy of his reputation.
I took a deep breath before speaking.
“There’s another patient.”
“Another patient?”
“The person who gave me the token said that there was only one person under heaven who could treat him. You.”
“Only I can treat him...”
The Divine Physician repeated the words quietly, then spoke.
“Birth, aging, sickness, and death are not things a mere human can decide. But if there is even the slightest possibility, I will do my best as a physician.”
“That’s enough... That’s all I need.”
There had been a time when my mother was sick.
The doctor in charge of her surgery had said the same thing.
I’ll do my best.
For Hayeon and me, those words had been our only hope, and the surgery had been a success.
Just as I had done with that doctor in the past, I tightly gripped the Divine Physician’s wrinkled hand.
“Please. Old Man Dong.”
The Divine Physician smiled benevolently, as though he understood everything.
“Let us see the patient first.”
After that came nothing but waiting and anxiety.
Once Jeok Cheongang, who had been lying on the pack frame, was carried into the hut, I paced back and forth, waiting for the Divine Physician and Mungyeong to emerge.
Butterflies and honeybees flitted through the flower field, and fresh green leaves sprouted from the trees, but I felt nothing.
It went well, right? It must have gone well.
I could not even bring myself to approach the hut, afraid that I might hear something negative.
I walked for a long time, endlessly repeating that single thought.
Only after the sunlight had faded and a pale darkness settled over the land did I return to the hut.
There, the exhausted Divine Physician and Mungyeong were waiting for me with faint smiles.
“I believe I can treat him.”
The instant I heard those words, all the strength drained from my legs, and a familiar alert pierced my ears.
Ding.

The others stared wide-eyed at Mungyeong after hearing the joy and deflation mingled in my words.
A suffocating silence descended over us, and Mungyeong shrank back.
“I-I’m sorry.
But I couldn’t tell you.”
“Why not?”
I regretted asking the moment the words left my mouth.
The Divine Physician had spent his entire life hiding his identity.
Of course his Disciple had kept silent.
If Venerable Myoryeong’s life had not been hanging by a thread, Mungyeong almost certainly would never have revealed his Master’s identity.
“Where is the Divine Physician—or rather, where is your Master?”
Mungyeong hesitated, then bit his lip tightly.
“But before that, could you promise me one thing?”
“I’ll keep the secret.
Absolutely.”
With that firm answer, I pulled something from inside my robe and held it out.
Lately, I had been taking it out of my Inventory and examining it whenever I had a spare moment.
The finest Chinese gallnuts come from Sichuan.
Mungyeong’s eyes widened when he saw the faint writing on the jade-colored porcelain shard.
“This is...”
“Do you recognize it?”
“Yes.
It’s unmistakably my Master’s handwriting.”
Mungyeong examined the Divine Physician’s Token from every angle, apparently fascinated, then let out a small exclamation.
“Come to think of it, my Master once told me that a very long time ago, he left a token with a famous physician and told him to come to Sichuan.
But how did you come to possess it, Young Master...?”
“The famous physician gave it to me directly.
There’s a patient whom no one but the Divine Physician can treat.”
I continued emphatically.
“There’s someone I have to save.”
“I don’t know who that person is, but... you hold them very dear, Young Master.”
Someone dear to me.
Yes.
I supposed that was true.
Jeok Cheongang was precious to me.
He had given me everything he had, and now it was my turn to protect him.
“Yes.
That’s right.”
Mungyeong smiled faintly and nodded.
“Come with me.
I’ll take you to my Master.”
Crunch.
Crunch.
The snow crunched beneath our feet with every step.
I looked around.
Bare branches covered in frost.
Thick white snow blanketing everything in sight.
It doesn’t get any less incredible.
Outside, it was early spring, and new shoots were beginning to emerge.
But the place we were walking through looked like the depths of winter after a heavy snowfall.
So this is a Mystic Gate Formation...
Mungyeong had led us to the very same mountain we had searched with the Qingcheng Sect.
But when we reached a certain point, he strained to move several rocks, and an entirely new path and landscape unfolded before us.
It was unlike anything we had ever seen.
Every last one of us had stood there with our mouths hanging open.
Mungyeong told us that the formation had been installed by the Master of Strange Illusions.
According to Gung Gibang, who had sprayed spit everywhere as he explained, the Master of Strange Illusions had been known as the greatest formation master under heaven in the distant past.
I had no idea what sort of connection he had shared with the Divine Physician, but he had installed something like this.
We had nearly wandered around for ages despite being right on top of the place.
No wonder nobody could find him.
What good was it to deploy top-tier Murim artists and countless government troops?
If they had searched each mountain one by one using ordinary methods, even half a century would not have been enough, let alone six months.
“Wow!
Woooow!”
Cheongpung, who had been running several steps ahead of us like a puppy let loose in a snowy field, cried out in delight.
I was about to scold him when the scenery changed completely the very next moment, and my mouth fell open too.
“...Whoa.
What the hell is this?”
The world had changed again in the space of a few steps.
The snow-white depths of winter had given way to spring in full bloom.
Everything around us was green, and nameless flowers were in full bloom.
Hyuk Mujin approached with a dazed expression and asked,
“Captain.
Am I seeing things?”
“I don’t know, Mujin.”
Even Gung Gibang, the most experienced in Murim among us, stood there with his mouth hanging open.
“Good heavens...
Hk!
Ptooey, ptooey!
What is this?”
“Butterflies?”
Oh, they really were butterflies.
And not just one or two.
Every color imaginable.
Hundreds of butterflies resting throughout the flower field took flight at once.
It was a spectacular sight.
Whoooosh.
Where had the wind suddenly come from?
And where was the bright sunlight pouring in from?
Every single thing I saw felt like one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
The pyramids have nothing on this.
There was a place where the seasons changed after only a few steps, so what were the pyramids compared to that?
Some Egyptian logistics officer probably just ran his workers ragged building them.
All the pharaoh had to do was put on a solemn face and say, “This pharaoh is disappointed in you,” a few times, and they would be hauling stones while getting whipped.
But this place...
This was on an entirely different level.
“Young Master Jin?”
“Huh?
Oh, yeah.”
“We’re almost there.
We only have to cross that hill.”
We hurriedly came to our senses and followed Mungyeong again.
Once we crossed the low hill covered in green grass, a small thatched hut came into view, standing alone on a flat stretch of land.
And...
He was there.
“Master!”
At Mungyeong’s shout, an old man planting something in the vegetable garden before the hut straightened his bent back.
His beard was as white as the snow we had seen along the way.
His eyes were clear and framed by deep wrinkles.
When he noticed us, the corners of his eyes curved gently.
“Some honored guests have arrived.”
We had finally found him.
The Divine Physician.
It was a long while before we properly spoke with the Divine Physician.
After examining Venerable Myoryeong, the Divine Physician had Mungyeong carry her into the hut.
The two of them did not emerge again until a shichen later.
“It has been a long time since anyone came to visit.”
The Divine Physician’s sudden voice was like a cool spring breeze.
I had been pacing around the hut and hurriedly bowed.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan pays his respects to the Divine Physician.”
“Dong Feng.”
“Pardon?”
“That is my name.
The title Divine Physician is too grand for me, so please call me Old Man Dong.”
How could I call the greatest physician under heaven Old Man Dong, as if he were some old man Kim at a neighborhood real estate office?
I was young enough to be his grandson, too.
But when I met the Divine Physician’s benevolent gaze, I had no choice but to quietly comply.
“Yes.
I will, Old Man Dong.”
“Thank you, Young Master Jin.”
The Divine Physician smiled gently, then exchanged greetings with everyone else, one by one.
He remained courteous even toward those of us who were far younger than him, and he never once seemed hurried.
“Hello!
I’m Cheongpung!”
He did not even lose his smile in front of the local lunatic.
“Heh heh.
You’re a very energetic person.
My name is Dong Feng.
You may call me Old Man Dong, just like the others.”
“But my grandfather told me I have to show respect to my elders.”
“Your grandfather gave you an excellent lesson.
But if our hearts are at ease with each other, what harm is there?
Just think of me as a friend who happens to be a little older than you.”
“A friend?”
“That’s right.
A friend.”
Cheongpung smiled brightly.
“Then let’s get along, Old Man Dong!”
“Heh heh.
Heh heh heh!”
He’s laughing?
Was he some kind of Murim Joker?
The type who laughed when he was angry and laughed when he was dumbfounded?
“Old Man Dong, have you ever tried candy?”
“I like sweets.
I used to enjoy candied hawthorn skewers, too.”
“Hey, me too!”
The setting looked like a healing movie, but the conversation was pure horror thriller.
In the end, Gung Gibang’s face went deathly pale.
He clamped both hands over Cheongpung’s mouth and slowly backed away.
The Divine Physician laughed heartily at the sight, then turned to Mungyeong.
“You have brought some interesting people.”
Mungyeong bowed deeply.
“I’m sorry, Master.
I brought them without your permission.”
“No, no.
Heaven brings people together through fate.
This, too, must be the natural order.
Wouldn’t you agree?”
His last question was directed at me.
I nodded and held out the Divine Physician’s Token I had prepared in advance.
“This is...”
“This is a token you left behind long ago, Divine Physician—or rather, Old Man Dong.
The Luoyang Strange Physician gave it to me and told me to seek you out.”
“I did?”
“Pardon?”
No way.
Had he forgotten about it?
The Divine Physician tilted his head.
Only after Mungyeong reminded him again did he let out a small exclamation.
“Ah, yes.
I remember now.
It happened so long ago that it had slipped my mind.”
“Whew.
For a moment, I thought you’d forgotten completely.”
“In any case, if you possess this token... that must mean something has happened that requires this old man’s aid.”
“Yes, that’s right.”
“Is it about the nun you brought here?
If so, there is no need to worry too much.
She has already made it past the immediate crisis.”
The Divine Physician looked toward the hut where Venerable Myoryeong lay and continued.
“It will not be an easy road, but... once the rest of her treatment is complete, sufficient rest should allow her to make a full recovery.”
It was the best news I had heard in a long time.
Not only had Venerable Myoryeong escaped the brink of death, but the Divine Physician truly possessed medical skill worthy of his reputation.
I took a deep breath before speaking.
“There’s another patient.”
“Another patient?”
“The person who gave me the token said that there was only one person under heaven who could treat him.
You.”
“Only I can treat him...”
The Divine Physician repeated the words quietly, then spoke.
“Birth, aging, sickness, and death are not things a mere human can decide.
But if there is even the slightest possibility, I will do my best as a physician.”
“That’s enough...
That’s all I need.”
There had been a time when my mother was sick.
The doctor in charge of her surgery had said the same thing.
I’ll do my best.
For Hayeon and me, those words had been our only hope, and the surgery had been a success.
Just as I had done with that doctor in the past, I tightly gripped the Divine Physician’s wrinkled hand.
“Please.
Old Man Dong.”
The Divine Physician smiled benevolently, as though he understood everything.
“Let us see the patient first.”
After that came nothing but waiting and anxiety.
Once Jeok Cheongang, who had been lying on the pack frame, was carried into the hut, I paced back and forth, waiting for the Divine Physician and Mungyeong to emerge.
Butterflies and honeybees flitted through the flower field, and fresh green leaves sprouted from the trees, but I felt nothing.
It went well, right?
It must have gone well.
I could not even bring myself to approach the hut, afraid that I might hear something negative.
I walked for a long time, endlessly repeating that single thought.
Only after the sunlight had faded and a pale darkness settled over the land did I return to the hut.
There, the exhausted Divine Physician and Mungyeong were waiting for me with faint smiles.
“I believe I can treat him.”
The instant I heard those words, all the strength drained from my legs, and a familiar alert pierced my ears.
Ding.
System Quest condition, Get Examined by the Divine Physician, completed! - Quest, Find Mr.
Shin in Sichuan, successfully completed!

chapters.title: Chapter 342
paragraphs: Finding Mr. Shin in Sichuan had been a Supreme Peak Grade Quest. With difficulty that vicious, the rewards were bound to be substantial.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
A massive EXP payout and the resulting Level Up. Even an achievement.
I dismissed the incessant System notifications and the holographic windows blocking my view. I couldn’t simply celebrate when the Divine Physician looked so grim.
“What’s wrong? You haven’t changed your mind, have you? You’re not about to tell me you can’t treat him after all, right?”
“Of course not. I may be an old quack, but if I give it my all, there is still plenty of hope.”
“Then why do you look like that...?”
He hesitated before letting out a soft sigh. The faint smile on his lips had vanished, replaced by deeply troubled lines.
“There are too many things we must prepare for the treatment.”
“Oh, if this is about the cost, you don’t need to worry.”

I might not look it, but I was the youngest son of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. It was common knowledge that the Jin Family had amassed a fortune through the northern trade routes over the past few years.
“If things get desperate, I can always borrow some money from this guy’s family. Hey, there are Hyuk Family textile shops in Sichuan too, aren’t there?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded, looking less than thrilled.
“There are. We’re textile merchants. It would be strange if we didn’t have a shop in Sichuan, considering how famous it is for silk.”
“Then let’s borrow some emergency cash. We can sell the shop if we have to, right?”
“Of course not.”
“I’ll pay you plenty of interest.”
“And if I refuse?”
“Then I’ll give you plenty of travel money for your journey to the next world.”
“...Just take it all. Go ahead and rip out the very foundations of my family while you’re at it.”
Okay, problem solved.
But for some reason, the Divine Physician’s expression remained dark.
His Master seemed unable to bring himself to speak, so Mungyeong stepped in.
“Um, Young Master Jin.”
“Yes?”
“That isn’t the biggest problem. The treatment will require an enormous amount of money, but some materials would be difficult to obtain no matter how much gold and silver we had.”
“Materials that are difficult to obtain...? Are you talking about an elixir?”

“Yes. Treating Great Hero Jeok requires an elixir that meets certain conditions. Such elixirs are extremely valuable and rare. If we begin searching now, we may have to wait several years before finding one.”
Several years?
That was far too long. Jeok Cheongang had only a few months left to live.
I was struck speechless. The Divine Physician continued in a somber voice.
“I believe a detailed explanation is in order. The patient has not regained consciousness because the balance within his body has been disrupted.”
“His balance?”

“All things in the world contain the energies of the Five Elements and exist in proper balance. The human body is no different. But the patient attempted to wield an enormous force and destroyed that balance.”
An enormous force?
The Divine Physician’s words brought something to mind.
Dance of the Fire God and Demon. The Fire Gate Clan’s ultimate secret technique, which drew out and amplified every ounce of power its user possessed.
So that was the cause.

In the distant past, Jeok Cheongang had earned the name Fire King by using the Dance of the Fire God and Demon against a thousand members of the Demonic Cult. But as the years passed, his old and diseased body could no longer endure that power. It had shattered.
“When a vessel breaks, whatever it held inside will inevitably leak out. Fortunately, there is a way to reverse the damage, but it requires an elixir rarely seen in this world.”
“An elixir rarely seen in this world...”
“And even among such elixirs, it must meet certain conditions.”
“Tell me. I’ll get it, no matter what it takes.”
The Divine Physician sighed and nodded.
“It will be extremely difficult, but what choice do we have? We must place our hopes in you, Young Master. Listen carefully to what I am about to say.”
“Yes.”
In a grave voice, the Divine Physician explained Jeok Cheongang’s condition, the method of treatment, and the requirements for the necessary elixir.
“Will you remember all of that?”
“Young Master?”
“Oh, yes.”
“I asked whether you remember all of it.”
“Yes. I remember everything. But this is... Whew.”
“Could you check—I mean, confirm that I heard everything correctly?”
“I was planning to do so anyway. Go ahead.”
I carefully began to speak.
“So, the excessive expenditure of power disrupted his balance, and the harmony between Yin and Yang was particularly badly damaged?”
“That is correct.”
“And the cause was an enormous amount of Scorching Yang Qi that had gone out of control.”
“Continue.”
“To restore that broken balance and bring everything back into harmony, we need an elixir—and an incredibly powerful one at that. And for that...”
Mungyeong quickly cut in.
“Among elixirs, it must possess the nature of Yin-Cold Qi. It must also contain at least one jiazi’s worth of energy.”
“Four months,” the Divine Physician said heavily. “If we cannot find one within four months, everything else will be pointless.”
At that moment, the conversation came to an end.
Ding.

System A Chain Quest, Thirty Thousand Li in Search of an Elixir, has been generated. - This is something you must accomplish. You cannot refuse! - Find an elixir containing at least one jiazi of energy and possessing the nature of Yin-Cold Qi!
I stared blankly at the holographic window before finally coming to my senses.
“Will that do?”
“Many other materials are necessary, but this will be the most important one—the core ingredient. You must depart immediately and search for the elixir...”
“Ah, yes.”
And so I departed.
I took two steps toward the Divine Physician, pulled something from inside my robe, and held it out.
“Here.”
“Take it.”
Master and Disciple stared blankly at me, then simultaneously reached out to accept the object.
“What is this?”
“Master, perhaps you should open it first.”
“W-Well, shall I?”
Click.
The Divine Physician swallowed nervously and carefully opened the wooden box. A pure, clear fragrance that seemed capable of purifying even the coronavirus wafted out as it revealed itself.
“Gasp!”
“Good heavens!”
“It’s a Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng. It contains at least one jiazi’s worth of energy and possesses the nature of Yin-Cold Qi. Is this enough?”
Eyes wide, the Divine Physician looked back and forth between me and the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, then nodded vigorously.
“It is enough!”
Ding.

System Quest conditions fulfilled! - Chain Quest, Thirty Thousand Li in Search of an Elixir, successfully completed! - Achievement, Mountain Herb Gatherer, acquired! - A substantial amount of EXP acquired! - Level Up!
As the System notifications rang out, Ju Hwaran suddenly came to mind.
Thank you, Young Lady Ju.

I let out a wry chuckle as I thought of how she had given it to me while passing the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng off as Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, worried I might feel burdened and refuse it otherwise.
Now I have a reason to stop by Shaanxi on the way back.
And when I did... I hoped Jeok Cheongang would be healthy again and traveling with me.
I turned to the Divine Physician, who still looked dazed.
“All right, then. What do we do next?”
The Divine Physician carefully tucked the wooden box into his robes and began walking.
“Follow me. Gyeong, remain here and look after the patients.”
“Yes, Master.”
Leaving Mungyeong behind as he answered respectfully, we followed the Divine Physician.
Swish!
A small figure sped along right beside me. Every time he extended one foot, a zhang of distance vanished and the wind swept past.
What was truly astonishing was that his feet never touched the ground.
With each faint tap of his toes, the blades of grass bent gently beneath him, then sprang back into place.
I narrowed my eyes.
Flying Over Grass?
Flying Over Grass was a realm in which one ran as though flying while stepping across blades of grass.

Martial artists who had mastered their movement techniques to the Peak realm could perform such feats. Treading Snow Without a Trace, which left no footprints even while running across snow, and Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water, which allowed one to walk across water as though it were solid ground, worked on similar principles.
Stepping on Empty Air, meanwhile, was a realm attainable only by Supreme Peak masters with internal energy to spare.
Of course, Flying Over Grass isn’t beyond me either if I put my mind to it.
Even so, the sight was astonishing because the person performing it was the Divine Physician.
I knew he had learned martial arts, but his movement technique is especially impressive.
I had realized the Divine Physician knew martial arts the moment we first met.
Though small in stature, he possessed vitality and resilience comparable to a young martial artist’s. The energy stored in his dantian was considerable as well.
His martial arts are First Rate, and his internal energy is probably around Peak.
As I quietly assessed him, the Divine Physician sensed my gaze. He turned his head and smiled.
“What is it?”
I answered honestly.
“Your movement technique is remarkable.”
“Heh heh. No matter how hard this old man tries, how could I compare with you, Young Master? I merely happened to learn it.”
“Honestly, before meeting the Divine Physician—or rather, Old Man Dong—I never imagined you had learned martial arts.”
“You must have been surprised. The others seem to feel the same.”
I glanced behind me. Everyone except Cheongpung looked ready to burst with curiosity.
There was no point being vague now. Better to ask him outright.
“This may be presumptuous, but may I ask how you came to learn martial arts?”
A physician practicing martial arts. It might have been an uncomfortable subject, but the Divine Physician did not avoid the question.
“When I was around twenty, shortly after becoming a medical apprentice, my Master personally instructed me.”
“Then was your Master perhaps...?”
“That is correct. My Master was a martial artist.”
The Divine Physician’s Master had been a martial artist. That was something I had never expected.
Seeing my expression, he let out a hearty laugh.
“Heh heh. There is no need to be surprised. By the time he accepted me as his Disciple, he had already left the Murim.”
“Oh, I see.”
“My Master had reached the highest realm both as a martial artist and as a physician. He told me he had become a physician to atone for all the lives he had taken.”
For some reason, I felt as though I understood.
I had accumulated killing karma too. At first, I swung my spear while thinking only of getting home and believing that this was merely a fictional world created by a game.
But everything was real. They were all living people.
By the time I realized that, it was already too late.
I could not stop, and I did not stop. I killed to survive. I killed because they were my enemies.
In the Murim and in the modern world.
At some point, the scent of blood had seeped deep into my body. It was a stench that no amount of washing could remove.
“...I see.”
At my belated reply, the Divine Physician gave me a gentle smile.

“It was simply a matter of choice. My Master chose the path he believed was right, and I did the same. However, so many people came looking for this old man that I had no choice but to learn martial arts for my own protection. I was born a dullard, so he scolded me quite often. Heh heh.”
Everyone has memories.
Perhaps remembering the days he had spent with his Master, the Divine Physician suddenly stopped walking in the middle of his laughter.
“Well, we have arrived.”
Crack.
A frozen leaf crumbled beneath someone’s foot.
We stood in an unusually cold valley within the Mystic Gate Formation surrounding the Divine Physician’s residence.
“Where exactly are we?”
“I call this place the Cold-Ice Land.”
Cold-Ice Land. A fitting name.
Though something like Yanggu in Gangwon Province or Moscow might have been even better.
I glanced at Hyuk Mujin, who had already begun shivering violently, then asked the most important question.
“What do we do now?”
“You will have quite a difficult time. We must find and dig up various ingredients, including the medicinal herbs needed for the initial stage of treatment.”
“That sounds simpler than I expected.”
“Let me see... A hundred roots of each should be enough.”
“Ah, yes. A hundred roots.”
“I said a hundred roots of each.”
“Yes. That’s what you said. A hundred roots.”
I nodded, then froze.
Wait. What had I just heard?
“A hundred roots each? Not a hundred in total?”
“That is correct.”
The Divine Physician continued with a hearty laugh.
“A hundred roots each of twenty-four different kinds.”
Ding.
System A Chain Quest, Herb Slave of Cold-Ice Land, has been generated. - This is something you must accomplish. You cannot refuse!

Click.
The Divine Physician swallowed nervously and carefully opened the wooden box.
A pure, clear fragrance that seemed capable of purifying even the coronavirus wafted out as it revealed itself.
“Gasp!”
“Good heavens!”
“It’s a Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.
It contains at least one jiazi’s worth of energy and possesses the nature of Yin-Cold Qi.
Is this enough?”
Eyes wide, the Divine Physician looked back and forth between me and the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, then nodded vigorously.
“It is enough!”
Ding.

System Quest conditions fulfilled! - Chain Quest, Thirty Thousand Li in Search of an Elixir, successfully completed! - Achievement, Mountain Herb Gatherer, acquired! - A substantial amount of EXP acquired! - Level Up!
As the System notifications rang out, Ju Hwaran suddenly came to mind.
Thank you, Young Lady Ju.

I let out a wry chuckle as I thought of how she had given it to me while passing the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng off as Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng, worried I might feel burdened and refuse it otherwise.
Now I have a reason to stop by Shaanxi on the way back.
And when I did...
I hoped Jeok Cheongang would be healthy again and traveling with me.
I turned to the Divine Physician, who still looked dazed.
“All right, then.
What do we do next?”
The Divine Physician carefully tucked the wooden box into his robes and began walking.
“Follow me.
Gyeong, remain here and look after the patients.”
“Yes, Master.”
Leaving Mungyeong behind as he answered respectfully, we followed the Divine Physician.
Swish!
A small figure sped along right beside me.
Every time he extended one foot, a zhang of distance vanished and the wind swept past.
What was truly astonishing was that his feet never touched the ground.
With each faint tap of his toes, the blades of grass bent gently beneath him, then sprang back into place.
I narrowed my eyes.
Flying Over Grass?
Flying Over Grass was a realm in which one ran as though flying while stepping across blades of grass.
Martial artists who had mastered their movement techniques to the Peak realm could perform such feats.

Treading Snow Without a Trace, which left no footprints even while running across snow, and Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water, which allowed one to walk across water as though it were solid ground, worked on similar principles.
Stepping on Empty Air, meanwhile, was a realm attainable only by Supreme Peak masters with internal energy to spare.
Of course, Flying Over Grass isn’t beyond me either if I put my mind to it.
Even so, the sight was astonishing because the person performing it was the Divine Physician.
I knew he had learned martial arts, but his movement technique is especially impressive.
I had realized the Divine Physician knew martial arts the moment we first met.
Though small in stature, he possessed vitality and resilience comparable to a young martial artist’s.
The energy stored in his dantian was considerable as well.
His martial arts are First Rate, and his internal energy is probably around Peak.
As I quietly assessed him, the Divine Physician sensed my gaze.
He turned his head and smiled.
“What is it?”
I answered honestly.
“Your movement technique is remarkable.”
“Heh heh.
No matter how hard this old man tries, how could I compare with you, Young Master?
I merely happened to learn it.”
“Honestly, before meeting the Divine Physician—or rather, Old Man Dong—I never imagined you had learned martial arts.”
“You must have been surprised.
The others seem to feel the same.”
I glanced behind me.
Everyone except Cheongpung looked ready to burst with curiosity.
There was no point being vague now.
Better to ask him outright.
“This may be presumptuous, but may I ask how you came to learn martial arts?”
A physician practicing martial arts.
It might have been an uncomfortable subject, but the Divine Physician did not avoid the question.
“When I was around twenty, shortly after becoming a medical apprentice, my Master personally instructed me.”
“Then was your Master perhaps...?”
“That is correct.
My Master was a martial artist.”
The Divine Physician’s Master had been a martial artist.
That was something I had never expected.
Seeing my expression, he let out a hearty laugh.
“Heh heh.
There is no need to be surprised.
By the time he accepted me as his Disciple, he had already left the Murim.”
“Oh, I see.”
“My Master had reached the highest realm both as a martial artist and as a physician.
He told me he had become a physician to atone for all the lives he had taken.”
For some reason, I felt as though I understood.
I had accumulated killing karma too.
At first, I swung my spear while thinking only of getting home and believing that this was merely a fictional world created by a game.
But everything was real.
They were all living people.
By the time I realized that, it was already too late.
I could not stop, and I did not stop.
I killed to survive.
I killed because they were my enemies.
In the Murim and in the modern world.
At some point, the scent of blood had seeped deep into my body.
It was a stench that no amount of washing could remove.
“...I see.”
At my belated reply, the Divine Physician gave me a gentle smile.
“It was simply a matter of choice.
My Master chose the path he believed was right, and I did the same.
However, so many people came looking for this old man that I had no choice but to learn martial arts for my own protection.
I was born a dullard, so he scolded me quite often.
Heh heh.”
Everyone has memories.
Perhaps remembering the days he had spent with his Master, the Divine Physician suddenly stopped walking in the middle of his laughter.
“Well, we have arrived.”
Crack.
A frozen leaf crumbled beneath someone’s foot.
We stood in an unusually cold valley within the Mystic Gate Formation surrounding the Divine Physician’s residence.
“Where exactly are we?”
“I call this place the Cold-Ice Land.”
Cold-Ice Land.
A fitting name.
Though something like Yanggu in Gangwon Province or Moscow might have been even better.
I glanced at Hyuk Mujin, who had already begun shivering violently, then asked the most important question.
“What do we do now?”
“You will have quite a difficult time.
We must find and dig up various ingredients, including the medicinal herbs needed for the initial stage of treatment.”
“That sounds simpler than I expected.”
“Let me see...
A hundred roots of each should be enough.”
“Ah, yes.
A hundred roots.”
“I said a hundred roots of each.”
“Yes.
That’s what you said.
A hundred roots.”
I nodded, then froze.
Wait.
What had I just heard?
“A hundred roots each?
Not a hundred in total?”
“That is correct.”
The Divine Physician continued with a hearty laugh.
“A hundred roots each of twenty-four different kinds.”
Ding.
System A Chain Quest, Herb Slave of Cold-Ice Land, has been generated. - This is something you must accomplish.
You cannot refuse!

chapters.title: Chapter 343
paragraphs: Whoooooosh.
“This wind is fucking brutal. Goddamn it.”
I shuddered as the bitter cold pierced straight through my leather clothes. Unaffected by Cold and Heat, my ass. More like Very Much Affected by Cold and Heat.
“Pfooh-chew!”
I turned around, wondering what bizarre sound that had been, and found Hyuk Mujin rubbing his blue-tinged nose.
When our eyes met, his eyes curved into hooks.
“What? What is it?”
“What are you looking at?”
“No, I was just fascinated by the sound of your sneeze...”
“Seriously? You find the strangest things fascinating. If you have that much time to spare, dig up another herb.”
“...All right. My bad.”
I quietly looked away and scanned the area for another herb.
It had already been five days since I had taken a job as a herb slave in Cold-Ice Land. The hierarchy between us had reversed a long time ago.
“Ah, what are you doing? There’s one right over there. There!”
“Oh. So there is.”
“Get your head in the game!”
Ugh. It wasn’t like I could punch him.
If he had followed a friend to Gangnam, at least the land prices would have gone up. Instead, Hyuk Mujin had followed me to Cold-Ice Land and was suffering through the worst ordeal of his life.
He had been dragged into all kinds of fights before and always stopped after grumbling a few times, so the fact that he was now glaring at me with murder in his eyes said everything.
“I’ll dig for herbs beyond that hill. Don’t stop working. I’ll come back and check on you every so often.”
“...Got it, you punk.”
Repeating the character for patience to myself, I gently dug through the snow and pulled up an herb.
The moment I placed it in the basket our exploitative employer—or rather, the Divine Physician—had issued to each of his herb slaves, a System notification rang out.
Ding.
System You gathered Cold-Ice Herb. - Remaining quantity: 100 / 100. - Gathering Cold-Ice Herb is complete!
“Whew. Finally finished another one.”
At least the finish line was coming into sight.
As I checked the Quest window to see how much remained, Gung Gibang approached me, shivering violently.
“Hey, how many are left?”
“About two hundred roots. If things go well, we might finish today.”
“Two hundred roots are still left?”
“Only two hundred. Hang in there a little longer.”
“No. Two hundred roots is far too many. By then, I’ll be a frozen corpse buried somewhere under this snow.”
What a load of crap.
Still trembling, Gung Gibang pulled a fire striker from inside his clothes and lit it.
He brought his face close to the tiny flame and murmured wistfully, “I miss my Master. I miss the days when I begged in the alley outside a warm inn...”
Was he the Little Match Girl?
I muttered, dumbfounded by his behavior.
“You were still a beggar back then.”
“At least I was a warm beggar. That’s a hundred times better than being a cold one.”
“...You have a point.”
“I want to go back to those days. A lazy noon, sunlight pouring down. A delicious-looking yellow dog strolling past...”
What the hell was a delicious-looking yellow dog?
Gung Gibang’s eyelids slowly drooped after he said something that would make any animal-protection group scream.
This bastard couldn’t possibly be—
“Hey! Hey!”
I hurriedly sent Scorching Yang Qi into his body.
He had to come to his senses somehow—
“It’s warm...”
“I said wake up, you lunatic!”
Smack! Smack!
It was no use. No matter how hard I slapped his cheeks, his eyes showed no sign of opening again.
I continued sending Scorching Yang Qi into him and shouted, “Is anyone there? Somebody get over here, quick!”
In response to my desperate cry, someone came sprinting over from far away.
“Benefactor! Benefactor!”
“Nice, Cheongpung! Quick, take this guy outside—”
Cheongpung ran over like the wind, beaming as he held something out to me.
“Benefactor, look! It’s the first snowman I’ve ever made!”
“You son of a bitch!”
The Divine Physician inspected all the herbs in the baskets and nodded.
“This should be enough.”
Ding.

System Chain Quest, Herb Slave of Cold-Ice Land, successfully completed! - Achievement, Mountain Herb Gatherer Who Returned Alive from Hell, acquired! - You acquired 10 bonus points for earning an achievement!
Just look at that achievement title.
I didn’t even have the strength to get angry anymore.
The Divine Physician looked over our utterly exhausted group before his gaze suddenly stopped on one person.
“Why is Young Master Cheongpung so dejected?”
Because I had smashed the first snowman Cheongpung had ever made with my Flame Divine Palm.
I glared murderously at the still-sullen Cheongpung and asked the Divine Physician, “So, are all the preparations complete now?”
“They are. With this quantity, we will be prepared for anything that may happen later.”
“Prepared?”
The Divine Physician nodded gravely.
“We do not know what may happen.”
I suddenly realized something I had forgotten.
The Divine Physician had never once been certain.
He had only seen a possibility and said that he would do his best.
It isn’t over until it’s over.
The words I whispered to myself whenever I faced a crisis now became a dagger stabbing into my chest.
In the end, there was only one thing I could say.
“Please... Please do your very best.”
“This old man will do everything within his power. I promise.”
Mungyeong, who stood beside the Divine Physician, spoke with conviction.
“I will also do everything I can to assist my Master.”
“Thank you.”
“There’s no need. It is only natural for a medical apprentice to do so.”
“Then when will the actual treatment begin?”
The Divine Physician considered the question for a moment before answering.

“Probably in seven days and nights. Until then, Mungyeong and I will combine and refine the twenty-four types of herbs you brought us, preparing them as ingredients for the Life-Restoring Great Technique.”
“All of them?”
“This is only a portion of what we need. Fortunately, I already possess the remaining ingredients required for the Life-Restoring Great Technique, which allowed us to shorten the preparation time.”
“What exactly is this Life-Restoring Great Technique...?”
The Divine Physician stroked his snow-white beard and answered.
“As I mentioned before, my Master was once a martial artist. He primarily practiced medicine among the common people, but he was also deeply versed in controlling qi.”
Hearing that, I had a rough idea where this was going.
Hyuk Mujin suddenly cut in with an exclamation.
“Martial artists! The Life-Restoring Great Technique was created to treat martial artists!”

“That is correct. The Master of Strange Illusions was one of them. After recovering from severe qi deviation thanks to the Life-Restoring Great Technique, he installed the Mystic Gate Formation for us before departing.”
For martial artists, qi deviation was practically a death sentence. Their internal energy reversed course, their qi and blood became tangled, and all their acupoints and dantian were damaged.
The easiest way to understand it was to imagine a small bomb exploding inside a person.
But he cured qi deviation.
If the Master of Strange Illusions had suffered qi deviation severe enough for the Divine Physician to describe it that way, he must have been little more than a walking corpse at the time.
Just hearing the story gave me some idea of how effective the Life-Restoring Great Technique was.
Then Old Master will definitely—
I quickly shook off the thought before it could finish forming.
There was no reason to be certain yet, nor any need to worry.
“Please take good care of him.”
“Until preparations for the technique are complete, no one may approach the place where the patient is being kept. Do you understand?”
“Yes.”
“By then, the Life-Restoring Great Technique will be ready, and we should have a clearer understanding of the patient’s condition. Please wait patiently until then.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
“Remember. Seven days and nights.”
But the Divine Physician was unable to keep his word.
He reappeared with Mungyeong after only three days, and the moment I saw their expressions, I knew something had happened.
“...What is it?”
After a long silence, it was Mungyeong—not the Divine Physician—who finally spoke.
“Formless Ultimate Poison.”
“What?”
“There is an unidentified, extremely deadly poison inside the patient’s body. That was the true cause.”
“W-Wait.”
My thoughts twisted into a chaotic knot.
Formless Ultimate Poison? Out of nowhere?
I looked at the Divine Physician in confusion.
“What does that mean?”
“Exactly what you heard.”
Looking incomparably more haggard than he had three days earlier, the Divine Physician continued.
“While preparing the technique and monitoring the patient’s condition, I discovered something strange. The Scorching Yang Qi, which should have been growing more rampant, was gradually subsiding.”
“Then isn’t that a good thing? What does some sudden poison have to do with—”
“We have not even performed the technique yet. How could the Scorching Yang Qi be decreasing on its own?”
“That...”
“Did you not notice anything strange?”
At that moment, a thought flashed through my mind.
During our journey from Henan to Sichuan, I had periodically stabilized Jeok Cheongang’s qi with True Qi Guidance. Yet despite my efforts, his Scorching Yang Qi had continued to diminish.
I thought he was simply growing weaker.
The Divine Physician sighed when he saw my expression harden.

“When one type of energy gains the upper hand, the opposing energy naturally diminishes. But the patient was different. His Yin-Cold Qi remained unchanged, while his Scorching Yang Qi was gradually dwindling.”
“Are you saying that was because of the poison?”

“I do not know how it happened, but a Formless Ultimate Poison lies hidden within the patient’s body—one that even I would not dare touch. Whether by great fortune or terrible misfortune, the rampaging Scorching Yang Qi happened to envelop the Formless Ultimate Poison and counteract it like poison against poison. Otherwise, he would have melted into a handful of bloody liquid long ago.”
I didn’t know when or how the poison the Divine Physician called Formless Ultimate Poison had entered Jeok Cheongang’s body.
But I understood one thing clearly: the Scorching Yang Qi was acting as a breakwater, holding back the spread of the poison.
“Then... then does that mean even the technique cannot cure him?”

“The Life-Restoring Great Technique can regulate his qi and untangle his disrupted qi and blood, but it is not enough to detoxify a poison like this. If we perform the technique as things stand... the Scorching Yang Qi will be calmed, but there will be nothing left to stop the poison.”
I shouted urgently, “I’ll find an antidote! The Sichuan Tang Clan is here, isn’t it?”
“...Young Master.”
The Divine Physician shook his head, his expression dark.
“I know very well that the Sichuan Tang Clan is the greatest authority under heaven when it comes to poison. But this poison...”
His voice trailed off, and my heart seemed to drop into my stomach.
Even the Sichuan Tang Clan isn’t enough?
Damn it. This was a truly fucking awful situation.
Right now, Jeok Cheongang had two savage wolves inside his body, each keeping the other in check.
If either one disappeared, the other would regain its freedom and run wild.
And now there was no way to detoxify the poison.
This is so fucked...!
Tap. Drip.
Drops of blood fell from my tightly clenched fist. My throat burned as though I had swallowed a fireball.
Just as I struggled to hold back the curses threatening to burst out, someone’s voice pierced my ears.
“There is a way.”
I opened my eyes and saw the boy’s face. Mungyeong continued, looking more serious than I had ever seen him.
“Let us go to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
The Divine Physician looked at his Disciple with a dark expression.
“Mungyeong. As you know, this Formless Ultimate Poison...”
“I know, Master. I clearly remember you saying that the Tang Clan’s poison arts focus on killing and that their detoxification techniques are lacking. But...”
Mungyeong looked straight at me with clear eyes.
“If the Sichuan Tang Clan possesses a legendary treasure—a divine artifact said to detoxify any poison under heaven—then it is possible.”
Ding.
System Quest, Myriad-Poison Ring, has been generated!
