“There is a way.”
I opened my eyes and saw the boy’s face.
Mungyeong continued, looking more serious than I had ever seen him.
“Let us go to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
The Divine Physician looked at his Disciple with a dark expression.
“Mungyeong.
As you know, this Formless Ultimate Poison...”
“I know, Master.
I clearly remember you saying that the Tang Clan’s poison arts focus on killing and that their detoxification techniques are lacking.
But...”
Mungyeong looked straight at me with clear eyes.
“If the Sichuan Tang Clan possesses a legendary treasure—a divine artifact said to detoxify any poison under heaven—then it is possible.”
Ding.
System Quest, Myriad-Poison Ring, has been generated!

chapters.title: Chapter 344
paragraphs: Ding.
System Chain Quest, Myriad-Poison Ring, has been generated! - There is something you must accomplish. You cannot refuse!
I stared at the holographic window that filled my vision along with the System notification.

System Quest Myriad-Poison Ring The Myriad-Poison Ring, said to absorb any poison under heaven, is a sacred artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan and one of the legends passed down through the Murim. Its owner and even its existence are uncertain, but for now, it is the only possible solution! Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Acquire the Myriad-Poison Ring—Incomplete Reward: A large amount of EXP Failure: Jeok Cheongang’s death
“A sacred artifact said to absorb any poison.”
Mungyeong nodded at my mutter.
“That is the Myriad-Poison Ring’s ability. However, there is one problem...”
“Its owner and even its existence are uncertain.”
“Yes. The Sichuan Tang Clan has denied the existence of the Myriad-Poison Ring several times.”
The Divine Physician added in a heavy voice, “That is why it is a legend. It is so ancient that it has survived only through word of mouth.”
After thinking for a moment, I suddenly opened my mouth.
“No. It exists.”
“Hmm?”
“The Myriad-Poison Ring definitely exists. It’s just being kept hidden.”
“How can you be so certain?”
Both the Divine Physician and Mungyeong, who had first brought up the Myriad-Poison Ring, stared at me with wide eyes.
“Obviously because...”
Because of the System.
This was a Chain Quest to treat Jeok Cheongang.
If the Myriad-Poison Ring truly did not exist, a Quest like this would never have been generated.
Of course, if I said that out loud, they would definitely think I was insane.

I smoothly continued, “If word got out that they possessed a sacred artifact like that, do you think people would leave them alone? The Sichuan Tang Clan is famous throughout the Murim for being stubbornly insular. Naturally, they would want to avoid the trouble.”

This was a world where people killed one another over a single coin or a dumpling. If the treasure in question were something like the Myriad-Poison Ring, just imagine how many flies would swarm around it.
It was a hastily improvised explanation, but convincing enough that everyone nodded.
“That makes sense. In fact, after conducting an extensive investigation into whether the Myriad-Poison Ring truly exists, even our sect—”
I looked at Gung Gibang, who had jumped in as though he had been waiting for the chance.
“Forget it. Stay here and tell Mujin the rest.”
“Huh? Stay? You want me to stay here with Hyuk Mujin?”
“Captain, what do you mean?”
“What do you think I mean? Exactly what you heard.”
I pointed at the two bewildered men in turn.
“Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang are staying here.”
“Why? Why me?”
“I want to go with you too! Please, don’t leave this vicious beggar and me behind!”
“What?! You dog-bone bastard!”
Smack! Smack!
Sometimes, a good beating was the best medicine. I shook my fists at the two men as they clutched the tops of their heads.
“Stop talking nonsense and stay here to guard Venerable Myoryeong. If anything happens, Gung Gibang, you contact me immediately.”
“Contact you? Is there a messenger pigeon here that can fly to the Sichuan Tang Clan?”
“What kind of beggar’s-foot-rag nonsense is that? If something happens, you come running so fast your feet catch fire.”
“What the hell?”
“If you don’t like it, tame one. I saw plenty of butterflies in the flower garden.”
It was a conclusion I had reached after a brief but coolheaded analysis.
Hyuk Mujin’s martial arts were the weakest among us, especially his movement technique, so I would leave him behind and keep Gung Gibang with him as a precaution against any unexpected situation.
Gung Gibang was a reasonably capable Peak master, and he was as quick on his feet as he was on the uptake. He should be able to handle any unforeseen crisis.
“Anyone dissatisfied with my decision or curious about something, raise your hand immediately.”
“Put that fist down before you ask.”
“I’ll just stay here.”
At that moment, an arm shot into the air. Cheongpung asked with an innocent expression, “What about me, Benefactor?”
“You’re coming with me to the Sichuan Tang Clan, Cheongpung.”
“Why?”
“Who knows what kind of trouble you’ll cause if I leave you behind? Don’t leave my sight even for a moment. Got it?”
“Yeees...”
At Cheongpung’s dejected reply, the Divine Physician spoke with pity in his eyes.
“Do not scold him too harshly. He seems like an innocent young man.”
“He is innocent. Innocent enough to start a forest fire and burn this whole place to the ground.”
“Hoho, surely he would not go that far.”
“I’ll wager Mujin’s left wrist that within a few days he’ll burn down your whole cottage, leave you homeless, and drive you into joining the Beggars’ Sect.”
The Divine Physician studied Cheongpung with a wary expression before answering.
“It would be best if he came with us.”
“A wise choice.”
“Gyeong, what will you do?”
Mungyeong thought deeply for a moment, then nodded as if he had made his decision.
“I will accompany you, Master. The Emei nun should have no trouble as long as she gets some rest.”
“I would appreciate that.”
The person I needed most right now was actually the Divine Physician. But having Mungyeong with us would be even better. He was always at his Master’s side, serving as a capable assistant.
Besides, he was the one who had first brought up the Myriad-Poison Ring.
The only thing left is figuring out how to obtain it.
Myriad-Poison Asura Tang Sadok. The answer would become clear once I faced the head of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
Once I had finished thinking, I turned to Cheongpung.
“Cheongpung, grab two A-frame carriers and two ropes. Make them big and sturdy.”
“Benefactor, why do we need the carriers and ropes?”
“We need to get there as fast as possible. It’d be a disaster if we dropped either of them along the way, so we’ll tie them down tight.”
The Divine Physician’s and Mungyeong’s faces turned deathly pale.
In the dark main hall, it was a long while after the middle-aged man entered before the old man spoke.
“More than fifty years ago, before you were even born, our family suffered a great humiliation. Do you know about it?”
At the Myriad-Poison Asura Tang Sadok’s words, the middle-aged man lowered his head.
“How could I not?”

“This old man was barely twenty at the time, and I witnessed it all with my own eyes. Our people died all around us, the armory burned, and the pavilions collapsed. We were defeated and forced to withdraw from Sichuan.”

The Great War raged for ten long years before ending in victory for the orthodox faction. The Tang Clan returned to Sichuan and rebuilt, but the scars from that time had been carved deep into everyone’s hearts.
“And yet, and yet, how!”
The instant green light flashed in Tang Sadok’s eyes, the middle-aged man held his breath as poisonous energy poured from Tang Sadok’s entire body.
“Hngh.”
“How can we suffer such humiliation again?”
Sssssss!
Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand pressed down on the table—or rather, melted it.
Not only the wood but even the iron fittings along the corners liquefied into black poison and flowed. The middle-aged man immediately prostrated himself.
“Please calm yourself, Family Head!”
Despite the middle-aged man’s plea, Tang Sadok’s anger did not easily subside.

His fury was only natural. Instead of finding the culprit who had harmed his father, Poison King Tang Taesang, he had come up empty and been forced to return after receiving an urgent message from the Qingcheng Sect.
“Who dares...!”
The message sent by the Qingcheng Sect had been brief. It had also been as shocking as the Poison King’s death.
He killed Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun and three Emei Elders all by himself.
And it had not been a surprise attack targeting a single person. It was said to have been a head-on fight.
Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun was a Supreme Peak master who could have vied for even the lowest seat among the Ten Kings. The three Elders with her were also seasoned Peak masters.
The culprit had single-handedly brought down the leadership of an entire sect, then vanished like a ghost.
There can’t be two masters of that level. It must have been the same bastard who harmed Father.
As his anger slowly subsided, wariness took its place.
He had decided to return not as a son but as the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. At the same time, he had not forgotten to pursue the culprit.
“What became of the Green Shadow Squad?”
“They divided into ten groups of five and scattered from Chengdu toward Qingcheng, Emei, Yishan, Sanhe, and the surrounding areas to carry out their missions.”
Even within the Sichuan Tang Clan, the Green Shadow Squad specialized in intelligence gathering and assassinating key targets.
They had been chiefly responsible for eliminating countless fiends immediately after the Great Faction War, but Tang Sadok felt an inexplicable sense of foreboding.
“Do not let your guard down. Strengthen the defenses of the Gate Guard Pavilion, and do not allow anyone to enter.”
“Yes.”
“You may leave.”
Tang Sadok watched the middle-aged man turn away cautiously, then suddenly spoke.
“Once this matter is over... hand the position of Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion to someone else and move to the Inner Hall.”
“F-Family Head?”
“I’m saying this as your uncle, not as the Family Head. You’re nearly fifty. How long did you think I would leave my only nephew at the Gate Guard Pavilion?”
“Th-Thank you, Uncle.”
Tang Sadok answered with a flick of his sleeve.
His nephew was not exceptional, but neither was there anything particularly lacking in him.
Tang Sadok had grown numb with time and lived for many years without thinking about it. Only recently had he begun remembering his elder brother, who had lost his life during the Great Faction War.
“I suppose I’m growing old too, Father.”
At Tang Sadok’s quiet monologue, spoken after he was left alone, his chest rose and fell. Then something slowly poked its head out.
Hiss. Hiss.
It had a body as white as snow, blue eyes, and a triangular head crowned with two horns. It was a snake.
A spiritual creature known throughout the Murim as the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, it was notorious for its ferocity. It flicked out its long tongue and licked Tang Sadok’s cheek.
“You little rascal...”
Tang Sadok’s stiff expression slowly softened.
He had a prickly personality and disliked meeting people, but he made an exception for this Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.
It was the first and last gift he had ever received from his father, the Poison King. Since Tang Sadok had no children of his own, the snake was more precious to him than anything.
“Hey, that tickles. You little thing.”
He was watching the snake’s antics with a faint smile when the sound of approaching footsteps grew louder.
The white body hurriedly slipped back inside Tang Sadok’s robes.
“What is it?”
“Family Head, it’s me.”
At the voice of his nephew, who had left only moments earlier, Tang Sadok affected a frown.
“Why have you come back?”
“Well, those people have come again.”
“Those people?”
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi Jin Taekyung and Huashan Divine Dragon Cheongpung.”
“I explicitly ordered that no one be allowed inside. Refuse them entry.”
“But... one of them may be the Divine Physician.”
“What? The Divine Physician?”
For once, even Tang Sadok could not hide his surprise.
Who was the Divine Physician? A man said to have reached the divine realm through his medical arts. A mysterious figure who had not shown himself for many long years.
Why had that very Divine Physician come to our family?
His hesitation did not last long. A hoarse voice escaped Tang Sadok’s lips.
“Let them in.”
“Are you the Divine Physician?”
Now that was some no-brakes macho-man talk.
Tang Sadok had asked the question out of nowhere without even pretending to look at us, and the Divine Physician let out a hearty laugh.
“This old man’s name is Dong Feng.”
“Then you are not the Divine Physician?”
“People have given this old man an undeserved name.”
“Seems you are, then.”
“You believe me rather easily.”
“Unless someone is desperate to die, no one tells lies in front of this old man.”
That was pretty damn convincing.
Tang Sadok slowly looked us over, a green glow shimmering in his eyes.
“The Divine Physician... You, whom the whole world has searched for without catching even a glimpse of you, have come looking for me. And you have brought young prodigies of the Murim with you. Why?”
“May I answer that?”
I stepped forward, and Tang Sadok’s gaze collided with mine in midair.
“Go ahead. If you say something nonsensical, be prepared to become a handful of blood...”
“Please lend me the Myriad-Poison Ring.”
At my own macho-man-with-no-brakes delivery, Tang Sadok’s pupils trembled.

chapters.title: Chapter 345
paragraphs: No matter how much the Murim was a veritable death zone crawling with murder and violence, people in every field learned to observe some decorum once they reached the upper ranks.
Especially when you were the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, one of the Five Great Families.
Tang Sadok might have been comfortable speaking bluntly, but he was not accustomed to others doing the same to him.
As I was doing now.
“Please lend me the Myriad-Poison Ring.”
The request struck him completely out of the blue.
His eyes twitched for a split second before he spoke.
“You still believe that ridiculous nonsense? I knew you were young, but you truly are a child.”
“I saw your eye twitch just now.”
“Nonsense!”
“Your voice gets louder when I hit a nerve, doesn’t it?”
“I told you it doesn’t exist!”
“Oh, now you’re clenching your fist.”
“I said I don’t have it!”
“If I search your pockets and find it, can I keep it?”
“Fine! Search me! If you don’t find it, I’ll take your head instead!”
“Oh, so you hid it somewhere else. In that case, I withdraw my request.”
“Grrr...!”
“What a loss...!”
“You insolent little bastard!”
Ah. I probably should have held back that last one.
After being hit by a fantastic barrage of combo attacks, Tang Sadok’s eyes rolled back.
I hurriedly shouted before he could scatter his hidden weapons.
“I only need to borrow it once! Just once!”
“I told you it doesn’t exist!”
“Fine, let’s say it doesn’t. Just hear me out.”
“Nothing you say will change my answer.”
“Even if I offered to deal with the culprit?”
“What?”
“The man who harmed Great Hero Tang Taesang, the Poison King.”
The next moment—
“You little brat! I’ve tolerated enough of your insolence—!”
Whoosh!
Green qi rose from Tang Sadok’s entire body like a shimmering haze. He glared at me with blazing eyes, then spoke in a low, cold voice.
“Do you truly wish to die?”
“I have a bright future ahead of me, so not particularly.”
“Punishing that man is our family’s responsibility. How dare an outsider like you—!”
Whoom!
An aura like a raging gale erupted and shook the pavilion. I stepped in front of the trembling Divine Physician and Mungyeong before answering.
“And how has that worked out?”

“The culprit is a master powerful enough to defeat the Poison King. He also evaded the Tang Clan’s eyes here in Sichuan and caused a bloodbath at the Emei Sect. Martial prowess clearly isn’t his only strength.”
Sichuan might have been vast, but the Tang Clan had been rooted here for countless years.
This was no different from losing track of a family enemy in their own front yard. Tang Sadok had led most of his family in pursuit, only to return empty-handed. His expression hardened.
“Are you accusing our family of incompetence?”
“Of course not.”
If the Sichuan Tang Clan was incompetent, most of the sects scattered throughout the realm might as well bolt their gates and withdraw from the martial world.
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the giants supporting the Murim. The problem was not that the Sichuan Tang Clan or the Emei Sect was incompetent.
The culprit was simply a monster.
“I’m only pointing out a possibility.”
“A possibility?”
“His martial arts are comparable to the Ten Kings, and he’s exceptionally skilled at escaping. Wouldn’t more people helping you improve the chances of catching him?”
“Our Green Shadow Squad is already pursuing him. I merely returned for a short while to prepare for any unforeseen circumstances. Before long, I will hunt him down and kill him.”
Tang Sadok’s sharp gaze swept over Cheongpung and me.
“We are the great Sichuan Tang Clan. We have no need for outsiders’ help. Least of all from greenhorns like you.”
“...Ah. Right.”
Hadn’t I already left the level of a mere young prodigy far behind?
Especially that guy.
I glanced at Cheongpung, who was blankly watching the exchange, and scratched the back of my head.
Well, I expected something like this.
Considering the Sichuan Tang Clan’s family tradition of doing everything their own damn way, his response came as no surprise.
That was why I had thought up a more enticing proposal on the way here.
“Then instead of greenhorns who came crawling out of nowhere, how about the Fire King?”
“Let’s say you somehow track the culprit down. He isn’t going to hold out his arm and ask you to hurry up and stick poison needles into his veins.”
One side would fight to survive. The other would fight to kill. A fierce battle was inevitable.
If the Sichuan Tang Clan committed its full strength, they might succeed in avenging the Poison King—but they would also have to brace themselves for enormous losses.
Countless members of the Tang Clan, whether from the direct line or the collateral branches, would die.
“Old Master—no, my Master—and the rest of us will help you. We’ll minimize the Sichuan Tang Clan’s losses and leave the culprit’s punishment to you, Family Head.”

“Your answer came half a beat late.”
“This is the path our ancestors took—the path our family has walked all these years. It is what made the Sichuan Tang Clan what it is!”
“I know. I know what path the Sichuan Tang Clan has walked.”
They were a close-knit family bound by blood. They never forgot a grudge, and their vengeance was merciless.
That was the path the Tang Family had walked—and the reason people both respected and feared them.
I continued quietly.
“But no one will point fingers at you for taking a shortcut once in a while. Especially if you choose that shortcut to reduce the number of family members who must be sacrificed.”

No. Even if he was, he was not the sort of ruthless Family Head who would put revenge above everything else.
If he were, he wouldn’t have returned to the family.

“Someone I know says it can.”
At my glance, the Divine Physician spoke.

“How long will it take?”
“Fifteen days. Fifteen days will be enough.”
“Fifteen days...”
Tang Sadok let out a low groan, then looked at the Divine Physician.

“I examined Great Hero Jeok’s condition once before. Though my medical knowledge is shallow compared to my expertise in poison arts, I could not determine what sort of symptoms he was suffering from. Is it truly possible?”
“It is possible.”
A clear voice rang out.
Mungyeong stepped forward and added a single sentence.
“The Divine Physician can do it.”
“What an audacious boy. Is he your Disciple?”
The Divine Physician answered Tang Sadok’s question with a faint smile before speaking.
“The Myriad-Poison Ring is essential if the patient is to recover. I understand your desire to conceal such a sacred artifact, but I ask that you show compassion and extend us your benevolence.”
“Benevolence, is it? Do you think the same?”
“Why are you asking me all of a sudden?”
“Speak. I want to hear your thoughts.”
“If you insist.”
I shrugged.
“Rather than benevolence, let’s call it gratitude and grudges.”
“Why?”
“Because this is the Murim. If someone helps you, isn’t it the way of the martial world to repay them?”
A faint smile touched the corner of Tang Sadok’s wrinkled mouth.
“That is far more pleasing to hear.”
“It sounds better, and it isn’t empty flattery.”
“What will you do if the culprit flees to some distant foreign land while Great Hero Jeok is being treated?”
“I’ll chase him down myself and bring him back. Ah, I’m not saying I’ll leave right away, of course. I won’t budge until my Master wakes up.”

“You’re an amusing bastard. Even tearing the culprit limb from limb wouldn’t be enough, but he is also an extraordinary master. Do you think a wet-behind-the-ears brat like you can capture someone like that?”
“If I can’t take him alive, I’ll kill him.”
“Ha... Hahahaha!”
Tang Sadok burst into uproarious laughter. When it finally subsided, he tossed out a casual remark.
“The Myriad-Poison Ring does not exist.”
“...What?”
What the fuck was he talking about?
Had this old man been playing me the entire time?
As the back of my head went numb, Tang Sadok continued.
“The Myriad-Poison Ring is nothing more than an old legend. Even among our blood relatives, it is merely a stale tale.”
“What do you mean, it doesn’t exist? It really doesn’t?”
“No one knows, and no one must ever know.”
“Fuck! Then you should have said that from the beginning! Have you been messing with me this whole—”
Ssssss.
I snapped my mouth shut before I could finish.
A pure-white snake had slowly crawled out of Tang Sadok’s robes and was staring fixedly at me, its tongue flicking.
What is that?
What was he, Voldemort? Why was a snake suddenly coming out of his clothes?
It even had horns, which no normal snake had. As I stared into its black eyes, the Divine Physician murmured in disbelief.
“A Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake...?”
Even the name sounded lethally venomous.
Tang Sadok laughed quietly when he saw me edging backward and stroked the snake’s triangular head.
“Don’t be afraid. It isn’t dangerous, so there’s no need to retreat.”
“Its name sounds fucking dangerous.”
“Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake?”
“Yes. What kind of name is that? It’s not like you’re calling it a golden retriever. Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake... Never mind. Does the Myriad-Poison Ring really not exist?”
“It isn’t called Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake. Its name is Mimi.”
“What?”
“Tang Mimi. That is the name I gave it.”
What was that supposed to mean? Terrifying...
As Tang Sadok lovingly stroked Mimi-chan, he suddenly looked at the Divine Physician.
“You must know that this creature is no ordinary Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.”
The Divine Physician nodded.

“As far as I know, a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake is a rare venomous creature that carries an extremely deadly poison. Its entire body is black, and its temperament is so ferocious that it can never be tamed. However...”
“As you can see, this one looks different and has an exceptionally gentle disposition.”
“But we do not know when it might suddenly turn on us. Is it not a venomous creature capable of killing a hundred cows with a single drop of its venom?”
“There is no need to worry. This one has no venom.”
“What?”
“To be precise... it would be more accurate to say that its venom is gone.”
With that, Tang Sadok met Mimi-chan’s gaze—or rather, the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake’s.
It lasted only a moment, but they had clearly communicated. The clever snake had understood its master’s intentions.
Hiss! Ssssss!
The snake lowered its head and let out a metallic hiss before spitting something onto Tang Sadok’s palm.
With a soft plop, the object emerged from the slime covering it.
That’s...
A ring.
Set into it was a black gemstone that seemed to contain all the darkness in the world.
Having absorbed even the deadly venom of the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, it gleamed with a beautiful yet ominous light.
“No way...”
As I stared at the ring in a daze, Tang Sadok’s low voice reached my ears.
“Remember this. No one knows, and no one must ever know.”
“Then...”
“Yes.”
Tang Sadok held it out to me.
“This is our family’s sacred artifact.”
The moment I took the ring with trembling hands, the chime I had been waiting for rang out.
Ding.

paragraphs: I examined the small ring closely. It was light and strange.
Its band was made of some unknown metal and covered in unfamiliar patterns. The gemstone set in its center gleamed darkly, as though it held the night sky within it.
So this is the Myriad-Poison Ring.
The sacred artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan—said to detoxify any poison—had fallen into my hands.

Its power had to be genuine if it could turn a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, a creature said to harbor an extraordinarily deadly venom, into a pet snake named Mimi-chan. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check.
Item Appraisal.
Beep.
System Item Appraisal failed! - A special condition must be met to appraise this Item!
“Huh?”
“What is it? Is there a problem?”
I vaguely brushed off Tang Sadok’s puzzled question.
“No. It’s just...”
“Just what?”
“The gemstone is pretty. It’s almost the same color as the snake’s eyes.”
A crease formed on Tang Sadok’s forehead.
I had momentarily forgotten that the old man standing before me was not only the Family Head of a great clan, but also a seasoned martial artist who had spent his entire life in the Murim.
Sure enough, Tang Sadok’s eyes widened as he bellowed.
“What nonsense!”
“Family Head, the thing is—”
“Our Mimi’s eyes are prettier!”
“What?”
“And that’s not all! I rub her down with fragrant oil every morning and evening, so she smells wonderful. Her teeth are pearly white too!”
“Ah... right.”
A seasoned martial artist, my ass. He was just a snake fanatic.
What kind of Family Head liked his pet snake more than his family’s sacred artifact?
At this point, I was starting to wonder whether Mimi-chan was the true sacred artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
But why can’t I appraise it?
I tried Item Appraisal again just in case, but the result was the same. If appraising it required some special condition, then I supposed a sacred artifact really was a sacred artifact.
It bothers me that I can’t confirm its effects, but it should work.
I turned to the Divine Physician. He had been watching with a smile, and he spoke as though he’d been waiting for me.

“The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake is no ordinary venomous snake, but a spiritual creature. Yet the ring rendered even its venom glands useless... We will have to try it before we know the full extent of its power, but it is certainly worthy of the name Myriad-Poison Ring.”
“In that case...”
“Without the Myriad-Poison Ring, the chance of success would have been a mere one percent. Now, I would place it above seventy percent.”
“Even with the Myriad-Poison Ring, it’s only seventy percent...?”
“This old man’s medical arts will supply the remaining thirty.”
“Whew. You should’ve said that from the start.”
The Divine Physician laughed heartily at my sigh of relief and stroked his beard.
“Now only one thing remains.”
“What is it?”
“A place to conduct the treatment.”
Tang Sadok abruptly cut in, his tone blunt.
“Have you forgotten where you are?”
“I am well aware that the Sichuan Tang Clan has its own clinic. However, treating Great Hero Jeok requires two specific conditions.”
“Name them.”
“First, it must be secluded, somewhere people cannot easily come and go. Second, it must receive no sunlight and be permeated by a bitter, bone-chilling cold.”
“Somewhere secluded, dark, and cold...”
Tang Sadok considered this for a moment, then let out a quiet laugh.
“As it happens, I know the perfect place. I shall take you there myself.”
“Thank you for your generosity, Family Head.”

“I am no benevolent Great Hero. This is merely a matter of gratitude and grudges between us. And if you ever reveal the existence of the Myriad-Poison Ring or allow word of it to spread outside the clan...”
I sighed and finished for him.
“I’ll be dragged off, dunked waist-deep in a vat of poison, and have holes punched through me with needles.”
“You have a poor imagination. Whatever you can imagine, you will suffer worse.”
“That won’t happen unless I lose my mind.”
“I certainly hope so... What are you doing here?”
Good question. What was that guy doing?
While we were talking, Cheongpung had crept over and was reaching toward Mimi-chan.
“Wow, she’s pretty. Can I touch her?”
“No.”
“Why not?”
“Hmph. Do you think she lets just anyone touch her? If I had not summoned her, she would never even have shown herself before you.”
“Mimi, Mimi. Come here.”
“What ridiculous nonsense—”
Hissssss.
Mimi-chan slithered down Tang Sadok’s shoulder and licked the back of Cheongpung’s hand.
“Gasp!”
“Mimi, Whirlwind!”
Whirlwind, my ass. He was ordering her to perform a technique even a person wouldn’t understand.
As expected, there was no telling what went on inside Cheongpung’s head.
Sssshk, sssshk, sssshhhk!
“...What the fuck?”
What had I just witnessed?
My jaw dropped as Mimi-chan began spinning wildly in a tight spiral.
“Wow! Good job, Mimi!”
“This can’t be! How could Mimi use Whirlwind on someone she’s never met before?”
“Wait, that’s a real technique?”
“That is not what matters right now!”
It seemed pretty important to me. At this rate, I wondered whether she might start firing a Thunderbolt or a Hyper Beam.
Can she evolve too...?
As I tried to decide whether the Myriad-Poison Ring or Mimi-chan was the true sacred artifact, Cheongpung beamed.
“I’m good with animals. When I lay in the grass at Huashan, birds, deer, and even tigers would come play with me. Hehe.”
What was he, some kind of Huashan druid?
Tang Sadok had been staring blankly at Cheongpung, still reeling from the shock of losing Mimi-chan to him. Now he raised an objection.
“Wait. Something strange slipped in at the end. Why would there be a tiger? How dare you tell such an obvious lie before this old man!”
“We were all about to say goodbye when the tiger tried to eat the deer, so I knocked it out with Crouching Tiger Fist!”
It sounded completely insane, no matter who heard it.
Which probably meant it was true.
Silence filled the main hall, making Mungyeong’s mutter ring out with unusual clarity.
“Is the Huashan I know a different Huashan...?”
I didn’t know about that, but one thing was certain.
If heaven and earth were ever overturned and Cheongpung somehow became Huashan’s Sect Leader, from that day onward, it would be your Huashan—not mine.
“...Let’s go. You said you would show us the place.”
“...Very well.”
Following Tang Sadok, we arrived at a cave on the distant outskirts of the Sichuan Tang Clan’s grounds.
Its entrance yawned open like a pitch-black maw.
Aside from two large braziers on either side, there was no one in sight.
“Where are we? It doesn’t look like anyone is guarding this place.”
“If no one is here, I suppose it must be feeding time.”
“Feeding?”
“You will understand once we enter. Follow me.”
Unlike the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s training hall, this cave did not run in a straight line.

We descended stone steps leading deep underground for what felt like ages. Eventually, we reached a narrow corridor barely wide enough for two people to pass through side by side, and a familiar smell invaded my nose.
Is this... the smell of blood?
A bad feeling came over me. I looked around and saw barred iron doors spaced along the corridor.
“Don’t tell me...”
“That is correct. This is our family’s underground prison.”
“...Not a torture chamber?”
“Oh, you will see plenty of those farther inside.”
What the hell had I just heard?
Everyone turned to stare at Tang Sadok, myself included, but he continued as though it were no big deal.

“Except for the Family Head’s Hall and a few other pavilions, this is the oldest space in the family compound. It must be well over two hundred years old by now. In any case, it is a historic place steeped in history.”
Forget its venerable history. I felt like I ought to leave a will before I got dragged any farther inside.
The more I thought about it, the more ridiculous it seemed.
“Isn’t it still just a prison?”
“Is that a problem?”
“Of course there is! You want us to treat Old Master—no, my Master—in here?”
“Not a single ray of sunlight reaches this place, and the chill permeates it to the bone. There is no more suitable location.”
“You said you conduct torture here, too.”
“Of course. Is that even worth asking?”
Anyone listening would have thought he was asking whether I wanted extra toppings on my pizza.
Just as I ran out of words, a hunched old man came limping toward us from the distance, accompanied by a faint glow.
“Family Head, what brings you here?”
“Ah, Old Man Gung. You’ve been working hard. How are they?”
“Oh, much the same as usual. I just checked whether they were still breathing. But who might these people be...?”
“They are guests of our family. Circumstances require them to stay in the prison for fifteen days. It won’t be too noisy, will it?”
“No, sir. Those still alive are little better than walking corpses, so it should be quiet.”
“When I saw him a few months ago, that Heavenly Power Demon fellow still seemed full of energy.”
“Ah, him? You needn’t worry about that one anymore.”
The hunched old man grinned, revealing a mouthful of almost entirely rotten teeth.
“He made such a racket that I drained every last bit of energy out of him. And since I was at it, I took a few other things too. Hehe.”
“You are always working hard.”
“Oh, Family Head, you flatter me. I only do it because I enjoy the work.”
As I listened to their conversation, I made a firm resolution.
I must never make an enemy of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
After exchanging a few more words with Old Man Gung, Tang Sadok spoke with a bright expression.
“Excellent. It seems the deepest and largest cell has just been vacated. We can use that one.”
I didn’t need to hear why it had been vacated.
It wasn’t as though someone had checked out at the prison’s front desk and walked away.
They must’ve checked in to the afterlife by now.
Even if this place met all the necessary conditions, could we really conduct a medical treatment here?
The Divine Physician had clearly thought the same thing. Mungyeong addressed his Master, who had put on a frown, in a calm voice.
“Master, are we not medical apprentices? For the patient’s sake, we must endure the place even if it displeases us.”
The Divine Physician let out a low groan before answering.
“...Yes. You are right. We shall do so.”
“And the people imprisoned here are certainly evil men who have committed countless murders. Please do not let it trouble you too much.”
Tang Sadok, who had been listening to their conversation, added his own remark.
“Well, well. You are quite composed for such a young medical apprentice. Divine Physician, as the boy said, every man imprisoned here is a thoroughly wicked fiend. Do not think poorly of our family.”
“This old man allowed his concern to lead him into discourtesy. I ask your generous forgiveness.”
“I shall gladly forgive you. Of course, the same does not apply to those bastards who harmed members of our family. Isn’t that right, Old Man Gung?”
Old Man Gung picked up a torch and let out a bizarre, metallic laugh.
“Come, then. This humble one will show you the way.”
For some reason, I felt as though I were following the Grim Reaper.
Judging by the atmosphere alone, that old man seems more dangerous than the culprit who killed the Poison King.
It had to be my imagination.
Yes. Definitely my imagination.
And so, we began walking toward the suite boasting the finest facilities in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.
“Hm?”
The middle-aged man suddenly looked around.
Winter had passed. The sky was clear, and the once-bare mountain forest was slowly regaining its green.
The valley in this nameless mountain was as peaceful as ever. Yet no matter how long he thought about it, he could not understand why he felt such a strange sense of déjà vu.
“How very strange. Very strange indeed...”
The middle-aged man muttered softly, then turned his head and asked,
“Don’t you agree?”
Grrk. Gk.
Blood bubbled up from the man’s gaping throat.
The fallen man glared up at the middle-aged man, his eyes burning with hatred.
“M-my family... will make you pay...”
“What boring last words. Then again, the Sichuan Tang Clan has always been like that.”
Crunch!
The middle-aged man wiped his leather shoe, drenched in blood and brain matter, against the grass before straightening.
Four corpses lay scattered around him.
He smiled at the sole surviving man.
“Now, will you answer my questions obediently, or would you prefer to writhe in unimaginable agony until you die?”
“For your information, the Poison King chose the latter. He held out for four days before finally dying.”
The man shuddered, then slowly closed his eyes.
A broad smile spread across the middle-aged man’s lips as he watched the man brace himself for death.
“Good. Let’s find out how long you can last.”

sentences.text: I examined the small ring closely.

Its band was made of some unknown metal and covered in unfamiliar patterns.
The gemstone set in its center gleamed darkly, as though it held the night sky within it.
So this is the Myriad-Poison Ring.

Its power had to be genuine if it could turn a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, a creature said to harbor an extraordinarily deadly venom, into a pet snake named Mimi-chan.

Item Appraisal.

A seasoned martial artist, my ass.
He was just a snake fanatic.
What kind of Family Head liked his pet snake more than his family’s sacred artifact?

But why can’t I appraise it?
I tried Item Appraisal again just in case, but the result was the same.
If appraising it required some special condition, then I supposed a sacred artifact really was a sacred artifact.
It bothers me that I can’t confirm its effects, but it should work.
I turned to the Divine Physician.

“Whew.

The Divine Physician laughed heartily at my sigh of relief and stroked his beard.

“What is it?”
“A place to conduct the treatment.”
Tang Sadok abruptly cut in, his tone blunt.
“Have you forgotten where you are?”
“I am well aware that the Sichuan Tang Clan has its own clinic.
However, treating Great Hero Jeok requires two specific conditions.”
“Name them.”
“First, it must be secluded, somewhere people cannot easily come and go.
Second, it must receive no sunlight and be permeated by a bitter, bone-chilling cold.”
“Somewhere secluded, dark, and cold...”
Tang Sadok considered this for a moment, then let out a quiet laugh.
“As it happens, I know the perfect place.
I shall take you there myself.”
“Thank you for your generosity, Family Head.”
“I am no benevolent Great Hero.
This is merely a matter of gratitude and grudges between us.
And if you ever reveal the existence of the Myriad-Poison Ring or allow word of it to spread outside the clan...”
I sighed and finished for him.

“You have a poor imagination.
Whatever you can imagine, you will suffer worse.”
“That won’t happen unless I lose my mind.”
“I certainly hope so...
What are you doing here?”
Good question.
What was that guy doing?
While we were talking, Cheongpung had crept over and was reaching toward Mimi-chan.
“Wow, she’s pretty.
Can I touch her?”
“No.”
“Why not?”
“Hmph.
Do you think she lets just anyone touch her?
If I had not summoned her, she would never even have shown herself before you.”
“Mimi, Mimi.
Come here.”
“What ridiculous nonsense—”
Hissssss.
Mimi-chan slithered down Tang Sadok’s shoulder and licked the back of Cheongpung’s hand.
“Gasp!”
“Mimi, Whirlwind!”
Whirlwind, my ass.
He was ordering her to perform a technique even a person wouldn’t understand.
As expected, there was no telling what went on inside Cheongpung’s head.
Sssshk, sssshk, sssshhhk!
“...What the fuck?”
What had I just witnessed?
My jaw dropped as Mimi-chan began spinning wildly in a tight spiral.
“Wow!
Good job, Mimi!”
“This can’t be!
How could Mimi use Whirlwind on someone she’s never met before?”
“Wait, that’s a real technique?”
“That is not what matters right now!”
It seemed pretty important to me.
At this rate, I wondered whether she might start firing a Thunderbolt or a Hyper Beam.
Can she evolve too...?
As I tried to decide whether the Myriad-Poison Ring or Mimi-chan was the true sacred artifact, Cheongpung beamed.
“I’m good with animals.
When I lay in the grass at Huashan, birds, deer, and even tigers would come play with me.
Hehe.”
What was he, some kind of Huashan druid?
Tang Sadok had been staring blankly at Cheongpung, still reeling from the shock of losing Mimi-chan to him.
Now he raised an objection.
“Wait.
Something strange slipped in at the end.
Why would there be a tiger?
How dare you tell such an obvious lie before this old man!”
“We were all about to say goodbye when the tiger tried to eat the deer, so I knocked it out with Crouching Tiger Fist!”
It sounded completely insane, no matter who heard it.
Which probably meant it was true.
Silence filled the main hall, making Mungyeong’s mutter ring out with unusual clarity.
“Is the Huashan I know a different Huashan...?”
I didn’t know about that, but one thing was certain.
If heaven and earth were ever overturned and Cheongpung somehow became Huashan’s Sect Leader, from that day onward, it would be your Huashan—not mine.
“...Let’s go.
You said you would show us the place.”
“...Very well.”

Aside from two large braziers on either side, there was no one in sight.

It doesn’t look like anyone is guarding this place.”
“If no one is here, I suppose it must be feeding time.”
“Feeding?”
“You will understand once we enter.
Follow me.”
Unlike the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s training hall, this cave did not run in a straight line.

A bad feeling came over me.

chapters.title: Chapter 347
paragraphs: The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison was dark and damp. There was also something about it that sent a chill down the spine.
Perhaps that was only natural. Countless people must have met their deaths here since the underground prison was built.
“Care for a drink?”
In that sense, the old man holding out a worn gourd was practically the Grim Reaper of the underground prison.
I briefly wondered how many people this diminutive, hunchbacked old man had done away with before answering.
“No, thank you.”
“If that’s what you want, then.”
Gulp, gulp.
Old Man Gung tilted the gourd back and wiped his mouth with his sleeve. The sleeve was so worn it looked ready to crumble, and it was covered in dark red stains that looked like blood.
“Ahh, that’s good.”
The potent scent of liquor drifted through the stench of blood lingering in the corridor and tickled the tip of my nose.
Drinking on duty. At the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that would have earned him a disciplinary report, but apparently that rule did not apply in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.
“I heard you’re one of the most renowned young prodigies in the Murim.”

It was obvious who he was talking to. Cheongpung and Tang Sadok had disappeared somewhere early on, while the Divine Physician and Mungyeong were busy purifying the prison and turning it into a treatment room.
I reluctantly answered.
“I wouldn’t say I’m that renowned. I can fart a little, though.”
“That’s not what I heard. As the Fire King’s successor, you could piss on the plaques of the Nine Sects and One Gang and get away with it.”
Old Man Gung grinned, baring teeth that had almost entirely rotted away.
“We’ve got a fellow locked up here who did just that.”
“Did what?”
“Pissed on the plaque of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang. The Kunlun Sect, I believe.”
“...There really are all kinds of people in this world.”
“Heh heh. He was once notorious even among the Demonic Cult’s fiends. Now he’s strapped to a rack, doing nothing but shitting blood. You must have seen him on your way in.”
“Did I?”
The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison was as winding and complicated as a maze. On the way here, I had seen dozens of cells holding more than ten prisoners.
That fellow who pissed on the Kunlun Sect’s plaque was probably one of them.
They were paying the price for their evil deeds. I did not feel even the slightest bit of sympathy for them.
No, it would be more accurate to say that I had no room to worry about something like that.
I didn’t expect to be this nervous.
The peculiar unease I had felt ever since entering the prison refused to fade.
It was the same feeling I’d had several years ago, when my mother went into surgery and I sat in a quiet corridor waiting to hear how it had gone.
It’ll be fine. Everything will be all right.
As I repeated those words to myself, the tightly shut cell door opened and a dozen servants carrying various cleaning tools came pouring out.
I addressed the last person to emerge.
“Is it done?”
The Divine Physician nodded, his expression bright.
In the space of two shichen, the cell behind him had been transformed into a fairly convincing treatment room.
“It is still far from satisfactory, but this should be functional enough.”
“Then...”
“Yes. We begin now.”
At last, all the preparations were complete.
The various medicines made by combining the twenty-four herbs gathered from the Cold-Ice Land had already been brought here. The treatment room was ready. Only one thing remained.
“Thank you all for your hard work. Would you mind giving us the room for a moment?”
At my words, the members of the Sichuan Tang Clan, including Old Man Gung, began to leave. I waited until they had disappeared, then reached inside my robes.
Inventory Open. Summon.
Something hard appeared in my empty palm. I had kept the Myriad-Poison Ring with me for safekeeping, but now I handed it to the Divine Physician.
The Divine Physician accepted the ring, slipped it onto his finger, and entered the prison cell while gesturing to me.
“Would you bring the patient in?”
I lowered the pack frame from my shoulders. A small figure came into view, accompanied by the faintest sound of breathing.
“Over here.”
I stepped into the prison cell with Jeok Cheongang in my arms. The floor was clean, but the stench had not completely disappeared and still lingered at the tip of my nose.
None of that mattered, however. The weight of Jeok Cheongang, light as a feather, made my chest ache unusually badly.
You’ve grown so weak.
A month and a half had already passed since we left the Murim Alliance in Henan and began our journey.
We had found the Divine Physician and secured his treatment far more quickly than I had expected, but Jeok Cheongang had continued to weaken day by day.
Swish.
I carefully laid him on the smooth white stone prepared in the center of the room.
It was a special object called Cold-Ice Stone, provided by Tang Sadok. The Divine Physician had said it would greatly aid Jeok Cheongang’s treatment.
“He’s sleeping soundly.”
Jeok Cheongang’s face was gaunt, but it also looked peaceful.
I gazed at his face, covered in wrinkles and age spots.
Memories of everything that had happened since our first meeting flashed before my eyes.
What an interesting kid.
The more I see of you, the stranger you seem. Whose disciple are you?
I clearly remembered the ill-tempered old man I had met at Jang Taebo’s house a year ago.
The roof is old. It leaks.
I also remembered the master who, unable to stop the wretched disciple he had cherished like family, blamed a perfectly sound roof as he wept tears of regret.
If you kill that bastard, I’ll kill you too.
I entrusted the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred artifact to that kid.
I’ll pass on everything I have to you.
From Shanxi to Henan, and from Henan to Anhui. Then came the year at Mount Jiuhua. I remembered every moment I had spent with him.
Jeok Cheongang had led me beyond the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I had followed him out into the vast world. We had always been together.
Well? Just as I told you, wasn’t it?
What are you talking about?
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon. Wasn’t it incredible?
His face and voice came back to me—the faint smile he wore even while vomiting blood.
Even the single remark he had tossed out on a day when the moon shone brilliantly, while trying to sound gruff.
Master, my ass. Call me Old Master.
“Old Master.”
Even when I called out loud, no answer came back.
I knew there wouldn’t be, yet I still called to him. Not because I hoped he would hear me, but because there was something I wanted to say.
“Did you know?”
I don’t, you idiot!
A dry laugh escaped me at the voice that seemed to echo from somewhere. I gripped Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled hand tightly and whispered,
“I’ve always wanted to call you Master.”
I did not know when it had begun. But at some point, I had realized it.
He was my Master, and I was his Disciple.
We had both been quietly turning those words over in our hearts.
“Young Master Jin. It is time.”
At the Divine Physician’s words, I tore my gaze away from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
Then I respectfully saluted the old physician standing there with a composed expression and the young Disciple beside him.
“Please... take good care of my Master.”
The two returned my salute.
“I will do my best.”
“I, too, will assist my Master and do everything in my power.”
Yes. That was enough.
Do everything one could, then leave the rest to heaven.
We had done everything within human power. All that remained was to entrust the outcome to the heavens.
God, Buddha, Allah, the Jade Emperor.
Whoever you are, if you help me just this once, I’ll never forget it.
I did not believe in gods, but I did believe there was some omniscient and omnipotent being above the heavens.
As I offered a brief prayer to that being whose face and name I did not know, the Divine Physician spoke solemnly.
“Remember this. Fifteen days—fifteen days. Until then, no one may approach.”
What should I do if it takes longer than fifteen days?
I swallowed the words hovering on the tip of my tongue. Now, I had no choice but to trust the two of them. There was only one thing I could say.
“I’ll stop anyone who tries to enter, even if I have to stake my life on it.”
“Is that everything?”
The middle-aged man looked down at his victim with impassive eyes.
The man’s limbs were bent at grotesque angles, and his skin had been flayed away. Reduced to a blood-soaked ruin, he wheezed in a voice as faint as an ant’s.
“I—I’ve already told you everything I know...”
“Aren’t you leaving out the most important part?”
“I don’t know. I truly don’t.”
Bloody tears streamed from his one remaining eye. His trouser legs, already drenched in blood, darkened further with urine.
The man forced out a trembling voice.
“Please... just kill me now...”
The middle-aged man stared into the man’s fading eye, then clicked his tongue.
“It seems you really are telling the truth.”
The man had already endured half a day of unimaginable torture.
If he had begged for his life, there might still have been room for doubt. But now that he was begging for death, the middle-aged man had no choice but to accept it.
Until now, no one had ever lied to the middle-aged man.
No one except the Poison King, Tang Taesang.
“I’ve seen the extent of your half-day’s courage. You may rest now.”
Whoosh—thud!

Along with the sound of a single gust of wind, the blood-soaked head jerked backward. A flick of the middle-aged man’s finger had pierced the man between the brows, and he died with a peaceful expression.
The middle-aged man stared down at the body of the man who had been a member of a collateral branch of the Sichuan Tang Clan and an operative of the Green Shadow Squad. Then he stretched out a hand.
Boom!
A thunderous roar rang out as a pit one zhang deep opened in the ground.
The five corpses scattered nearby were neatly stacked inside it and covered with earth, all within moments.
“The Green Shadow Squad... So those gnats have latched on.”
Muttering under his breath, the middle-aged man looked beyond the winding mountain ridge. West, toward the Sichuan Tang Clan.
I should have killed Tang Sadok when he came out.
That had been a mistake. The Poison King’s resistance had been fiercer than expected, and purging the poison had taken considerable time. It had even cost him an arm.

Emei or Qingcheng might have been another matter, but the Sichuan Tang Clan was exceptionally vigilant and heavily defended. Even for him, storming the place alone after losing an arm would be too much.
But his life has only been extended by a few days. The outcome will not change.
He had long since grasped every movement taking place in Sichuan.
All preparations were complete to hunt the three tigers crouching in Sichuan—Emei, Qingcheng, and the Tang Clan.
Now...
It was time to summon the hunters.
Whoosh!
The middle-aged man moved as though gliding. Distance vanished with every step, and the scenery swept past him.
At last, he stopped before a cliff deep in the mountains.
“This is the place.”
Without hesitation, the middle-aged man reached out and placed a hand against the cliff.
The next instant—
Vwoom.
A resonant hum rang out, and the cliff collapsed.
No. It would be more accurate to say that space itself had warped. The weathered stones and boulders vanished, revealing a vast hollow concealed behind them.
The sorcerers’ Mystic Gate Formation. It never stops being impressive.
But compared to what he was about to do, even this was nothing more than a parlor trick.
Step. Step. Step.
The middle-aged man strode into the darkness blanketing the hollow. At its heart, he stopped in the center of a strange pattern carved into the floor and drew upon his internal energy.
A dark red haze poured from his entire body.
The instant it touched the pattern—
“Lord of Heaven!”
Flash!
At the middle-aged man’s cry, the pattern blazed to life. A black flash—dark yet bright, impossible to describe—filled the entire hollow.
Then the light vanished, and a thunderous chorus filled the space it left behind.
“We pay our respects to the Western Heaven Demon Lord!”
“We pay our respects to the Demon Lord!”
Hundreds of tiger hunters stood before him in pitch-black robes, their eyes devoid of emotion and their auras sharp as blades.
A faint smile touched the lips of the middle-aged man—the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

“Care for a drink?”
In that sense, the old man holding out a worn gourd was practically the Grim Reaper of the underground prison.
I briefly wondered how many people this diminutive, hunchbacked old man had done away with before answering.
“No, thank you.”
“If that’s what you want, then.”
Gulp, gulp.
Old Man Gung tilted the gourd back and wiped his mouth with his sleeve.
The sleeve was so worn it looked ready to crumble, and it was covered in dark red stains that looked like blood.
“Ahh, that’s good.”
The potent scent of liquor drifted through the stench of blood lingering in the corridor and tickled the tip of my nose.
Drinking on duty.
At the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that would have earned him a disciplinary report, but apparently that rule did not apply in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.
“I heard you’re one of the most renowned young prodigies in the Murim.”
It was obvious who he was talking to.
Cheongpung and Tang Sadok had disappeared somewhere early on, while the Divine Physician and Mungyeong were busy purifying the prison and turning it into a treatment room.
I reluctantly answered.
“I wouldn’t say I’m that renowned.
I can fart a little, though.”
“That’s not what I heard.
As the Fire King’s successor, you could piss on the plaques of the Nine Sects and One Gang and get away with it.”
Old Man Gung grinned, baring teeth that had almost entirely rotted away.
“We’ve got a fellow locked up here who did just that.”
“Did what?”
“Pissed on the plaque of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang.
The Kunlun Sect, I believe.”
“...There really are all kinds of people in this world.”
“Heh heh.
He was once notorious even among the Demonic Cult’s fiends.
Now he’s strapped to a rack, doing nothing but shitting blood.
You must have seen him on your way in.”
“Did I?”
The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison was as winding and complicated as a maze.
On the way here, I had seen dozens of cells holding more than ten prisoners.
That fellow who pissed on the Kunlun Sect’s plaque was probably one of them.
They were paying the price for their evil deeds.
I did not feel even the slightest bit of sympathy for them.
No, it would be more accurate to say that I had no room to worry about something like that.
I didn’t expect to be this nervous.
The peculiar unease I had felt ever since entering the prison refused to fade.
It was the same feeling I’d had several years ago, when my mother went into surgery and I sat in a quiet corridor waiting to hear how it had gone.
It’ll be fine.
Everything will be all right.
As I repeated those words to myself, the tightly shut cell door opened and a dozen servants carrying various cleaning tools came pouring out.
I addressed the last person to emerge.
“Is it done?”
The Divine Physician nodded, his expression bright.
In the space of two shichen, the cell behind him had been transformed into a fairly convincing treatment room.
“It is still far from satisfactory, but this should be functional enough.”
“Then...”
“Yes.
We begin now.”
At last, all the preparations were complete.
The various medicines made by combining the twenty-four herbs gathered from the Cold-Ice Land had already been brought here.
The treatment room was ready.
Only one thing remained.
“Thank you all for your hard work.
Would you mind giving us the room for a moment?”
At my words, the members of the Sichuan Tang Clan, including Old Man Gung, began to leave.
I waited until they had disappeared, then reached inside my robes.
Inventory Open.
Summon.
Something hard appeared in my empty palm.
I had kept the Myriad-Poison Ring with me for safekeeping, but now I handed it to the Divine Physician.
The Divine Physician accepted the ring, slipped it onto his finger, and entered the prison cell while gesturing to me.
“Would you bring the patient in?”
I lowered the pack frame from my shoulders.
A small figure came into view, accompanied by the faintest sound of breathing.
“Over here.”
I stepped into the prison cell with Jeok Cheongang in my arms.
The floor was clean, but the stench had not completely disappeared and still lingered at the tip of my nose.
None of that mattered, however.
The weight of Jeok Cheongang, light as a feather, made my chest ache unusually badly.
You’ve grown so weak.
A month and a half had already passed since we left the Murim Alliance in Henan and began our journey.
We had found the Divine Physician and secured his treatment far more quickly than I had expected, but Jeok Cheongang had continued to weaken day by day.
Swish.
I carefully laid him on the smooth white stone prepared in the center of the room.
It was a special object called Cold-Ice Stone, provided by Tang Sadok.
The Divine Physician had said it would greatly aid Jeok Cheongang’s treatment.
“He’s sleeping soundly.”
Jeok Cheongang’s face was gaunt, but it also looked peaceful.
I gazed at his face, covered in wrinkles and age spots.
Memories of everything that had happened since our first meeting flashed before my eyes.
What an interesting kid.
The more I see of you, the stranger you seem.
Whose disciple are you?
I clearly remembered the ill-tempered old man I had met at Jang Taebo’s house a year ago.
The roof is old.
It leaks.
I also remembered the master who, unable to stop the wretched disciple he had cherished like family, blamed a perfectly sound roof as he wept tears of regret.
If you kill that bastard, I’ll kill you too.
I entrusted the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred artifact to that kid.
I’ll pass on everything I have to you.
From Shanxi to Henan, and from Henan to Anhui.
Then came the year at Mount Jiuhua.
I remembered every moment I had spent with him.
Jeok Cheongang had led me beyond the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I had followed him out into the vast world.
We had always been together.
Well?
Just as I told you, wasn’t it?
What are you talking about?
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon.
Wasn’t it incredible?
His face and voice came back to me—the faint smile he wore even while vomiting blood.
Even the single remark he had tossed out on a day when the moon shone brilliantly, while trying to sound gruff.
Master, my ass.
Call me Old Master.
“Old Master.”
Even when I called out loud, no answer came back.
I knew there wouldn’t be, yet I still called to him.
Not because I hoped he would hear me, but because there was something I wanted to say.
“Did you know?”
I don’t, you idiot!
A dry laugh escaped me at the voice that seemed to echo from somewhere.
I gripped Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled hand tightly and whispered,
“I’ve always wanted to call you Master.”
I did not know when it had begun.
But at some point, I had realized it.
He was my Master, and I was his Disciple.
We had both been quietly turning those words over in our hearts.
“Young Master Jin.
It is time.”
At the Divine Physician’s words, I tore my gaze away from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
Then I respectfully saluted the old physician standing there with a composed expression and the young Disciple beside him.
“Please... take good care of my Master.”
The two returned my salute.
“I will do my best.”
“I, too, will assist my Master and do everything in my power.”
Yes.
That was enough.
Do everything one could, then leave the rest to heaven.
We had done everything within human power.
All that remained was to entrust the outcome to the heavens.
God, Buddha, Allah, the Jade Emperor.
Whoever you are, if you help me just this once, I’ll never forget it.
I did not believe in gods, but I did believe there was some omniscient and omnipotent being above the heavens.
As I offered a brief prayer to that being whose face and name I did not know, the Divine Physician spoke solemnly.
“Remember this.
Fifteen days—fifteen days.
Until then, no one may approach.”
What should I do if it takes longer than fifteen days?
I swallowed the words hovering on the tip of my tongue.
Now, I had no choice but to trust the two of them.
There was only one thing I could say.
“I’ll stop anyone who tries to enter, even if I have to stake my life on it.”
“Is that everything?”
The middle-aged man looked down at his victim with impassive eyes.
The man’s limbs were bent at grotesque angles, and his skin had been flayed away.
Reduced to a blood-soaked ruin, he wheezed in a voice as faint as an ant’s.
“I—I’ve already told you everything I know...”
“Aren’t you leaving out the most important part?”
“I don’t know.
I truly don’t.”
Bloody tears streamed from his one remaining eye.
His trouser legs, already drenched in blood, darkened further with urine.
The man forced out a trembling voice.
“Please... just kill me now...”
The middle-aged man stared into the man’s fading eye, then clicked his tongue.
“It seems you really are telling the truth.”
The man had already endured half a day of unimaginable torture.
If he had begged for his life, there might still have been room for doubt.
But now that he was begging for death, the middle-aged man had no choice but to accept it.
Until now, no one had ever lied to the middle-aged man.
No one except the Poison King, Tang Taesang.
“I’ve seen the extent of your half-day’s courage.
You may rest now.”
Whoosh—thud!
Along with the sound of a single gust of wind, the blood-soaked head jerked backward.
A flick of the middle-aged man’s finger had pierced the man between the brows, and he died with a peaceful expression.
The middle-aged man stared down at the body of the man who had been a member of a collateral branch of the Sichuan Tang Clan and an operative of the Green Shadow Squad.
Then he stretched out a hand.
Boom!
A thunderous roar rang out as a pit one zhang deep opened in the ground.
The five corpses scattered nearby were neatly stacked inside it and covered with earth, all within moments.
“The Green Shadow Squad...
So those gnats have latched on.”
Muttering under his breath, the middle-aged man looked beyond the winding mountain ridge.
West, toward the Sichuan Tang Clan.
I should have killed Tang Sadok when he came out.
That had been a mistake.
The Poison King’s resistance had been fiercer than expected, and purging the poison had taken considerable time.
It had even cost him an arm.
Emei or Qingcheng might have been another matter, but the Sichuan Tang Clan was exceptionally vigilant and heavily defended.
Even for him, storming the place alone after losing an arm would be too much.
But his life has only been extended by a few days.
The outcome will not change.
He had long since grasped every movement taking place in Sichuan.
All preparations were complete to hunt the three tigers crouching in Sichuan—Emei, Qingcheng, and the Tang Clan.
Now...
It was time to summon the hunters.
Whoosh!
The middle-aged man moved as though gliding.
Distance vanished with every step, and the scenery swept past him.
At last, he stopped before a cliff deep in the mountains.
“This is the place.”
Without hesitation, the middle-aged man reached out and placed a hand against the cliff.
The next instant—
Vwoom.
A resonant hum rang out, and the cliff collapsed.
No.
It would be more accurate to say that space itself had warped.
The weathered stones and boulders vanished, revealing a vast hollow concealed behind them.
The sorcerers’ Mystic Gate Formation.
It never stops being impressive.
But compared to what he was about to do, even this was nothing more than a parlor trick.
Step.
Step.
Step.
The middle-aged man strode into the darkness blanketing the hollow.
At its heart, he stopped in the center of a strange pattern carved into the floor and drew upon his internal energy.
A dark red haze poured from his entire body.
The instant it touched the pattern—
“Lord of Heaven!”
Flash!
At the middle-aged man’s cry, the pattern blazed to life.
A black flash—dark yet bright, impossible to describe—filled the entire hollow.
Then the light vanished, and a thunderous chorus filled the space it left behind.
“We pay our respects to the Western Heaven Demon Lord!”
“We pay our respects to the Demon Lord!”
Hundreds of tiger hunters stood before him in pitch-black robes, their eyes devoid of emotion and their auras sharp as blades.
A faint smile touched the lips of the middle-aged man—the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

chapters.title: Chapter 348
paragraphs: The black-robed men stood in neat ranks and files. The sheer number of them—several hundred—was not the only thing filling the enormous cavern.
It was their aura.
The suffocating aura emanating from the men—their eyes deep-set, their bodies upright as iron towers—was swallowing the cavern.
And towering over them all stood one man—a giant in his own right.
“Third Fiend.”
Vwoom.
His voice, infused with profound internal energy, bored into the black-robed men’s ears. They shuddered, and the three old men at the front were no exception.
They stepped forward several paces, then prostrated themselves at the middle-aged man’s feet in perfect unison.
“The juniors of the Qilian Mountains pay their respects to the Western Heaven Demon Lord.”
Their faces, builds, and voices—everything about the three old men was astonishingly alike.
They were brothers born from the same womb.

Their mother had died giving birth to them, and their father had abandoned his young children and left. Stranded in the barren land of Qinghai, the three brothers hid near the vast mountain range to escape the scorn of others.
Then, one day, after everyone had forgotten them, the brothers returned.
They returned as the Qilian Three Fiends.
“You’ve aged quite a bit since I last saw you. I suppose I could call you the Three Old Men now.”
“N-no, my lord. How could the likes of us be called old while you are here?”
The Qilian Three Fiends had once been fiends who dyed Qinghai Province red with blood. Yet before the Western Heaven Demon Lord, they were nothing more than docile lambs.
The Qilian Three Fiends swallowed hard, then opened their mouths at the same time, as if they were one person.
“B-but, my lord. Forgive us for saying so, but your arm...”
“This?”
The Western Heaven Demon Lord looked down at the empty sleeve where one of his arms should have been and answered in a dry voice.
“It was the price I paid for two lives.”
“Does that mean...”
“The two old fossils from the Tang Clan and Emei are no longer of this world.”
The air inside the cavern trembled with agitation.
Who were the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun? They were giants who had left their mark on the history of the Murim, Supreme Peak masters who had dominated an entire era.
And yet...
Both had met their end at the hands of a single man.
The Qilian Three Fiends and the black-robed men stared at their leader in awe.
“Th-then...”
“Yes.”
A fierce light flashed in the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes.
“The time has finally come.”
Right now, my eyes are closed.
I focus my mind in the quiet darkness. As a voice pierces my ears, someone’s figure takes shape in the darkness.
Neither tall nor short, the young man hiding claws behind an innocent smile is Cheongpung.
“First, I’ll use Crouching Tiger Fist to target my Benefactor’s shoulder, chest, and stomach in that order.”
The imaginary Cheongpung moves through the darkness.
Fast.
He erases the distance in a single step and rushes in, his fist blurring. I can almost hear the fierce whistle of air being torn apart.
“I can dodge that easily. I’ll retreat half a step diagonally and throw a punch at your flank.”
“I’ll use Chaotic Flower Hand to redirect your force as I retreat, then counter with Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.”
“What form?”
“One Cut Under Heaven.”
One Cut Under Heaven was among the most powerful supreme forms of the Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.
Even back when Cheongpung and I had sparred regularly, I had chosen to evade that technique rather than block it.
“Isn’t that a little excessive?”
“Given who my opponent is, I have to give it everything I’ve got.”
“What happened to calling me Benefactor?”
“That’s one thing, and this is another. Hehe. Anyway, One Cut Under Heaven.”
One Cut Under Heaven.
It wasn’t difficult to imagine how the attack would come.
In the darkness, Cheongpung uses Chaotic Flower Hand to redirect my force and retreat without taking the blow. The instant his hand reaches his waist, a flash bursts forth.
Sshk!
With a spine-chilling hiss, Sword Energy surges out horizontally.
I can see it vividly before me.
What should I do?
I don’t have to think long.
“I’ll deflect it. First form of the Fire Dragon Divine Spear—Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.”
“You won’t be able to block it.”
“When was the last time we fought?”
“Hmm. About a year ago.”
“If you think about it one way, that’s short. If you think about it another, it’s a long time. It was long for me. Long enough for a single day to feel like ten years.”
“Think again. Are you sure I can’t block it?”
Cheongpung was silent for a moment before answering. His voice had sunk low.
“I was wrong. If it’s you, Benefactor... I think you can.”
“Then let’s continue.”
Cheongpung and I devoted ourselves to discussing martial arts for a long while.

It had been more than a year since we had actually crossed hands, but from the Star-Array Grand Banquet until now, we had come to know each other’s martial arts and skill levels well enough to make this possible.
“Three steps to the left. Plum Blossom Five-Point Finger.”
“Plum Blossom Five-Point Finger is an excellent martial art, but it won’t matter as long as I protect my vital points. I’ll follow you in and strike your chest with Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”
Within the scenes we each imagine, the battle surges back and forth.
One hundred exchanges. Two hundred.
Before long, our imagined bout passes five hundred exchanges. Then Cheongpung suddenly speaks.
“I’ll use Dark Fragrance Drift to close to within two steps, then Plum Blossom Three-Ridge Sword.”
All of a sudden?

Cheongpung was weaker than me in close combat. He had learned Huashan’s outstanding supreme martial arts, but perhaps because the sect’s roots lay in sword techniques, the Fire Gate Clan had a slight advantage when it came to palm techniques.
And yet he was coming in this close...
Ah. So that’s it.
I had suspected as much, but this was Cheongpung, all right.
I opened my eyes with a hollow laugh. When I didn’t answer for a long while, Cheongpung cautiously opened his eyes to a narrow slit and asked,
“Benefactor, why?”
“That’s enough for today.”
“Ah! Why?”
“Because it would be a shame.”
“What?”
“Let’s fight for real later. Not through a discussion like this. Let’s actually cross weapons.”
It would be too unsatisfying to decide the outcome through an imagined exchange. I meant that we should settle it later with both of us fighting at full strength.
Cheongpung was as innocent as a child, but by no means stupid. Surely that was enough for him to understand—
“Why would we cross weapons? Wouldn’t they collide?”
No.
Maybe he really was just an idiot.
While I regretted my hasty judgment, Cheongpung began pestering me.
“I’m bored, Benefactor. Can’t we keep going?”
“Oh, Cheongpung. Did you hear about that?”
“About what?”
I gazed intently at Cheongpung and parted my lips.
“I heard there’s a former imperial chef at the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“An imperial chef?”
“Apparently, his cooking is incredible. Especially his pastries and sweets.”
Gasp.
Cheongpung’s eyes glazed over for a moment, but he soon shook his head vigorously.
“N-no. I have to stay here with you and watch over Grandpa Jeok.”
“It’s fine. I’m staying here anyway, so—”
“Then I’ll be back!”
“...Sure. Go ahead.”
Whoosh!
What was that? Some kind of bullet movement technique?
Once Cheongpung had vanished at the speed of light, I looked around.
A bleak chill and a foul stench permeated the underground prison. I hadn’t taken a single step outside since the treatment began.
“It’s only the fourth day.”
The words escaped me like a sigh.

Time passed far more slowly in the underground prison than I had imagined. Not because the place never saw a ray of sunlight, but because of the anxiety and tension felt only by those who were waiting.
Perhaps that was why every day felt like my blood was drying up.
“Maybe I should have stayed in front of the treatment room.”
Even as I said it, I shook my head. There was nothing I could do by pacing in front of the treatment room door anyway.

With my five senses already sharpened to their limit, I would only listen to every sound coming from inside until I could no longer bear it, then retreat and pace through the underground prison at a distance.
Just as I was doing now.
Still, it’s awfully quiet now that I’m alone.
With Cheongpung, who had stuck to me like glue for the past three days, suddenly gone, I felt strangely empty.
Tang Sadok had forbidden even Old Man Gung from entering the prison, so I was completely alone now.
No. Come to think of it, I’m not alone.
I wasn’t talking about the Divine Physician and Mungyeong, who were probably completely absorbed in treating Jeok Cheongang.
There were ten or so prisoners trapped in the underground prison, waiting for the day they would die.
They were my roommates.
Not exactly the best roommates, though.
They weren’t the kind who left the toilet unflushed or constantly brought their lovers over. Every one of them was a fiend who had earned a notorious name throughout the martial world.
Even if they were imprisoned, there was no way sharing a space with men like that could be enjoyable.
And the most troublesome part was...
Dong. Ddong. Ddeeeong.
I’m the one who has to feed them.
I frowned at the familiar tolling of the bell.
With Old Man Gung gone, someone had to make sure the prisoners were still alive and bring them their meals.
That someone was me.
The bell that had just rung was the signal from outside announcing mealtime.
At least it’s only once a day.
Still, bothersome was bothersome. I sighed and started walking.
In a corner of the prison, a battered old wooden barrel awaited me, filled with scraps of food haphazardly mixed together.
It had been poured down through a hole connected to the surface. Calling it a meal was generous. It was basically a slop bucket.
No one’s around, so I guess it’s feeding time.
There was a reason Tang Sadok had used the word feed three days ago.
The Sichuan Tang Clan treated the prisoners here like dogs and pigs.
No, dogs and pigs had it better. At least livestock didn’t have to worry about surprise visits from Old Man Gung carrying an assortment of torture implements and wearing an eerie smile.
“Heave-ho.”
Adopting the mindset of a zookeeper, I carried the slop bucket around the prison.

Beyond the thick iron bars, prisoners sat with their arms and legs bound in steel chains. All I had to do was open each door, step inside, scoop up a heaping ladleful, and dump it into the battered bowl set before them.
Whenever I did that, the prisoners, who had been lying limp and helpless after prolonged imprisonment and torture, would make their eyes flash and strike up a conversation.
“Never seen your face before.”
“You’ve been seeing me for three days. What kind of bullshit is that?”
“Release me. I’ll teach you martial arts that can look down on all under heaven.”
“Judging by the fact that you’re rotting in here, they sound like martial arts the whole world can look down on.”
“You insolent bastard... The moment I get out of here, I’ll tear you apart and kill you myself.”
“Oh, impressive. I’ll be sure to pass that along to Old Man Gung.”
“Please! Anything but that!”
The attempts to win me over never stopped.

Some offered to teach me their martial arts. A middle-aged beauty who had once drained the vital essence of the Tang Clan’s direct line through a technique of harvesting yang to replenish yin even tried to seduce me.
“Child. Why don’t you come a little closer? I’ll show you heaven.”
“Kirara Asuka. Grandma Uehara.”
“...What?”
“The mainland still has a long way to go compared to the island nation. Stop talking nonsense and eat your damn food.”
“You little—Hey! You turtle bastard!”
I ignored her spiteful shouting and headed toward the last prison cell.
In the most secluded and damp corner was a strange man with disheveled hair.
He’s the quietest old man in this prison.
He was also the most dangerous.
The severed sinews and meridians in his limbs and the restraints several times heavier and sturdier than those of the other prisoners were proof enough.
Rattle. Thump.
The old man stared silently at the bowl of unidentifiable food before suddenly speaking.
“I heard you talking about this old man.”
I stopped short.
Not because it was the first time I had heard his voice in three days, but because I had no idea what he meant.
“Talking about you? When did I do that?”
“Three days ago. Did that Gung fellow not mention me?”
“Gung fellow? Old Man Gung?”
I searched my memory for a moment, then looked at the old man with newfound surprise.
“Oh. Then are you the one who pissed on the Kunlun Sect’s signboard?”
“Yes. This old man is the Heavenly Power Demon—”
“So you were the Kunlun Sect’s public-pissing criminal.”
The old man—the Heavenly Power Demon—had an eyelid that twitched.
