Cheongpung and I devoted ourselves to discussing martial arts for a long while.

It had been more than a year since we had actually crossed hands, but from the Star-Array Grand Banquet until now, we had come to know each other’s martial arts and skill levels well enough to make this possible.
“Three steps to the left.
Plum Blossom Five-Point Finger.”
“Plum Blossom Five-Point Finger is an excellent martial art, but it won’t matter as long as I protect my vital points.
I’ll follow you in and strike your chest with Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”
Within the scenes we each imagine, the battle surges back and forth.
One hundred exchanges.
Two hundred.
Before long, our imagined bout passes five hundred exchanges.
Then Cheongpung suddenly speaks.
“I’ll use Dark Fragrance Drift to close to within two steps, then Plum Blossom Three-Ridge Sword.”
All of a sudden?
Cheongpung was weaker than me in close combat.
He had learned Huashan’s outstanding supreme martial arts, but perhaps because the sect’s roots lay in sword techniques, the Fire Gate Clan had a slight advantage when it came to palm techniques.
And yet he was coming in this close...
Ah.
So that’s it.
I had suspected as much, but this was Cheongpung, all right.
I opened my eyes with a hollow laugh.
When I didn’t answer for a long while, Cheongpung cautiously opened his eyes to a narrow slit and asked,
“Benefactor, why?”
“That’s enough for today.”
“Ah!
Why?”
“Because it would be a shame.”
“What?”
“Let’s fight for real later.
Not through a discussion like this.
Let’s actually cross weapons.”
It would be too unsatisfying to decide the outcome through an imagined exchange.
I meant that we should settle it later with both of us fighting at full strength.
Cheongpung was as innocent as a child, but by no means stupid.
Surely that was enough for him to understand—
“Why would we cross weapons?
Wouldn’t they collide?”
No.
Maybe he really was just an idiot.
While I regretted my hasty judgment, Cheongpung began pestering me.
“I’m bored, Benefactor.
Can’t we keep going?”
“Oh, Cheongpung.
Did you hear about that?”
“About what?”
I gazed intently at Cheongpung and parted my lips.
“I heard there’s a former imperial chef at the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“An imperial chef?”
“Apparently, his cooking is incredible.
Especially his pastries and sweets.”
Gasp.
Cheongpung’s eyes glazed over for a moment, but he soon shook his head vigorously.
“N-no.
I have to stay here with you and watch over Grandpa Jeok.”
“It’s fine.
I’m staying here anyway, so—”
“Then I’ll be back!”
“...Sure.
Go ahead.”
Whoosh!
What was that?
Some kind of bullet movement technique?
Once Cheongpung had vanished at the speed of light, I looked around.
A bleak chill and a foul stench permeated the underground prison.
I hadn’t taken a single step outside since the treatment began.
“It’s only the fourth day.”
The words escaped me like a sigh.
Time passed far more slowly in the underground prison than I had imagined.
Not because the place never saw a ray of sunlight, but because of the anxiety and tension felt only by those who were waiting.
Perhaps that was why every day felt like my blood was drying up.
“Maybe I should have stayed in front of the treatment room.”
Even as I said it, I shook my head.
There was nothing I could do by pacing in front of the treatment room door anyway.

With my five senses already sharpened to their limit, I would only listen to every sound coming from inside until I could no longer bear it, then retreat and pace through the underground prison at a distance.
Just as I was doing now.
Still, it’s awfully quiet now that I’m alone.
With Cheongpung, who had stuck to me like glue for the past three days, suddenly gone, I felt strangely empty.
Tang Sadok had forbidden even Old Man Gung from entering the prison, so I was completely alone now.
No.
Come to think of it, I’m not alone.
I wasn’t talking about the Divine Physician and Mungyeong, who were probably completely absorbed in treating Jeok Cheongang.
There were ten or so prisoners trapped in the underground prison, waiting for the day they would die.
They were my roommates.
Not exactly the best roommates, though.
They weren’t the kind who left the toilet unflushed or constantly brought their lovers over.
Every one of them was a fiend who had earned a notorious name throughout the martial world.
Even if they were imprisoned, there was no way sharing a space with men like that could be enjoyable.
And the most troublesome part was...
Dong.
Ddong.
Ddeeeong.
I’m the one who has to feed them.
I frowned at the familiar tolling of the bell.
With Old Man Gung gone, someone had to make sure the prisoners were still alive and bring them their meals.
That someone was me.
The bell that had just rung was the signal from outside announcing mealtime.
At least it’s only once a day.
Still, bothersome was bothersome.
I sighed and started walking.
In a corner of the prison, a battered old wooden barrel awaited me, filled with scraps of food haphazardly mixed together.
It had been poured down through a hole connected to the surface.
Calling it a meal was generous.
It was basically a slop bucket.
No one’s around, so I guess it’s feeding time.
There was a reason Tang Sadok had used the word feed three days ago.
The Sichuan Tang Clan treated the prisoners here like dogs and pigs.
No, dogs and pigs had it better.
At least livestock didn’t have to worry about surprise visits from Old Man Gung carrying an assortment of torture implements and wearing an eerie smile.
“Heave-ho.”
Adopting the mindset of a zookeeper, I carried the slop bucket around the prison.
Beyond the thick iron bars, prisoners sat with their arms and legs bound in steel chains.
All I had to do was open each door, step inside, scoop up a heaping ladleful, and dump it into the battered bowl set before them.
Whenever I did that, the prisoners, who had been lying limp and helpless after prolonged imprisonment and torture, would make their eyes flash and strike up a conversation.
“Never seen your face before.”
“You’ve been seeing me for three days.
What kind of bullshit is that?”
“Release me.
I’ll teach you martial arts that can look down on all under heaven.”
“Judging by the fact that you’re rotting in here, they sound like martial arts the whole world can look down on.”
“You insolent bastard...
The moment I get out of here, I’ll tear you apart and kill you myself.”
“Oh, impressive.
I’ll be sure to pass that along to Old Man Gung.”
“Please!
Anything but that!”
The attempts to win me over never stopped.
Some offered to teach me their martial arts.
A middle-aged beauty who had once drained the vital essence of the Tang Clan’s direct line through a technique of harvesting yang to replenish yin even tried to seduce me.
“Child.
Why don’t you come a little closer?
I’ll show you heaven.”
“Kirara Asuka.
Grandma Uehara.”
“...What?”
“The mainland still has a long way to go compared to the island nation.
Stop talking nonsense and eat your damn food.”
“You little—Hey!
You turtle bastard!”
I ignored her spiteful shouting and headed toward the last prison cell.
In the most secluded and damp corner was a strange man with disheveled hair.
He’s the quietest old man in this prison.
He was also the most dangerous.
The severed sinews and meridians in his limbs and the restraints several times heavier and sturdier than those of the other prisoners were proof enough.
Rattle.
Thump.
The old man stared silently at the bowl of unidentifiable food before suddenly speaking.
“I heard you talking about this old man.”
I stopped short.
Not because it was the first time I had heard his voice in three days, but because I had no idea what he meant.
“Talking about you?
When did I do that?”
“Three days ago.
Did that Gung fellow not mention me?”
“Gung fellow?
Old Man Gung?”
I searched my memory for a moment, then looked at the old man with newfound surprise.
“Oh.
Then are you the one who pissed on the Kunlun Sect’s signboard?”
“Yes.
This old man is the Heavenly Power Demon—”
“So you were the Kunlun Sect’s public-pissing criminal.”
The old man—the Heavenly Power Demon—had an eyelid that twitched.

chapters.title: Chapter 349
paragraphs: After a brief silence, the Heavenly Power Demon spoke.
“...A public-urination criminal? Do not call this old man by such a disgraceful name.”
Ah. My mistake.
It seemed the fiend who had once spread his infamy throughout the world found that title rather unpleasant.
After giving it some thought, I offered him a more appropriate alternative.
“Hmm. How about bedwetter?”
“Y-you little...”
“If you don’t like that, then The New Nation’s Little Pisser.”
“This old man did not wet himself!”
“Then He Who Peed. A Midsummer Night’s Pee, featuring the Kunlun Sect.”
I clicked my tongue at the Heavenly Power Demon, who couldn’t even come up with a response.

“I don’t know what got into you and made you start talking all of a sudden, but I don’t want to hear it, and I don’t want to talk to you. So eat your damn food and relieve yourself to your heart’s content. Shit, piss, or both at the same time. Whatever you want.”
“W-wait.”
Good grief. What a pain.
I had finished handing out the food and was about to leave the underground prison when I turned around with an irritated scowl.
“What?”
“There is something I wish to ask.”
“And if you have something to ask, am I obligated to answer?”
But the Heavenly Power Demon, seized by an inexplicable desperation, refused to back down. Wearing scraps of what might once have been called clothing, he opened his mouth with a gleam in his eyes.
“The Divine Cult. What has become of the Divine Cult?”
“The Divine Cult?”
“Yes, the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult!”
“Oh. The Demonic Cult.”
The different names used by the two sides had confused me for a moment.
To most Murim warriors, myself included, it was your Demonic Cult. But to members of the Demonic Cult, it could only be our Divine Cult.
Especially for the Heavenly Power Demon standing before me. Wasn’t he a fiend whose notoriety had once been considerable even among the Demonic Cult’s members?
“What, have you been locked up so long that you’re feeling homesick?”
“Tell me.”
“That’s easy enough.”
I gave a short laugh and continued.
“I don’t know either.”
“...What?”
“How would I know what the Demonic Cult is doing, holed up all the way out there? If a new inmate from the Demonic Cult ends up in the cell next to yours, ask him.”
The Heavenly Power Demon stared at me as if he couldn’t understand.
“Are you not the Fire King’s successor? Yet you claim to know nothing about the Divine Cult?”
“...How did you know that?”
“My dantian may be ruined, but these old ears still work.”
“You’re remarkably spry for your age. How much do you know?”
“Only that the Fire King is here to have his injuries treated.”
“Hmm.”
He was a rather perceptive old man.

Cheongpung had mentioned Jeok Cheongang’s name several times, but never loudly enough for the other prisoners to hear. Even if the Heavenly Power Demon had overheard him, it would have been difficult to infer the circumstances from those conversations alone.
He keeps his mouth shut and his ears open.
He was different from the other prisoners, who tried every possible trick to win me over the moment they saw an opening.
I found myself growing slightly interested in the old man before me.
“But why are you so curious about news of the Demonic Cult? You’ve been imprisoned for ages.”
“It has been forty-odd years.”
“The Great Faction War had already ended around then. Don’t you have a general idea of what happened?”
“A general idea?”
The Heavenly Power Demon smiled bitterly.
“Few people know the Divine Cult better than this old man.”
“Sounds like you pissed on things there too.”
“This old man was once an Elder of the Great Heavenly Demon Divine Cult. It was I who obeyed the august command of the Cult Leader, subjugated Qinghai, and fired the opening shot of the holy war.”
“Holy war, my ass.”
Despite my curt response, I was secretly surprised.
He’s a bigger deal than I thought.
From the bits and pieces I had picked up, the Demonic Cult had immensely powerful fiends known as the Ten Elders or the Seven Elders or something like that.

I had assumed he wasn’t an ordinary fiend after hearing that he’d pissed all over the Kunlun Sect’s signboard. But I had never imagined that the shabby old man waiting to die in an underground prison had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult.
“You knew nothing about this old man, I suppose.”
“Of course not. That was ages ago. Today was the first time I’d even heard the title Heavenly Power Demon.”
“...Heh. Has it truly been so long already?”
As the Heavenly Power Demon let out a hollow, self-mocking laugh, I leaned against the prison wall.
“So what does a former Demonic Cult Elder from forty years ago want to ask me?”
“Tell me everything you know about the Divine Cult. Every piece of recent news, without adding or omitting anything.”
“I don’t know. Something about this feels off.”
“This old man has already passed his ninetieth year. Both body and spirit are exhausted. This is the final request of an old man who has already been given his day to die.”
“The request of a fiend who committed all kinds of atrocities, you mean.”

“Atrocities... I will gladly pay for the lives I have taken. But what, exactly, makes something demonic? The Divine Cult and your people opposed each other for many years, each standing by its own convictions. We merely lost the struggle in which we staked our fate. That is all.”
The Heavenly Power Demon continued in a clear voice, almost lamenting.

“Can that alone determine who was right and who was wrong? The world back then was like a powder keg that could explode at any moment. Had your side crossed Gansu and Qinghai first and reached the Divine Cult, you would have slaughtered our followers beneath the paltry excuses of serving the greater good and rooting out evil at its source.”
“But from what I’ve heard...”
“Boy.”
His quiet voice silenced me.
A pair of eyes blazed more fiercely than ever as they stared into mine.
They were not the eyes of an old man whose martial arts had been completely crippled, waiting for the day he would die.
They belonged to a general and Supreme Peak master who had once led an army and swept across the world.

“This old man saw it with his own eyes and experienced it firsthand. I saw how cruel men could become in a war of killing and being killed. Neither the followers of the Divine Cult who cried out for holy war nor the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang who called for the extermination of demons were exceptions. Even...”
At that moment, the fire in his eyes died away. Only his bitter voice remained, scattering through the air like ash.

“Even the Cult Leader was no exception. He lost the convictions with which he had begun and fell into corruption. Yes. Perhaps, as you orthodox faction warriors claim, the Divine Cult truly had become a Demonic Cult.”
The Heavenly Power Demon’s words left my thoughts tangled.
In a way, what he had just said aligned with something I had recently come to understand.
Good people and bad people exist everywhere.
The Demonic Cult and the orthodox Murim had been at odds for ages, each holding a match as they watched the other across a powder keg ready to explode.
The Demonic Cult had ultimately been the one to light the fuse. But what if the orthodox faction had struck the first match?
Would the Roaring Fury Swordsman and the Taeeul Merciless Sword have spared ordinary Demonic Cult civilians who knew nothing of martial arts?
No way.
For a moment, those two men overlapped with the Heavenly Power Demon in my mind.
Who was white, and who was black? Was there something unknown hidden in the history that had already passed?
Damn it. I don’t know.
I bit my lip hard and pulled my back away from the cold wall.
“There’s no point telling me any of that.”
The Heavenly Power Demon nodded weakly.
“...I know. Nothing is more futile than speaking of a past already gone.”
“And I’m not as knowledgeable about the Demonic Cult as you think. If that well-informed beggar were here instead, he might’ve been able to give you the news you want.”
“Did the Divine Cult fall?”
“I don’t know. Apparently not. From what I’ve heard, it has managed to survive somehow.”
Dark Heaven’s name had drawn so much attention lately that it was easy to forget, but the Demonic Cult remained the orthodox Murim’s eternal archenemy.
And with a possible connection between the Demonic Cult and Dark Heaven now under suspicion, the Murim Alliance headquarters in Henan was probably busy investigating both.
“I did hear that the Demonic Cult suffered devastating losses in the Great Faction War and shrank to a shadow of its former self.”
The Central Plains was not called the center of the world for nothing.

Unlike the orthodox Murim, which had recovered a considerable portion of its losses by absorbing the region’s abundant resources, goods, and population like a sponge, the Demonic Cult had been forced into the Tianshan Mountains while bearing the full weight of its tremendous losses.
“...Of course. It was a war in which the Divine Cult mobilized its full strength.”
He muttered under his breath, a self-mocking smile touching his lips.

“Heh. We once swallowed half the world, and now we are reduced to this pitiful state. I should have stopped the Cult Leader, even at the cost of my life, when he accepted vicious criminals like the Qilian Three Fiends and the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts. Then again, that was when the Cult Leader himself began to change.”
“The Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
“You may not know of them, but long ago, there were men called—”
“Oh, I know them.”
“What? You know the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
I nodded as if it were obvious.
“I don’t know much about the Qilian Three Fiends, but I know the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts.”
“How can someone who has never even heard this old man’s title know of the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
“Well, you see...”
I scratched the back of my head and continued.
“I tend to remember the title of anyone I’ve fought. Especially masters of that caliber.”
“...W-what? You fought the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”

“Technically, I only fought one of them—the Yang Ghost. Our Old Master—no, Master—killed the Yang Ghost. The Yin Ghost was killed by some crazy bastard and followed his friend to the afterlife. Anyway, do these fucking bastards think Henan is Gotham City...?”
The Heavenly Power Demon froze with his mouth hanging open, then hurriedly poured out his questions.
“T-the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts! How did those men survive and reappear in the Murim? And in Henan, no less? Did the Divine Cult launch a surprise attack on Shaolin?”
“They did raise hell at Shaolin, but it wasn’t the Demonic Cult’s doing.”
“Th-then who was responsible? Who did it?”
I had expected as much, but the Heavenly Power Demon truly knew nothing about the current state of the Murim.
The only outsider he ever spoke to was Old Man Gung.
Not that the old man is the type to explain things out of kindness.
Not unless he considered severing tendons a form of kindness.
After a moment’s thought, I decided to tell him the truth.
The Heavenly Power Demon had no chance of leaving the underground prison before his death anyway.
Besides, Dark Heaven’s existence had once been top secret, but word was already spreading among the major sects. Telling him would cause no harm.
“Uh, I’m not sure how to put this.”
“Tell me. Quickly!”
“Hold on.”
Ah, right.
At last, I found the perfect term. Impressed by my own brilliance, I opened my mouth.
“They changed jobs.”

“I don’t know whether they joined another company or merely transferred to a different department, but until they died, they were working for a group called Dark Heaven instead of the Demonic Cult...”
In the end, I couldn’t finish.
Hurried footsteps approached, and a familiar face appeared.
“B’factor!”
“Swallow what’s in your mouth before you talk.”
“B’factor! B’factor! Try this too! It’s delish!”
“What’s with all the ‘B’factors’? Are you looking for the police chief who lives in Namcheon-dong?”
“B’factor!”
“Yeah, yeah. I’m sure you went to the sauna, ate together, and did the whole nine yards.”
“It’s weally delish!”
Cheongpung had stuffed both cheeks full of snacks, and he was still carrying an armful of food wrapped in paper.
I pulled out a nicely roasted duck leg and was about to sink my teeth into it when I remembered the man I had momentarily forgotten and held it out to him.
“Want one?”
Only then did I finally see the Heavenly Power Demon, frozen like a stone statue.

“How can someone who has never even heard this old man’s title know of the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
“Well, you see...”
I scratched the back of my head and continued.
“I tend to remember the title of anyone I’ve fought.
Especially masters of that caliber.”
“...W-what?
You fought the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts?”
“Technically, I only fought one of them—the Yang Ghost.
Our Old Master—no, Master—killed the Yang Ghost.
The Yin Ghost was killed by some crazy bastard and followed his friend to the afterlife.
Anyway, do these fucking bastards think Henan is Gotham City...?”
The Heavenly Power Demon froze with his mouth hanging open, then hurriedly poured out his questions.
“T-the Yin-Yang Twin Ghosts!
How did those men survive and reappear in the Murim?
And in Henan, no less?
Did the Divine Cult launch a surprise attack on Shaolin?”
“They did raise hell at Shaolin, but it wasn’t the Demonic Cult’s doing.”
“Th-then who was responsible?
Who did it?”
I had expected as much, but the Heavenly Power Demon truly knew nothing about the current state of the Murim.
The only outsider he ever spoke to was Old Man Gung.
Not that the old man is the type to explain things out of kindness.
Not unless he considered severing tendons a form of kindness.
After a moment’s thought, I decided to tell him the truth.
The Heavenly Power Demon had no chance of leaving the underground prison before his death anyway.
Besides, Dark Heaven’s existence had once been top secret, but word was already spreading among the major sects.
Telling him would cause no harm.
“Uh, I’m not sure how to put this.”
“Tell me.
Quickly!”
“Hold on.”
Ah, right.
At last, I found the perfect term.
Impressed by my own brilliance, I opened my mouth.
“They changed jobs.”

“I don’t know whether they joined another company or merely transferred to a different department, but until they died, they were working for a group called Dark Heaven instead of the Demonic Cult...”
In the end, I couldn’t finish.
Hurried footsteps approached, and a familiar face appeared.
“B’factor!”
“Swallow what’s in your mouth before you talk.”
“B’factor!
B’factor!
Try this too!
It’s delish!”
“What’s with all the ‘B’factors’?
Are you looking for the police chief who lives in Namcheon-dong?”
“B’factor!”
“Yeah, yeah.
I’m sure you went to the sauna, ate together, and did the whole nine yards.”
“It’s weally delish!”
Cheongpung had stuffed both cheeks full of snacks, and he was still carrying an armful of food wrapped in paper.
I pulled out a nicely roasted duck leg and was about to sink my teeth into it when I remembered the man I had momentarily forgotten and held it out to him.
“Want one?”
Only then did I finally see the Heavenly Power Demon, frozen like a stone statue.

chapters.title: Chapter 350
paragraphs: Step. Step.
As always, I made my rounds carrying the slop bucket.

Time moved slowly in the underground prison, yet it passed as steadily as the clock at the Ministry of National Defense. I was already entering my sixth day down here, and the routine was gradually becoming familiar.
Clank. Screeeech.
I opened the rusted bars and strode into a cell filled with filth and stagnant water.
An old man bound to a torture rack greeted me with a sly grin.
“You’ve come?”
He was the Killing Ghost, who had joined the Demonic Cult during the Great Faction War and killed more than a hundred martial artists of the orthodox faction.
Now reduced to a toothless old man, he continued through slurred words.
“I tell you this for the last time...”
I cut him off as I scooped up some slop with a long ladle.
“Didn’t you say yesterday was the last time?”
“This time, it truly is the last.”
“Sure. And tomorrow will be the real, real last time.”
I’d been through this countless times over the past six days. It wasn’t even surprising anymore.
The old man flinched at my indifference, then shouted, “You! Become my Disciple!”
“You! Get hit.”
Whack!
The ladle struck him squarely on the crown, and the old man writhed in pain. The chains binding his limbs swayed and clattered noisily.
“Graaaagh!”
“Keep it down. You’re loud.”
“Ugh! You little bastard!”
The old man was about to start yelling at the top of his lungs when his eyes suddenly widened and his nostrils flared.
He had caught the scent of oil beneath the prison’s stench.
“W-what is that smell?”
“Nothing you need to know about.”
“Roast duck. It’s roast duck! Do you have liquor too?”
“What liquor?”
“Liar! That aroma is unmistakably Jiannan Chun!”
“...With a sense of smell like that, you’re on the level of a drug-sniffing dog.”
“Hand it over! Now!”
Whack!
“Graaaagh!”
“It belongs to someone else. Just eat your damn slop.”
I set down the bucket and headed for the last cell.
Far deeper and darker than the others, it held a familiar old monster who was waiting for me.
Clank.
“I brought your meal.”

“You must have had a hard time waiting. By the way, why is it so cold in here? Your sleeping arrangements must be terribly uncomfortable. Should I ask the Tang Clan to lay down an animal-hide blanket for you?”
So this was how he wanted to play it.
Despite my soft, gentle tone, as soothing as a cat’s paw, the Heavenly Power Demon remained stubbornly silent.
Ever since what had happened three days ago, he had kept his eyes and mouth firmly closed.
Of course, that wasn’t enough to make me give up.
“Come on, don’t be like that. Try some of this.”
I took out a sheet of grease-stained paper and unfolded it.
A whole duck, coated in spices and roasted to perfection, revealed itself in all its plump glory. As a bonus, its mouthwatering aroma was strong enough to drive away the stench of the cell.
“What is this? It’s roast duck made by a former imperial chef. I tried some myself, and the duck is definitely tender. The flavor is very consistent too.”
“And roast duck calls for liquor. Jiannan Chun, the famous liquor of Sichuan! Liquor and meat suit a Great Hero like the Heavenly Power Demon, don’t they?”
A frigid silence settled over the already chilly cell.
I kept smiling brightly at the Heavenly Power Demon as he sat cross-legged. At last, I let out a deep sigh.
“Fuck, I can’t do this anymore.”

For three days, I’d bent over backward to please him. I’d softened my voice, spoken with scrupulous politeness, praised him as a Great Hero of benevolence and righteousness, and kissed his ass shamelessly.
But the Heavenly Power Demon had refused every offer and comfort I provided. No matter how much food or clothing I brought him, he never touched any of it.
“I’ve done more than enough by now. Are you really going to keep this up?”
“I’m only being this courteous because I’m such a gentleman. What do you think will happen if the Sichuan Tang Clan finds out, huh?”
At that moment, the Heavenly Power Demon finally spoke without opening his eyes. It was the first time I’d heard his voice in three whole days, and it had grown terribly hoarse.
“Do so.”
“What?”
“This old man has endured enough torture to be sick of it. Even if I depart this world, I will have no regrets.”
He had spent more than forty years imprisoned in the underground prison. Faced with his serene detachment, like some enlightened monk, I clicked my tongue.
“Good grief. You really don’t make things easy. Is it really so difficult to tell me only what you know about Dark Heaven?”
“I have said all there is to say. Kill this old man or torture him. Do as you please.”
“No, what kind of old man is this?”
But the Heavenly Power Demon had already sealed his lips again. He probably wouldn’t open them a second time.
“...What a stubborn old man.”
I heaved a sigh deep enough to sink the earth, placed the liquor and roast duck within his reach, and turned away.
“Fine. For now, just eat that. You haven’t had anything in three days.”
Even as I spoke, I knew. Whether I returned tomorrow, the day after, or three days from now, the food would still be exactly where I’d left it, stone cold and untouched.
“Damn it.”
With the Heavenly Power Demon fed—or at least served—I finished my rounds and dropped to the floor in a corridor far from the cells.
The Heavenly Power Demon.
His rigid face and that indescribable look in his eyes kept flashing through my mind. There was no mistaking the agitation those two words—Dark Heaven—had stirred in him.
The problem was that he refused to say a word about it.
But he definitely knew about Dark Heaven long ago.
I hadn’t heard it directly from the Heavenly Power Demon, but it was already as good as established fact.
The real question was how he knew about Dark Heaven, and how much he knew.
I slowly retraced the conversation I’d had with the Heavenly Power Demon three days ago.
After putting the brain that had earned me seventh-tier school grades through its paces, I arrived at only one plausible conclusion.
Dark Heaven and the Demonic Cult are deeply connected.
No. They might even be one and the same.

The Heavenly Power Demon had once been an Elder of the Demonic Cult. Even after spending forty years imprisoned and tortured in the underground prison, he had never lost his loyalty to the Cult. His silence was proof enough.
If Dark Heaven were an enemy of the Demonic Cult, he would’ve talked by now.
Then what the hell was Dark Heaven? Some splinter faction that had broken away from the Demonic Cult? Or another organization created within the Demonic Cult itself?
A branch of Shincheonji called Sick Shincheonji. Something like that.
Whatever they were, one thing was certain: the bastards were a plague.
I’d been lost in thought for quite some time when Cheongpung appeared with a spring in his step, trailing a sweet aroma behind him.
“Hey!”
“...Your grandpa lives on Lotus Peak at Huashan, right?”
Cheongpung swallowed what was in his mouth before answering.
“No! He’s in Henan right now!”
“Yeah, sure.”
Why did I even bother talking to him?
The mountain of food piled in Cheongpung’s arms left me speechless. I was starting to feel sorry for the former imperial chef, and I’d never even seen the man’s face.
“You went out for all this?”
“Yes! And while I was at it, I brought a letter from the Beggars’ Sect.”
“...Shouldn’t that be the other way around?”
“Hehe.”
“Don’t smile. I’ll get attached.”
I answered gruffly and accepted the letter Cheongpung held out.
When I unfolded the grimy paper—wherever he’d been keeping it, it couldn’t have been clean—three strands of yellow dog hair drifted out.
A three-knot Disciple. The branch leader sent it.
Just as I’d expected, the letter was addressed to Gung Gibang from the Beggars’ Sect’s Chengdu branch leader.
Of course, Gung Gibang was at the Divine Physician’s secret refuge, so the branch leader had probably sent it to me for convenience.
A moment later, when I looked up from the letter, Cheongpung asked, “What does it say?”
“Nothing much. They’re still searching.”
The Beggars’ Sect had originally combed through Sichuan with a fine-tooth comb in search of the Divine Physician, but it had since changed targets.
Now it was hunting the culprit who had murdered the Poison King and the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun.
Not that a man like that would be easy to catch.
Tang Sadok had initially insisted on settling the matter with the Sichuan Tang Clan’s strength alone, but his attitude had changed after he lent me the Myriad-Poison Ring.
Yet even with the Tang Clan’s full cooperation, the culprit’s trail had vanished like a ghost.
“Do you think they’ll find him?”
“Who knows? We’ll have to hope for the best. We have the Beggars’ Sect, and the Tang Clan’s Green Shadow Squad are experts in reconnaissance and pursuit. Surely they’ll turn up something.”
“What about the government troops?”
“They seem to be pulling their weight too.”
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, wielded tremendous influence.
Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, had readily agreed to my request to search for the culprit instead of the Divine Physician.
The individual fighting ability of the government troops couldn’t compare to that of Murim warriors, but their sheer numbers—several thousand men—couldn’t be ignored.
“Wow! Thousands?”
“I don’t know the exact number, but apparently they’re swarming all over the place. You saw the government troops too, didn’t you, Cheongpung? On our way back to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Oh, but there weren’t that many when I saw them.”
“...Of course not. Did you think thousands of men would all travel together?”
It wasn’t difficult to imagine the government troops gathered in groups of three or five according to their assigned formations, stopping and searching people.
The government troops are gradually expanding their search area and advancing toward Qingcheng and Emei. They appear to be searching for the culprit while preparing for a possible incident.
I read the last line of the letter and let out a quiet laugh.
They’re doing better than I expected.

Won Gyun, the City Lord of Sichuan Province, looked every inch the corrupt official, but apparently he wasn’t completely incompetent. Either that, or the military officer in charge of this operation knew what he was doing.
But what if they still can’t find him after all this?
I’d talked a big game in front of Tang Sadok, so the thought was seriously worrying.
Of course, Jeok Cheongang’s safe recovery came first.
I glanced at the treatment room, whose door remained firmly shut, then casually asked Cheongpung, “What kind of food did you bring?”
“Sho mush!”
“...Finish what’s in your mouth. I’ll take care of the rest.”
Jang Il was a two-knot Disciple of the Beggars’ Sect.

He had become one out of necessity rather than choice. He’d heard a rumor that anyone who formally joined the Beggars’ Sect, underwent the initiation ceremony, and became an official Disciple would receive a whole dumpling.
What could an eight-year-old beggar brat who hadn’t eaten in four days have known?
Clutching his empty stomach, he had gone to the Chengdu branch and become a Beggars’ Sect disciple that very day.
“They only gave me half a dumpling, too. Just thinking about it still makes my teeth grind. Goddamn it.”
The beggars listening to Jang Il yawned quietly. They’d already heard the story dozens of times.
More than ten years had passed, but Jang Il’s anger had yet to subside.
“I gritted my teeth over that half dumpling and worked my way up to deputy branch leader. So you lot should...”
As the story showed signs of dragging on, the three one-knot Disciples exchanged glances.
“Oh! My stomach suddenly hurts!”
“Gasp! Mine too!”
“Ugh, the latrine! Where’s the latrine?”
“You little bastards!”
Jang Il shouted, but the three beggars had already bolted.
“Those damn brats... Just wait until they come back.”
That was when a group of men caught Jang Il’s eye.
Uniform clothing and weapons. Their lack of military discipline was an added bonus. The sight was familiar enough that Jang Il muttered,
“Government troops.”
These days, government troops were more common than neighborhood stray dogs.
Normally, they slacked off so thoroughly that no one ever saw them, but now that the high and mighty had stepped in, they seemed to be scrambling to at least put on a show.
They said they were expanding the search area. Are they already this far out?
As he wondered about it, a middle-aged military officer who appeared to be leading the group approached him with a smile.
“Are you, by any chance, a Beggars’ Sect disciple?”
Jang Il nodded casually.
“As you can see.”
“I thought so when I saw your knots.”
“Anyone can tell just by looking. Still, you’ve made good time. You’re already this far out.”
“Ah, they say the Beggars’ Sect has the finest intelligence network under heaven. I suppose you already knew we were coming?”
“This much is nothing out of the ordinary for our Sect.”
The military officer smiled along with the smug Jang Il.
“But there are no villages nearby, and hardly anyone passes through here. Why are you alone?”
“Don’t ask. The branch leader kept nagging me, so I brought a few men out for some fresh air. Things have been pretty noisy lately with all this talk of a murderer and whatnot.”
“I see.”
“Well then, take care...”
Jang Il never finished.
The moment the officer nodded with a smile, something cold pierced his chest.
Shnk!
...Huh?
Cough.
Jang Il stared blankly at the sword buried in his chest and coughed up blood.
Why? How?
The questions never escaped his lips. His knees buckled as he stared at the officer through clouding eyes.
His face struck the new shoots just beginning to emerge from the earth, and a cold voice reached his ears.
“Find the others. They should be nearby.”
“As you command.”
“Stupid beggar bastard. Why did he have to be here of all places...?”
That was the last thing Jang Il heard.
He was twenty-five years old.
The young beggar died in a secluded forest two days from Emei Sect.

“Ah, they say the Beggars’ Sect has the finest intelligence network under heaven.
I suppose you already knew we were coming?”
“This much is nothing out of the ordinary for our Sect.”
The military officer smiled along with the smug Jang Il.
“But there are no villages nearby, and hardly anyone passes through here.
Why are you alone?”
“Don’t ask.
The branch leader kept nagging me, so I brought a few men out for some fresh air.
Things have been pretty noisy lately with all this talk of a murderer and whatnot.”
“I see.”
“Well then, take care...”
Jang Il never finished.
The moment the officer nodded with a smile, something cold pierced his chest.
Shnk!
...Huh?
Cough.
Jang Il stared blankly at the sword buried in his chest and coughed up blood.
Why?
How?
The questions never escaped his lips.
His knees buckled as he stared at the officer through clouding eyes.
His face struck the new shoots just beginning to emerge from the earth, and a cold voice reached his ears.
“Find the others.
They should be nearby.”
“As you command.”
“Stupid beggar bastard.
Why did he have to be here of all places...?”
That was the last thing Jang Il heard.
He was twenty-five years old.
The young beggar died in a secluded forest two days from Emei Sect.
